1387    /// the Session's SURBs unadmitted.
1388    fn peek_admission_token(&self) -> AdmissionToken {
1389        self.admission_token.get().copied().unwrap_or(AdmissionToken::NONE)
1390    }
1391
1392    /// Records a target announced by a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive, if it is the largest so far.
1393    ///
1394    /// Monotone on purpose, matching the ring it widens: the announcement stream is a slew, and the
1395    /// last value seen is the one the Entry is filling toward. Recorded even before `commit` has
1396    /// sized the ring, which is the window the Exit's `SessionEstablished`-before-commit ordering
1397    /// opens; [`peek_raised_surb_target`](Self::peek_raised_surb_target) then lets the commit start
1398    /// from the largest figure already announced rather than from establishment's.
1399    fn note_raised_surb_target(&self, target: usize) {
1400        self.raised_surb_target
1401            .fetch_max(target, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
1402        // Pairs with the fence after `commit` records the admission token. The two sides are a
1403        // store-then-load handshake across *two* cells: this side records the target and then reads
1404        // the token, `commit` writes the token and then reads the target. With both sides `Relaxed`
1405        // and no fence, a weakly ordered CPU lets each read the other's old value — the keep-alive
1406        // sees no token (so its raise is a no-op) while `commit` sees no target (so it sizes from the
1407        // establishment figure). The balancer set-point has already moved by then, so the
1408        // `!= announced` guard in `handle_keep_alive` never retries the raise and the ring stays
1409        // undersized for the Session's life. The fence makes sure at least one side sees the other.
1410        std::sync::atomic::fence(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
1411    }
1412
1413    /// The largest target announced since establishment, or `None` while none has been.
1414    fn peek_raised_surb_target(&self) -> Option<usize> {
1415        match self.raised_surb_target.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
1416            0 => None,
1417            target => Some(target),
1418        }
1419    }
1420}
1421
1422/// Counts the SURB a return packet will take as consumed in `estimator`, and attaches the refund that
1423/// gives it back.
1424///
1425/// The Exit counts as it hands a packet on, because its reserve and admission decisions need the count
1426/// at once. The packet can still be dropped before it takes a SURB: the PIX egress gate may never admit
1427/// it (see [`acquire_egress_permit`]), and routing resolution may find no SURB within its wait. The
1428/// refund then counts the SURB as given back in this estimator (see [`SurbRefund`]). It points at the
1429/// estimator itself, so it reaches the Session that counted the packet whatever has happened to the
1430/// Session's slot since, and it never touches the slot.
1431///
1432/// The refund restores the held count the fill reserve and the drain budget read, and nothing else:
1433/// the balancer's level, which the egress rate and the level reports follow, saturates at zero and
1434/// has already absorbed a count made while it was empty (see
1435/// [`SurbFlowEstimator::estimate_surbs_refunded`]).
1436fn count_return_packet_surb(estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator, mut data: ApplicationDataOut) -> ApplicationDataOut {
1437    estimator.consumed.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
1438    data.surb_refund = SurbRefund::to(estimator.refunded.clone());
1439    data
1440}
1441
1442/// The Exit's control over the single Exit → Entry keep-alive stream a Session runs.
1443///
1444/// One stream, two producers with different jobs, and this is what reconciles them:
1445///
1446/// * the **SURB-level notification**, sent every `surb_balance_notify_period`, which tells the Entry's balancer how
1447///   many SURBs the Exit believes it holds. It is the signal that asks for more, so it is exempt from the SURB reserve;
1448///   but it is a return packet like any other, so it goes out only to an Entry that has shown it refills, and only
1449///   while the Exit's estimate shows a SURB to send it on (see [`admit`](Self::admit));
1450/// * **PIX fill**, whose rate the supervisor plans once a second so that a funded cycle completes inside its own
1451///   deadline even if the application never sends a byte.
1452///
1453/// The effective rate is the faster of the two, because both are the same packet: a keep-alive
1454/// carrying the SURB level is exactly what fill needs to send, and sending two streams of them would
1455/// double the traffic to say the same thing twice. Every shipped Entry already parses it, counts it
1456/// as a consumed SURB so its balancer refills, and — since the fix that precedes this — credits it as
1457/// service against the successor gate.
1458pub(crate) struct PixFillControl {
1459    session_id: SessionId,
1460    /// The rate limiter of the keep-alive stream this steers.
1461    controller: RateController,
1462    /// The configured SURB-level notification period, if the node has one.
1463    ///
1464    /// `None` disables the notification half entirely; the stream then runs at the fill rate alone,
1465    /// which is how a PIX Session on a node with `surb_balance_notify_period: None` still fills.
1466    notify_period: Option<Duration>,
1467    /// SURBs that must remain estimated-available before a *fill* packet is let through.
1468    ///
1469    /// The *effective* reserve for this Session, not the configured one: the Entry decides how deep
1470    /// the Exit's SURB buffer for the Session is, so a reserve above what the Entry ever intends to
1471    /// supply would refuse every fill packet forever. See [`effective_surb_reserve`].
1472    min_surb_reserve: u64,
1473    /// The Session's SURB flow estimate, which is what the reserve is measured against.
1474    estimator: AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
1475    /// The Session's balancer state, read for whether the Entry has shown that it refills this side's
1476    /// SURBs ([`counterparty_refills`](BalancerStateValues::counterparty_refills)): the evidence that a
1477    /// SURB-level notification has a reader.
1478    surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
1479    state: parking_lot::Mutex<PixFillState>,
1480}
1481
1482struct PixFillState {
1483    /// Whether the initial notification delay has elapsed.
1484    ///
1485    /// The notification stream deliberately waits one period before starting, so a Session that
1486    /// closes immediately never sends one. Fill does not wait, and must not be held behind this.
1487    notify_started: bool,
1488    /// The rate the PIX supervisor last asked for. [`FillRate::ZERO`] when it is not filling.
1489    fill: FillRate,
1490    /// When a packet was last let through as the SURB-level notification.
1491    ///
1492    /// The two producers share a stream, so nothing about a packet says which of them it belongs to.
1493    /// This is what makes the distinction: one packet per notification period is the notification and
1494    /// is exempt from the SURB reserve, and everything above that rate is fill and is not.
1495    last_notify_at: Option<Instant>,
1496    /// Whether the SURB reserve is currently withholding fill, so `hopr_pix_sessions_stalled` counts
1497    /// this Session once per stall rather than once per refused packet.
1498    withholding: bool,
1499    /// Whether this stream is draining the SURB buffer of a Session that has already been closed.
1500    ///
1501    /// Set once, by [`PixFillControl::enter_drain`], and never cleared: a drain ends with the
1502    /// Session, and the stream with it.
1503    draining: bool,
1504}
1505
1506impl PixFillControl {
1507    fn new(
1508        session_id: SessionId,
1509        controller: RateController,
1510        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
1511        min_surb_reserve: u64,
1512        estimator: AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
1513        surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
1514    ) -> Self {
1515        Self {
1516            session_id,
1517            controller,
1518            notify_period,
1519            // Clamped rather than trusted: a `SessionManager` can be built from a config that never
1520            // went through `validate_pix_supervision`, and a zero reserve would let fill spend the
1521            // Session's last SURB. `effective_surb_reserve` applies the same floor, so this is only
1522            // load-bearing for the tests that construct a control directly.
1523            min_surb_reserve: min_surb_reserve.max(1),
1524            estimator,
1525            surb_mgmt,
1526            state: parking_lot::Mutex::new(PixFillState {
1527                notify_started: false,
1528                fill: FillRate::ZERO,
1529                last_notify_at: None,
1530                withholding: false,
1531                draining: false,
1532            }),
1533        }
1534    }
1535
1536    /// Turns the SURB-level notification on, after its initial delay.
1537    ///
1538    /// A no-op once the Session is draining, for the reason [`enter_drain`](Self::enter_drain)
1539    /// gives — and it has to be checked here rather than only there, because the one-shot delay task
1540    /// holds a clone of this control and nothing bounds how long an operator may make its period.
1541    pub(crate) fn start_notify(&self) {
1542        let mut state = self.state.lock();
1543        if state.draining {
1544            return;
1545        }
1546        state.notify_started = true;
1547        self.apply(&state);
1548    }
1549
1550    /// Puts the stream into post-close drain mode, silencing the SURB-level notification.
1551    ///
1552    /// Returns `false` if the stream was draining already, which is how two closes racing through
1553    /// `begin_surb_drain` settle which of them owns the drain. The read and the write have to be one
1554    /// lock acquisition for that: callers that each saw [`is_draining`](Self::is_draining) before
1555    /// either wrote it would both start a drain, and both tell the supervisor about it.
1556    ///
1557    /// The notification is the single packet [`admit_at`](Self::admit_at) exempts from the SURB
1558    /// reserve, and the exemption exists for one reason: it is the message that asks the Entry for
1559    /// more SURBs. It asks on behalf of a Session that a drain has already lost — the Entry itself
1560    /// may well still be there, but nothing is left to act on the request — so leaving it on would
1561    /// originate below the reserve into a buffer nothing is refilling, which is the one failure mode
1562    /// [`PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve`](crate::supervision::PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve)
1563    /// exists to prevent, since a return packet with no SURB holds up every packet this node
1564    /// originates. With it off, `notification_due` is always false and the reserve is the only gate.
1565    pub(crate) fn enter_drain(&self) -> bool {
1566        let mut state = self.state.lock();
1567        if state.draining {
1568            return false;
1569        }
1570        state.draining = true;
1571        state.notify_started = false;
1572        self.apply(&state);
1573        true
1574    }
1575
1576    /// Whether this Session is draining its SURB buffer after having been closed.
1577    pub(crate) fn is_draining(&self) -> bool {
1578        self.state.lock().draining
1579    }
1580
1581    /// The SURBs this Session could still spend on a drain, net of the reserve it must leave behind.
1582    ///
1583    /// An estimate and an upper bound at that — ring-buffer overwrites, store eviction and
1584    /// invalidated relayers are all unobserved — which is why the supervisor weighs it against a
1585    /// cycle's whole remaining emission rather than a discounted one. The reserve subtracted is the
1586    /// *effective* one already derived for this Session, not the configured ceiling.
1587    pub(crate) fn drainable_surbs(&self) -> u64 {
1588        self.estimator.saturating_diff().saturating_sub(self.min_surb_reserve)
1589    }
1590
1591    /// Applies a rate planned by the PIX supervisor.
1592    pub(crate) fn set_fill(&self, rate: FillRate) {
1593        let mut state = self.state.lock();
1594        if state.fill == rate {
1595            return;
1596        }
1597        state.fill = rate;
1598        self.apply(&state);
1599    }
1600
1601    /// The rate the stream is currently running at — the faster of the two producers.
1602    ///
1603    /// The production path never asks: [`apply`](Self::apply) derives it and hands it straight to the
1604    /// controller, which is the only consumer that matters. This exists so the merge rule can be
1605    /// tested as the rule it is, rather than inferred from packet timings.
1606    #[cfg(test)]
1607    pub(crate) fn effective_rate(&self) -> FillRate {
1608        Self::effective(&self.state.lock(), self.notify_period)
1609    }
1610
1611    fn effective(state: &PixFillState, notify_period: Option<Duration>) -> FillRate {
1612        let notify = state
1613            .notify_started
1614            .then_some(notify_period)
1615            .flatten()
1616            .map(FillRate::once_per);
1617        let fill = (!state.fill.is_zero()).then_some(state.fill);
1618        match (notify, fill) {
1619            (Some(notify), Some(fill)) if fill.as_packets_per_sec() > notify.as_packets_per_sec() => fill,
1620            (Some(notify), _) => notify,
1621            (None, Some(fill)) => fill,
1622            (None, None) => FillRate::ZERO,
1623        }
1624    }
1625
1626    fn apply(&self, state: &PixFillState) {
1627        let rate = Self::effective(state, self.notify_period);
1628        // A zero period would trip the controller's own assertion. `FillRate` never carries one —
1629        // `ZERO` is one second and the two constructors take a validated period — so this is a
1630        // belt-and-braces floor rather than a case that arises.
1631        self.controller
1632            .set_rate_per_unit(rate.packets as usize, rate.per.max(Duration::from_micros(1)));
1633        trace!(
1634            session_id = %self.session_id,
1635            packets = rate.packets,
1636            per = ?rate.per,
1637            "applied the exit keep-alive rate"
1638        );
1639    }
1640
1641    /// Decides whether the next keep-alive may go out, and books it if so.
1642    ///
1643    /// The SURB-level notification is exempt from the SURB reserve: it is the message that asks the Entry
1644    /// for more SURBs, so holding it to the reserve would be refusing to ask for the thing that is
1645    /// scarce. It still needs two things, because it is a return packet like any other.
1646    ///
1647    /// * **A reader.** The Entry must have shown that it refills this side's SURBs
1648    ///   ([`counterparty_refills`](BalancerStateValues::counterparty_refills)), which is any keep-alive from its
1649    ///   balancer, flagged or not, but not a manual ping ([`KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing`]): only an Entry with a SURB
1650    ///   balancer sends one of its own accord. An Entry without a balancer attaches a SURB to each data packet and acts
1651    ///   on no report, so every report to it spends a SURB to say nothing. This is decided from what this side has seen
1652    ///   and not from the target the Entry announced, because that is a figure the peer picks, and a report sent on the
1653    ///   strength of it can find no SURB.
1654    /// * **A SURB to send it on.** The estimate must be above zero. With none, the report would not go: the routing
1655    ///   resolver holds a return packet that finds no SURB for the whole of `surb_resolution_wait` and holds every
1656    ///   packet this node originates with it (gnosis_vpn#748).
1657    ///
1658    /// A notification that is due and withheld on either count keeps its slot: the next packet to ask is still
1659    /// classified as the notification, and goes out as soon as both hold. The withheld packet has used its release
1660    /// from the rate limiter, though, so with no fill running that next packet is up to a notification period away,
1661    /// and with one running it is the next fill packet. A withheld notification is also not mistaken for fill. While
1662    /// the PIX supervisor runs a fill, the packet is fill and meets the reserve like any other; while none runs, it
1663    /// is dropped.
1664    ///
1665    /// Fill above that rate is refused while the estimate is below the reserve, and that refusal is
1666    /// not an optimisation. A return packet that finds no SURB is not dropped — the routing resolver
1667    /// holds it, and with it every packet this node originates, for the whole of
1668    /// `surb_resolution_wait`. An Exit filling a cycle down to its last SURB would therefore stall
1669    /// the Session it is filling for, and every other Session on the node with it.
1670    ///
1671    /// # Which packet is the notification
1672    ///
1673    /// Nothing about a packet says which producer it belongs to, so the notification is the first one
1674    /// released no sooner than a period after the last — *less a slack of
1675    /// `min(MAX_WAIT_CHUNK, period / 2)`*, which is what keeps the classification from resting on
1676    /// scheduling latency. The rate limiter that releases these packets sleeps in chunks of
1677    /// [`MAX_WAIT_CHUNK`], re-reads its controller on each wake, and rounds a rate into an integer
1678    /// packet count, so a stream asked for one packet per period releases them a shade over or a
1679    /// shade under it. Compared against the period exactly, a period the controller rounds short by a
1680    /// microsecond would classify every other notification as fill — counted in
1681    /// `hopr_session_pix_fill_packets_total` and, below the reserve, dropped. That is the signal
1682    /// asking the Entry for the SURBs whose absence caused the drop, and it runs on every Exit
1683    /// Session with a `surb_balance_notify_period` configured, PIX or not.
1684    ///
1685    /// The slack cannot let fill masquerade as the notification: `last_notify_at` advances to the
1686    /// instant the packet actually went out, so only the *first* packet past the slack window is the
1687    /// notification, and every fill packet that follows it inside the period is still fill and is
1688    /// still bounded by the reserve. The cap at half the period is what stops a very short period
1689    /// from having its window widened away to nothing.
1690    pub(crate) fn admit(&self) -> bool {
1691        self.admit_at(Instant::now())
1692    }
1693
1694    /// [`admit`](Self::admit) against a caller-supplied instant, so the classification can be tested
1695    /// as the rule it is rather than by sleeping out a period and hoping the scheduler cooperates.
1696    fn admit_at(&self, now: Instant) -> bool {
1697        let mut state = self.state.lock();
1698
1699        // Due *slightly early*: see the classification rule on `admit`. The slack is what keeps this
1700        // from resting on the scheduling latency of the stream that releases the packet.
1701        let notification_due = state.notify_started
1702            && self.notify_period.is_some_and(|period| {
1703                let slack = MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(period / 2);
1704                state
1705                    .last_notify_at
1706                    .is_none_or(|at| now.saturating_duration_since(at) >= period.saturating_sub(slack))
1707            });
1708
1709        if notification_due {
1710            if self.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills() && self.estimator.saturating_diff() > 0 {
1711                state.last_notify_at = Some(now);
1712                return true;
1713            }
1714
1715            // Withheld. With no fill running, the slot is not fill either: letting it fall through to the reserve
1716            // check would send a report every period, labelled as fill, from any Session that is above the reserve
1717            // and has no Entry reading it.
1718            if state.fill.is_zero() {
1719                return false;
1720            }
1721        }
1722
1723        if self.estimator.saturating_diff() >= self.min_surb_reserve {
1724            Self::set_withholding(&mut state, false);
1725            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
1726            telemetry::record_pix_fill_packet();
1727            return true;
1728        }
1729
1730        debug!(
1731            session_id = %self.session_id,
1732            reserve = self.min_surb_reserve,
1733            estimate = self.estimator.saturating_diff(),
1734            "withholding a PIX fill keep-alive to stay above the SURB reserve"
1735        );
1736        Self::set_withholding(&mut state, true);
1737        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
1738        telemetry::pix::record_pix_fill_backoff(telemetry::pix::PixFillBackoff::SurbReserve);
1739        false
1740    }
1741
1742    /// Moves the `surb_starved` gauge on the edges only, so it counts stalled Sessions rather than
1743    /// refused packets — the same distinction `PixGateBlockEpisode` draws for the egress gate.
1744    fn set_withholding(state: &mut PixFillState, withholding: bool) {
1745        if state.withholding == withholding {
1746            return;
1747        }
1748        state.withholding = withholding;
1749        crate::supervision::telemetry::emit_sessions_stalled(
1750            crate::supervision::telemetry::PixStallCause::SurbStarved,
1751            if withholding { 1 } else { -1 },
1752        );
1753    }
1754}
1755
1756/// Returns this Session's `surb_starved` count if it was withholding when it went away.
1757///
1758/// `Drop` rather than a call on the close paths, for the reason `PixGateBlockEpisode` gives: a
1759/// Session can end by teardown, by drain, or by its last `Arc` going out of scope in a task nobody
1760/// is waiting on, and this is the one mechanism that covers all three. Without it a Session that
1761/// dies mid-stall leaves the gauge standing for the life of the process.
1762impl Drop for PixFillControl {
1763    fn drop(&mut self) {
1764        Self::set_withholding(self.state.get_mut(), false);
1765    }
1766}
1767
1768/// The SURB reserve one Session's fill actually respects.
1769///
1770/// [`PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve`](crate::supervision::PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve) is a
1771/// *ceiling* rather than the value used, and it has to be, because the two sides of the comparison
1772/// are chosen by different nodes. The reserve is measured against the Exit's estimate of its own SURB
1773/// buffer for the Session, and how deep that buffer is is the *Entry's* decision — it announces its
1774/// balancer target in the lower 32 bits of the options word in `StartInitiation::additional_data`. An operator sizing
1775/// the reserve against a production buffer therefore also decides, unintentionally, that every Session
1776/// whose Entry asks for a shallower one can never be filled at all: the estimate never reaches the
1777/// reserve, every fill packet is withheld, and the funded cycle strands on `max_recovery_time` while
1778/// the logs report only a backoff.
1779///
1780/// A quarter of the announced target is what the reserve is for expressed as a proportion: it leaves
1781/// fill three quarters of whatever buffer the Entry chose and keeps the last quarter for the
1782/// application, which is the side that has something waiting on it. The configured value still binds
1783/// wherever it is the smaller of the two — at the shipped 500 against the worked profile's 7 000-SURB
1784/// target, a quarter is 1 750, so the derivation is inert on a production-sized Session and only
1785/// engages on one whose Entry asked for less than four times the configured reserve.
1786///
1787/// Floored at one, for the same reason the constructor clamps: a zero reserve is fill spending the
1788/// Session's last SURB, and an Entry announcing a three-SURB buffer would otherwise produce exactly
1789/// that.
1790fn effective_surb_reserve(configured: u64, announced_target: u64) -> u64 {
1791    configured.min(announced_target / 4).max(1)
1792}
1793
1794/// One Session's reservation against the node's live reconstructor-cycle budget.
1795///
1796/// Charged when a PIX Session is accepted and returned when its Session closes. Deliberately a
1797/// projection rather than a measurement: the alternative is to weigh the reconstructor's actual
1798/// state and refuse a share once it is too large, which loses the cycle of whichever Session
1799/// happened to arrive last rather than of the one that inflated it. A reservation taken up front can
1800/// only ever refuse a Session that does not exist yet.
1801#[derive(Debug)]
1802pub(crate) struct CycleBudgetReservation {
1803    bytes: u64,
1804    outstanding: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
1805    /// Whether [`release`](Self::release) has already run, so it can be called from both the close
1806    /// path and `Drop` without the budget being returned twice.
1807    released: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
1808}
1809
1810impl CycleBudgetReservation {
1811    /// Returns the reservation to the node's budget. Idempotent.
1812    ///
1813    /// Called explicitly by [`close_session`], and by `Drop` as the backstop.
1814    ///
1815    /// Both, and not just `Drop`, because the slot lives in a `moka` cache: `remove` hands the value
1816    /// back but drops the cache's own clone during a later maintenance pass, so a purely
1817    /// refcount-driven release would return the budget at an unpredictable time — and a node whose
1818    /// Sessions all closed could still refuse the next one. The explicit call makes the release
1819    /// simultaneous with the closure that caused it; the flag is what keeps the deferred drop from
1820    /// crediting it a second time.
1821    fn release(&self) {
1822        if self.released.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
1823            return;
1824        }
1825        // Saturating, so a release the flag somehow failed to suppress could not wrap the counter
1826        // into a budget that admits everything.
1827        let outstanding = self
1828            .outstanding
1829            .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |held| {
1830                Some(held.saturating_sub(self.bytes))
1831            })
1832            .unwrap_or_default()
1833            .saturating_sub(self.bytes);
1834
1835        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
1836        crate::telemetry::pix::record_cycle_bytes_released(self.bytes);
1837
1838        trace!(
1839            released = self.bytes,
1840            outstanding, "released live-cycle budget reservation"
1841        );
1842    }
1843}
1844
1845impl Drop for CycleBudgetReservation {
1846    fn drop(&mut self) {
1847        self.release();
1848    }
1849}
1850
1851/// Commits `guard`, admitting `session_id` into the SURB store for `capacity` SURBs.
1852///
1853/// Free function rather than a method on [`SessionManager`] because the guard borrows the manager's
1854/// cache, so a method would fight the same borrow the call sites are already inside. `surb_admission`
1855/// is passed separately for the same reason — the call sites hold `&self` while the guard holds the
1856/// cache borrow.
1857///
1858/// The slot is re-read from the cache rather than kept from allocation: the token `admit` returns has
1859/// to land in the *cached* copy of the slot, and that copy and the one the guard rolled in are two
1860/// clones of one value — see [`SessionSlot::claim_admission_token`] for why the cell they share is
1861/// behind an `Arc`. Re-reading is what keeps this honest when the cache has since handed the entry to
1862/// another reader: they all share the one cell.
1863///
1864/// An absent slot is not an error: the Session *was* established on this path, and `commit` runs with
1865/// `None` so the guard is still marked committed and the Session still counted. The teardown that
1866/// removed the slot already decremented `METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS` and logged "session closed", so
1867/// skipping the commit here would drift the gauge down by one and leave that close unpaired (see
1868/// [`SessionSlotGuard::commit`]).
1869///
1870/// A slot found by key that is *not* the one this establishment allocated is treated exactly like an
1871/// absent one, and for the same reason: the re-read is by a reusable pseudonym, so between this
1872/// Session's `SessionEstablished` send and its parked commit a teardown can remove its slot and a
1873/// successor Session can be allocated under the same key. Admitting into the successor's slot would
1874/// stamp the successor's ring with this Session's token, and the successor's own commit would then
1875/// find the cell occupied and retire the successor's live admission — dropping a running Session to
1876/// the quarantine, the failure this whole seam exists to prevent. The guard holds its own slot's
1877/// [`AdmissionCell`], so the re-read can reject a foreign slot by identity; the commit itself still
1878/// runs, since this Session *was* established.
1879fn commit_slot_guard(
1880    guard: &mut SessionSlotGuard<'_>,
1881    sessions: &moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
1882    session_id: SessionId,
1883    surb_admission: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>>,
1884    capacity: usize,
1885) {
1886    // Re-read so the token lands in the cached copy; `None` means a teardown already removed it, and
1887    // the commit below still runs — only the admission is skipped. A slot that has since been
1888    // reallocated to another Session on this same pseudonym is discarded the same way: its cell is not
1889    // the guard's, so it is not this commit's to admit into.
1890    let slot = sessions
1891        .get(&session_id)
1892        .filter(|slot| Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.admission_token, guard.admission_token()));
1893
1894    guard.commit(
1895        slot.as_ref(),
1896        surb_admission.get().map(|a| a.as_ref() as &dyn SurbAdmissionControl),
1897        capacity,
1898    );
1899}
1900
1901/// RAII guard that rolls back a freshly inserted [`SessionSlot`] unless the
1902/// session setup is explicitly [committed](SessionSlotGuard::commit).
1903///
1904/// Establishing a session involves several fallible steps *after* the slot has
1905/// been inserted into the Session cache (constructing the [`HoprSession`],
1906/// notifying about the new session, sending the establishment message, ...).
1907/// If any of these steps fails, the already inserted slot would otherwise linger
1908/// in the cache until idle eviction, blocking the pseudonym (and counting towards
1909/// `maximum_sessions`) in the meantime.
1910///
1911/// Dropping this guard without committing removes the slot and tears down the
1912/// partially initialized session. Since Moka's removal is asynchronous and Rust
1913/// has no asynchronous `Drop`, the cleanup is performed on a spawned task.
1914struct SessionSlotGuard<'a> {
1915    sessions: &'a moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
1916    active_sessions: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
1917    session_id: SessionId,
1918    /// The SURB-store seam, cloned from the manager at allocation so `commit` and `Drop` can both
1919    /// reach it without holding the manager borrow. Held rather than looked up at call time because
1920    /// the rollback in `Drop` runs after the establishing task has already failed, and a guard that
1921    /// captured the manager's borrow there would fight the lifetimes for no gain.
1922    admission: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>>,
1923    /// The packet pipeline's SURB-resolution window, cloned at allocation with the seam for the same
1924    /// reason: the rollback's deferred retire has to wait it out, and the guard outlives the
1925    /// establishing call that could otherwise read the manager's config.
1926    surb_resolution_wait: Duration,
1927    /// The admission-token cell of the slot this guard allocated, so a commit that re-reads the cache
1928    /// by key can tell its own slot from a successor's — see [`AdmissionCell`] and
1929    /// [`commit_slot_guard`].
1930    admission_cell: AdmissionCell,
1931    committed: bool,
1932}
1933
1934impl<'a> SessionSlotGuard<'a> {
1935    fn new(
1936        sessions: &'a moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
1937        session_id: SessionId,
1938        active_sessions: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
1939        admission: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>>,
1940        surb_resolution_wait: Duration,
1941        admission_cell: AdmissionCell,
1942    ) -> Self {
1943        Self {
1944            sessions,
1945            active_sessions,
1946            session_id,
1947            admission,
1948            surb_resolution_wait,
1949            admission_cell,
1950            committed: false,
1951        }
1952    }
1953
1954    /// The admission-token cell of the slot this guard allocated. [`commit_slot_guard`] compares it
1955    /// against the cell of the slot the cache hands back for the same key, so a slot reallocated to a
1956    /// successor Session is recognised as foreign.
1957    fn admission_token(&self) -> &AdmissionCell {
1958        &self.admission_cell
1959    }
1960
1961    /// Marks the session as successfully established, preventing the slot from
1962    /// being rolled back when this guard is dropped.
1963    ///
1964    /// Logs "new session established" here, on both the Entry and the Exit side, so that every
1965    /// "session closed" line from [`close_session`] has a matching start line.
1966    ///
1967    /// This is also where the Session's pseudonym is admitted into the SURB store: deliberately
1968    /// here, at the point the Session becomes live, and not in
1969    /// [`allocate_session_slot`](SessionManager::allocate_session_slot), which runs while the Start
1970    /// handshake is still in flight — admitting there would put an unauthenticated peer into the
1971    /// store's admitted class, the exact state the admission control exists to prevent
1972    /// (hoprnet#8515). The Exit's negotiated ring target is likewise only known by the time its
1973    /// branch reaches `commit`, which allocation is too early to see.
1974    ///
1975    /// `admission` is `Some` on every production path — the guard carries the manager's seam, and
1976    /// `capacity` is the buffer target the ring is sized from. On the Exit that is the one the Entry
1977    /// announced, or the node's maximum when it announced none; the Entry's own commits always pass
1978    /// the node's `maximum_surb_buffer_size`. The `Option` keeps the guard usable from tests and
1979    /// callers that run without a store.
1980    ///
1981    /// The token `admit` returns lands in the slot's own cell rather than on the guard: the guard is
1982    /// gone by the time the Session is torn down, and the teardown reads the token from the slot it
1983    /// removes. Writing it here, after the `admit`, is what lets a later `release_session_slot`
1984    /// retire exactly this admission.
1985    ///
1986    /// `slot` is the cached copy when the caller could still find it *and* it is this establishment's
1987    /// own, and `None` when the slot was already torn down or has been reallocated to a successor
1988    /// Session on the same pseudonym — [`commit_slot_guard`] discards the latter before calling here.
1989    /// Committing without a slot is still a commit: the Session *was* established (the Exit sends
1990    /// `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so an Entry can close or answer with a
1991    /// `SessionId`-scoped `SessionError` in that window), so the guard must be marked committed and
1992    /// the Session counted, or the teardown's decrement would leave `METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS` drifting
1993    /// down and `close_session` would log a "session closed" with no matching "new session
1994    /// established". Only the `admit` is skipped — there is no cell left to carry its token.
1995    ///
1996    /// When a slot *is* present, it is this Session's own (the caller checked), so its cell arbitrates
1997    /// against a teardown racing this commit and nothing else can be writing to it. The teardown claims
1998    /// the cell (see [`SessionSlot::claim_admission_token`]), so if this commit's own `set` fails, a
1999    /// teardown has already passed the point where it read the cell: it saw nothing to retire, and this
2000    /// admission would otherwise leak a ring no teardown ever removes. The commit therefore retires it
2001    /// — immediately, not deferred: the deferral exists so a closing Session's own return-routed
2002    /// notification still finds its ring, but here the Session is already gone and no packet of its is
2003    /// in flight for this admission, which was never visible to the pipeline.
2004    fn commit(&mut self, slot: Option<&SessionSlot>, admission: Option<&dyn SurbAdmissionControl>, capacity: usize) {
2005        self.committed = true;
2006        tracing::info!(session_id = %self.session_id, "new session established");
2007
2008        // Only a slot that is this Session's own can carry the admission's token to a teardown, so
2009        // `None` means nothing to admit for: either the Session was torn down — its teardown already
2010        // ran its (no-op) retire, and any batch a peer sends meanwhile lands in the quarantine like any
2011        // other unadmitted one — or the pseudonym was reallocated to a successor, whose ring is not
2012        // this admission's to stamp. The commit itself — logging and the metric below — still happens.
2013        if let (Some(admission), Some(slot)) = (admission, slot) {
2014            // The Exit commits after it has answered `SessionEstablished`, so a `BalancerTarget`
2015            // keep-alive can have announced a raised target before the ring exists. Admit at the
2016            // larger of the two: the ring is sized once here, and a raise that arrived in that
2017            // window must not be lost until the Entry announces it again.
2018            let announced = capacity.max(slot.peek_raised_surb_target().unwrap_or(0));
2019            let token = admission.admit(&self.session_id, announced);
2020            if slot.admission_token.set(token).is_err() {
2021                // A teardown claimed the cell first, so nothing will retire this admission. Retire
2022                // it here — see the doc comment for why this is immediate rather than deferred.
2023                tracing::debug!(
2024                    session_id = %self.session_id,
2025                    "session was torn down while it committed; retiring the admission it could not record"
2026                );
2027                admission.retire(&self.session_id, token);
2028            } else if {
2029                // Pairs with the fence in `note_raised_surb_target`: either this side sees the
2030                // recorded target, or a concurrent keep-alive sees the token this `set` just wrote
2031                // and raises the ring itself. See that method for the failure the pair rules out.
2032                std::sync::atomic::fence(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
2033                true
2034            } && let Some(raised) = slot.peek_raised_surb_target().filter(|&raised| raised > announced)
2035            {
2036                // The target moved again between the admit and the token being recorded; widen for
2037                // it rather than leave the ring a step behind until the next announcement.
2038                admission.raise_target(&self.session_id, token, raised);
2039            }
2040        }
2041
2042        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
2043        METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS.increment(1.0);
2044    }
2045}
2046
2047impl Drop for SessionSlotGuard<'_> {
2048    fn drop(&mut self) {
2049        if !self.committed {
2050            // The session setup failed after the slot was inserted: remove it so it does
2051            // not block the pseudonym until idle eviction.
2052            let session_id = self.session_id;
2053            warn!(%session_id, "rolling back partially established session slot after setup failure");
2054            if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.remove(&session_id) {
2055                self.active_sessions.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
2056                // Not `close_session`: the Session was never established, so there is no
2057                // "session closed" line to pair with "new session established".
2058                //
2059                // The token is `NONE` by construction — admission happens at `commit`, and this
2060                // guard never committed — so the retire is the no-op that keeps every teardown wired
2061                // through the same seam without asking the store's accounting to trust that. Claiming
2062                // the cell rather than reading it keeps every teardown using one protocol.
2063                let token = slot.claim_admission_token();
2064                release_session_slot(
2065                    session_id,
2066                    slot,
2067                    ClosureReason::Eviction,
2068                    self.admission.get().cloned(),
2069                    surb_retire_grace(self.surb_resolution_wait),
2070                    token,
2071                );
2072            }
2073        }
2074    }
2075}
2076
2077/// Why an inbound session data packet was dropped without being delivered.
2078///
2079/// All three are ordinary consequences of a session tearing down or being briefly overwhelmed, not
2080/// faults: a departing counterparty leaves packets in flight that arrive after its slot's sink is
2081/// gone or after the slot itself is deregistered. They are reported as a [`DispatchResult::Dropped`]
2082/// outcome rather than an `Err` precisely so the caller does not log them at `ERROR` — the loud
2083/// teardown-race spam this distinction exists to remove.
2084#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2085pub enum DropReason {
2086    /// The slot is still registered but its data sink (receiver) has been dropped
2087    /// (`TrySendError::Disconnected`). The common case when a session is being torn down.
2088    SinkClosed,
2089    /// The slot's inbox is full (`TrySendError::Full`): genuine backpressure, the reader is not
2090    /// keeping up. Distinct from [`SinkClosed`](Self::SinkClosed) because it is transient, not a
2091    /// teardown.
2092    SinkFull,
2093    /// No slot for this session id is registered (formerly the `UnknownData` error): the session
2094    /// was fully deregistered before this packet arrived.
2095    Unregistered,
2096    /// A Start-protocol message that names no state on this node it could ever be handled by:
2097    /// neither a Session slot nor a pending initiation under the pseudonym it arrives under. That
2098    /// includes one naming a *registered* Session under a mismatched sender pseudonym, which speaks
2099    /// about someone else's Session. Rejected at dispatch, before it can occupy a shared handler;
2100    /// benign, and quiet for the same reason the others are.
2101    StaleStartMessage,
2102}
2103
2104/// Indicates the result of processing a message.
2105#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2106pub enum DispatchResult {
2107    /// Session or Start protocol message has been processed successfully.
2108    Processed,
2109    /// The message was not related to Start or Session protocol.
2110    Unrelated(ApplicationDataIn),
2111    /// The message belonged to a session but could not be delivered and was dropped. Benign — see
2112    /// [`DropReason`]. Reported as `Ok` so the caller logs it quietly instead of as an `ERROR`.
2113    Dropped(DropReason),
2114}
2115
2116/// Configuration of the PIX protocol for incoming Sessions on Exit nodes.
2117#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, smart_default::SmartDefault, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
2118#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
2119pub struct IncomingSessionPixConfig {
2120    /// If set to true, incoming Session without the [`Capability::UsePIX`] will be rejected.
2121    ///
2122    /// Default `false`.
2123    #[default(false)]
2124    pub enforce_pix: bool,
2125    /// Acceptable range of data quota in bytes.
2126    ///
2127    /// With dynamic SSA batches enabled, the Exit selects the smallest batch up to
2128    /// [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`] whose total `batch_size × quota_per_ssa` is inside this
2129    /// range. With dynamic batches disabled, the Entry's per-SSA quota itself must be inside the
2130    /// range and the configured batch size is used exactly. An offer that satisfies neither rule is
2131    /// rejected before the Session is established.
2132    ///
2133    /// The default is derived from the default PIX dimensions
2134    /// ([`crate::DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA`] × ([`crate::DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY`] +
2135    /// [`crate::DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES`])) rather than hard-coded, so that an Entry running the
2136    /// default configuration is always accepted. The upper bound is exactly
2137    /// [`DEFAULT_PIX_SSA_QUOTA`]. Since every dynamic batch has at least one member, that upper bound
2138    /// still caps the data served by any one SSA cycle. Accepting larger dimensions would raise both
2139    /// that exposure and the reconstructor memory held per Session, so an Exit that wants to serve
2140    /// them must widen this range explicitly.
2141    ///
2142    /// The quota it is compared against counts the surplus — `polys × (threshold + surplus) ×
2143    /// PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE` — so this bounds the traffic actually served rather than the
2144    /// fraction of it the threshold accounts for. It used to bound only the latter, which understated
2145    /// the exposure by the surplus factor: 3.47× at the deployed dimensions.
2146    ///
2147    /// Defaults to `DEFAULT_PIX_SSA_QUOTA / 4 ..= DEFAULT_PIX_SSA_QUOTA`
2148    /// (≈ 157 MiB to ≈ 630 MiB, inclusive).
2149    #[default(_code = "DEFAULT_PIX_SSA_QUOTA / DEFAULT_PIX_QUOTA_RANGE_SPAN..=DEFAULT_PIX_SSA_QUOTA")]
2150    pub quota_range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<u64>,
2151    /// Ceiling on the live Exit-side reconstructor state this node will commit to, in bytes.
2152    ///
2153    /// **This, not [`SessionManagerConfig::maximum_sessions`], is what bounds reconstructor
2154    /// memory.** A PIX Session reserves `MAX_OVERLAPPING_BATCHES × ssas_per_request ×
2155    /// hopr_protocol_pix::peak_cycle_bytes(offered params)` when it is accepted and holds it until
2156    /// it closes; a Session that does not fit is refused with
2157    /// [`StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable`] before any state is allocated for it. The reservation
2158    /// is computed from the parameters the *peer* offered, so a Session asking for smaller
2159    /// dimensions costs proportionally less of the budget.
2160    ///
2161    /// Enforced at admission rather than validated as a product of the configuration, for the reason
2162    /// `SsaReconstructorConfig::max_ack_buffer_bytes` gives: `maximum_sessions` validates to
2163    /// 100 000, and the resulting product is a number no node could hold, so validating it would
2164    /// only ever reject the shipping defaults. Counting what has actually been committed to is
2165    /// indifferent to how the ceiling was configured.
2166    ///
2167    /// Default is 3 GiB. At the default dimensions a Session reserves ≈30.7 MiB — two overlapping
2168    /// batches of one cycle's peak each — so this admits 100 concurrent PIX Sessions with ≈1.7 MiB to
2169    /// spare, comfortably covering the 10–30 clients per Exit the calibration profile models. That
2170    /// is exactly the 100 Sessions a node manages by default (`maximum_managed_sessions`), which at
2171    /// these dimensions reserve ≈2.998 GiB — so with every default in place the two limits meet and
2172    /// this budget is what binds as soon as peers offer a costlier split of the same quota or that
2173    /// limit is raised. The margin is pinned by
2174    /// `default_live_cycle_budget_admits_the_default_managed_session_count`.
2175    ///
2176    /// A ceiling on *reservations*, not an allocation: nothing is claimed up front, and because the
2177    /// reservation is denominated at the adversarial peak, a node serving conforming peers holds an
2178    /// order of magnitude less than it has reserved. The number exists to stop an Exit selling more
2179    /// service than its memory can hold, not to describe what it will typically use.
2180    #[default(3 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)]
2181    pub max_live_cycle_bytes: u64,
2182    /// Deadlines, fault limits and service budget the Exit-side PIX supervisor enforces on a
2183    /// Session.
2184    ///
2185    /// These live together rather than spread across this struct because they are only meaningful
2186    /// as a set: [`crate::validate_pix_supervision`] checks them against each other and against the
2187    /// reconstructor's lifetimes, and the node's config validator runs that at load time.
2188    pub supervision: SupervisorConfig,
2189}
2190
2191impl IncomingSessionPixConfig {
2192    /// The terms one Session is judged on, once the session server has had its say.
2193    ///
2194    /// The configured [`quota_range`](Self::quota_range) is an envelope, not a default: it is what
2195    /// [`validate_incoming_session_pix_config`] checked the deadlines and memory ceiling against,
2196    /// and what [`start_protocol_channel_capacity`] sized a preallocated ring from, both once at
2197    /// startup. So a decision's range is *intersected* with it rather than replacing it — a Session
2198    /// may be held to less than the node advertises, never to more than it was configured to
2199    /// honour. An operator wanting a wider class configures a wider envelope and narrows the rest.
2200    ///
2201    /// [`enforce_pix`](Self::enforce_pix) carries no such coupling and is simply overridden.
2202    fn effective_for(&self, decision: &SessionAdmissionDecision) -> EffectivePixAdmission {
2203        let quota_range = match &decision.pix_quota_range {
2204            Some(narrowed) => {
2205                *self.quota_range.start().max(narrowed.start())..=*self.quota_range.end().min(narrowed.end())
2206            }
2207            None => self.quota_range.clone(),
2208        };
2209
2210        EffectivePixAdmission {
2211            enforce_pix: decision.enforce_pix.unwrap_or(self.enforce_pix),
2212            quota_range,
2213            allow_dynamic_ssa_batches: self.supervision.allow_dynamic_ssa_batches,
2214            ssas_per_request: self.supervision.ssas_per_request,
2215        }
2216    }
2217
2218    /// The supervisor configuration for Sessions accepted under these settings.
2219    pub fn supervisor_config(&self) -> SupervisorConfig {
2220        self.supervision.clone()
2221    }
2222}
2223
2224/// The PIX terms a single incoming Session is admitted on.
2225///
2226/// Lighter than the whole [`IncomingSessionPixConfig`] because only these four fields vary per
2227/// Session: everything else the supervisor enforces is validated as a set at startup and stays
2228/// node-wide. Narrowing the quota only makes those deadlines more generous, which is why they need
2229/// not travel with it.
2230#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
2231pub(crate) struct EffectivePixAdmission {
2232    /// Whether this Session must offer PIX at all.
2233    enforce_pix: bool,
2234    /// Quota window this Session's offer must land in, already intersected with the node's envelope.
2235    quota_range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<SsaQuota>,
2236    /// Whether a batch may be derived from the offer, rather than taken as configured.
2237    allow_dynamic_ssa_batches: bool,
2238    /// Largest batch the Exit will ask for.
2239    ssas_per_request: usize,
2240}
2241
2242impl EffectivePixAdmission {
2243    /// Selects the batch size with which an Entry's per-SSA quota is acceptable.
2244    ///
2245    /// Dynamic mode walks from one upwards so it asks for no more Entry work, deposits or Exit
2246    /// reconstructor state than necessary. Fixed mode is the legacy rule: validate one SSA against
2247    /// the range, then request exactly the configured batch size.
2248    fn ssa_batch_size_for_quota(&self, quota_per_ssa: SsaQuota) -> Option<usize> {
2249        let configured_batch = self.ssas_per_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE);
2250
2251        if !self.allow_dynamic_ssa_batches {
2252            return self.quota_range.contains(&quota_per_ssa).then_some(configured_batch);
2253        }
2254
2255        (1..=configured_batch).find(|batch_size| {
2256            quota_per_ssa
2257                .checked_mul(*batch_size as u64)
2258                .is_some_and(|batch_quota| self.quota_range.contains(&batch_quota))
2259        })
2260    }
2261}
2262
2263/// Bit position of the 64-bit options word within `StartInitiation::additional_data`.
2264///
2265/// The options word (PIX parameters and SURB balancer target) occupies the most significant 64 bits;
2266/// the least significant 64 bits are currently unused and always sent as `0`.
2267const INITIATION_OPTIONS_SHIFT: u32 = u64::BITS;
2268
2269/// Places the 64-bit options word into the most significant half of `StartInitiation::additional_data`,
2270/// leaving the (currently unused) least significant half zero.
2271#[inline]
2272const fn into_initiation_additional_data(options: u64) -> u128 {
2273    (options as u128) << INITIATION_OPTIONS_SHIFT
2274}
2275
2276/// Inverse of [`into_initiation_additional_data`], ignoring the least significant half.
2277#[inline]
2278const fn initiation_options(additional_data: u128) -> u64 {
2279    (additional_data >> INITIATION_OPTIONS_SHIFT) as u64
2280}
2281
2282/// Decodes the incentivization the Entry offered, before anyone is asked what to do about it.
2283///
2284/// `Ok(None)` is a peer that offered none. `Err` is one whose offer this node cannot read or
2285/// cannot share a curve with, which is refused on its own — no policy could rescue it, and both
2286/// questions are cheaper than the round trip to the session server that follows.
2287///
2288/// Split out from `SessionManager::check_pix_params` so the session server can be
2289/// told what was offered: it decides the terms, and terms relative to an offer need the offer.
2290fn decode_pix_offer(
2291    req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
2292) -> Result<Option<PixParams>, StartErrorReason> {
2293    if !req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX) {
2294        return Ok(None);
2295    }
2296
2297    // Unpacking is what enforces the protocol ranges on the three dimensions, and what rejects a
2298    // suite identifier no curve claims — leaving only "a known curve, but not ours" below.
2299    let params = PixParams::try_from_additional_data(initiation_options(req.additional_data)).map_err(|error| {
2300        debug!(
2301            challenge = req.challenge,
2302            %error,
2303            "client offered PIX parameters outside the protocol ranges"
2304        );
2305        StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams
2306    })?;
2307
2308    // The Exit decides the curve, and it decides it by refusing anything else: nothing here
2309    // is negotiated, because there is nothing to negotiate — the suite is fixed at build
2310    // time on both sides. Checked before the quota because it is the cheaper question and
2311    // because a suite mismatch makes the dimensions meaningless anyway, and checked at all
2312    // because every later PIX field is sized by it. Refusing here means the Exit's own
2313    // commitments, the first curve-sized bytes in the exchange, are never sent to a peer
2314    // that would read their boundaries in the wrong place.
2315    if params.suite() != LOCAL_PIX_SUITE {
2316        warn!(
2317            challenge = req.challenge,
2318            offered = %params.suite(),
2319            ours = %LOCAL_PIX_SUITE,
2320            "refusing a client offering a PIX curve suite this node was not built for"
2321        );
2322        return Err(StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams);
2323    }
2324
2325    Ok(Some(params))
2326}
2327
2328/// Validates the incoming-PIX invariants that span quota, supervision and memory settings.
2329///
2330/// `max_session_packet_rate` is the fastest a Session is assumed to go. Without fill it bounds
2331/// `max_recovery_time` directly; with fill it caps the `fill.max_rate` the deadline may count on.
2332pub fn validate_incoming_session_pix_config(
2333    cfg: &IncomingSessionPixConfig,
2334    max_session_packet_rate: u64,
2335) -> errors::Result<()> {
2336    if cfg.quota_range.is_empty() {
2337        return Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(
2338            "PIX quota_range must be non-empty (start must not exceed end)".into(),
2339        ));
2340    }
2341    if max_session_packet_rate == 0 {
2342        return Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(
2343            "maximum assumed PIX Session packet rate must be non-zero".into(),
2344        ));
2345    }
2346    // Named here although `validate_pix_supervision` also refuses it, because that runs later on both
2347    // paths: with fill enabled a zero deadline would otherwise surface as an infinite fill rate.
2348    if cfg.supervision.max_recovery_time.is_zero() {
2349        return Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(
2350            "PIX max_recovery_time must be non-zero".into(),
2351        ));
2352    }
2353
2354    let worst_cycle_packets = *cfg.quota_range.end() / PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE;
2355
2356    // `max_recovery_time` has to leave a cycle of the widest accepted quota time to complete, and what
2357    // completes it depends on fill. With fill enabled the Exit finishes an under-served cycle itself, so
2358    // the bound is the fill ceiling's own arithmetic below. Without it only application traffic does,
2359    // and the Exit has no rate of its own to reason from.
2360    if cfg.supervision.fill.enabled {
2361        // The fill ceiling has to clear the rate a cycle of the widest accepted quota actually needs,
2362        // or the mechanism that exists to complete idle cycles cannot complete the very ones it
2363        // admits. The arithmetic is the planner's own, taken at the moment fill starts: the whole
2364        // cycle remains, the aim point sits `finish_fraction` of the way through `max_recovery_time`,
2365        // and the loss margin is paid on top. `max_recovery_time` is the *configured* per-cycle budget
2366        // rather than a deadline observed at run time, so this is a property of the configuration and
2367        // can be decided here.
2368        //
2369        // The ceiling counts only up to `max_session_packet_rate`: fill faster than any Session is
2370        // assumed to carry cannot finish a cycle any sooner.
2371        let fill = &cfg.supervision.fill;
2372        // Before the arithmetic, not after it. `validate_pix_supervision` also range-checks these two,
2373        // but it runs later on both paths that reach here — `SessionManager::start` calls this first,
2374        // and in `HoprProtocolConfig` this is a field validator while that is a schema-level one. The
2375        // `mul_f64` below panics on a `NaN` or negative fraction, so an unchecked one aborts the node
2376        // at config load rather than being reported; a fraction above one silently lowers the floor.
2377        crate::supervision::validate_fill_fractions(fill)?;
2378
2379        let horizon = cfg.supervision.max_recovery_time.mul_f64(fill.finish_fraction);
2380        // Still guarded although both factors are non-zero: a nanosecond-scale deadline times a
2381        // fraction rounds to zero, and dividing by it would report an infinite requirement.
2382        let floor = if horizon.is_zero() {
2383            u64::MAX
2384        } else {
2385            (worst_cycle_packets as f64 * (1.0 + fill.loss_margin) / horizon.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as u64
2386        };
2387        if (fill.max_rate as u64).min(max_session_packet_rate) < floor {
2388            let remedy = if floor > max_session_packet_rate {
2389                "raise max_recovery_time"
2390            } else {
2391                "raise fill.max_rate or max_recovery_time"
2392            };
2393            return Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(format!(
2394                "PIX fill.max_rate is {} (counted up to {max_session_packet_rate} packets/s), but the largest \
2395                 accepted quota ({} bytes) is {worst_cycle_packets} packets and needs at least {floor} packets/s to \
2396                 finish inside {horizon:?} with a {} loss margin; {remedy}",
2397                fill.max_rate,
2398                cfg.quota_range.end(),
2399                fill.loss_margin,
2400            )));
2401        }
2402    } else {
2403        // Refused only if even a Session at the fastest assumed rate could not finish a cycle in time,
2404        // so this rejects a deadline that is impossible rather than one that is merely tight.
2405        let needed = Duration::from_secs(worst_cycle_packets.div_ceil(max_session_packet_rate));
2406        if cfg.supervision.max_recovery_time < needed {
2407            return Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(format!(
2408                "PIX max_recovery_time is {:?}, but with fill disabled the largest accepted quota ({} bytes) is \
2409                 {worst_cycle_packets} packets and needs at least {needed:?} even at {max_session_packet_rate} \
2410                 packets/s",
2411                cfg.supervision.max_recovery_time,
2412                cfg.quota_range.end(),
2413            )));
2414        }
2415    }
2416
2417    let widest = max_cycle_budget_for_quota(*cfg.quota_range.end(), cfg.supervision.ssas_per_request);
2418    if cfg.max_live_cycle_bytes < widest {
2419        return Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(format!(
2420            "PIX max_live_cycle_bytes is {}, but one Session offering the largest accepted quota ({} bytes) reserves \
2421             up to {widest} bytes of reconstructor state",
2422            cfg.max_live_cycle_bytes,
2423            cfg.quota_range.end(),
2424        )));
2425    }
2426
2427    Ok(())
2428}
2429
2430/// Configuration for the [`SessionManager`].
2431#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, smart_default::SmartDefault)]
2432pub struct SessionManagerConfig {
2433    /// The maximum chunk of data that can be written to the Session's input buffer.
2434    ///
2435    /// Clamped to the socket's supported frame size range, preserving boundaries within that range.
2436    ///
2437    /// Default is [`SESSION_MTU`], i.e. exactly one segment per frame.
2438    #[default(SESSION_MTU)]
2439    pub frame_mtu: usize,
2440
2441    /// The maximum time for an incomplete frame to stay in the Session's output buffer.
2442    ///
2443    /// Must exceed the worst-case SURB replenishment latency on the return path.
2444    /// The SURB balancer replenishes via KeepAlive every ~2 s; the retry loop in
2445    /// the routing resolver sleeps 5 ms per attempt and can block for the full
2446    /// replenishment cycle.  Setting this below the KeepAlive period causes the
2447    /// sequencer to discard frames that arrive after a SURB-starved peer finally
2448    /// gets new SURBs and sends its echo.
2449    ///
2450    /// Default is 3 s.
2451    #[default(Duration::from_secs(3))]
2452    pub max_frame_timeout: Duration,
2453
2454    /// Maximum number of segments to buffer in the downstream transport of a Session's socket.
2455    /// If 0 is given, the transport is unbuffered.
2456    ///
2457    /// Default is 0.
2458    #[default(0)]
2459    pub max_buffered_segments: usize,
2460
2461    /// Abandon the frame due next once this many later frames are waiting behind it, rather than
2462    /// holding them for the whole of [`Self::max_frame_timeout`].
2463    ///
2464    /// The two answer different questions. `max_frame_timeout` is how long a *missing* frame is
2465    /// waited for, and is set here to exceed the ~2 s SURB KeepAlive so a starved peer's late echo
2466    /// is not discarded. This bounds how much *already received* data is held hostage during that
2467    /// wait -- a cost paid once per gap, which compounds as later frames queue up.
2468    ///
2469    /// Without it, a session that cannot retransmit waits the full timeout for a frame that will
2470    /// never arrive. Measured on a 5-node cluster after killing a return relayer: 98.5 % of bytes
2471    /// returned over the wire, 0.60 % reached the application, and the application-side
2472    /// inter-arrival median sat exactly on the 3 s timeout.
2473    ///
2474    /// The right value tracks reordering depth -- throughput x latency spread / frame size -- so
2475    /// it is deployment-specific. Tune with `SessionConfig::max_frames_behind_gap`; too low converts
2476    /// ordinary reordering into loss, too high leaves the stall in place.
2477    ///
2478    /// Default is 256, which is roughly 3-4x the reordering depth of the cluster it was measured
2479    /// on (~0.5 MB/s over paths spread across 10-260 ms, 1500 B frames, so ~70-85 frames in
2480    /// flight out of order). The margin is not cosmetic: at 64 -- about one reordering depth --
2481    /// a *healthy* baseline dropped from 100 % to 92.2 % arrival, because ordinary reordering was
2482    /// being read as loss. At 256 the same baseline returned 100 % while a return relayer killed
2483    /// mid-session still recovered 97.1 %, against 0.60 % with the bound absent.
2484    ///
2485    /// Default is 256.
2486    #[default(Some(256))]
2487    pub max_frames_behind_gap: Option<usize>,
2488
2489    /// The base timeout for initiation of Session initiation.
2490    ///
2491    /// The actual timeout is adjusted according to the number of hops for that Session:
2492    /// `t = initiation_time_out_base * (num_forward_hops + num_return_hops + 2)`
2493    ///
2494    /// Default is 500 milliseconds.
2495    #[default(Duration::from_millis(500))]
2496    pub initiation_timeout_base: Duration,
2497
2498    /// Timeout for Session to be closed due to inactivity.
2499    ///
2500    /// Default is 180 seconds.
2501    #[default(Duration::from_secs(180))]
2502    pub idle_timeout: Duration,
2503
2504    /// Minimum interval at which an establishing Session's cache slot is refreshed
2505    /// ("touched") to keep [`idle_timeout`](Self::idle_timeout) from evicting it while
2506    /// SURBs pre-load.
2507    ///
2508    /// The touch period is [`idle_timeout`](Self::idle_timeout)` / 2`, floored to this
2509    /// value so it never drops below a sane minimum for very short idle timeouts.
2510    ///
2511    /// Default is 100 milliseconds.
2512    #[default(Duration::from_millis(100))]
2513    pub min_session_touch_period: Duration,
2514
2515    /// The sampling interval for SURB balancer.
2516    /// It will make SURB control decisions regularly at this interval.
2517    ///
2518    /// Default is 100 milliseconds.
2519    #[default(Duration::from_millis(100))]
2520    pub balancer_sampling_interval: Duration,
2521
2522    /// Initial packets per second egress rate on an incoming Session.
2523    ///
2524    /// This only applies to incoming Sessions without the [`Capability::NoRateControl`] flag set.
2525    ///
2526    /// Default is 10 packets/second.
2527    #[default(10)]
2528    pub initial_return_session_egress_rate: usize,
2529
2530    /// Minimum period of time for which a SURB buffer at the Exit must
2531    /// endure if no SURBs are being received.
2532    ///
2533    /// In other words, it is the minimum period of time an Exit must withstand when
2534    /// no SURBs are received from the Entry at all. To do so, the egress traffic
2535    /// will be shaped accordingly to meet this requirement.
2536    ///
2537    /// This only applies to incoming Sessions without the [`Capability::NoRateControl`] flag set.
2538    ///
2539    /// Default is 5 seconds, minimum is 1 second.
2540    #[default(Duration::from_secs(5))]
2541    pub minimum_surb_buffer_duration: Duration,
2542
2543    /// Indicates the maximum number of SURBs in the SURB buffer to be requested when creating a new Session.
2544    ///
2545    /// This value is theoretically capped by the size of the global transport SURB ring buffer,
2546    /// so values greater than that do not make sense. This value should be ideally set equal
2547    /// to the size of the global transport SURB RB.
2548    ///
2549    /// On the Exit it is also the largest target it takes from an Entry, and the target the SURB ring of
2550    /// a Session is sized from when its Entry announces none.
2551    ///
2552    /// Default is 10 000 SURBs.
2553    #[default(10_000)]
2554    pub maximum_surb_buffer_size: usize,
2555
2556    /// If set, the Session recipient (Exit) will notify the Session initiator (Entry) about
2557    /// its SURB balance for the Session using keep-alive packets periodically.
2558    ///
2559    /// Keep in mind that each notification also costs 1 SURB, so the notification period should
2560    /// not be too frequent.
2561    ///
2562    /// The Exit sends it only to an Entry that has shown it runs a SURB balancer, by having sent a
2563    /// keep-alive (whether or not that keep-alive announces a target, but not a manual ping), and only while the
2564    /// Exit's own estimate of the SURBs it holds for the Session is above 0. An Entry without a balancer
2565    /// attaches a SURB to each data packet and reads no report. The notification carries the Exit
2566    /// balancer's level on a rate-controlled Session, and the Exit's own count of its SURBs on a
2567    /// `NoRateControl` one, which runs no balancer.
2568    ///
2569    /// Default is None (no notification sent to the client), minimum is 1 second.
2570    #[default(None)]
2571    pub surb_balance_notify_period: Option<Duration>,
2572
2573    /// If set, the Session initiator (Entry) will notify the Session recipient (Exit) about
2574    /// the local SURB balancer target using keep-alive packets from the SURB balancer.
2575    ///
2576    /// This is useful when the client plans to change the SURB balancer target dynamically.
2577    ///
2578    /// For a Session that announced a target, the Exit sizes the SURB ring from it, and widens the ring
2579    /// when a raised one arrives. A rate-controlled Exit also takes its balancer's set-point, its egress
2580    /// cap (`max_surbs_per_sec`) and the SURB reserve it holds back for its keep-alives from the target,
2581    /// and follows every change the Entry announces, lowered as well as raised.
2582    ///
2583    /// With this off, the Exit only knows the target announced at establishment, and no change to it
2584    /// is seen, lower or higher. A rate-controlled Exit then keeps its ring, balancer, egress cap and
2585    /// keep-alive reserve at the establishment target: an Entry that raises its target does not lift
2586    /// the Exit's egress cap or widen its ring, and one that lowers it to that reserve or below may
2587    /// leave the Exit holding its data back for good, waiting for a stock the Entry no longer keeps. A
2588    /// Session that announces no target at establishment, as an Entry without a SURB balancer or any
2589    /// `NoRateControl` Entry does, gets the full ring from the start, so turning this off costs it
2590    /// nothing. The Exit's SURB-level reports are unaffected: it recognises a balancing Entry by its
2591    /// balancer's keep-alives, flagged or not.
2592    ///
2593    /// Default is true.
2594    #[default(true)]
2595    pub surb_target_notify: bool,
2596
2597    /// Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed.
2598    ///
2599    /// Default is 10_000.
2600    #[default(10_000)]
2601    pub maximum_sessions: usize,
2602
2603    /// How many packets can be buffered if the [`HoprSession`] input socket is not fast enough.
2604    ///
2605    /// Controls the capacity of the internal `crossfire` channel used for each session slot.
2606    ///
2607    /// Default is 10 000.
2608    #[default(10000)]
2609    pub session_forward_capacity: usize,
2610
2611    /// Configuration of the PIX protocol for the Exit nodes.
2612    pub pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig,
2613
2614    /// Maximum number of SSA commitments this node, acting as an Entry, will accept in a single
2615    /// [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`].
2616    ///
2617    /// This is the Entry's protection against a misbehaving Exit, not a preference: every accepted
2618    /// entry costs a full `new_ssa_commitment`, thousands of outbound `SsaCommit` packets and its own
2619    /// on-chain deposit, so without a cap one inbound packet amplifies into minutes of CPU, a large
2620    /// packet burst, and as many simultaneous deposits as the wire format admits. An over-cap request
2621    /// is rejected in full, before any commitment is generated or any `ReadyToDeposit` is emitted, and
2622    /// the Exit is told with a `SessionError` — see `refuse_ssa_request`.
2623    ///
2624    /// It must be at least the `ssas_per_request` of every Exit this node connects to — see
2625    /// [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request) for why a mismatch
2626    /// loses every Session.
2627    ///
2628    /// Clamped to `1..=`[`MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE`] in [`SessionManager::new`].
2629    ///
2630    /// Defaults to [`DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST`] (2).
2631    #[default(DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST)]
2632    pub max_ssas_per_ssa_request: usize,
2633
2634    /// How long the Exit waits for the session server to say whether a Session is admitted.
2635    ///
2636    /// The wait sits inside the peer's own initiation timeout, so it has to be comfortably shorter
2637    /// than [`initiation_timeout_base`](Self::initiation_timeout_base): a server slower than the
2638    /// peer is patient refuses every Session it is asked about, and does so after the peer has
2639    /// already given up. [`SessionManager::new`] rejects a configuration where it is not.
2640    ///
2641    /// Expiring refuses the Session — the alternative, admitting on the node's own terms, would let
2642    /// an overloaded or wedged server silently disable every rule the operator wrote.
2643    ///
2644    /// Default is 2 seconds.
2645    #[default(Duration::from_secs(2))]
2646    pub session_admission_timeout: Duration,
2647
2648    /// How long the packet pipeline retries a return-routed packet whose SURBs have not arrived
2649    /// before dropping it.
2650    ///
2651    /// The composition root supplies this from its own packet-pipeline config, because the retire of
2652    /// a closing Session's SURB admission must wait it out — the teardown's grace is this window plus
2653    /// a small margin. A Session
2654    /// teardown that retired before the window closed would drop the closing Exit's own
2655    /// return-routed notification mid-lookup, and the Entry would then never learn that its Session
2656    /// was gone. The manager cannot see the pipeline config, so it is threaded here rather than
2657    /// pinned against a default that an operator's larger setting would silently invalidate.
2658    ///
2659    /// Default is 6 seconds, the packet pipeline's own default.
2660    #[default(Duration::from_secs(6))]
2661    pub surb_resolution_wait: Duration,
2662}

2664// Type-erased sink used by the `SessionManager` to notify about newly incoming sessions.
2665// The errors produced by the underlying sink are remapped into `SessionManagerError`.
2666type BoxSink<T> = Pin<Box<dyn Sink<T, Error = SessionManagerError> + Send>>;
2667
2668type SessionNotifiers = (
2669    Arc<hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::Mutex<BoxSink<IncomingSession>>>,
2670    crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::Array<(SessionId, ClosureReason)>>,
2671);

2673/// What an incoming packet did to the SURB store, as the packet pipeline reported it.
2674///
2675/// Carried to the Start protocol handler along with the message, because the conversion of the packet's
2676/// data into a [`HoprStartProtocol`] drops the packet info, and with it these two counts. Booked with
2677/// [`account_incoming_surbs`].
2678#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
2679struct SurbsStored {
2680    /// SURBs the packet carried, clamped to what fits beside its message
2681    /// ([`ApplicationDataIn::num_surbs_with_msg`]).
2682    saved: u64,
2683    /// SURBs the store lost on arrival: dropped for capacity, and, since a newer SURB generation clears
2684    /// the store, the stock that generation wiped (`IncomingPacketInfo::num_evicted_surbs`).
2685    evicted: u64,
2686}
2687
2688impl SurbsStored {
2689    fn of(data: &ApplicationDataIn) -> Self {
2690        Self {
2691            saved: data.num_surbs_with_msg() as u64,
2692            evicted: data.packet_info.num_evicted_surbs as u64,
2693        }
2694    }
2695}

2697// Sink for processing Start protocol messages, each with what its packet did to the SURB store.
2698// Must be within Arc to be shared across SessionManager clones.
2699// The inner OnceLock is set once in `start()` and read in `dispatch_message`.
2700// The packet info travels along because a Start message cannot always be judged by its content alone:
2701// see `refuse_pix_over_direct_return_path`. What the packet did to the SURB store travels too, taken
2702// before the conversion into a `HoprStartProtocol` consumes the data it is counted from: the part
2703// dispatch could not book itself, which is all of it only for an opening that creates its Session.
2704type StartProtocolMsgSink = Arc<
2705    OnceLock<
2706        crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::Array<(HoprPseudonym, HoprStartProtocol, IncomingPacketInfo, SurbsStored)>>,
2707    >,
2708>;

2710/// PIX protocol toolbox to enable [`SessionManager`] to use PIX protocol.
2711#[derive(Clone)]
2712pub struct PixToolbox {
2713    share_generator: Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
2714    share_processor: Arc<SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>>,
2715    pix_events: crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::Array<HoprSessionOutPixEvent>>,
2716}
2717
2718impl PixToolbox {
2719    pub fn new(
2720        share_generator: Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
2721        share_processor: Arc<SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>>,
2722    ) -> (Self, impl futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent>) {
2723        let (pix_events, pix_events_rx) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<HoprSessionOutPixEvent>(1024);
2724        (
2725            Self {
2726                share_generator,
2727                share_processor,
2728                pix_events,
2729            },
2730            pix_events_rx.into_stream(),
2731        )
2732    }
2733}
