2735/// Manages lifecycles of Sessions.
2736///
2737/// Once the manager is [started](SessionManager::start), the [`SessionManager::dispatch_message`]
2738/// should be called for each [`ApplicationData`] received by the node.
2739/// This way, the `SessionManager` takes care of proper Start sub-protocol message processing
2740/// and correct dispatch of Session-related packets to individual existing Sessions.
2741///
2742/// Secondly, the manager can initiate new outgoing sessions via [`SessionManager::new_session`],
2743/// probe sessions using [`SessionManager::ping_session`]
2744/// and list them via [`SessionManager::active_sessions`].
2745///
2746/// Since the `SessionManager` operates over the HOPR protocol,
2747/// the message transport `S` is required.
2748/// Such transport must also be `Clone`, since it will be cloned into all the created [`HoprSession`] objects.
2749///
2750/// ## SURB balancing
2751///
2752/// The manager also can take care of automatic [SURB balancing](SurbBalancerConfig) per Session.
2753///
2754/// With each packet sent from the session initiator over to the receiving party, zero to 2 SURBs might be delivered.
2755/// When the receiving party wants to send reply packets back, it must consume 1 SURB per packet. This
2756/// means that if the difference between the SURBs delivered and SURBs consumed is negative, the receiving party
2757/// might soon run out of SURBs. If SURBs run out, the reply packets will be dropped, causing likely quality of
2758/// service degradation.
2759///
2760/// In an attempt to counter this effect, there are two co-existing automated modes of SURB balancing:
2761/// *local SURB balancing* and *remote SURB balancing*.
2762///
2763/// ### Local SURB balancing
2764///
2765/// Local SURB balancing is performed on the sessions that were initiated by another party (and are
2766/// therefore incoming to us).
2767/// The local SURB balancing mechanism continuously evaluates the rate of SURB consumption and retrieval,
2768/// and if SURBs are running out, the packet egress shaping takes effect. This by itself does not
2769/// avoid the depletion of SURBs but slows it down in the hope that the initiating party can deliver
2770/// more SURBs over time. This might happen either organically by sending effective payloads that
2771/// allow non-zero number of SURBs in the packet, or non-organically by delivering KeepAlive messages
2772/// via *remote SURB balancing*. Both are governed by the initiator's estimate of our buffer, so
2773/// signalling SURB distress is what tells it to keep the organic ones coming.
2774///
2775/// The egress shaping is done automatically, unless the Session initiator sets the [`Capability::NoRateControl`]
2776/// flag during Session initiation.
2777///
2778/// ### Remote SURB balancing
2779///
2780/// Remote SURB balancing is performed by the Session initiator. The SURB balancer estimates the number of SURBs
2781/// delivered to the other party, and also the number of SURBs consumed by seeing the amount of traffic received
2782/// in replies.
2783/// When enabled, a desired target level of SURBs at the Session counterparty is set. According to measured
2784/// inflow and outflow of SURBs to/from the counterparty, the production of non-organic SURBs is started
2785/// via keep-alive messages (sent to counterparty) and is controlled to maintain that target level.
2786///
2787/// In other words, the Session initiator tries to compensate for the usage of SURBs by the counterparty by
2788/// sending new ones via the keep-alive messages.
2789///
2790/// The same estimate also governs *organic* production: once the counterparty is estimated to be at
2791/// its target, outgoing Session data packets carry no SURBs at all, and they return to one per packet
2792/// as soon as the estimate falls back below target. Without that, a balancer could correctly silence
2793/// its keep-alives while organic SURBs kept pouring into a full buffer — where each one evicts an
2794/// older SURB and destroys the PIX share it was carrying. A `SurbDistress` or `OutOfSurbs` signal
2795/// from the counterparty overrides the estimate and restores production immediately, which is what
2796/// makes it safe to act on an estimate that forward-path loss can inflate.
2797///
2798/// This mechanism is configurable via the `surb_management` field in [`SessionClientConfig`].
2799///
2800/// ### Possible scenarios
2801///
2802/// There are 4 different scenarios of local vs. remote SURB balancing configuration, but
2803/// an equilibrium (= matching the SURB production and consumption) is most likely to be reached
2804/// only when both are configured (the ideal case below):
2805///
2806/// #### 1. Ideal local and remote SURB balancing
2807///
2808/// 1. The Session recipient (Exit) set the `initial_return_session_egress_rate`, `max_surb_buffer_duration` and
2809///    `maximum_surb_buffer_size` values in the [`SessionManagerConfig`].
2810/// 2. The Session initiator (Entry) sets the [`target_surb_buffer_size`](SurbBalancerConfig) which matches the
2811///    [`maximum_surb_buffer_size`](SessionManagerConfig) of the counterparty.
2812/// 3. The Session initiator (Entry) does *NOT* set the [`Capability::NoRateControl`] capability flag when opening
2813///    Session.
2814/// 4. The Session initiator (Entry) sets [`max_surbs_per_sec`](SurbBalancerConfig) slightly higher than the
2815///    `maximum_surb_buffer_size / max_surb_buffer_duration` value configured at the counterparty.
2816///
2817/// In this situation, the maximum Session egress from Exit to the Entry is given by the
2818/// `maximum_surb_buffer_size / max_surb_buffer_duration` ratio. If there is enough bandwidth,
2819/// the (remote) SURB balancer sending SURBs to the Exit will stabilize roughly at this rate of SURBs/sec,
2820/// and the whole system will be in equilibrium during the Session's lifetime (under ideal network conditions).
2821///
2822/// #### 2. Remote SURB balancing only
2823///
2824/// 1. The Session initiator (Entry) *DOES* set the [`Capability::NoRateControl`] capability flag when opening Session.
2825/// 2. The Session initiator (Entry) sets `max_surbs_per_sec` and `target_surb_buffer_size` values in
2826///    [`SurbBalancerConfig`]
2827///
2828/// In this one-sided situation, the Entry node floods the Exit node with SURBs,
2829/// only based on its estimated consumption of SURBs at the Exit. The Exit's egress is not
2830/// rate-limited at all. If the Exit runs out of SURBs at any point in time, it will simply drop egress packets.
2831///
2832/// This configuration could potentially only lead to an equilibrium
2833/// when the `SurbBalancer` at the Entry can react fast enough to Exit's demand.
2834///
2835/// #### 3. Local SURB balancing only
2836///
2837/// 1. The Session recipient (Exit) set the `initial_return_session_egress_rate`, `max_surb_buffer_duration` and
2838///    `maximum_surb_buffer_size` values in the [`SessionManagerConfig`].
2839/// 2. The Session initiator (Entry) does *NOT* set the [`Capability::NoRateControl`] capability flag when opening
2840///    Session.
2841/// 3. The Session initiator (Entry) does *NOT* set the [`SurbBalancerConfig`] at all when opening Session.
2842///
2843/// In this one-sided situation, the Entry node does not provide any additional SURBs at all (except the
2844/// ones that are naturally carried by the egress packets which have space to hold SURBs). It relies
2845/// only on the Session egress limiting of the Exit node.
2846/// The Exit will limit the egress roughly to the rate of natural SURB occurrence in the ingress.
2847///
2848/// This configuration could potentially only lead to an equilibrium when uploading non-full packets
2849/// (ones that can carry at least a single SURB), and the Exit's egress is limiting itself to such a rate.
2850/// If Exit's egress reaches low values due to SURB scarcity, the upper layer protocols over Session might break.
2851///
2852/// #### 4. No SURB balancing on each side
2853///
2854/// 1. The Session initiator (Entry) *DOES* set the [`Capability::NoRateControl`] capability flag when opening Session.
2855/// 2. The Session initiator (Entry) does *NOT* set the [`SurbBalancerConfig`] at all when opening Session.
2856///
2857/// In this situation, no additional SURBs are being produced by the Entry and no Session egress rate-limiting
2858/// takes place at the Exit.
2859///
2860/// This configuration can only lead to an equilibrium when Entry sends non-full packets (ones that carry
2861/// at least a single SURB) and the Exit is consuming the SURBs (Session egress) at a slower or equal rate.
2862/// Such configuration is very fragile, as any disturbances in the SURB flow might lead to a packet drop
2863/// at the Exit's egress.
2864///
2865/// ### SURB decay
2866///
2867/// In a hypothetical scenario of a non-zero packet loss, the Session initiator (Entry) might send a
2868/// certain number of SURBs to the Session recipient (Exit), but only a portion of it is actually delivered.
2869/// The Entry has no way of knowing that and assumes that everything has been delivered.
2870/// A similar problem happens when the Exit uses SURBs to construct return packets, but only a portion
2871/// of those packets is actually delivered to the Entry. At this point, the Entry also subtracts
2872/// fewer SURBs from its SURB estimate at the Exit.
2873///
2874/// In both situations, the Entry thinks there are more SURBs available at the Exit than there really are.
2875///
2876/// To compensate for a potential packet loss, the Entry's estimation of Exit's SURB buffer is regularly
2877/// diminished by a percentage of the `target_surb_buffer_size`, even if no incoming traffic from the
2878/// Exit is detected.
2879///
2880/// This behavior can be controlled via the `surb_decay` field of [`SurbBalancerConfig`].
2881///
2882/// ### SURB balance and target notification
2883///
2884/// The Session recipient (Exit) can notify the Session initiator (Entry) periodically about its estimated
2885/// number of SURBs for the Session. This can help the Entry to adjust its approximation of that level so
2886/// that its Local SURB balancer can better intervene.
2887/// This can be set using the `surb_balance_notify_period` field of [`SessionManagerConfig`] for the Exit.
2888///
2889/// Likewise, the Entry can inform the Exit about its desired SURB buffer target so that the Exit
2890/// can better accommodate its Remote SURB balancing.
2891/// This can be set using the `surb_target_notify` field of the [`SessionManagerConfig`] of each new Session.
2892///
2893/// Both mechanisms leverage the Keep Alive message to report the respective values.
2894///
2895/// ## PIX (Protocol for Incentivization of eXits) Protocol Flow
2896///
2897/// When a Session is opened with the [`Capability::UsePIX`] flag, the following protocol
2898/// runs between the Entry (initiator) and Exit (recipient) to provide on-chain payment
2899/// guarantees for the data relayed through the Session.
2900///
2901/// ### 1. PIX Parameter Negotiation (Session Initiation)
2902///
2903/// During [`SessionManager::new_session`], the Entry encodes its PIX SSA (Session Stealth
2904/// Address) parameters — a [`PixParams`] quadruple of `polys_per_ssa`, `shares_per_poly`,
2905/// `surplus_shares` and the curve `suite` — into the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit options word
2906/// carried in the most significant 64 bits of the `StartSession.additional_data` field, via
2907/// [`PixParams::into_additional_data`]. The first two describe how many polynomials and shares each
2908/// SSA will use; the third is how many extra shares per polynomial the Entry emits to absorb losses. Those three define
2909/// the data quota per SSA, which is `polys × (threshold + surplus) × SESSION_MTU` — the surplus is priced in rather
2910/// than free, since a cycle emits it whether or not any share is lost (see `pix_params_to_quota`).
2911///
2912/// The fourth is not a dimension and does not enter the quota: it names the elliptic curve the
2913/// Entry's build instantiates PIX over, which fixes the width of every curve-sized field later in
2914/// the handshake. It is fixed at build time on both sides and is therefore not negotiated — the Exit
2915/// refuses anything but its own, below.
2916///
2917/// What is announced is built from the installed [`SsaShareGenerator`]'s
2918/// [`SsaGeneratorConfig`](hopr_protocol_pix::SsaGeneratorConfig), never from the caller: the
2919/// generator is what produces the shares that go on the wire, so advertising anything else would
2920/// let the Session proceed while emitting shares the Exit cannot reconstruct. The dimensions are
2921/// therefore not configurable per Session — [`Capability::UsePIX`] is the whole per-Session switch,
2922/// and a node with no PIX toolbox installed refuses the Session. That check runs before the
2923/// initiation challenge slot is reserved, so a node that cannot serve PIX at all cannot have its
2924/// challenge slots exhausted by repeated requests for it.
2925///
2926/// The caller never needs to know the resulting quota in advance: it is computed node-side and
2927/// handed back per SSA in [`AgreedSsaQuota::quota_per_ssa`], which is what sizes the deposit.
2928///
2929/// On the Exit side, `check_pix_params` validates these parameters against:
2930/// - The protocol ranges, which [`PixParams::try_from_additional_data`] enforces as it unpacks.
2931/// - The configured [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::quota_range`] (by default ≈157 MiB–630 MiB). Dynamic admission checks
2932///   the smallest `batch_size × quota_per_ssa` up to the configured maximum; fixed admission checks the per-SSA quota
2933///   itself and retains the configured exact batch.
2934/// - Optionally, [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::enforce_pix`] rejects Sessions that do not offer PIX.
2935/// - The Exit only checks the *product* `polys × (threshold + surplus)`, not the individual values, so the Entry can
2936///   split it to suit its computing power. The computation is easily parallelizable in the number of polynomials, but
2937///   not in threshold. The surplus is inside that product, so redundancy is bought rather than taken: a cycle emits
2938///   `threshold + surplus` shares per polynomial come what may, and the deposit covers all of them.
2939///
2940/// If parameters are rejected, a [`StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams`] error is returned.
2941///
2942/// ### 2. Exit SSA Request (`SsaRequest` → Entry)
2943///
2944/// Once the PIX parameters are accepted, the Exit spawns a `SessionPixSupervisor`, whose opening
2945/// `RequestSsa` action has `send_ssa_request` create a new SSA commitment via the server-side
2946/// [`SsaReconstructor`]. This produces an *Exit commitment* (a group element) that is sent back to
2947/// the Entry as a [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`].
2948///
2949/// One action, and therefore one message, carries the batch selected during admission: no more than
2950/// [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request) SSAs at
2951/// contiguous indices, sharing the single `params` field, since every SSA in a Session uses the same
2952/// dimensions. The Entry caps what it will accept at
2953/// [`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`], and rejects an over-cap request in full while
2954/// replying with an `UnacceptablePixParams` [`StartErrorType`], so the Exit does not have to infer the
2955/// refusal from a deadline. The default is a batch of one, which is byte-for-byte the unbatched
2956/// exchange.
2957///
2958/// From here the supervisor owns the cycle's deadlines: `max_ssa_delivery_time` for the Entry's
2959/// commitment, then `max_deposit_wait` for the funds, then the recovery deadlines. Missing any of
2960/// them closes the Session with `ClosureReason::PixFailure`. The first two are multiplied by the batch
2961/// size, because a batch asks the Entry for that many commitment sets and that many deposits before
2962/// any of them can fairly be called late.
2963///
2964/// The opening request is sent once. A *successor* request is not: the Entry's successor gate drops
2965/// one that comes before its predecessor's returned packets have earned it, and says nothing, and a
2966/// request can equally be lost on the return path. So while a successor batch is unanswered — none
2967/// of its commitment has arrived — and an earlier generation is still being served, the supervisor
2968/// emits `ResendSsaRequest` every
2969/// [`ssa_request_resend_interval`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssa_request_resend_interval), which has
2970/// the action driver send the stored message again, byte for byte, and pushes the batch's
2971/// `max_ssa_delivery_time` deadline with it. The Entry answers a repeat of a request it already
2972/// committed to with a no-op once it has published the batch in full. The exception is a repeat
2973/// that arrives more than `SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE` after the batch went out, which says the
2974/// bursts were lost after the transport took them; they are sent again, without a second
2975/// `ReadyToDeposit`. A batch whose publication the transport cut short is finished instead, with
2976/// whole bursts and the `ReadyToDeposit`s still owed, whenever the Exit asks again. A request that
2977/// arrives while the Entry is still processing another one is dropped rather than queued. The
2978/// re-sends end once every member of the batch has reported a part of its commitment, and once the
2979/// batch reaches the front nothing is sent and the deadline runs out as it always did.
2980///
2981/// ### 3. Entry SSA Commitment (`SsaCommit` → Exit)
2982///
2983/// Upon receiving the [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`], the Entry's `handle_ssa_request`
2984/// generates a *client commitment* using the shared [`SsaShareGenerator`] (which is also
2985/// used by the packet pipeline to embed PIX shares into return-path SURBs). The client
2986/// commitment is combined with the Exit commitment to derive the on-chain deposit address
2987/// via [`HoprPixSpec::group_to_deposit_address`].
2988///
2989/// The Entry then sends one or more [`SsaClientCommitmentMessage`]s back to the Exit and
2990/// emits a [`HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit`] to the upper layer, signaling that
2991/// funds can be deposited at the computed address.
2992///
2993/// "One or more" is well over a hundred at the deployed dimensions — one commitment per polynomial,
2994/// chunked to packet size — and the Exit can use *none* of it until every message has landed, since
2995/// the SSA commitment is the sum of them all. A single lost packet therefore used to cost the whole
2996/// Session on `max_ssa_delivery_time`, typically after the Entry had already been told to fund the
2997/// address.
2998///
2999/// So a partially delivered commitment is repaired rather than waited out. Each arriving message
3000/// reports `SessionPixEvent::CommitmentProgress`, which arms (and re-arms) the supervisor's
3001/// [`commitment_recommit_interval`](crate::SupervisorConfig::commitment_recommit_interval); if
3002/// delivery then goes quiet with the set incomplete, `RequestCommitmentRetransmission` has
3003/// `send_commitment_retransmission_request` ask the Entry — via an `SsaRequest` whose
3004/// [`missing`](hopr_protocol_start::SsaServerCommitmentMessage::missing) scope names the polynomial
3005/// runs the reconstructor never received — to re-send exactly those. The Entry answers in
3006/// `handle_ssa_recommit` from the bytes it sent the first time, advancing nothing and announcing no
3007/// second deposit. A cycle for which *nothing* arrived never asks: it has no scope to name, and the
3008/// delivery deadline remains what ends it.
3009///
3010/// ### 4. Deposit Awaiting (Exit Side)
3011///
3012/// The Exit receives the client commitment messages in `handle_ssa_commit`, inserts the
3013/// coefficient commitments into the [`SsaReconstructor`], and extracts the deposit address.
3014/// It emits [`HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded`] to the upper layer with the
3015/// [`AgreedSsaQuota`] and a channel to confirm the deposit.
3016///
3017/// A verifiable commitment is what starts the deposit clock, so the supervisor is told
3018/// (`CommitmentVerified`) before anything can be reported against it. A `PixDepositObserver` task
3019/// then forwards every confirmation arriving on that channel as `DepositConfirmed`: top-ups
3020/// accumulate, and the supervisor is what decides when enough has landed. The observer carries no
3021/// timeout of its own — `max_deposit_wait` is the deadline, and a second authority racing the
3022/// first is exactly what the supervisor exists to prevent. If the upper layer drops the sender
3023/// without ever confirming, the observer reports that (`DepositObserverClosed`) rather than
3024/// letting the deadline run out on a deposit that is never coming.
3025///
3026/// Once the deposit suffices, the SSA moves to *recovering*. Its recovery deadlines start when it
3027/// reaches the front, and its deposit releases the egress gate only while it is there. When a paid
3028/// front leaves—whether recovered or retired after a tolerated failure—an unfunded successor
3029/// restores its own bounded predeposit allowance; an already funded successor stays open but starts
3030/// a fresh served-without-progress ceiling.
3031///
3032/// ### 5. SSA Collection, Recovery and Pipelining
3033///
3034/// As the Entry sends return-path SURBs during the Session, each SURB can carry a PIX
3035/// share generated from the client's polynomial set. The Exit's [`SsaReconstructor`]
3036/// collects these shares and reports how far the cycle has got via
3037/// [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::RecoveryProgress`]; `dispatch_pix_event` forwards those snapshots to
3038/// the supervisor, which uses them both to reset `max_recovery_idle` and to keep the gate serving.
3039///
3040/// When the last cycle of a batch reaches the *early recovery threshold* (≈85%), an
3041/// [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaAlmostRecovered`] event fires and the supervisor answers with a
3042/// `RequestSsa` action for the next batch — pipelining the costly commitment exchange with the tail
3043/// of share collection. If that cycle is still awaiting its own commitment or deposit, the request
3044/// waits for funding; if two generations still own cycle state, it waits for one to be fully
3045/// released. Those checks are independent of the configurable share-order policy.
3046///
3047/// Once fully recovered, [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered`] fires, allowing the Exit to
3048/// unlock and redeem the deposited funds. The reconstructor releases the live cycle immediately;
3049/// the supervisor retains a short tombstone, whose expiry emits `RetireSsa` to drop that cycle's
3050/// [`SsaCommitmentGuard`] and abort its deposit observer. The next batch is requested here if
3051/// `SsaAlmostRecovered` has not already done so. Observers are keyed by SSA index, so retiring one
3052/// cycle never cancels a pipelined successor's.
3053///
3054/// ### 6. Unverifiable Shares
3055///
3056/// Shares are not checked individually. Once a polynomial has collected `threshold` of them,
3057/// the reconstructor interpolates its constant term and compares it against the commitment; if
3058/// they disagree, at least one of those shares did not come from the committed polynomial and an
3059/// [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares`] event fires, carrying the reconstructor's running
3060/// total for the SSA rather than a delta.
3061///
3062/// The first such report closes the Session, unconditionally and with nothing to configure. The
3063/// failed polynomial is never retried, and the SSA is the sum of every polynomial's constant term,
3064/// so the cycle is already unrecoverable and can never pay; closing immediately caps what a
3065/// malicious Entry is served at `threshold` packets. The running total is logged rather than
3066/// accumulated. See `SessionPixSupervisor::on_unverifiable_shares` for why no tolerance is offered.
3067///
3068/// ### Configuring PIX at the Exit
3069///
3070/// The Exit configures PIX via [`IncomingSessionPixConfig`] within [`SessionManagerConfig`].
3071///
3072/// The [`PixToolbox`] (holding the [`SsaShareGenerator`] and [`SsaReconstructor`]) must
3073/// be provided via [`SessionManager::start`] for PIX to function.
3074pub struct SessionManager<S> {
3075    // Keeps track of Session initiations requests on the Client side.
3076    session_initiations: SessionInitiationCache,
3077    session_notifiers: Arc<OnceLock<SessionNotifiers>>,
3078    start_protocol_tx: StartProtocolMsgSink,
3079    /// Authoritative session count for admission control.
3080    /// Incremented atomically inside `allocate_session_slot` before the cache insertion,
3081    /// and decremented at every removal path (explicit close, eviction, guard rollback).
3082    active_sessions: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
3083    sessions: moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
3084    msg_sender: Arc<OnceLock<S>>,
3085    pix_toolbox: Arc<OnceLock<PixToolbox>>,
3086    cfg: SessionManagerConfig,
3087    /// Per-SessionId waiters notified when a new session slot is allocated. Lets message
3088    /// handlers that arrive before the slot insertion completes (e.g. SsaRequest vs
3089    /// SessionEstablished) await the slot once instead of busy-looping with sleeps.
3090    /// Keyed by SessionId so that only waiters for the relevant session are woken.
3091    ///
3092    /// Holds at most one live waiter per SessionId: `handle_ssa_request` refuses a request that
3093    /// finds another one already waiting, rather than parking a second shared Start handler.
3094    slot_allocated: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Vec<oneshot::Sender<()>>>>>,
3095    /// Pseudonyms of outgoing Session initiations currently in flight.
3096    ///
3097    /// `session_initiations` is keyed by challenge, but a Start message arriving from the peer
3098    /// names the Session by its pseudonym. This is the pseudonym-keyed half, so `dispatch_message`
3099    /// can tell in one lookup whether an inbound `SsaRequest` belongs to an initiation this node is
3100    /// still making — the only case in which waiting for a slot is legitimate. Entries are removed
3101    /// by [`PendingOutgoingGuard`] on every failure path and once the slot exists; the TTL is a
3102    /// backstop matching `session_initiations`'.
3103    ///
3104    /// An initiation claims its entry atomically (see `new_session`), so a marker is owned by at
3105    /// most one attempt at a time: a second initiation for a pseudonym that is still pending is
3106    /// refused rather than allowed to overwrite the first one's reservation. The value is a
3107    /// per-claim token, which lets [`PendingOutgoingGuard`] tell its own claim from a newer one
3108    /// that reused the name after the TTL backstop expired the older marker.
3109    pending_outgoing: moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>,
3110    /// Serialises `handle_ssa_request` per pseudonym.
3111    ///
3112    /// Start messages are processed under `for_each_concurrent`, so without this several
3113    /// `SsaRequest`s for one pseudonym run at once — and each reads the successor gate's admission
3114    /// state before any of them has advanced it. Every racer passes, and the Entry commits to (and
3115    /// funds) as many batches as the Exit cared to send, which is exactly what the gate exists to
3116    /// stop. The generator's own monotonic index is the backstop that keeps this from being a
3117    /// correctness hole, but it only rejects *equal or lower* indices: an Exit numbering its batches
3118    /// upwards races past it.
3119    ///
3120    /// An async lock rather than a blocking one because the guarded region awaits — commitment
3121    /// generation goes to a blocking pool, and publication awaits the transport. It is only ever
3122    /// `try_lock`ed, though: a request that finds it held is refused rather than parked on a shared
3123    /// Start handler behind the holder (see `handle_ssa_request`).
3124    ///
3125    /// A `moka` cache rather than a map, for its idle eviction: a `HashMap` keyed by pseudonym would
3126    /// otherwise retain one entry per Session for the life of the process.
3127    ssa_request_locks: moka::future::Cache<HoprPseudonym, Arc<futures::lock::Mutex<()>>>,
3128    /// Live reconstructor-cycle bytes this node has committed to, summed over every PIX Session.
3129    ///
3130    /// The counterpart of `active_sessions`, and the reason that one is not sufficient: a Session is
3131    /// admitted on a slot count, but what it costs the reconstructor is set by the dimensions its
3132    /// peer offered. Charged in `handle_incoming_session_initiation` and returned by
3133    /// [`CycleBudgetReservation`]'s `Drop`, so no removal path has to remember to decrement it.
3134    live_cycle_bytes: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
3135    /// Where incoming Sessions are put to the session server for an admission decision.
3136    ///
3137    /// Unset on a node that runs no session server — an Entry, or a relay — where there is nobody to
3138    /// ask and every Session is admitted on this node's own terms.
3139    /// Behind a `Mutex` so every request goes through *one* sender.
3140    ///
3141    /// `futures::channel::mpsc` gives each cloned `Sender` its own guaranteed slot on top of the
3142    /// buffer, so sending through a fresh clone each time would let the queue grow with the number
3143    /// of concurrent initiations — the bound would not bound. `try_send` never blocks, so the lock
3144    /// is held only for the enqueue itself.
3145    admission_tx: Arc<OnceLock<parking_lot::Mutex<SessionAdmissionSink>>>,
3146    /// The SURB-store admission seam, set once by the composition root after construction.
3147    ///
3148    /// Injected late — rather than through [`SessionManager::new`] — because the only in-tree
3149    /// implementation wraps the SURB store, which is built in the same crate as this manager's
3150    /// caller but cannot be named here (`hopr-transport-session` does not depend on
3151    /// `hopr-protocol-hopr`). A manager without one still works: it simply never admits, and every
3152    /// Session's SURBs then live in the store's quarantine class, which is why
3153    /// [`set_surb_admission`](Self::set_surb_admission) exists and why a missed call is observable
3154    /// in the store's own admission metrics rather than silent here.
3155    surb_admission: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>>,
3156}
3157
3158impl<S> Clone for SessionManager<S> {
3159    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
3160        Self {
3161            session_initiations: self.session_initiations.clone(),
3162            session_notifiers: self.session_notifiers.clone(),
3163            start_protocol_tx: self.start_protocol_tx.clone(),
3164            active_sessions: self.active_sessions.clone(),
3165            live_cycle_bytes: self.live_cycle_bytes.clone(),
3166            sessions: self.sessions.clone(),
3167            cfg: self.cfg.clone(),
3168            msg_sender: self.msg_sender.clone(),
3169            pix_toolbox: self.pix_toolbox.clone(),
3170            slot_allocated: Arc::clone(&self.slot_allocated),
3171            pending_outgoing: self.pending_outgoing.clone(),
3172            ssa_request_locks: self.ssa_request_locks.clone(),
3173            admission_tx: self.admission_tx.clone(),
3174            surb_admission: self.surb_admission.clone(),
3175        }
3176    }
3177}
3178
3179fn session_config(cfg: &SessionManagerConfig, capabilities: Capabilities) -> HoprSessionConfig {
3180    session_config_with(cfg, capabilities, None)
3181}
3182
3183/// As [`session_config`], with the initiating session's own head-of-line bound.
3184///
3185/// `None` inherits the node default; `Some(0)` disables the bound for this session; `Some(n)` sets
3186/// it. The zero-disables convention matches the node setting, so the per-session
3187/// and node-wide knobs cannot mean opposite things by the same value.
3188///
3189/// Sessions accepted from a peer pass `None`: the bound governs how *we* reassemble what arrives,
3190/// so it is ours to choose, not the initiator's to impose on us.
3191fn session_config_with(
3192    cfg: &SessionManagerConfig,
3193    capabilities: Capabilities,
3194    max_frames_behind_gap: Option<usize>,
3195) -> HoprSessionConfig {
3196    // Only a session that cannot recover the missing frame should abandon it early. With
3197    // retransmission the gap is a request away, so waiting is productive and cutting it short
3198    // would discard data that was on its way back; without it the wait is for something that is
3199    // never coming, and every frame behind the gap is held for nothing.
3200    let can_retransmit =
3201        capabilities.contains(Capability::RetransmissionAck) || capabilities.contains(Capability::RetransmissionNack);
3202
3203    // The session's own value when it stated one, the node's otherwise. `Some(0)` disables the
3204    // bound at either level -- a threshold of zero would abandon every gap before a single frame
3205    // arrived behind it, which nobody wants and which the sequencer would silently clamp to one.
3206    let bound = match max_frames_behind_gap.or(cfg.max_frames_behind_gap) {
3207        Some(0) | None => None,
3208        Some(n) => Some(n),
3209    };
3210
3211    HoprSessionConfig {
3212        capabilities,
3213        frame_mtu: cfg.frame_mtu,
3214        frame_timeout: cfg.max_frame_timeout,
3215        max_buffered_segments: cfg.max_buffered_segments,
3216        max_frames_behind_gap: (!can_retransmit).then_some(bound).flatten(),
3217    }
3218}

3220#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
3221fn initialize_session_telemetry(
3222    session_id: SessionId,
3223    cfg: &SessionManagerConfig,
3224    capabilities: Capabilities,
3225    surb_estimator: Option<&AtomicSurbFlowEstimator>,
3226    surb_mgmt: Option<&Arc<BalancerStateValues>>,
3227) {
3228    initialize_session_metrics(session_id, session_config(cfg, capabilities));
3229    set_session_state(&session_id, SessionLifecycleState::Active);
3230    if let (Some(estimator), Some(mgmt)) = (surb_estimator, surb_mgmt) {
3231        set_session_balancer_data(&session_id, estimator.clone(), mgmt.clone());
3232    }
3233}
3234
3235/// Caps how many SURBs an outgoing Session data packet may carry, per the SURB balancer.
3236///
3237/// Every finite `max_surbs` is gated by the balancer's target: the packet carries the client's number
3238/// of SURBs while the counterparty is estimated to be below its target, and none once it is at or above
3239/// it. The default of `1` is the plain case. A larger client value, which exists to save the balancer
3240/// work on highly asymmetric traffic, is gated the same way, so no setting but `usize::MAX` can hold
3241/// the counterparty more than one packet's SURBs above the target. An explicit `0` always wins, whatever
3242/// the estimate. `usize::MAX` leaves the packet's existing limit untouched and is the one way to opt out
3243/// of the gate.
3244///
3245/// The gate is [`BalancerStateValues::organic_surbs_per_packet`], which yields `0` once the
3246/// counterparty is estimated to be at its target. That zero is the whole point of the function:
3247/// without it, the balancer can silence its keep-alives and still have organic SURBs pouring into a
3248/// full buffer, where each one evicts an older SURB and destroys the PIX share it carried. It also
3249/// bounds the stock the counterparty holds, which is what lets a SURB generation change wipe it at a
3250/// cost the PIX surplus can absorb.
3251///
3252/// One exception: while data goes out into a silence (see [`BalancerStateValues::silence_sustain`]),
3253/// a closed gate gives exactly one SURB per packet, whatever the client asked for. The estimate that
3254/// closed it is fed by the counterparty, and the counterparty has not been heard from for a while, so
3255/// the estimate cannot see the stock draining and would hold the gate shut until it is empty. One SURB
3256/// per data packet is about what the counterparty spends answering it: no burst, bounded by the data
3257/// rate, and it ends with the first report or reply.
3258///
3259/// Nothing else has to change to keep the SURB accounting straight. This runs in front of the
3260/// counting sink, so `estimate_surbs_with_msg` reports the capped figure; and the PIX share for a
3261/// SURB is drawn per SURB while it is built, so a cap of `0` draws no share at all and leaves it
3262/// queued for a packet that can actually deliver it.
3263fn cap_organic_surbs(data: &mut ApplicationDataOut, max_surbs: usize, surb_mgmt: &BalancerStateValues) {
3264    if max_surbs == usize::MAX {
3265        return;
3266    }
3267    // This packet is going out, which is what a silence is measured against.
3268    surb_mgmt.note_sent();
3269    let cap = if max_surbs == 0 {
3270        0
3271    } else if surb_mgmt.organic_surbs_per_packet() > 0 {
3272        max_surbs
3273    } else if surb_mgmt.silence_sustain() {
3274        1
3275    } else {
3276        0
3277    };
3278    data.packet_info.get_or_insert_default().max_surbs_in_packet = cap;
3279}
3280
3281/// Books what a Start-protocol packet did to an incoming Session's SURB store: the SURBs it carried and
3282/// the ones the store lost to it. A no-op for an outgoing Session, whose counterparty stores no SURBs of
3283/// ours.
3284///
3285/// Every Start message from the Entry delivers SURBs into the Session's ring exactly as a data packet
3286/// does, whatever the message is: a keep-alive, an `SsaCommit`, the opening `StartSession`. Booking only
3287/// the keep-alives left the others' SURBs out of the Exit's level while the evictions they caused later
3288/// were booked, so once a ring sized off the announced target ran full, the estimate sank below the
3289/// target for good and the Exit's egress controller, which follows it, sent nothing at all.
3290///
3291/// What the packet carried is booked, not a message's `max_surbs()`: that is how many fit beside it,
3292/// what the sender was allowed to send rather than what the store took. And the evictions, which are
3293/// how a SURB generation wipe, and any overflow, reaches the Exit's level.
3294///
3295/// Returns whether it booked anything, i.e. whether `slot` is an incoming Session.
3296fn book_start_message_surbs(slot: &SessionSlot, session_id: &SessionId, stored: SurbsStored) -> bool {
3297    if !matches!(slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Return(_)) {
3298        return false;
3299    }
3300    account_incoming_surbs(&slot.surb_estimator, stored.saved, stored.evicted);
3301    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
3302    telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(session_id, stored.saved);
3303    #[cfg(not(feature = "telemetry"))]
3304    let _ = session_id;
3305    true
3306}
3307
3308/// Books an incoming packet's SURBs into the Exit's flow estimator.
3309///
3310/// `saved` SURBs entered the store and `evicted` older ones were dropped to make room for them. Both
3311/// are recorded so that `produced - consumed - evicted` tracks what the store actually holds: without
3312/// the eviction term the estimate stays inflated by every SURB the full store ever discarded, long
3313/// after they are gone -- which leaves the keep-alive level report and the PIX fill reserve both
3314/// reading a level that never falls. `evicted` also carries the stock a newer SURB generation wiped,
3315/// which is what lets the Exit's level report drop to match after the Entry advances the generation.
3316///
3317/// Called for every packet that delivers SURBs to an incoming Session, and there are two kinds: Session
3318/// data packets, in the `session_rx` inspectors of `new_session`, and Start protocol messages, through
3319/// [`book_start_message_surbs`], which `dispatch_message` calls for every Start message and the Start
3320/// task for an opening `StartSession`. The Entry's balancer mints its SURBs as keep-alives as much as in
3321/// data, so a booking in only one of them misses the other's share. Split out from the receive closure
3322/// so the accounting can be unit-tested on its own.
3323fn account_incoming_surbs(estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator, saved: u64, evicted: u64) {
3324    estimator
3325        .produced
3326        .fetch_add(saved, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3327    estimator
3328        .evicted
3329        .fetch_add(evicted, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3330}
3331
3332/// Removes an outgoing Session's pseudonym from the manager's pending index when dropped.
3333///
3334/// The index is keyed by the pseudonym the initiation is made under, but the paths that would
3335/// otherwise clear it key on the peer-supplied `session_id`, which arrives in the establishment
3336/// reply and is never checked against the pseudonym — a mismatched one would clear someone else's
3337/// marker, and every early return and a dropped future would clear no one's. The guard ties the
3338/// cleanup to the pseudonym actually inserted, so no path has to remember it.
3339///
3340/// The removal is ownership-checked rather than a plain `remove`, because the marker's TTL is only
3341/// a backstop and the guard can outlive it: an initiation that times out runs almost to the TTL,
3342/// so a few ticks of clock skew — or a task descheduled between the await resolving and the future
3343/// being polled to completion — put the drop past expiry. Once expired, moka reports the key as
3344/// absent, so a newer initiation for the same pseudonym can claim the name again; when this guard
3345/// then drops, an unconditional `remove` would tear down the newer attempt's marker and leave its
3346/// in-flight initiation invisible to the dispatch filter, which would drop that Session's
3347/// `SsaRequest`s as `StaleStartMessage`. Comparing the entry's generation token restricts the
3348/// removal to the marker this guard's own claim created.
3349struct PendingOutgoingGuard<'a> {
3350    pending: &'a moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>,
3351    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
3352    token: PendingOutgoingToken,
3353}
3354
3355impl Drop for PendingOutgoingGuard<'_> {
3356    fn drop(&mut self) {
3357        // `and_compute_with` reads under moka's per-key compute lock and reports an expired entry
3358        // as absent, so an expired marker of ours falls through to `Op::Nop` and nothing is left
3359        // to clean up; a marker another attempt claimed after our expiry is likewise left to that
3360        // attempt's own guard.
3361        self.pending.entry(self.pseudonym).and_compute_with(
3362            |entry: Option<moka::Entry<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>>| {
3363                match entry {
3364                    // Still ours.
3365                    Some(entry) if entry.value() == &self.token => moka::ops::compute::Op::Remove,
3366                    // Absent (expired, or already removed by the success path), or a newer
3367                    // attempt's claim: nothing to do.
3368                    _ => moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop,
3369                }
3370            },
3371        );
3372    }
3373}
3374
3375/// Per-claim token distinguishing one initiation's marker from another attempt's under the same
3376/// pseudonym.
3377///
3378/// Uniqueness only has to hold for the lifetime of one claim, which the atomic claim in
3379/// `new_session` serialises: two guards for the same pseudonym never overlap on a live marker.
3380/// A per-process counter is enough for that, and `Copy` keeps the token cheap to move into and
3381/// compare inside the compute closure.
3382#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
3383struct PendingOutgoingToken(u64);
3384
3385impl PendingOutgoingToken {
3386    fn next() -> Self {
3387        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
3388        static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
3389        Self(NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed))
3390    }
3391}
3392
3393async fn send_via_msg_sender<S, D>(
3394    msg_sender: &mut S,
3395    routing: DestinationRouting,
3396    data: D,
3397    error_context: &'static str,
3398) -> errors::Result<()>
3399where
3400    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
3401    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
3402    D: TryInto<ApplicationData>,
3403    D::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
3404{
3405    let app_data: ApplicationData = data.try_into().map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
3406    msg_sender
3407        .send((routing, ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(app_data)))
3408        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT))
3409        .await
3410        .map_err(|_| {
3411            error!("timeout sending {error_context}");
3412            TransportSessionError::Timeout
3413        })?
3414        .map_err(|error| {
3415            error!(%error, "failed to send {error_context}");
3416            SessionManagerError::other(error)
3417        })?;
3418    Ok(())
3419}
3420
3421/// The batch most recently put on the wire by the PIX action driver, with the message that carried it.
3422///
3423/// The one thing [`SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest`] can send again. See
3424/// [`SessionManager::spawn_pix_action_driver`].
3425type LastSsaRequest = (Vec<SsaId<HoprPseudonym>>, HoprStartProtocol);
3426
3427/// What the action driver does with a [`SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest`].
3428///
3429/// The decision is separate from the driver so that each refusal is observable on its own: all of them
3430/// look the same from outside — nothing goes on the wire and the supervisor is told the batch can no
3431/// longer be sent — and the driver's I/O loop is the wrong place to pin which of the three it was.
3432#[derive(Debug)]
3433enum ResendDecision<'a> {
3434    /// Send this message, which is the stored request itself and so goes out byte for byte as before.
3435    Send(&'a HoprStartProtocol),
3436    /// The ids are not the batch last sent: a report about an earlier batch, or the batch has been
3437    /// retired since. Another tick would meet the same answer.
3438    NotLastRequest,
3439    /// A member's Exit registration no longer exists — retired, or idled out past
3440    /// `incomplete_commitment_lifetime` — so the Entry's answer would find nothing to match
3441    /// (`MissingSsaCommitment`).
3442    RegistrationGone,
3443    /// Every member's commitment is already complete. The Entry has answered in full; what is left is
3444    /// not a request to send again.
3445    CommitmentComplete,
3446}
3447
3448/// Decides whether `ssa_ids` can be re-sent, and with what.
3449///
3450/// Sent only if `ssa_ids` is exactly the batch of `last_request`, every member still has a
3451/// registration, and at least one of them is still waiting for its commitment (a non-empty
3452/// `missing_commitment_runs`). A member whose commitment is complete is no reason to refuse: the
3453/// supervisor re-sends the whole batch until *every* member has heard from the Entry, because the
3454/// Entry publishes a batch one member after another and may have been cut short before the later ones,
3455/// and the Entry's repeat branch publishes only the members it still owes. It sends the bursts of the
3456/// others again only when the repeat comes long enough after the batch went out to mean they were lost.
3457///
3458/// Every member is read, with no early exit, because reading a registration refreshes its idle timer —
3459/// see [`SsaReconstructor::missing_commitment_runs`] — which is what keeps a registration alive across
3460/// the Entry's silence. A mismatch is decided before any registration is read, since the batch is not
3461/// one this driver can send anyway; a missing registration decides before completeness does.
3462fn resend_payload<'a>(
3463    last_request: Option<&'a LastSsaRequest>,
3464    ssa_ids: &[SsaId<HoprPseudonym>],
3465    processor: &SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>,
3466) -> ResendDecision<'a> {
3467    let Some((_, message)) = last_request.filter(|(sent_ids, _)| sent_ids.as_slice() == ssa_ids) else {
3468        return ResendDecision::NotLastRequest;
3469    };
3470
3471    let (mut gone, mut pending) = (false, false);
3472    for ssa_id in ssa_ids {
3473        match processor.missing_commitment_runs(ssa_id, 1) {
3474            None => gone = true,
3475            Some(runs) => pending |= !runs.is_empty(),
3476        }
3477    }
3478    match (gone, pending) {
3479        (true, _) => ResendDecision::RegistrationGone,
3480        (false, false) => ResendDecision::CommitmentComplete,
3481        (false, true) => ResendDecision::Send(message),
3482    }
3483}
3484
3485/// Forgets `last_request` when `retired` is one of its members.
3486///
3487/// A batch with a retired member is not one the Entry can still be asked to commit to as a whole, and
3488/// the supervisor ends its re-sends. The stored message goes with it, so a `ResendSsaRequest` that was
3489/// already queued finds nothing to send. Left to the registration check in [`resend_payload`] alone,
3490/// that refusal would depend on the reconstructor having dropped the retired member's registration.
3491fn forget_request_of(last_request: &mut Option<LastSsaRequest>, retired: &SsaId<HoprPseudonym>) {
3492    if last_request
3493        .as_ref()
3494        .is_some_and(|(sent_ids, _)| sent_ids.contains(retired))
3495    {
3496        *last_request = None;
3497    }
3498}
3499
3500/// The messages of one cycle's client commitment, as [`SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple`] splits it.
3501type CommitmentBurst = Vec<SsaClientCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixCommitmentProof>>;
3502
3503/// Puts one cycle's commitment burst on the wire and, only once all of it is out, announces its deposit
3504/// address.
3505///
3506/// The order is the point: the deposit must not begin before the Exit holds the complete commitment it
3507/// derives the deposit key from. If a send fails the burst stops where it is and nothing is announced;
3508/// the caller still owes the cycle its publication and decides what to do about that. The same goes
3509/// for an announcement that cannot be queued: the Exit then holds the whole commitment, but the
3510/// upper layer was never told to fund it.
3511async fn publish_commitment<S>(
3512    pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
3513    msg_sender: &mut S,
3514    routing: &DestinationRouting,
3515    burst: CommitmentBurst,
3516    quota: &AgreedSsaQuota,
3517    error_context: &'static str,
3518) -> errors::Result<()>
3519where
3520    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
3521    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
3522{
3523    let ssa_index = quota.ssa_id.ssa_index();
3524    for commitment_msg in burst {
3525        send_via_msg_sender(
3526            msg_sender,
3527            routing.clone(),
3528            HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(commitment_msg),
3529            error_context,
3530        )
3531        .await?;
3532    }
3533
3534    tracing::debug!(%ssa_index, "all Entry SSA commitment messages were sent out");
3535
3536    // Notify the new SSA deposit address *after* all commitment messages have been sent out
3537    // successfully, so the deposit cannot begin before the Exit has the complete commitment to
3538    // reconstruct the deposit key.
3539    pix_toolbox
3540        .pix_events
3541        .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit(quota.clone()))
3542        .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::other(anyhow!("failed to notify new deposit ssa")))?;
3543    tracing::info!(
3544        %ssa_index, deposit_address = %quota.deposit_address, quota_per_ssa = quota.quota_per_ssa,
3545        "generated client SSA commitment and deposit address"
3546    );
3547    Ok(())
3548}
3549
3550/// Puts a claimed member back after its publication failed, and reports the cut.
3551///
3552/// The single place a cut-short publication is logged — once, at `warn!`, with the member and how many
3553/// are still owed — and turned into an error: the non-fatal [`SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted`], whichever
3554/// path was publishing. The Session is untouched and the Exit is told nothing; whether it asks again is
3555/// its own business (see [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`]).
3556fn publication_cut_short(
3557    session_id: SessionId,
3558    ssa_state: &SessionSsaState,
3559    claim: ClaimedPublication,
3560    cause: &TransportSessionError,
3561) -> TransportSessionError {
3562    let ssa_index = claim.quota.ssa_id.ssa_index();
3563    ssa_state.restore_unpublished(claim);
3564    let still_owed = ssa_state.unpublished_indices().len();
3565    tracing::warn!(
3566        %session_id, %ssa_index, still_owed, error = %cause,
3567        "publishing the SSA commitment was cut short; it stays owed until the Exit asks again"
3568    );
3569    SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
3570        "publication of the SSA commitment for {ssa_index} was cut short ({cause}); {still_owed} member(s) still owed"
3571    ))
3572    .into()
3573}
3574
3575/// Finishes publishing the batch an interrupted publication left behind, member by member in ascending
3576/// order, stopping at the first transport failure.
3577///
3578/// Each member still owed is *claimed* first — removed from [`SessionSsaState`]'s unpublished set,
3579/// which is what makes it this call's alone — and then published in full: its whole burst, rebuilt
3580/// from the material the generator retains for the cycle, and only then the `ReadyToDeposit` that was
3581/// owed. Every member that is published here is published whole, and by exactly one caller, so a
3582/// resumption can neither announce a deposit twice nor race the original publication or another
3583/// resumption into doing so. A member whose publication fails goes back, the failure is reported
3584/// through [`publication_cut_short`], and the members after it were never claimed, so all of them stay
3585/// owed for the next attempt.
3586///
3587/// The whole burst is re-sent rather than only what went missing, because what went missing is not
3588/// known: the Entry's send failed at some message and says nothing about the ones the transport
3589/// accepted before it, and the Exit's request names parts of a commitment it may not even have started
3590/// to receive. That costs one of the cycle's
3591/// [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS) answers, and
3592/// that cap is what bounds how often a cycle can be re-published. Once it is spent the generator
3593/// refuses (`PixError::InvalidInput`), and so it does when nothing is retained for the cycle any more
3594/// (`PixError::MissingSsaCommitment`): either way the cycle can never be published again, so it is
3595/// dropped from the owed set with a single warning rather than kept to cost a blocking `recommit` and
3596/// a log line on every re-send. It is never announced, and nothing is stranded by that. Dropping one
3597/// member does not stop the others, and the call is successful if the rest were published.
3598///
3599/// A resumption is reached only through a repeat of the request or a scoped re-request that names an
3600/// owed cycle, so it covers what the Exit asks about. See [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`] for what
3601/// nothing prompts.
3602async fn resume_publication<S>(
3603    session_id: SessionId,
3604    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
3605    routing: &DestinationRouting,
3606    ssa_state: &SessionSsaState,
3607    pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
3608    msg_sender: &mut S,
3609) -> errors::Result<()>
3610where
3611    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
3612    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
3613{
3614    /// How resuming one member ended, short of a transport failure.
3615    enum Resumed {
3616        Published,
3617        /// The generator will never produce this cycle's burst again.
3618        Unpublishable(hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError<HoprPseudonym>),
3619    }
3620
3621    let whole_cycle = [(
3622        0,
3623        ssa_state.params.polys_per_ssa() as hopr_protocol_pix::PolynomialIndex - 1,
3624    )];
3625
3626    for ssa_index in ssa_state.unpublished_indices() {
3627        let Some(claim) = ssa_state.claim_unpublished(ssa_index) else {
3628            // Published, or being published, by someone else since the list was read.
3629            continue;
3630        };
3631
3632        let generator = pix_toolbox.share_generator.clone();
3633        let outcome: errors::Result<Resumed> = async {
3634            let recommitted = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
3635                move || generator.recommit(&pseudonym, ssa_index, whole_cycle),
3636                "client_ssa_recommitment",
3637            )
3638            .await
3639            .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
3640            let commitment = match recommitted {
3641                Ok(commitment) => commitment,
3642                Err(
3643                    error @ (hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::InvalidInput
3644                    | hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::MissingSsaCommitment),
3645                ) => return Ok(Resumed::Unpublishable(error)),
3646                Err(error) => return Err(SessionManagerError::PixError(error).into()),
3647            };
3648            let burst =
3649                SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, commitment).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
3650            publish_commitment(
3651                pix_toolbox,
3652                msg_sender,
3653                routing,
3654                burst,
3655                &claim.quota,
3656                "re-published client SSA commitment message",
3657            )
3658            .await?;
3659            Ok(Resumed::Published)
3660        }
3661        .await;
3662
3663        match outcome {
3664            Ok(Resumed::Published) => {
3665                ssa_state.complete_publication(claim, Instant::now());
3666                tracing::info!(%session_id, %ssa_index, "finished publishing an interrupted SSA commitment");
3667            }
3668            Ok(Resumed::Unpublishable(cause)) => {
3669                // Not put back: it can never be published, so owing it would only repeat this.
3670                tracing::warn!(
3671                    %session_id, %ssa_index, error = %cause,
3672                    "the SSA commitment can no longer be published and is dropped; its deposit is never announced"
3673                );
3674                drop(claim);
3675            }
3676            Err(error) => return Err(publication_cut_short(session_id, ssa_state, claim, &error)),
3677        }
3678    }
3679    Ok(())
3680}
3681
3682/// Sends the whole burst of each of `members` again, rebuilt from the material the generator
3683/// retains, and announces nothing.
3684///
3685/// This answers a repeat that arrives too late to have crossed the batch's bursts (see
3686/// [`SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE`]): some member's burst went out and none of it reached the Exit. The
3687/// repeat names the whole batch, not the member that is missing, so every announced member is sent
3688/// again, and a member the Exit already holds absorbs the copy. There is no `ReadyToDeposit`,
3689/// because each of `members` was announced when its publication completed (see
3690/// [`OwedPublications::announced`]).
3691///
3692/// Each re-send spends one of the cycle's
3693/// [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS), the same
3694/// budget a scoped re-request draws on. Once the generator refuses to rebuild a cycle, because that
3695/// budget is spent or its material is gone, the cycle is no longer counted as announced, so later
3696/// repeats do not ask again. A transport failure stops the re-send where it is and is the non-fatal
3697/// [`SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted`]. The Exit's next repeat after the grace tries again.
3698async fn republish_commitments<S>(
3699    session_id: SessionId,
3700    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
3701    routing: &DestinationRouting,
3702    ssa_state: &SessionSsaState,
3703    pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
3704    msg_sender: &mut S,
3705    members: Vec<SsaIndex>,
3706) -> errors::Result<()>
3707where
3708    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
3709    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
3710{
3711    let whole_cycle = [(
3712        0,
3713        ssa_state.params.polys_per_ssa() as hopr_protocol_pix::PolynomialIndex - 1,
3714    )];
3715
3716    for ssa_index in members {
3717        let generator = pix_toolbox.share_generator.clone();
3718        let recommitted = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
3719            move || generator.recommit(&pseudonym, ssa_index, whole_cycle),
3720            "client_ssa_recommitment",
3721        )
3722        .await
3723        .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
3724        let commitment = match recommitted {
3725            Ok(commitment) => commitment,
3726            Err(
3727                error @ (hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::InvalidInput
3728                | hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::MissingSsaCommitment),
3729            ) => {
3730                ssa_state.forget_announced(ssa_index);
3731                tracing::warn!(
3732                    %session_id, %ssa_index, error = %error,
3733                    "a lost SSA commitment can no longer be re-sent"
3734                );
3735                continue;
3736            }
3737            Err(error) => return Err(SessionManagerError::PixError(error).into()),
3738        };
3739
3740        let burst =
3741            SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, commitment).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
3742        let num_messages = burst.len();
3743        for commitment_msg in burst {
3744            if let Err(error) = send_via_msg_sender(
3745                msg_sender,
3746                routing.clone(),
3747                HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(commitment_msg),
3748                "re-sent client SSA commitment message",
3749            )
3750            .await
3751            {
3752                tracing::warn!(
3753                    %session_id, %ssa_index, %error,
3754                    "re-sending a lost SSA commitment was cut short; the Exit's next repeat tries again"
3755                );
3756                return Err(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
3757                    "re-sending the SSA commitment for {ssa_index} was cut short ({error})"
3758                ))
3759                .into());
3760            }
3761        }
3762
3763        tracing::info!(%session_id, %ssa_index, num_messages, "re-sent the whole commitment of a published SSA");
3764    }
3765    Ok(())
3766}
3767
3768impl<S> SessionManager<S>
3769where
3770    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
3771    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
3772{
3773    /// Creates a new instance given the [`config`](SessionManagerConfig).
3774    pub fn new(mut cfg: SessionManagerConfig) -> Self {
3775        let maximum_sessions = cfg.maximum_sessions;
3776        cfg.surb_balance_notify_period = cfg
3777            .surb_balance_notify_period
3778            .map(|p| p.max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD));
3779        cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration = cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION);
3780
3781        // Ensure the Frame MTU is at least the size of the Session segment MTU payload
3782        cfg.frame_mtu = cfg.frame_mtu.max(SESSION_MTU);
3783        cfg.max_frame_timeout = cfg.max_frame_timeout.max(MIN_FRAME_TIMEOUT);
3784
3785        // Both SSA batch knobs are range-validated in `HoprProtocolConfig`, but nothing in this crate
3786        // calls `validate()` — clamp here so a programmatically built config cannot ask for a batch of
3787        // zero (no request would ever be sent) or one large enough to blow past what
3788        // `MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE` exists to bound.
3789        cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request = cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE);
3790        cfg.pix_config.supervision.ssas_per_request =
3791            cfg.pix_config.supervision.ssas_per_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE);
3792
3793        // Every supervisor duration, for the same reason and with more riding on it. A duration the
3794        // monotonic clock cannot represent makes `Instant::checked_add` return `None`, and every phase
3795        // reads an absent deadline as *no deadline* — so an over-large value does not produce a distant
3796        // deadline, it silently disables the rule. `validate_pix_supervision` rejects such a config, but
3797        // only a node built from a config file goes through it.
3798        //
3799        // Representability is necessary and not sufficient, though: `max_recovery_idle` also has to
3800        // stay under the reconstructor's `unused_verifier_lifetime`, or the supervisor waits on a
3801        // cycle whose state was reclaimed hours earlier. Clamping only to the monotonic-clock cap left
3802        // exactly that — `Duration::MAX` became 24 h against a 30-minute default lifetime — so the
3803        // normalized config was representable and still invalid.
3804        //
3805        // The reconstructor is not installed until `start`, so the *default* configuration is what
3806        // this can normalize against. `start` re-checks against the one actually installed, which is
3807        // where a caller pairing a non-default reconstructor is caught.
3808        //
3809        // The two batch-scaled deadlines are clamped by the scaled value, since that is what is armed;
3810        // dividing by the batch size (already clamped to at least 1 above) is what keeps the product
3811        // under the cap.
3812        {
3813            use hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig;
3814
3815            let sup = &mut cfg.pix_config.supervision;
3816            let cap = crate::supervision::MAX_SUPERVISOR_DURATION;
3817            let per_cycle_cap = cap / sup.ssas_per_request as u32;
3818            sup.max_ssa_delivery_time = sup.max_ssa_delivery_time.min(per_cycle_cap);
3819            sup.max_deposit_wait = sup.max_deposit_wait.min(per_cycle_cap);
3820            sup.max_recovery_time = sup.max_recovery_time.min(cap);
3821            sup.tombstone_retention_window = sup.tombstone_retention_window.min(cap);
3822
3823            // Strictly under the lifetime, which is what `validate_pix_supervision` requires; a
3824            // saturating subtraction keeps a pathologically short lifetime from wrapping. The lower
3825            // bound is not clamped: raising a too-small value would be inventing a policy rather than
3826            // bounding one, and it is what `validate_pix_supervision` reports.
3827            let idle_cap = SsaReconstructorConfig::default()
3828                .unused_verifier_lifetime
3829                .saturating_sub(Duration::from_secs(1))
3830                .min(cap);
3831            sup.max_recovery_idle = sup.max_recovery_idle.min(idle_cap);
3832
3833            // The fill heartbeat is armed as a deadline like the rest, so it takes the same cap. The
3834            // rate ceiling is clamped for a different reason: `RateController::MIN_DELAY` makes
3835            // anything above `MAX_FILL_RATE` unrepresentable, and a controller that silently ignores
3836            // the one bound on this node's self-generated egress is worse than one that is loud about
3837            // refusing it — which is what `validate_pix_supervision` does for a config that was
3838            // validated. This branch is for the programmatic ones that never were.
3839            //
3840            // The heartbeat needs the *lower* bound for the same reason the ceiling needs its upper
3841            // one, and it is the one that bites: a zero period makes `FillRate::as_packets_per_sec`
3842            // report zero, so the planner's own floor is zero, every branch of `FillPlanner::bound`
3843            // that returns the heartbeat returns a zero period, and `PixFillControl::apply` hands
3844            // `set_rate_per_unit(1, 1µs)` to the controller — which `MIN_DELAY` turns into 10 000
3845            // packets/s. The one clamp that exists to bound self-generated egress is bypassed by the
3846            // one field that was left unbounded below. The floor is the exact dual of the ceiling —
3847            // the period of `MAX_FILL_RATE` — rather than a new number, so the two cannot drift; an
3848            // inverted heartbeat/ceiling pair is already resolved ceiling-wins inside `bound`, which
3849            // is what makes any positive floor safe here.
3850            sup.fill.heartbeat = sup
3851                .fill
3852                .heartbeat
3853                .clamp(Duration::from_secs(1) / crate::supervision::MAX_FILL_RATE, cap);
3854            sup.fill.max_rate = sup.fill.max_rate.clamp(1, crate::supervision::MAX_FILL_RATE);
3855        }
3856
3857        // The admission wait is spent inside the peer's initiation timeout, so a value at or above
3858        // it buys nothing: the peer has already given up by the time the wait expires, and the
3859        // Session was refused anyway. Clamped to one leg of that budget, leaving the other for the
3860        // Start exchange the decision is part of. Clamped rather than rejected because every other
3861        // cross-field rule in this constructor normalizes, and because the ceiling is derived from a
3862        // field the caller may also have left at its default.
3863        cfg.session_admission_timeout = cfg.session_admission_timeout.min(initiation_timeout_max_one_way(
3864            cfg.initiation_timeout_base,
3865            RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS,
3866        ));
3867
3868        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
3869        METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS.set(0.0);
3870
3871        let active_sessions: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize> = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
3872        let active_sessions_for_listener = active_sessions.clone();
3873
3874        let msg_sender = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
3875        let initiation_timeout =
3876            2 * initiation_timeout_max_one_way(cfg.initiation_timeout_base, RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS);
3877        let pix_toolbox: Arc<OnceLock<PixToolbox>> = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
3878        // Captured by the eviction listener below, which is built here and has no `&self` to read
3879        // later — same shape as `active_sessions_for_listener`. Cloned before the closure moves the
3880        // last binding, since the struct literal needs its own handle to the same lock.
3881        let surb_admission_for_listener: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>> = Arc::default();
3882        let surb_admission_in_struct = surb_admission_for_listener.clone();
3883        // The retire grace the listener's teardowns wait out, captured for the same reason: the
3884        // closure has no `&self`, and the window is operator-configurable, so it cannot be re-derived
3885        // from a literal at the call site.
3886        let surb_resolution_wait_for_listener = cfg.surb_resolution_wait;
3887        Self {
3888            msg_sender: msg_sender.clone(),
3889            session_initiations: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
3890                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
3891                .time_to_live(initiation_timeout)
3892                .build(),
3893            sessions: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
3894                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
3895                .time_to_idle(cfg.idle_timeout)
3896                .eviction_listener(move |session_id: Arc<SessionId>, entry: SessionSlot, reason| {
3897                    // The seam is captured at cache-build time rather than read from the
3898                    // manager here: this closure is not `&self`, and the eviction may fire
3899                    // long after the manager that built the cache has been cloned elsewhere.
3900                    let surb_admission = surb_admission_for_listener.get().cloned();
3901                    match &reason {
3902                        moka::notification::RemovalCause::Expired | moka::notification::RemovalCause::Size => {
3903                            trace!(?session_id, ?reason, "session evicted from the cache");
3904                            // Reconstructor state is released by `close_session` aborting the PIX
3905                            // action driver: the driver owns an `SsaCommitmentGuard` per live cycle,
3906                            // and dropping its future drops them. That bounds the release to the
3907                            // cycles actually in flight, where enumerating every index this Session
3908                            // had ever used was unbounded in its lifetime.
3909                            active_sessions_for_listener.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
3910                            let token = entry.claim_admission_token();
3911                            close_session(
3912                                *session_id.as_ref(),
3913                                entry,
3914                                ClosureReason::Eviction,
3915                                surb_admission,
3916                                surb_retire_grace(surb_resolution_wait_for_listener),
3917                                token,
3918                            );
3919                        }
3920                        _ => {}
3921                    }
3922                })
3923                .build(),
3924            pix_toolbox,
3925            session_notifiers: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
3926            start_protocol_tx: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
3927            active_sessions,
3928            live_cycle_bytes: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),
3929            cfg,
3930            slot_allocated: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
3931            pending_outgoing: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
3932                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
3933                .time_to_live(initiation_timeout)
3934                .build(),
3935            // Idle rather than live TTL, and generous: the entry only has to outlive the requests that
3936            // race for it, and one evicted between two cycles is simply recreated by the next request.
3937            // Matches the generator's own per-pseudonym cache, which is what the guarded region reads.
3938            ssa_request_locks: moka::future::Cache::builder()
3939                .time_to_idle(Duration::from_secs(1800))
3940                .build(),
3941            admission_tx: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
3942            surb_admission: surb_admission_in_struct,
3943        }
3944    }
3945
3946    /// Starts the instance with the given `msg_sender` `Sink`
3947    /// and a channel `new_session_notifier` used to notify when a new incoming session is opened to us.
3948    ///
3949    /// Optionally, the PIX processor and event sink can be provided for handling PIX protocol.
3950    /// If not specified, the `SessionManager` will not handle PIX protocol.
3951    ///
3952    /// `admission` is where incoming Sessions are put to the session server for a per-Session
3953    /// decision before they are established. Without it — an Entry, or a relay, or any caller that
3954    /// installed no session server — every Session is admitted on this node's own configured terms,
3955    /// which is the behaviour of a node that does not distinguish between targets.
3956    ///
3957    /// This method must be called prior to any calls to [`SessionManager::new_session`] or
3958    /// [`SessionManager::dispatch_message`].
3959    pub fn start<T>(
3960        &self,
3961        msg_sender: S,
3962        new_session_notifier: T,
3963        pix: Option<PixToolbox>,
3964        admission: Option<SessionAdmissionSink>,
3965    ) -> errors::Result<Vec<AbortHandle>>
3966    where
3967        T: futures::Sink<IncomingSession> + Send + 'static,
3968        T::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
3969    {
3970        // Every fallible check runs before the first `OnceLock::set` below.
3971        //
3972        // `start` publishes the manager's started state through those locks, and a `OnceLock` cannot
3973        // be un-set. Validating after `msg_sender` had been filled left a manager that reports
3974        // `is_started() == false` — no workers, no notifier — and yet refuses every retry with
3975        // `AlreadyStarted`: neither running nor recoverable, out of what is an ordinary configuration
3976        // error the caller could have corrected and retried on the same instance.
3977        if let Some(pix) = pix.as_ref() {
3978            validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&self.cfg.pix_config, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE)?;
3979
3980            // The authoritative cross-component check, and the first moment it can be made: the
3981            // supervisor's deadlines are meaningless without the reconstructor lifetimes they race
3982            // against, and the reconstructor arrives here rather than at construction.
3983            //
3984            // `SessionManager::new` normalizes against the *default* reconstructor config, which is
3985            // what makes the common programmatic case correct without an API break. A caller that
3986            // pairs a supervisor config with a non-default reconstructor is caught here instead — as
3987            // an error rather than a clamp, because at this point both halves were chosen
3988            // deliberately and silently overriding one of them would be the wrong answer.
3989            crate::supervision::validate_pix_supervision(
3990                &self.cfg.pix_config.supervision,
3991                pix.share_processor.config(),
3992            )?;
3993        }
3994
3995        self.msg_sender
3996            .set(msg_sender)
3997            .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::AlreadyStarted)?;
3998
3999        if let Some(pix) = pix {
4000            self.pix_toolbox
4001                .set(pix)
4002                .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::AlreadyStarted)?;
4003        }
4004
4005        if let Some(admission) = admission {
4006            self.admission_tx
4007                .set(parking_lot::Mutex::new(admission))
4008                .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::AlreadyStarted)?;
4009        }
4010
4011        // Re-map the user-provided sink errors to `SessionManagerError` and erase the concrete
4012        //  type so that the `SessionManager` does not need to be generic over it. This also avoids
4013        // having to spawn a separate task to forward items between channels: senders simply lock
4014        // the sink and send directly.
4015        let new_session_notifier: BoxSink<IncomingSession> =
4016            Box::pin(new_session_notifier.sink_map_err(SessionManagerError::other));
4017        let new_session_notifier = Arc::new(hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::Mutex::new(new_session_notifier));
4018
4019        let (session_close_tx, session_close_rx) =
4020            crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async(self.cfg.maximum_sessions + 10);
4021        self.session_notifiers
