4022            .set((new_session_notifier, session_close_tx))
4023            .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::AlreadyStarted)?;
4024
4025        let (start_protocol_tx, start_protocol_rx) =
4026            crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async(start_protocol_channel_capacity(&self.cfg));
4027        let _ = self.start_protocol_tx.set(start_protocol_tx);
4028
4029        let myself = self.clone();
4030        let closure_diag = hopr_utils::runtime::diagnostics::ConcurrentDiagnostics::new(
4031            "session_close_for_each_concurrent",
4032            module_path!(),
4033            file!(),
4034            line!(),
4035        );
4036        let ah_closure_notifications = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable_named!(
4037            "session_close_notifications",
4038            session_close_rx.into_stream().for_each_concurrent(
4039                self.cfg.maximum_sessions + 10,
4040                move |(session_id, closure_reason)| {
4041                    let myself = myself.clone();
4042                    let closure_diag = closure_diag.clone();
4043                    closure_diag.wrap(|| {
4044                        // These notifications come from the Sessions themselves once
4045                        // an empty read is encountered, which means the closure was done by the
4046                        // other party.
4047                        //
4048                        // Routed through `close_session_with_reason` rather than removing the slot
4049                        // here, so that this path — the one an Exit-side session server actually
4050                        // closes on — can answer with a SURB drain like every other. Identical
4051                        // behaviour when it does not.
4052                        if !myself.close_session_with_reason(&session_id, closure_reason) {
4053                            // Do not treat this as an error
4054                            debug!(
4055                                ?session_id,
4056                                ?closure_reason,
4057                                "could not find session id to close, maybe the session is already closed"
4058                            );
4059                        }
4060                        futures::future::ready(())
4061                    })
4062                }
4063            )
4064        );
4065
4066        // This is necessary to evict expired entries from the caches if
4067        // no session-related operations happen at all.
4068        // This ensures the dangling expired sessions are properly closed
4069        // and their closure is timely notified to the other party.
4070        let myself = self.clone();
4071        let ah_session_expiration = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
4072            let jitter = hopr_api::types::crypto_random::random_float_in_range(1.0..1.5);
4073            let timeout = 2 * initiation_timeout_max_one_way(
4074                myself.cfg.initiation_timeout_base,
4075                RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS,
4076            )
4077            .min(myself.cfg.idle_timeout)
4078            .mul_f64(jitter)
4079                / 2;
4080            futures_time::stream::interval(timeout.into())
4081                .for_each(|_| async {
4082                    trace!("executing session cache evictions");
4083                    myself.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
4084                    myself.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
4085                })
4086                .await;
4087        });
4088
4089        // Begin processing of Start protocol messages
4090        let myself = self.clone();
4091        let ah_start_protocol = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable_named!(
4092            "session_start_protocol_processor",
4093            start_protocol_rx.into_stream().for_each_concurrent(
4094                Some(self.cfg.maximum_sessions + 10),
4095                move |(pseudonym, protocol_msg, packet_info, stored)| {
4096                    let myself = myself.clone();
4097                    async move {
4098                        let result = match protocol_msg {
4099                            HoprStartProtocol::StartSession(session_req) => {
4100                                match myself
4101                                    .refuse_pix_over_direct_return_path(
4102                                        pseudonym,
4103                                        &session_req,
4104                                        packet_info.min_return_path_hops,
4105                                    )
4106                                    .await
4107                                {
4108                                    Ok(false) => {
4109                                        let opened =
4110                                            myself.handle_incoming_session_initiation(pseudonym, session_req).await;
4111                                        // The opening's SURBs are in the pseudonym's ring already, promoted
4112                                        // into the admitted class with it, but arrived before the Session
4113                                        // existed, so dispatch could not book them. Without them the Exit's
4114                                        // estimate starts, and stays, below what the ring holds. What the
4115                                        // ring lost as they arrived is not this Session's to book: its
4116                                        // estimate never counted that stock, which a newer generation
4117                                        // superseded from an earlier Session under the pseudonym, and an
4118                                        // opening's few SURBs do not overflow a ring on their own.
4119                                        if opened.is_ok()
4120                                            && let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.get(&pseudonym)
4121                                        {
4122                                            let _ = book_start_message_surbs(
4123                                                &slot,
4124                                                &pseudonym,
4125                                                SurbsStored { evicted: 0, ..stored },
4126                                            );
4127                                        }
4128                                        opened
4129                                    }
4130                                    refused => refused.map(|_| ()),
4131                                }
4132                            }
4133                            HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(est) => myself.handle_session_established(est).await,
4134                            HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(error_type) => {
4135                                myself.handle_session_error(pseudonym, error_type).await
4136                            }
4137                            HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(msg) => myself.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, msg).await,
4138                            HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(client_commit_msg) => {
4139                                myself.handle_ssa_commit(pseudonym, client_commit_msg).await
4140                            }
4141                            HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(server_commit_msg) => {
4142                                myself.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, server_commit_msg).await
4143                            }
4144                        };
4145
4146                        match result {
4147                            Ok(()) => {}
4148                            // Dropped on purpose and not a fault: the request lock, the successor
4149                            // gate (early or under-served), the stale-index check and a repeat whose
4150                            // interrupted publication could not be finished all refuse this way. The
4151                            // handler has already logged the first occurrence of a gate or stale
4152                            // refusal at the level it deserves, and the peer re-asks — which can
4153                            // succeed for all of them but a stale request.
4154                            Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(reason))) => {
4155                                tracing::debug!(%reason, "Start protocol message not admitted");
4156                            }
4157                            Err(error) => tracing::error!(%error, "failed to process Start protocol message"),
4158                        }
4159                    }
4160                }
4161            )
4162        );
4163
4164        Ok(vec![ah_closure_notifications, ah_session_expiration, ah_start_protocol])
4165    }
4166
4167    /// Check if [`start`](SessionManager::start) has been called and the instance is running.
4168    pub fn is_started(&self) -> bool {
4169        self.session_notifiers.get().is_some()
4170    }
4171
4172    /// Installs the SURB-store admission seam this manager calls at Session establishment and
4173    /// teardown.
4174    ///
4175    /// Late-injected through a `OnceLock` for the same reason `msg_sender` and `admission_tx` are:
4176    /// the only in-tree implementation wraps the SURB store, which the composition root builds
4177    /// alongside — but never inside — this crate. `false` means a controller was already installed,
4178    /// which no in-tree caller can produce (it installs exactly one, right after construction) and
4179    /// is reported rather than ignored so a double-wired node is visible at the call site.
4180    ///
4181    /// Leaving it unset is *functional*, not fatal: the manager then never admits, and every
4182    /// Session's SURBs land in the store's quarantine class. That failure mode is what the store's
4183    /// admission counters exist to surface, which is why this does not fall back to a no-op
4184    /// controller that would hide the absence.
4185    pub fn set_surb_admission(&self, ctl: Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>) -> bool {
4186        self.surb_admission.set(ctl).is_ok()
4187    }
4188
4189    /// Atomically allocates a new [`SessionSlot`] for `session_id` and returns an RAII
4190    /// [`SessionSlotGuard`] for it.
4191    ///
4192    /// Establishing a session involves several fallible steps *after* the slot has been
4193    /// inserted. The returned guard rolls the slot back - tearing the partially
4194    /// established session down via [`close_session`] - unless it is
4195    /// [committed](SessionSlotGuard::commit).
4196    ///
4197    /// The active-sessions gauge is incremented here, atomically with the insertion and
4198    /// the guard creation, precisely so that it is always paired with the guard's
4199    /// rollback decrement (performed through [`close_session`]). This keeps the gauge
4200    /// accurate: it is never decremented for a slot that was not counted in the first
4201    /// place, and every counted slot is decremented exactly once when it leaves the cache.
4202    ///
4203    /// Returns `None` if a slot for `session_id` already exists; in that case nothing is
4204    /// inserted, the gauge is left untouched, and no guard is produced. The atomic `entry`
4205    /// API guarantees that only one concurrent caller can claim the slot for a given
4206    /// pseudonym (avoiding a TOCTOU race), which also rules out loopback sessions onto
4207    /// ourselves.
4208    ///
4209    /// Capacity is enforced by an atomic counter incremented *before* the cache insertion,
4210    /// making it impossible for two concurrent callers (with different session IDs) to both
4211    /// succeed when the cache is already at `maximum_sessions`.
4212    fn allocate_session_slot(&self, session_id: SessionId, slot: SessionSlot) -> Option<SessionSlotGuard<'_>> {
4213        // Try to claim a session slot before touching the cache. `fetch_update` atomically
4214        // increments only if the value is strictly below the limit, preventing two concurrent
4215        // callers from both succeeding when already at capacity.
4216        let counter = &self.active_sessions;
4217        #[allow(clippy::incompatible_msrv)]
4218        let did_reserve = counter
4219            .try_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |n| {
4220                (n < self.cfg.maximum_sessions).then_some(n + 1)
4221            })
4222            .is_ok();
4223
4224        if !did_reserve {
4225            return None;
4226        }
4227
4228        // Lift the slot's admission cell out before the slot is moved into the cache: the guard keeps
4229        // it so `commit_slot_guard` can recognise the cached slot as this establishment's own by cell
4230        // identity, even though the key it re-reads by is a reusable pseudonym.
4231        let admission_cell = slot.admission_token.clone();
4232
4233        let result =
4234            self.sessions
4235                .entry(session_id)
4236                .and_compute_with(|entry: Option<moka::Entry<SessionId, SessionSlot>>| {
4237                    if entry.is_none() {
4238                        moka::ops::compute::Op::Put(slot)
4239                    } else {
4240                        // Duplicate key — release the reservation so the counter stays accurate.
4241                        counter.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4242                        moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop
4243                    }
4244                });
4245
4246        match result {
4247            moka::ops::compute::CompResult::Inserted(_) => {
4248                // Notify any waiting message handler (e.g. handle_ssa_request) that the slot
4249                // is now available. Drain and signal the senders registered for this SessionId.
4250                if let Some(waiters) = self
4251                    .slot_allocated
4252                    .lock()
4253                    .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
4254                    .remove(&session_id)
4255                {
4256                    for w in waiters {
4257                        let _ = w.send(());
4258                    }
4259                }
4260                // take_guard borrows self, so the guard stores the counter and the admission seam
4261                // as clones rather than borrowing them.
4262                Some(SessionSlotGuard::new(
4263                    &self.sessions,
4264                    session_id,
4265                    counter.clone(),
4266                    self.surb_admission.clone(),
4267                    self.cfg.surb_resolution_wait,
4268                    admission_cell,
4269                ))
4270            }
4271            _ => None,
4272        }
4273    }
4274
4275    /// Initiates a new outgoing Session to `destination` with the given configuration.
4276    ///
4277    /// If the Session's counterparty does not respond within
4278    /// the [configured](SessionManagerConfig) period,
4279    /// this method returns [`TransportSessionError::Timeout`].
4280    ///
4281    /// It will also fail if the instance has not been [started](SessionManager::start).
4282    pub async fn new_session(
4283        &self,
4284        destination: Address,
4285        target: SessionTarget,
4286        cfg: SessionClientConfig,
4287    ) -> errors::Result<HoprSession> {
4288        self.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
4289        if self.cfg.maximum_sessions <= self.active_sessions.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
4290            return Err(SessionManagerError::TooManySessions.into());
4291        }
4292
4293        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
4294
4295        let (tx_initiation_done, rx_initiation_done): (
4296            crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::One<_>>,
4297            crossfire::AsyncRx<crossfire::mpsc::One<_>>,
4298        ) = crossfire::mpsc::build(crossfire::mpsc::One::new());
4299
4300        let current_ssa_state = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
4301
4302        let mut additional_data = 0_u64;
4303
4304        // SURB balancer target announcement is encoded in the lower 32-bits of the options word.
4305        //
4306        // Only a target this Entry actually balances toward is announced. An Entry without a SURB
4307        // balancer (`surb_management` is `None`, as for a hoprd `responseBuffer` below two packets)
4308        // announces none, on this branch as on the `NoRateControl` one, and sends no keep-alives to
4309        // announce one later. It used to announce the balancer-rate fallback instead (the initial
4310        // return egress rate times the minimum buffer duration, 50 at the defaults), which the Exit
4311        // cannot tell from a real target of 50: it admitted a ring of 75 SURBs for it, and nothing
4312        // ever widened that ring. A zero is what lets the Exit tell, and give such a Session the full
4313        // ring (see `ring_surb_target` in `handle_incoming_session_initiation`).
4314        //
4315        // The Exit still needs a figure for its own balancer and fill reserve, and now takes it from
4316        // its own configuration. The initial egress rate is a constant (10) in the transport, but the
4317        // minimum buffer duration is an operator setting (`balancer_minimum_surb_buffer_duration`,
4318        // 5 s by default), so the Entry's and the Exit's could differ, and the Exit never had a reason
4319        // to prefer the Entry's. An Exit that predates this takes the same fallback on a zero.
4320        if !cfg.capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl) {
4321            additional_data |= cfg
4322                .surb_management
4323                .map(|c| c.target_surb_buffer_size)
4324                .unwrap_or(0)
4325                .min(u32::MAX as u64);
4326        }
4327
4328        // PIX quota parameter announcement is encoded in the upper 32-bits of the options word.
4329        // Run these validations BEFORE reserving the initiation challenge slot so that a
4330        // repeated invalid request cannot exhaust all challenge slots.
4331        if cfg.capabilities.contains(Capability::UsePIX) {
4332            // PIX requires at least 1 intermediate hop on the return path so that PIX
4333            // shares can be encrypted with the first relayer's ticket-challenge solution
4334            // (`HalfKey`) and delivered via return-path SURBs. With 0 intermediate hops
4335            // (a direct Exit→Entry SURB), there is no relayer to provide the challenge
4336            // solution, so shares are never embedded — the ongoing PIX share delivery
4337            // mechanism is dead and the Exit's quota is never replenished.
4338            if cfg.return_path_options.count_hops() == 0 {
4339                return Err(SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow!(
4340                    "UsePIX requires at least 1 intermediate hop on the return path, got 0"
4341                ))
4342                .into());
4343            }
4344
4345            // Validate that PIX toolbox is available before advertising UsePIX
4346            let pix_toolbox = self
4347                .pix_toolbox
4348                .get()
4349                .ok_or_else(|| SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow!("UsePIX requested but no PIX toolbox installed")))?;
4350
4351            // The installed generator is what actually produces the shares that go on the wire, so
4352            // it — not the caller — is the source of the announced parameters. Letting a caller name
4353            // them instead would allow a Session to proceed while producing shares the Exit cannot
4354            // reconstruct, so the dimensions are not a per-Session choice at all: `UsePIX` is the
4355            // whole switch, and everything downstream (the per-SSA quota, and so the deposit amount
4356            // reported to the funding strategy in `AgreedSsaQuota`) is derived from what follows.
4357            // The same source for the dimensions and for the curve suite: `HoprPixSpec` is what the
4358            // installed generator is instantiated over, so the announced suite cannot disagree with
4359            // the one that will actually produce the shares.
4360            let gen_cfg = pix_toolbox.share_generator.config();
4361            let params = PixParams::try_from_config::<HoprPixSpec>(gen_cfg)
4362                .map_err(|error| SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow!("invalid PIX dimensions: {error}")))?;
4363
4364            let _ = current_ssa_state.set(SessionSsaState::new(params));
4365            additional_data = params.into_additional_data(additional_data as u32);
4366        }
4367
4368        let (challenge, _) = insert_into_next_slot(
4369            &self.session_initiations,
4370            |ch| {
4371                if let Some(challenge) = ch {
4372                    ((challenge + 1) % hopr_api::types::crypto_random::MAX_RANDOM_INTEGER).max(MIN_CHALLENGE)
4373                } else {
4374                    hopr_api::types::crypto_random::random_integer(MIN_CHALLENGE, None)
4375                }
4376            },
4377            |_| tx_initiation_done,
4378            Some(self.cfg.maximum_sessions as u64),
4379        )
4380        .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NoChallengeSlots)?; // almost impossible with u64
4381
4382        // Prepare the session initiation message in the Start protocol
4383        trace!(challenge, ?cfg, "initiating session with config");
4384        let start_session_msg = HoprStartProtocol::StartSession(StartInitiation {
4385            challenge,
4386            target,
4387            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(cfg.capabilities),
4388            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(additional_data),
4389        });
4390
4391        let pseudonym = cfg.pseudonym.unwrap_or(HoprPseudonym::random());
4392        // Atomically claim the pseudonym in `pending_outgoing` before the initiation is sent so
4393        // that a fast Exit's `SsaRequest` — which names the Session by this pseudonym, not by the
4394        // challenge — finds it at dispatch. The guard removes it on every path below that does not
4395        // reach `drop(_pending_guard)`: each early return, a dropped future, and the two
4396        // `allocate_session_slot` failures, which are keyed by the peer-supplied `session_id` and
4397        // so cannot clear it themselves.
4398        //
4399        // The claim, not a plain `insert`, because `moka`'s `insert` would silently overwrite an
4400        // existing reservation: two concurrent `new_session` calls under the same explicit
4401        // pseudonym would both hold a guard over one shared marker, and the first one to finish
4402        // would clear it while the other is still in flight — an `SsaRequest` for that initiation
4403        // would then fail the dispatch filter and be dropped as `StaleStartMessage`. Refusing the
4404        // overlapping initiation instead keeps each marker owned by exactly one attempt.
4405        //
4406        // The claim happens AFTER the challenge reservation above, so a failed claim must also
4407        // release that reservation: it was taken for an initiation that never starts, and leaving
4408        // it would shrink the initiation window for every later attempt.
4409        let token = PendingOutgoingToken::next();
4410        let claim_result = self.pending_outgoing.entry(pseudonym).and_compute_with(
4411            |entry: Option<moka::Entry<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>>| {
4412                if entry.is_none() {
4413                    moka::ops::compute::Op::Put(token)
4414                } else {
4415                    // Another initiation already holds this pseudonym.
4416                    moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop
4417                }
4418            },
4419        );
4420        if !matches!(claim_result, moka::ops::compute::CompResult::Inserted(_)) {
4421            self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge);
4422            return Err(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
4423                "an outgoing Session initiation under pseudonym {pseudonym} is already in flight"
4424            ))
4425            .into());
4426        }
4427        let _pending_guard = PendingOutgoingGuard {
4428            pending: &self.pending_outgoing,
4429            pseudonym,
4430            token,
4431        };
4432        let forward_routing = DestinationRouting::Forward {
4433            destination: Box::new(destination.into()),
4434            pseudonym: Some(pseudonym), // Session must use a fixed pseudonym already
4435            forward_options: cfg.forward_path_options.clone(),
4436            return_options: cfg.return_path_options.clone().into(),
4437        };
4438
4439        // Send the Session initiation message
4440        info!(challenge, %pseudonym, %destination, "new session request");
4441        send_via_msg_sender(
4442            &mut msg_sender,
4443            forward_routing.clone(),
4444            start_session_msg,
4445            "session request message",
4446        )
4447        .await
4448        .map_err(|error| {
4449            self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge);
4450            TransportSessionError::packet_sending(error)
4451        })?;
4452
4453        // The timeout is given by the number of hops requested
4454        let initiation_timeout: futures_time::time::Duration = initiation_timeout_max_one_way(
4455            self.cfg.initiation_timeout_base,
4456            cfg.forward_path_options.count_hops() + cfg.return_path_options.count_hops() + 2,
4457        )
4458        .into();
4459
4460        // Await session establishment response from the Exit node or timeout
4461
4462        trace!(challenge, "awaiting session establishment");
4463        match rx_initiation_done
4464            .into_stream()
4465            .try_next()
4466            .timeout(initiation_timeout)
4467            .await
4468        {
4469            Ok(Ok(Some(est))) => {
4470                // Session has been established, construct it
4471                let session_id = est.session_id;
4472                debug!(challenge = est.orig_challenge, ?session_id, "started a new session");
4473
4474                let (session_tx, session_rx) =
4475                    crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(self.cfg.session_forward_capacity);
4476                let (session_rx, session_rx_ah) = hopr_utils::runtime::DropAbortable::new(session_rx.into_stream());
4477
4478                let mut abort_handles = AbortableList::default();
4479                abort_handles.insert(SessionHandles::Ingress, session_rx_ah);
4480
4481                let notifier = self
4482                    .session_notifiers
4483                    .get()
4484                    .map(|(_, notifier)| {
4485                        let notifier = notifier.clone();
4486                        Box::new(move |session_id: SessionId, reason: ClosureReason| {
4487                            let _ = notifier
4488                                .try_send((session_id, reason))
4489                                .inspect_err(|error| error!(%session_id, %error, "failed to notify session closure"));
4490                        })
4491                    })
4492                    .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
4493
4494                // NOTE: the Exit node can have different `max_surb_buffer_size`
4495                // setting on the Session manager, so it does not make sense to cap it here
4496                // with our maximum value.
4497                if let Some(balancer_config) = cfg.surb_management {
4498                    let surb_estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
4499                    let surbs_per_keep_alive = KeepAliveMessage::from(session_id).max_surbs()? as u32;
4500
4501                    // Sender responsible for keep-alive and Session data will be counting produced SURBs
4502                    let surb_estimator_clone = surb_estimator.clone();
4503                    let full_surb_scoring_sender =
4504                        msg_sender.with(move |(routing, data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
4505                            let produced = data.estimate_surbs_with_msg() as u64;
4506                            // Count how many SURBs we sent with each packet
4507                            surb_estimator_clone
4508                                .produced
4509                                .fetch_add(produced, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4510                            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
4511                            telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(&session_id, produced);
4512                            futures::future::ok::<_, S::Error>((routing, data))
4513                        });
4514
4515                    let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::from(balancer_config));
4516                    // The counterparty's store is the same bounded ring buffer as ours, so its
4517                    // capacity bounds what our `produced - consumed` estimate can legitimately
4518                    // claim it is holding.
4519                    surb_mgmt.set_counterparty_buffer_capacity(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64);
4520
4521                    // For standard Session data we first reduce the number of SURBs we want to produce,
4522                    // unless requested to always max them out
4523                    let max_surbs_in_packet = cfg.max_surbs_per_data_packet;
4524                    let surb_mgmt_for_tx = surb_mgmt.clone();
4525                    let reduced_surb_scoring_sender = full_surb_scoring_sender.clone().with(
4526                        // NOTE: this is put in-front of the `full_surb_scoring_sender`,
4527                        // so that its estimate of SURBs gets automatically updated based on
4528                        // the `max_surbs_in_packets` set here.
4529                        move |(routing, mut data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
4530                            cap_organic_surbs(&mut data, max_surbs_in_packet, &surb_mgmt_for_tx);
4531                            futures::future::ok::<_, S::Error>((routing, data))
4532                        },
4533                    );
4534
4535                    // Spawn the SURB-bearing keep alive stream towards the Exit. Suspended until the
4536                    // balancer below gives the controller a rate.
4537                    let ka_controller = RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1));
4538                    let ka_abort_handle = utils::spawn_keep_alive_stream(
4539                        session_id,
4540                        full_surb_scoring_sender,
4541                        forward_routing.clone(),
4542                        if self.cfg.surb_target_notify {
4543                            SurbNotificationMode::Target
4544                        } else {
4545                            SurbNotificationMode::DoNotNotify
4546                        },
4547                        surb_mgmt.clone(),
4548                        &ka_controller,
4549                        // The Entry's balancer owns this stream outright and there is no second
4550                        // producer to arbitrate between, so every packet the rate limiter releases is
4551                        // one the balancer asked for.
4552                        || true,
4553                    );
4554                    abort_handles.insert(SessionHandles::KeepAlive, ka_abort_handle);
4555
4556                    // The Exit holds nothing yet, which is the state a wipe leaves it in: pace the
4557                    // first fill like the refill after one, or the PID commands its ceiling from the
4558                    // first tick and the flood loses the replies the verdicts are made of. The target
4559                    // is set from the configuration here, so this is the point it first is non-zero;
4560                    // the `BalancerTarget` keep-alive path is the Exit receiving the Entry's target,
4561                    // and does not arm anything.
4562                    // At least one keep-alive a second, so that a small target is not filled a SURB or
4563                    // two at a time and the Session left waiting for its first keep-alive.
4564                    surb_mgmt.set_pacing_floor(u64::from(surbs_per_keep_alive));
4565                    surb_mgmt.arm_refill_pacing();
4566
4567                    // Spawn the SURB balancer, which will decide on the initial SURB rate.
4568                    debug!(%session_id, ?balancer_config ,"spawning entry SURB balancer");
4569                    let balancer = SurbBalancer::new(
4570                        session_id,
4571                        // The setpoint and output limit is immediately reconfigured by the SurbBalancer
4572                        PidBalancerController::from_gains(PidControllerGains::from_env_or_default()),
4573                        surb_estimator.clone(),
4574                        // Convert the requested SURB rate to packets using the keep-alive's capacity.
4575                        SurbControllerWithCorrection(ka_controller, surbs_per_keep_alive),
4576                        surb_mgmt.clone(),
4577                    );
4578
4579                    let (level_stream, balancer_abort_handle) =
4580                        balancer.start_control_loop(self.cfg.balancer_sampling_interval);
4581                    abort_handles.insert(SessionHandles::Balancer, balancer_abort_handle);
4582
4583                    let returned_packets = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0));
4584
4585                    // Insert the slot before the SURB readiness wait so any echo packets that
4586                    // arrive during pre-loading are accepted rather than dropped as unknown.
4587                    // Early return from the wait below drops slot_guard uncommitted, which removes
4588                    // the slot and calls close_session → abort_all() on the spawned tasks.
4589                    let mut slot_guard = self
4590                        .allocate_session_slot(
4591                            session_id,
4592                            SessionSlot {
4593                                session_tx,
4594                                routing_opts: forward_routing.clone(),
4595                                abort_handles: Arc::new(parking_lot::Mutex::new(abort_handles)),
4596                                surb_mgmt: surb_mgmt.clone(),
4597                                surb_estimator: surb_estimator.clone(),
4598                                current_ssa_state,
4599                                // Entry side: the Exit is authoritative for the PIX lifecycle, so
4600                                // there is no supervisor here and nothing gates egress.
4601                                pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
4602                                pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
4603                                pix_fill: Default::default(),
4604                                returned_packets: returned_packets.clone(),
4605                                // Nor does it hold reconstructor state: the live-cycle budget is
4606                                // charged by the side that reconstructs.
4607                                cycle_budget: None,
4608                                admission_token: Default::default(),
4609                                raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
4610                            },
4611                        )
4612                        .ok_or_else(|| {
4613                            // Session already exists; it means it is most likely a loopback attempt
4614                            error!(%session_id, "session already exists - loopback attempt");
4615                            // The slot will never exist for this pseudonym, so the pending-initiation
4616                            // marker must not outlive this attempt: leaving it would let later
4617                            // `SsaRequest`s for it pass the dispatch filter and park a handler waiting
4618                            // on a slot that never arrives. Dropped on the way out of the closure, the
4619                            // guard removes the marker keyed by the pseudonym it was inserted under.
4620                            SessionManagerError::Loopback
4621                        })?;
4622
4623                    // The slot now exists, so inbound traffic for this Session passes the dispatch
4624                    // filter on the session registry alone; the pending-initiation marker has served
4625                    // its purpose. Cleared here, before the SURB readiness wait below, which can take
4626                    // seconds, rather than after it.
4627                    drop(_pending_guard);
4628
4629                    // Prevent the slot from being evicted by time_to_idle while SURBs are
4630                    // pre-loading. Each `get()` call resets the idle timer; the task is
4631                    // aborted as soon as the readiness wait resolves.
4632                    let sessions_keepalive = self.sessions.clone();
4633                    let touch_period = (self.cfg.idle_timeout / 2).max(self.cfg.min_session_touch_period);
4634                    let slot_keepalive = hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::spawn(async move {
4635                        loop {
4636                            hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(touch_period).await;
4637                            let _ = sessions_keepalive.get(&session_id);
4638                        }
4639                    });
4640
4641                    // The session is ready once a quarter of the target is believed to be at the
4642                    // counterparty: that is the point the first replies can come home, and a quarter of
4643                    // the target is already several seconds of replies at any rate the balancer sustains.
4644                    // The first fill is paced at a fifth of the target a second, so this arrives after
4645                    // about 1.25 s whatever the target, where half the target took about 2.5 s.
4646                    //
4647                    // TODO: consider making this interactive = other party reports the exact level periodically
4648                    let wait_result = level_stream
4649                        .skip_while(|current_level| {
4650                            futures::future::ready(*current_level < balancer_config.target_surb_buffer_size / 4)
4651                        })
4652                        .next()
4653                        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(SESSION_READINESS_TIMEOUT))
4654                        .await;
4655                    slot_keepalive.abort();
4656                    match wait_result {
4657                        Ok(Some(surb_level)) => {
4658                            info!(%session_id, surb_level, "session is ready");
4659                        }
4660                        Ok(None) => {
4661                            return Err(
4662                                SessionManagerError::other(anyhow!("surb balancer was cancelled prematurely")).into(),
4663                            );
4664                        }
4665                        Err(_) => {
4666                            warn!(%session_id, "session didn't reach target SURB buffer size in time");
4667                        }
4668                    }
4669
4670                    #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
4671                    METRIC_NUM_INITIATED_SESSIONS.increment();
4672
4673                    let surb_estimator_for_rx = surb_estimator.clone();
4674                    let session = HoprSession::new_with_surb_state(
4675                        session_id,
4676                        forward_routing,
4677                        session_config_with(&self.cfg, cfg.capabilities, cfg.max_frames_behind_gap),
4678                        (
4679                            reduced_surb_scoring_sender,
4680                            session_rx.inspect(move |_| {
4681                                // The Exit's SURB signals are recorded in `dispatch_message`, upstream
4682                                // of this: they override the organic SURB gate, and a packet dropped
4683                                // before it reaches here would take the override with it.
4684
4685                                // Received packets = SURB consumption estimate
4686                                // The received packets always consume a single SURB.
4687                                surb_estimator_for_rx
4688                                    .consumed
4689                                    .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4690                                // Same event, separate counter, on purpose — see `returned_packets`.
4691                                returned_packets.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4692                                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
4693                                telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
4694                            }),
4695                        ),
4696                        Some(notifier),
4697                        // Entry (sending) side: give flow control the SURB balancer state as its
4698                        // anti-grief down-only ceiling, and the client's opt-in flow-control config.
4699                        Some(surb_mgmt.clone()),
4700                        cfg.flow_control,
4701                    )?;
4702
4703                    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
4704                    initialize_session_telemetry(
4705                        session_id,
4706                        &self.cfg,
4707                        cfg.capabilities,
4708                        Some(&surb_estimator),
4709                        Some(&surb_mgmt),
4710                    );
4711
4712                    // Admitted at the established point, not at allocation: this is the first moment
4713                    // the Session exists on our terms. `maximum_surb_buffer_size` is what this Entry
4714                    // announced as its target, so the store sizes the ring off the buffer we
4715                    // actually intend to fill.
4716                    commit_slot_guard(
4717                        &mut slot_guard,
4718                        &self.sessions,
4719                        session_id,
4720                        self.surb_admission.clone(),
4721                        self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size,
4722                    );
4723                    Ok(session)
4724                } else {
4725                    // Routine for short-lived sessions (health checks, bridges); not a fault.
4726                    tracing::debug!(%session_id, "session ready without SURB balancing");
4727
4728                    // Counted here too, unlike `surb_estimator`: the PIX successor gate reads this,
4729                    // and a knob that binds on some Sessions and not others is how a deposit gate
4730                    // silently becomes a gate that never opens.
4731                    let returned_packets = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0));
4732                    let returned_packets_for_rx = returned_packets.clone();
4733
4734                    // Disabled SURB management: a default state has a zero target, which reads as
4735                    // `is_disabled()` and so caps organic SURBs at one per packet — this branch's
4736                    // behaviour, expressed through the same policy the balancing branch uses rather
4737                    // than restated as a literal below.
4738                    let surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues> = Default::default();
4739
4740                    // Insert the slot and obtain a guard that rolls it back if any
4741                    // subsequent setup step fails.
4742                    let mut slot_guard = self
4743                        .allocate_session_slot(
4744                            session_id,
4745                            SessionSlot {
4746                                session_tx,
4747                                routing_opts: forward_routing.clone(),
4748                                abort_handles: Arc::new(parking_lot::Mutex::new(abort_handles)),
4749                                surb_mgmt: surb_mgmt.clone(),
4750                                surb_estimator: Default::default(), // No SURB estimator needed
4751                                current_ssa_state,
4752                                // Entry side: the Exit is authoritative for the PIX lifecycle.
4753                                pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
4754                                pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
4755                                pix_fill: Default::default(),
4756                                returned_packets,
4757                                // Nor does it hold reconstructor state: the live-cycle budget is
4758                                // charged by the side that reconstructs.
4759                                cycle_budget: None,
4760                                admission_token: Default::default(),
4761                                raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
4762                            },
4763                        )
4764                        .ok_or_else(|| {
4765                            // Session already exists; it means it is most likely a loopback attempt
4766                            error!(%session_id, "session already exists - loopback attempt");
4767                            // The slot will never exist for this pseudonym, so the pending-initiation
4768                            // marker must not outlive this attempt: leaving it would let later
4769                            // `SsaRequest`s for it pass the dispatch filter and park a handler waiting
4770                            // on a slot that never arrives. Dropped on the way out of the closure, the
4771                            // guard removes the marker keyed by the pseudonym it was inserted under.
4772                            SessionManagerError::Loopback
4773                        })?;
4774
4775                    // The slot now exists, so inbound traffic for this Session passes the dispatch
4776                    // filter on the session registry alone; the pending-initiation marker has served
4777                    // its purpose.
4778                    drop(_pending_guard);
4779
4780                    #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
4781                    METRIC_NUM_INITIATED_SESSIONS.increment();
4782
4783                    // For standard Session data we first reduce the number of SURBs we want to produce,
4784                    // unless requested to always max them out
4785                    let max_surbs_in_packet = cfg.max_surbs_per_data_packet;
4786                    let surb_mgmt_for_tx = surb_mgmt.clone();
4787                    let reduced_surb_sender =
4788                        msg_sender.with(move |(routing, mut data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
4789                            cap_organic_surbs(&mut data, max_surbs_in_packet, &surb_mgmt_for_tx);
4790                            futures::future::ok::<_, S::Error>((routing, data))
4791                        });
4792
4793                    let session = HoprSession::new(
4794                        session_id,
4795                        forward_routing,
4796                        session_config_with(&self.cfg, cfg.capabilities, cfg.max_frames_behind_gap),
4797                        (
4798                            reduced_surb_sender,
4799                            session_rx.inspect(move |_| {
4800                                returned_packets_for_rx.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4801                            }),
4802                        ),
4803                        Some(notifier),
4804                    )?;
4805
4806                    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
4807                    initialize_session_telemetry(session_id, &self.cfg, cfg.capabilities, None, None);
4808
4809                    // Same admission point as the balanced branch above, with the same announced
4810                    // target: a Session without SURB balancing still holds a return path worth
4811                    // protecting.
4812                    commit_slot_guard(
4813                        &mut slot_guard,
4814                        &self.sessions,
4815                        session_id,
4816                        self.surb_admission.clone(),
4817                        self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size,
4818                    );
4819                    Ok(session)
4820                }
4821            }
4822            Ok(Ok(None)) => {
4823                self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge);
4824                Err(SessionManagerError::other(anyhow!(
4825                    "internal error: sender has been closed without completing the session establishment"
4826                ))
4827                .into())
4828            }
4829            Ok(Err(error)) => {
4830                // The other side did not allow us to establish a session
4831                let challenge = match error.identifier {
4832                    ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(c) => c,
4833                    ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(_) => {
4834                        // This arm should only ever receive pre-establishment errors.
4835                        // Log the id if it matters for debugging.
4836                        0
4837                    }
4838                };
4839                error!(
4840                    %challenge, ?error,
4841                    "the other party rejected the session initiation with error"
4842                );
4843                // A rejected initiation can never become a Session, so nothing legitimate can name
4844                // its pseudonym any more. `handle_session_error` removes the *challenge*, but only
4845                // this call knows the pseudonym the rejection was made under — which the guard
4846                // removes here.
4847                Err(TransportSessionError::Rejected(error.reason))
4848            }
4849            Err(_) => {
4850                // Timeout waiting for a session establishment
4851                error!(challenge, "session initiation attempt timed out");
4852
4853                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
4854                METRIC_RECEIVED_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&["timeout"]);
4855
4856                self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge);
4857                Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)
4858            }
4859        }
4860    }
4861
4862    /// Sends a keep-alive packet with the given [`SessionId`].
4863    ///
4864    /// This currently "fires & forgets" and does not expect nor await any "pong" response.
4865    ///
4866    /// The keep-alive is marked as a manual ping ([`KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing`]), so an Exit does not
4867    /// take it for a sign that this Session's Entry runs a SURB balancer: a ping, whatever SURBs it
4868    /// brings, starts neither the Exit's SURB-level reports nor the reserve it keeps for them. An Exit
4869    /// that predates the mark does take it for one.
4870    pub async fn ping_session(&self, id: &SessionId) -> errors::Result<()> {
4871        if let Some(session_data) = self.sessions.get(id) {
4872            trace!(session_id = ?id, "pinging manually session");
4873            let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
4874            send_via_msg_sender(
4875                &mut msg_sender,
4876                session_data.routing_opts.clone(),
4877                HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
4878                    session_id: *id,
4879                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing.into(),
4880                    additional_data: 0,
4881                }),
4882                "session ping message",
4883            )
4884            .await
4885            .map_err(TransportSessionError::packet_sending)
4886        } else {
4887            Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into())
4888        }
4889    }
4890
4891    /// Asks the deposit pool for the data to attach to a batch of SSAs, and collects its answers.
4892    async fn request_deposit_data(
4893        pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
4894        session_id: SessionId,
4895        ssa_indices: &[SsaIndex],
4896    ) -> errors::Result<HoprPixDepositData> {
4897        let deposit_ids = ssa_indices
4898            .iter()
4899            .map(|&ssa_index| PixAddressId::new(&session_id, ssa_index))
4900            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
4901
4902        let (deposit_data_created, deposit_data_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(ssa_indices.len().max(1));
4903
4904        if pix_toolbox
4905            .pix_events
4906            .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositDataRequest(PixDepositDataRequest {
4907                deposit_ids,
4908                deposit_data_created,
4909            }))
4910            .is_err()
4911        {
4912            return Err(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(format!(
4913                "session {session_id} has no listener for the deposit data request"
4914            ))
4915            .into());
4916        }
4917
4918        let mut outstanding = ssa_indices
4919            .iter()
4920            .map(|&ssa_index| PixAddressId::new(&session_id, ssa_index))
4921            .collect::<std::collections::HashSet<_>>();
4922        let requested = outstanding.len();
4923
4924        let mut deposit_data = HoprPixDepositData::with_capacity(requested);
4925        {
4926            let replies = deposit_data_rx
4927                .take(2 * requested)
4928                .take_until(futures_time::task::sleep(futures_time::time::Duration::from(
4929                    DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
4930                )));
4931            futures::pin_mut!(replies);
4932            while let Some(entry) = replies.next().await {
4933                outstanding.remove(&entry.id);
4934                deposit_data.push(entry);
4935                if outstanding.is_empty() {
4936                    break;
4937                }
4938            }
4939        }
4940
4941        // Counted here rather than left to `deposit_data_for_batch`, which sees the same shortfall
4942        // but cannot tell a pool that went quiet from one that answered about the wrong SSAs. Both
4943        // are fatal; only one of them is fixed by making the pool faster.
4944        if !outstanding.is_empty() {
4945            return Err(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(format!(
4946                "session {session_id} got {} of {requested} requested deposit data entries within \
4947                 {DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT:?} ({} replies read in total)",
4948                requested - outstanding.len(),
4949                deposit_data.len(),
4950            ))
4951            .into());
4952        }
4953
4954        Ok(deposit_data)
4955    }
4956
4957    /// Spawns the task that carries out one Session's supervisor actions.
4958    ///
4959    /// The supervisor decides; this executes. Keeping the two apart is what lets the state machine
4960    /// be pure and exhaustively tested, and it means every side effect a PIX Session can have is
4961    /// visible in one `match`.
4962    ///
4963    /// The task owns an [`SsaCommitmentGuard`] per SSA it has requested and one Session retirement
4964    /// scope. Terminal actions retire through the frontier before releasing their guard; aborting
4965    /// the task drops every remaining guard and then the Session's compact frontier. No state grows
4966    /// with the number of cycles the Session completed.
4967    fn spawn_pix_action_driver(
4968        &self,
4969        session_id: SessionId,
4970        slot: &SessionSlot,
4971        action_rx: ActionRx,
4972        reply_routing: DestinationRouting,
4973    ) -> hopr_utils::runtime::AbortHandle {
4974        let myself = self.clone();
4975        let gate = slot
4976            .pix_egress_gate
4977            .get()
4978            .cloned()
4979            .expect("the gate is installed before the driver is spawned");
4980        let share_processor = self
4981            .pix_toolbox
4982            .get()
4983            .expect("the PIX toolbox is installed before a PIX action driver is spawned")
4984            .share_processor
4985            .clone();
4986        let retirement_scope = share_processor.begin_retirement_scope(session_id);
4987        // Captured rather than looked up per report: the lookup that finds a slot refreshes its idle
4988        // timer, and the one arm that must not do that is the re-send of an unanswered request.
4989        let supervisor = slot.pix_supervisor.get().cloned();
4990
4991        hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
4992            let _retirement_scope = retirement_scope;
4993            // The vector owns each registration until a terminal action explicitly retires it or
4994            // dropping this future releases it during whole-Session teardown.
4995            let mut owned_ssas: Vec<SsaCommitmentGuard<HoprPixSpec>> = Vec::new();
4996            // The batch most recently put on the wire, with the exact message that carried it.
4997            //
4998            // What `ResendSsaRequest` sends again. Kept rather than rebuilt because a rebuilt request is
4999            // not the same request: its Exit secrets are random, so it would commit the Exit to a
5000            // different set than the one registered, and the deposit pool answers a batch once. Only the
5001            // latest batch is kept — the supervisor re-sends only an unanswered one, and a batch is
5002            // requested only after the one before it has been answered. Dropped when a member is
5003            // retired, since a request for a registration that no longer exists can only be refused.
5004            let mut last_request: Option<LastSsaRequest> = None;
5005
5006            let close_reason = loop {
5007                let Ok(action) = action_rx.recv().await else {
5008                    // The worker is gone without having said why, which is a failure of the
5009                    // supervisor itself rather than of the Session it was watching.
5010                    break Some(SessionPixCloseReason::SupervisorUnavailable);
5011                };
5012
5013                match action {
5014                    SessionPixAction::RequestSsa { ssa_ids, params } => {
5015                        let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.get(&session_id) else {
5016                            // The Session went away underneath us; report the failure so the
5017                            // supervisor stops waiting on an action that can never complete.
5018                            myself
5019                                .report_ssa_request(
5020                                    &session_id,
5021                                    None,
5022                                    SessionPixAction::RequestSsa { ssa_ids, params },
5023                                    false,
5024                                )
5025                                .await;
5026                            continue;
5027                        };
5028                        match myself.send_ssa_request(session_id, &slot, &ssa_ids, params).await {
5029                            Ok((guards, request)) => {
5030                                owned_ssas.extend(guards);
5031                                last_request = Some((ssa_ids.clone(), request));
5032                                // One confirmation per index: the supervisor arms each cycle's
5033                                // commitment deadline on its own `SsaRequestSent`, and they were all
5034                                // put on the wire by the one send that just succeeded.
5035                                if let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get() {
5036                                    for ssa_id in &ssa_ids {
5037                                        if supervisor
5038                                            .send_event(SessionPixEvent::SsaRequestSent(*ssa_id))
5039                                            .await
5040                                            .is_err()
5041                                        {
5042                                            error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting events");
5043                                            break;
5044                                        }
5045                                    }
5046                                }
5047                            }
5048                            Err(error) => {
5049                                // Every guard was dropped by the early return inside
5050                                // `send_ssa_request`, so the whole batch of indices is released — none
5051                                // of them is left registered for a cycle that will never be asked for.
5052                                error!(
5053                                    %session_id, %error, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(),
5054                                    "failed to send ssa request"
5055                                );
5056
5057                                // A pool that could not supply deposit data ends the Session here
5058                                // rather than reporting the failure onwards. The other failures are
5059                                // transient or already self-correcting, and the supervisor is the
5060                                // right judge of them; this one is neither. The data only ever
5061                                // travels in the `SsaRequest` that carries the commitments, so it
5062                                // cannot be supplied later, and the pool will not answer a retry it
5063                                // did not answer the first time.
5064                                //
5065                                // Named rather than folded into the supervisor's `PixFailure`,
5066                                // because it points at this node's own pool while every reason the
5067                                // supervisor has points at the peer — and the Entry is told with a
5068                                // reason it can act on rather than the generic one.
5069                                if matches!(
5070                                    error,
5071                                    TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(_))
5072                                ) {
5073                                    myself.stop_pix_fill(&session_id);
5074                                    gate.poison();
5075                                    owned_ssas.clear();
5076                                    myself
5077                                        .notify_session_error(
5078                                            session_id,
5079                                            reply_routing.clone(),
5080                                            StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
5081                                            "session error due to missing deposit data",
5082                                        )
5083                                        .await;
5084                                    myself.close_session_with_reason(&session_id, ClosureReason::MissingDepositData);
5085                                    return;
5086                                }
5087
5088                                if let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get()
5089                                    && supervisor
5090                                        .send_action_result(
5091                                            // Only the discriminant and the ids are read on the
5092                                            // failure path, so the dimensions are echoed back
5093                                            // rather than zeroed — `PixParams` has no zero value,
5094                                            // and inventing one would be a lie about what was sent.
5095                                            SessionPixAction::RequestSsa { ssa_ids, params },
5096                                            false,
5097                                        )
5098                                        .await
5099                                        .is_err()
5100                                {
5101                                    error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting results");
5102                                }
5103                            }
5104                        }
5105                    }
5106                    SessionPixAction::RequestCommitmentRetransmission { ssa_id, params } => {
5107                        // Failure is logged and dropped rather than reported back. Unlike
5108                        // `RequestSsa` this action is not a step the Session depends on: it repeats
5109                        // on its own interval, and the commitment deadline is still the backstop, so
5110                        // a dropped ask costs one interval rather than the Session.
5111                        if let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.get(&session_id)
5112                            && let Err(error) = myself
5113                                .send_commitment_retransmission_request(session_id, &slot, ssa_id, params)
5114                                .await
5115                        {
5116                            error!(%session_id, %ssa_id, %error, "failed to re-request ssa commitment parts");
5117                        }
5118                    }
5119                    SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest { ssa_ids } => {
5120                        // `contains_key` rather than `get`, which would refresh the Session's idle
5121                        // timer: a Session that is otherwise dead would then be kept alive by its own
5122                        // re-sends for as long as the predecessor's clocks run. The routing needs no
5123                        // slot — it is the reply routing this driver was spawned with.
5124                        if !myself.sessions.contains_key(&session_id) {
5125                            continue;
5126                        }
5127
5128                        // Never `send_ssa_request`: it registers a fresh Exit commitment, which the
5129                        // reconstructor refuses as a duplicate of the pending one, and its failure
5130                        // path closes the Session as `SupervisorUnavailable`. A re-send is allowed to
5131                        // fail without costing the Session anything.
5132                        //
5133                        // Deciding also reads each member's registration, which is what keeps it from
5134                        // idling out after `incomplete_commitment_lifetime`: a pending registration
5135                        // is not refreshed by anything else while the Entry is silent. A batch that
5136                        // is not the last one sent, or whose registration is gone or complete, can
5137                        // only be refused, so it is not sent.
5138                        let message = match resend_payload(last_request.as_ref(), &ssa_ids, &share_processor) {
5139                            ResendDecision::Send(message) => message,
5140                            refusal => {
5141                                tracing::debug!(
5142                                    %session_id, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(), ?refusal,
5143                                    "cannot re-send the SSA request"
5144                                );
5145                                if let Some(supervisor) = supervisor.as_ref()
5146                                    && supervisor
5147                                        .send_action_result(SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest { ssa_ids }, false)
5148                                        .await
5149                                        .is_err()
5150                                {
5151                                    tracing::error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting results");
5152                                }
5153                                continue;
5154                            }
5155                        };
5156
5157                        // Failure is logged and dropped, as for the re-request above, and nothing is
5158                        // reported back: the supervisor pushed the batch's deadline when it emitted
5159                        // this and will emit another on its next tick. `SsaRequestSent` is not sent
5160                        // either — the batch was confirmed when it was first requested.
5161                        match myself.msg_sender.get().cloned() {
5162                            Some(mut msg_sender) => {
5163                                if let Err(error) = send_via_msg_sender(
5164                                    &mut msg_sender,
5165                                    reply_routing.clone(),
5166                                    message.clone(),
5167                                    "re-sent session SSA commitment request message",
5168                                )
5169                                .await
5170                                {
5171                                    tracing::error!(%session_id, %error, "failed to re-send the ssa request");
5172                                }
5173                            }
5174                            None => {
5175                                tracing::error!(%session_id, "cannot re-send the ssa request - manager not started")
5176                            }
5177                        }
5178                    }
5179                    SessionPixAction::ReleaseService => {
5180                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5181                        crate::telemetry::set_pix_gate_mode(&session_id, true);
5182                    }
5183                    SessionPixAction::WithholdService => {
5184                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5185                        crate::telemetry::set_pix_gate_mode(&session_id, false);
5186                    }
5187                    // Gate control is applied synchronously by the supervisor worker. The action
5188                    // reaches this I/O driver only to preserve observability and ordering, which
5189                    // makes it the one periodic point with the reconstructor in hand: refresh the
5190                    // node-wide occupancy gauge here. The walk covers every live cycle on the node and
5191                    // notifications come per acknowledgement batch per Session, so it runs at most once
5192                    // a second node-wide (`HELD_SHARES_REFRESH_PERIOD`), not on every notification.
5193                    // Progress behind the front asks for the same refresh, with nothing for the gate.
5194                    SessionPixAction::ProgressNotification | SessionPixAction::RefreshHeldShares =>
5195                    {
5196                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5197                        if crate::telemetry::pix::held_shares_refresh_due() {
5198                            crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
5199                        }
5200                    }
5201                    SessionPixAction::SetFillRate(rate) => {
5202                        // Looked up per action rather than captured, because the Session may already
5203                        // be gone: the supervisor plans against state it holds itself, and the slot
5204                        // can be evicted underneath it. A missing slot needs no rate — its stream is
5205                        // already aborted.
5206                        if let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.get(&session_id)
5207                            && let Some(fill) = slot.pix_fill.get()
5208                        {
5209                            fill.set_fill(rate);
5210                            // Inside the guard for the same reason the lookup is: `close_session`
5211                            // removes this Session's metric state and *then* aborts the tasks, and
5212                            // the abort is not synchronous, so a queued `SetFillRate` can still be
5213                            // processed afterwards. Setting the gauge there would re-create the
5214                            // `session_id` label series with nothing left to remove it again.
5215                            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5216                            crate::telemetry::set_pix_fill_rate(&session_id, rate.as_packets_per_sec());
5217                        }
5218                    }
5219                    SessionPixAction::RetireSsa(ssa_id) => {
5220                        share_processor.retire_ssa(ssa_id);
5221                        // The retired cycle's shares are gone, and nothing else refreshes the gauge
5222                        // until another notification comes due, which a node with no other PIX
5223                        // Session may never send. Retirement is once per cycle, so unthrottled.
5224                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5225                        crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
5226                        owned_ssas.retain(|guard| guard.ssa_id() != Some(&ssa_id));
5227                        forget_request_of(&mut last_request, &ssa_id);
5228                        if let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.get(&session_id) {
5229                            slot.abort_handles
5230                                .lock()
5231                                .abort_one(&SessionHandles::PixDepositObserver(ssa_id.ssa_index().get()));
5232                        }
5233                    }
5234                    SessionPixAction::Close(reason) => break Some(reason),
5235                }
5236            };
5237
5238            let Some(reason) = close_reason else {
5239                // The cycles this driver holds go with it; see the refresh after the teardown below.
5240                owned_ssas.clear();
5241                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5242                crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
5243                return;
5244            };
5245
5246            // Read before `stop_pix_fill`, which silences the stream either way. Keyed on the drain
5247            // rather than on the reason, which is a strict superset of it: a *stalled* drain closes
5248            // with `RecoveryIdle` or `RecoveryDeadline`, and that is likewise the ordinary end of a
5249            // Session an operator has already closed rather than something to page anyone about.
5250            let draining = myself
5251                .sessions
5252                .get(&session_id)
5253                .is_some_and(|slot| slot.pix_fill.get().is_some_and(|fill| fill.is_draining()));
5254            if draining {
5255                info!(%session_id, %reason, "pix supervisor ended the post-close SURB drain");
5256            } else {
5257                error!(%session_id, %reason, "pix supervisor closed the session");
5258            }
5259
5260            // Unblock anything parked on the gate before tearing down: the supervisor that would
5261            // have woken it is the thing that just stopped. Fill is silenced alongside it, and for a
5262            // sharper reason — the gate holds packets back, while fill would go on *originating*
5263            // them, return-routed to a pseudonym whose SURBs are about to be gone.
5264            myself.stop_pix_fill(&session_id);
5265            gate.poison();
5266            owned_ssas.clear();
5267            // Releasing the guards removed the Session's cycles from the reconstructor; refresh the
5268            // gauge now rather than leave their shares counted until another Session's notification.
5269            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5270            crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
5271
5272            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5273            crate::telemetry::pix::record_pix_closure(reason);
5274
5275            // Return this Session's share of the node-level aggregates now, rather than leaving it
5276            // to `close_session` below. The notification between here and there is a network send
5277            // with its own timeout, and for the whole of it the Session is closed — its supervisor
5278            // has stopped and its gate is poisoned — while `hopr_pix_sessions_active` would still
5279            // be counting it. Idempotent, so `close_session` remains the backstop for every other
5280            // path into it.
5281            if let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.get(&session_id)
5282                && let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get()
5283            {
5284                supervisor.telemetry.release();
5285            }
5286
5287            // Tell the Entry, so it can drop its side rather than wait out its own timeout. The
5288            // Session is closed either way, so a send failure here changes nothing.
5289            //
5290            // Except after a drain, where the Session the report would be about is already gone and
5291            // the report is return-routed: sending it would spend a SURB out of a buffer that may
5292            // already be empty, which is precisely the origination this whole path exists to avoid.
5293            // It would also be new behaviour rather than preserved behaviour, since an Exit-side
5294            // close sends the Entry nothing today — and `draining` is set before the supervisor's
5295            // verdict, so this covers a refused drain as well as a completed one.
5296            if !draining {
5297                myself.notify_pix_failure(session_id, reply_routing).await;
5298            }
5299
5300            if let Some(slot) = myself.sessions.remove(&session_id) {
5301                myself.active_sessions.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
5302                let token = slot.claim_admission_token();
5303                close_session(
5304                    session_id,
5305                    slot,
5306                    ClosureReason::PixFailure,
5307                    myself.surb_admission.get().cloned(),
5308                    surb_retire_grace(myself.cfg.surb_resolution_wait),
5309                    token,
5310                );
5311            }
5312        })
5313    }
5314
5315    /// Starts the Exit's single Exit → Entry keep-alive stream and installs the handle that steers it.
5316    ///
5317    /// Called for every PIX Session, and for any Session with a configured
5318    /// `surb_balance_notify_period` — the SURB-level notification and PIX fill are the same packet
5319    /// sent for different reasons, so they share one stream and one rate controller. See
5320    /// [`PixFillControl`].
5321    ///
5322    /// Returns without spawning anything when neither producer applies, which is an Exit Session that
5323    /// is not PIX on a node that has switched the notification off. Such a Session originates nothing,
