5324    /// which is what it did before this existed.
5325    ///
5326    /// The notification is not sent to just any Entry. A report spends one of the Session's SURBs, and
5327    /// an Entry with no SURB balancer reads nothing: it attaches a SURB to each data packet and sends
5328    /// no keep-alives. [`PixFillControl::admit`] therefore lets a report out only once the Entry has
5329    /// shown that it refills (by a keep-alive, flagged or not, but not a manual ping) and the Exit's own estimate shows
5330    /// a SURB to spend on it. That is decided per packet rather than here, once, because the evidence arrives
5331    /// after the Session is established.
5332    ///
5333    /// Deliberately not passed through the PIX egress gate. These packets carry no payload; gating
5334    /// them would let an exhausted predeposit budget silence the very signal the Entry needs in order
5335    /// to fund the Session, turning a stall into a teardown. The bound that does apply is
5336    /// [`PixFillControl::admit`]'s SURB reserve, which is about this node's own ability to send at
5337    /// all rather than about what the peer has paid for.
5338    ///
5339    /// `announced_surb_target` is the SURB buffer target the Entry asked for, and it is what that
5340    /// reserve is derived against — see [`effective_surb_reserve`]. It has to be, because the
5341    /// configured reserve is an absolute count while the buffer it is measured against is the Entry's
5342    /// choice; a Session whose Entry asks for a shallower buffer than the configured reserve could
5343    /// otherwise never be filled at all.
5344    fn spawn_exit_keep_alive(
5345        &self,
5346        session_id: SessionId,
5347        slot: &SessionSlot,
5348        msg_sender: S,
5349        is_pix: bool,
5350        announced_surb_target: u64,
5351    ) {
5352        let notify_period = self.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period;
5353        if notify_period.is_none() && !is_pix {
5354            return;
5355        }
5356
5357        let configured_reserve = self.cfg.pix_config.supervision.fill.min_surb_reserve;
5358        let min_surb_reserve = effective_surb_reserve(configured_reserve, announced_surb_target);
5359
5360        // Created here and shared: the sink wrapper below has to hold the same control the stream is
5361        // rate-limited by, so that it can tell a notification packet from a fill packet.
5362        let controller = RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1));
5363        let control = Arc::new(PixFillControl::new(
5364            session_id,
5365            controller.clone(),
5366            notify_period,
5367            min_surb_reserve,
5368            slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
5369            slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
5370        ));
5371
5372        let control_for_admission = control.clone();
5373        let surb_estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
5374        let ka_abort_handle = utils::spawn_keep_alive_stream(
5375            session_id,
5376            // Consumption is counted in the sink rather than at the rate limiter, so it counts what
5377            // was actually sent: a packet the admission predicate dropped consumed no SURB, and
5378            // counting it would walk the Exit's own level estimate down until it starved itself of
5379            // the very reserve that dropped it.
5380            msg_sender.with(move |(routing, data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
5381                let data = count_return_packet_surb(&surb_estimator, data);
5382                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5383                telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
5384                futures::future::ok::<_, S::Error>((routing, data))
5385            }),
5386            slot.routing_opts.clone(),
5387            SurbNotificationMode::Level(slot.surb_estimator.clone()),
5388            slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
5389            &controller,
5390            move || control_for_admission.admit(),
5391        );
5392
5393        slot.abort_handles
5394            .lock()
5395            .insert(SessionHandles::KeepAlive, ka_abort_handle);
5396        let _ = slot.pix_fill.set(control.clone());
5397
5398        if let Some(period) = notify_period {
5399            // Delayed by one period, as it always was: a Session that closes immediately should not
5400            // have sent a level report about SURBs it never used. Fill is not held behind this — the
5401            // supervisor's first rate applies the moment it is planned.
5402            //
5403            // Registered so `close_session` can abort it. It is a one-shot, but it holds a clone of
5404            // the control for the whole period, and nothing bounds how long an operator may make that.
5405            let notify_delay = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
5406                hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(period).await;
5407                control.start_notify();
5408            });
5409            slot.abort_handles
5410                .lock()
5411                .insert(SessionHandles::SurbNotifyDelay, notify_delay);
5412        }
5413
5414        // An order of magnitude is the point at which the operator's intent and the Session's shape
5415        // have stopped being about the same deployment. A configured reserve of `R` is a reserve
5416        // sized for a buffer of `4R`; the derivation only lowers it tenfold once the Entry announces
5417        // under `4R / 10`, so this fires exactly on a Session whose buffer is an order of magnitude
5418        // shallower than the one this node was configured against. Fill still runs — a derived
5419        // reserve is strictly better than one that refuses every packet forever — but it is worth
5420        // saying out loud once, when the stream starts, rather than once per withheld packet.
5421        if min_surb_reserve.saturating_mul(10) < configured_reserve {
5422            warn!(
5423                %session_id,
5424                configured = configured_reserve,
5425                effective = min_surb_reserve,
5426                announced_surb_target,
5427                "the PIX fill SURB reserve was lowered by more than an order of magnitude to fit the SURB buffer \
5428                 target the entry announced for this session"
5429            );
5430        }
5431
5432        debug!(
5433            %session_id, ?notify_period, is_pix,
5434            surb_reserve = min_surb_reserve,
5435            announced_surb_target,
5436            "started the exit keep-alive stream"
5437        );
5438    }
5439
5440    /// Silences a Session's PIX fill, leaving its SURB-level notification alone.
5441    ///
5442    /// Called on every path that is about to tear a Session down. `close_session` aborts the stream
5443    /// outright, so this is not what stops it — it is what stops the *extra* traffic in the window
5444    /// between a supervisor deciding the Session is over and the teardown reaching the stream. Every
5445    /// packet originated in that window is return-routed to a pseudonym whose SURBs are gone, and one
5446    /// packet the routing resolver cannot resolve holds up every packet this node originates.
5447    fn stop_pix_fill(&self, session_id: &SessionId) {
5448        if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(session_id)
5449            && let Some(fill) = slot.pix_fill.get()
5450        {
5451            fill.set_fill(FillRate::ZERO);
5452        }
5453    }
5454
5455    /// Reports an action outcome to a Session's supervisor, if it still has one.
5456    async fn report_ssa_request(
5457        &self,
5458        session_id: &SessionId,
5459        slot: Option<&SessionSlot>,
5460        action: SessionPixAction,
5461        ok: bool,
5462    ) {
5463        let slot = match slot {
5464            Some(slot) => Some(slot.clone()),
5465            None => self.sessions.get(session_id),
5466        };
5467        if let Some(slot) = slot
5468            && let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get()
5469            && supervisor.send_action_result(action, ok).await.is_err()
5470        {
5471            error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting results");
5472        }
5473    }
5474
5475    /// Best-effort `SessionError` for an already-established Session, identified by its `SessionId`.
5476    ///
5477    /// Best-effort in the strict sense: the outcome is logged and discarded. Every caller is on a path
5478    /// that has already decided the Session is over, so there is nothing a failed send could change —
5479    /// and the peer has a deadline of its own as the backstop either way. What the notice buys is
5480    /// promptness and attribution: the peer tears down in about a round trip, with the reason in its
5481    /// log, instead of waiting out a timer that names the timer rather than the cause.
5482    ///
5483    /// The peer's `handle_session_error` closes the Session on a `SessionId`-identified error and sends
5484    /// nothing back, so there is no error exchange to loop.
5485    async fn notify_session_error(
5486        &self,
5487        session_id: SessionId,
5488        routing: DestinationRouting,
5489        reason: StartErrorReason,
5490        context: &'static str,
5491    ) {
5492        let Some(mut msg_sender) = self.msg_sender.get().cloned() else {
5493            warn!(%session_id, %reason, context, "cannot send session error - manager not started");
5494            return;
5495        };
5496        match send_via_msg_sender(
5497            &mut msg_sender,
5498            routing,
5499            HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
5500                identifier: ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(session_id),
5501                reason,
5502            }),
5503            context,
5504        )
5505        .await
5506        {
5507            Ok(()) => {
5508                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
5509                METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
5510            }
5511            Err(error) => warn!(%session_id, %reason, %error, context, "failed to send session error"),
5512        }
5513    }
5514
5515    /// Best-effort notice to the Entry that this Session died for PIX reasons.
5516    async fn notify_pix_failure(&self, session_id: SessionId, reply_routing: DestinationRouting) {
5517        self.notify_session_error(
5518            session_id,
5519            reply_routing,
5520            StartErrorReason::Unknown,
5521            "session error after pix failure",
5522        )
5523        .await;
5524    }
5525
5526    /// Registers an Exit commitment for every index in `ssa_indices` and asks the Entry to commit to
5527    /// the matching SSAs — all in a single [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`].
5528    ///
5529    /// Driven by the supervisor's [`RequestSsa`](SessionPixAction::RequestSsa) action, which is what
5530    /// allocates the indices and fixes the dimensions — this only carries it out. Taking them as
5531    /// arguments rather than re-reading them from the slot keeps one source of truth for what was
5532    /// negotiated: the commitments registered here and the parameters the message advertises cannot
5533    /// disagree with what the supervisor is timing.
5534    ///
5535    /// One message for the whole batch, and one `params` field covering all of it, which is correct:
5536    /// every SSA in a Session uses the same negotiated dimensions. The Entry enforces its own ceiling
5537    /// on how many it will accept ([`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`]) and refuses an
5538    /// over-cap batch in full, so a batch larger than the peer allows loses the Session — see
5539    /// [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request).
5540    ///
5541    /// Installs no deadline of its own: every timeout that used to be armed here now belongs to the
5542    /// supervisor, which can see the whole cycle rather than just this one step.
5543    ///
5544    /// Returns the exact [`HoprStartProtocol`] message that went on the wire alongside the guards, so the
5545    /// caller can send *that* again for [`ResendSsaRequest`](SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest). A
5546    /// rebuilt request would not be the same one: the Exit secrets behind its commitments are random,
5547    /// and the deposit data is whatever the pool answered the first time. The message is cloned before
5548    /// it is sent, and its encoding is deterministic, so a repeat is byte-identical.
5549    ///
5550    /// The returned [`SsaCommitmentGuard`]s own their registrations until the caller transfers or drops
5551    /// them. Handing them out rather than retaining them here is what makes the failure path safe:
5552    /// this function has fallible steps after the registrations exist — including partway through the
5553    /// batch — and an early return from any of them releases every one of them. That matters more for
5554    /// a batch than for a single SSA: without it one failed send would strand every index it had
5555    /// registered, and since the supervisor does not reuse an index, the Session could never recover.
5556    async fn send_ssa_request(
5557        &self,
5558        session_id: SessionId,
5559        slot: &SessionSlot,
5560        ssa_ids: &[SsaId<HoprPseudonym>],
5561        params: PixParams,
5562    ) -> errors::Result<(Vec<SsaCommitmentGuard<HoprPixSpec>>, HoprStartProtocol)> {
5563        let Some(first_ssa_id) = ssa_ids.first().copied() else {
5564            return Err(SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow!("ssa request with no indices")).into());
5565        };
5566
5567        let pix_toolbox = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
5568        // Clone kept on this task: `pix_toolbox` itself is moved into the blocking commitment task,
5569        // while the deposit-data request below needs it here.
5570        let pix_toolbox_local = pix_toolbox.clone();
5571        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
5572
5573        // One blocking task for the whole batch rather than one per SSA: each commitment is a single
5574        // random scalar and one generator multiplication, so per-task overhead would dominate.
5575        let ids = ssa_ids.to_vec();
5576        let (exit_commitments, guards) = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
5577            move || {
5578                let mut commitments = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());
5579                let mut guards = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());
5580                for ssa_id in ids {
5581                    let (commitment, guard) = pix_toolbox
5582                        .share_processor
5583                        .new_guarded_exit_commitment(ssa_id, params)?;
5584                    commitments.push((ssa_id.ssa_index(), HoprPixGroupElement(commitment.to_bytes())));
5585                    guards.push(guard);
5586                }
5587                Ok::<_, hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError<HoprPseudonym>>((commitments, guards))
5588            },
5589            "server_ssa_commitment",
5590        )
5591        .await
5592        .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?
5593        .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)?;
5594
5595        info!(
5596            %session_id, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(), %params, %first_ssa_id,
5597            "generated exit commitments for the SSA batch"
5598        );
5599
5600        // Ask the deposit pool for the data to attach to this batch, and keep what it produced: the
5601        // Exit needs it twice. Once now, to put on the wire, and once per SSA later, to hand back to
5602        // the pool with the deposit address in `DepositNeeded` — by which point the batch it came
5603        // from is long gone.
5604        //
5605        // A pool that does not answer fails the batch here, which drops `guards` and releases every
5606        // registration it made. That is the only safe direction: deposit data reaches the Entry in
5607        // this message or not at all, so a batch sent without it buys service the Entry can never
5608        // pay for.
5609        let ssa_indices = ssa_ids.iter().map(|ssa_id| ssa_id.ssa_index()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
5610        let deposit_data = Self::request_deposit_data(&pix_toolbox_local, session_id, &ssa_indices).await?;
5611
5612        if !self.sessions.contains_key(&session_id) {
5613            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
5614        }
5615
5616        let deposit_data = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &ssa_indices, deposit_data)?;
5617        if let Some(ssa_state) = slot.current_ssa_state.get() {
5618            ssa_state.remember_sent_deposit_data(&deposit_data);
5619        }
5620
5621        // Construct and send the Exit SSA commitment request message.
5622        // The parameters were previously verified to be acceptable.
5623        let data = HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(
5624            session_id,
5625            params,
5626            exit_commitments,
5627            deposit_data,
5628        ));
5629
5630        send_via_msg_sender(
5631            &mut msg_sender,
5632            slot.routing_opts.clone(),
5633            data.clone(),
5634            "session SSA commitment request message",
5635        )
5636        .await
5637        .map_err(TransportSessionError::packet_sending)?;
5638
5639        Ok((guards, data))
5640    }
5641
5642    /// Asks the Entry to re-send the parts of one SSA's commitment that never arrived.
5643    ///
5644    /// The Entry's answer to an `SsaRequest` is hundreds of packets and the reconstructor can use
5645    /// none of it until every one has landed, so a single drop used to cost the Session on
5646    /// `max_ssa_delivery_time` — after the Entry had already been told to fund the cycle. This is the
5647    /// repair: the reconstructor says which polynomial runs are missing, and the Entry re-sends
5648    /// exactly those.
5649    ///
5650    /// Deliberately *not* built on [`send_ssa_request`](Self::send_ssa_request), whose every step is
5651    /// wrong here. It registers no Exit commitment — the cycle already has one, and registering a
5652    /// second for the same index is refused as a duplicate — allocates no index, and asks the deposit
5653    /// pool for nothing, since the deposit data of this cycle travelled with the request that created
5654    /// it. Nothing it does can earn the Entry a deposit, which is what makes it safe to repeat.
5655    ///
5656    /// The scope is read here rather than carried in the action: what is missing changes as the burst
5657    /// continues to arrive, and the freshest answer is both smaller and the one that converges.
5658    async fn send_commitment_retransmission_request(
5659        &self,
5660        session_id: SessionId,
5661        slot: &SessionSlot,
5662        ssa_id: SsaId<HoprPseudonym>,
5663        params: PixParams,
5664    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
5665        let pix_toolbox = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
5666        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
5667
5668        // Asked of the encoder, so the scope cannot be sized against a restated layout — see
5669        // `StartProtocol::max_missing_runs`.
5670        let max_runs = HoprStartProtocol::max_missing_runs(&session_id).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5671
5672        let Some(runs) = pix_toolbox.share_processor.missing_commitment_runs(&ssa_id, max_runs) else {
5673            // The registration is gone — retired, or expired after
5674            // `incomplete_commitment_lifetime` — so there is nothing left for a retransmission to
5675            // complete. The commitment deadline is what ends the Session; saying so here is the only
5676            // way an operator learns which of the two it was.
5677            warn!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "cannot re-request commitment parts for a cycle the reconstructor no longer holds");
5678            return Ok(());
5679        };
5680
5681        if runs.is_empty() {
5682            // The commitment completed between the timer firing and this running. Its
5683            // `CommitmentVerified` is already on its way to the supervisor, which clears the timer.
5684            debug!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "commitment completed before its parts could be re-requested");
5685            return Ok(());
5686        }
5687
5688        let missing_polynomials: u32 = runs.iter().map(|(first, last)| (last - first) as u32 + 1).sum();
5689        info!(
5690            %session_id, %ssa_id, runs = runs.len(), missing_polynomials,
5691            "re-requesting the SSA commitment parts that did not arrive"
5692        );
5693
5694        send_via_msg_sender(
5695            &mut msg_sender,
5696            slot.routing_opts.clone(),
5697            HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(
5698                session_id,
5699                params,
5700                [(ssa_id.ssa_index(), runs)],
5701            )),
5702            "ssa commitment retransmission request",
5703        )
5704        .await
5705        .map_err(TransportSessionError::packet_sending)?;
5706
5707        Ok(())
5708    }

5710    /// Returns the current number of active sessions.
5711    pub fn num_active_sessions(&self) -> usize {
5712        self.active_sessions.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
5713    }
5714
5715    /// Returns [`SessionIds`](SessionId) of all currently active sessions.
5716    pub fn active_sessions(&self) -> Vec<SessionId> {
5717        self.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
5718        self.sessions.iter().map(|(k, _)| *k).collect()
5719    }
5720
5721    /// Explicitly closes the session with the given `id`.
5722    ///
5723    /// Removes the entry from the internal session cache, closes the data channel,
5724    /// and aborts any auxiliary tasks. Returns `true` if a session was found and
5725    /// closed, `false` otherwise.
5726    ///
5727    /// This avoids waiting for the idle timeout (`time_to_idle`) or the LRU
5728    /// capacity bound to evict the entry, which is the desired behaviour when
5729    /// the caller (e.g. REST `DELETE /session`) knows the session is finished.
5730    ///
5731    /// One case departs from that: an Exit-side PIX Session with
5732    /// [`fill.drain_after_close`](crate::PixFillConfig::drain_after_close) on and spendable SURBs
5733    /// left starts a SURB drain instead of being torn down (see `begin_surb_drain`). The data path
5734    /// still ends at once, but the session slot and the keep-alive stream stay in place until the
5735    /// supervisor closes the Session — whether because the funded cycle recovered or because the
5736    /// drain was refused — and `true` then means "found, and now draining" rather than "found and
5737    /// closed".
5738    pub fn close_session(&self, id: &SessionId) -> bool {
5739        self.close_session_with_reason(id, ClosureReason::Eviction)
5740    }
5741
5742    /// Answers an Exit-side close by draining the Session's buffered SURBs, when that is worth doing.
5743    ///
5744    /// A PIX Session can end long before the cycle it was funded for does. The deposit that cycle was
5745    /// paid is released only once its whole emission has ridden back to the Entry, and the address it
5746    /// sits at derives from both nodes' commitments — so tearing the Session down mid-cycle strands
5747    /// money both sides have already parted with. When the Exit still holds enough SURBs to finish,
5748    /// it keeps the keep-alive stream running instead, and the Session's slot with it, until the
5749    /// supervisor closes the Session for good.
5750    ///
5751    /// Returns `None` when this close was **not** answered here, which is every case the caller must
5752    /// handle exactly as it always has; `Some(v)` is the value
5753    /// [`close_session_with_reason`](Self::close_session_with_reason) should return. `Some` currently
5754    /// always carries `true` — a drain is only ever started for a Session that was found — but the
5755    /// value is returned rather than assumed so that the two outcomes stay distinguishable if a
5756    /// future refusal path wants to report one.
5757    ///
5758    /// The order of the checks is load-bearing:
5759    ///
5760    /// 1. the configuration, so that with `drain_after_close` (or `fill.enabled`) off nothing below runs and every
5761    ///    close path is byte-for-byte what it was;
5762    /// 2. the slot, by `get` rather than `remove` — the lookup also refreshes the idle timer the drain lives on;
5763    /// 3. an Exit-side PIX Session, so an Entry-side or non-PIX Session falls straight through;
5764    /// 4. an already-draining Session: a `WriteClosed`/`EmptyRead` is the end-of-stream our own ingress abort produces
5765    ///    and is absorbed, while anything else — a second operator close, or a peer `SessionError` — forces the hard
5766    ///    teardown, which is the operator's way to overrule a drain;
5767    /// 5. a PIX failure already tearing the Session down, which nothing here should interfere with;
5768    /// 6. the SURB estimate, which is the one half of the predicate this layer can answer — see the comment on it for
5769    ///    why answering it here rather than leaving it all to the supervisor matters;
5770    /// 7. and only then the stream is put into drain mode, **before** the supervisor is told, so that no packet can be
5771    ///    classified as the reserve-exempt notification in the window between the supervisor deciding and the stream
5772    ///    learning.
5773    ///
5774    /// What it does *not* do is decrement `active_sessions` or remove the slot: the supervisor's own
5775    /// `Close` teardown does both, whether the drain completes or is refused a channel hop later.
5776    /// `Balancer`, `KeepAlive`, `SurbNotifyDelay`, `PixActionDriver` and the deposit observers are
5777    /// all left running; only the ingress is aborted, so the session server sees its end of the
5778    /// stream as promptly as it would have.
5779    fn begin_surb_drain(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason) -> Option<bool> {
5780        let fill_cfg = &self.cfg.pix_config.supervision.fill;
5781        if !(fill_cfg.enabled && fill_cfg.drain_after_close) {
5782            return None;
5783        }
5784
5785        let slot = self.sessions.get(id)?;
5786        let supervisor = slot.pix_supervisor.get()?;
5787        let fill = slot.pix_fill.get()?;
5788
5789        if fill.is_draining() {
5790            return answer_while_draining(reason);
5791        }
5792
5793        if matches!(reason, ClosureReason::PixFailure | ClosureReason::MissingDepositData) {
5794            return None;
5795        }
5796
5797        // Nothing to drain *with* is decidable here, and cheaply, unlike whether there is anything
5798        // worth draining *for* — which needs the cycle state only the supervisor holds. Asking it
5799        // anyway would defer the teardown of every PIX Session by however long the action driver
5800        // takes to reach the answer, and a driver mid-`send_ssa_request` can be seconds away from
5801        // that. So a Session whose estimate is already at or below its reserve is torn down here and
5802        // now, exactly as it always was: no rate the supervisor could plan would put a packet on the
5803        // wire against a buffer that shallow.
5804        let drainable_surbs = fill.drainable_surbs();
5805        if drainable_surbs == 0 {
5806            return None;
5807        }
5808
5809        // The check above is only a fast path: `close_session_with_reason` is reached from the
5810        // operator, the closure notifier and `handle_session_error` independently, so two closes can
5811        // both read it as false. The transition is what actually decides, and the loser is answered
5812        // as it would have been had the two been serialized rather than concurrent — which is what
5813        // keeps the supervisor from being told a Session closed twice.
5814        if !fill.enter_drain() {
5815            return answer_while_draining(reason);
5816        }
5817
5818        if !supervisor.try_send_event(SessionPixEvent::SessionClosed { drainable_surbs }) {
5819            return None;
5820        }
5821
5822        // The data path ends here regardless of what the supervisor decides: a writer parked on the
5823        // egress gate is waiting for a Session that has gone, and the reader's end-of-stream is what
5824        // the session server is waiting for.
5825        if let Some(gate) = slot.pix_egress_gate.get() {
5826            gate.poison();
5827        }
5828        slot.abort_handles.lock().abort_one(&SessionHandles::Ingress);
5829
5830        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5831        set_session_state(id, SessionLifecycleState::Closing);
5832
5833        info!(
5834            session_id = %id,
5835            ?reason,
5836            drainable_surbs,
5837            "session closed at the exit — draining its buffered SURBs into the funded cycle"
5838        );
5839        Some(true)
5840    }
5841
5842    /// [`close_session`](Self::close_session) with the reason spelled out.
5843    ///
5844    /// The reason is what the operator reads when a PIX Session stops, and the failures are hard to
5845    /// tell apart from the outside, so a caller that knows which one it is says so.
5846    ///
5847    /// `true` means the Session was found and dealt with. Since
5848    /// [`begin_surb_drain`](Self::begin_surb_drain), "dealt with" also covers "found, and now
5849    /// draining its remaining SURBs into a funded cycle" — in which case the slot is deliberately
5850    /// left in place until the supervisor's own teardown removes it.
5851    fn close_session_with_reason(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason) -> bool {
5852        if let Some(handled) = self.begin_surb_drain(id, reason) {
5853            return handled;
5854        }
5855
5856        if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.remove(id) {
5857            self.active_sessions.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
5858            // Reconstructor state is released by `close_session` aborting the PIX action driver,
5859            // whose commitment guards retire on drop.
5860            let token = slot.claim_admission_token();
5861            close_session(
5862                *id,
5863                slot,
5864                reason,
5865                self.surb_admission.get().cloned(),
5866                surb_retire_grace(self.cfg.surb_resolution_wait),
5867                token,
5868            );
5869            true
5870        } else {
5871            false
5872        }
5873    }

5875    /// Updates the configuration of the SURB balancer on the given [`SessionId`].
5876    ///
5877    /// Returns an error if the Session with the given `id` does not exist, or
5878    /// if it does not use SURB balancing.
5879    pub fn update_surb_balancer_config(&self, id: &SessionId, config: SurbBalancerConfig) -> errors::Result<()> {
5880        let cfg = self
5881            .sessions
5882            .get(id)
5883            .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession)?
5884            .surb_mgmt;
5885
5886        // Only update the config if there already was one before
5887        if !cfg.is_disabled() {
5888            cfg.update(&config);
5889            Ok(())
5890        } else {
5891            Err(SessionManagerError::other(anyhow!("session does not use SURB balancing")).into())
5892        }
5893    }

5895    /// Retrieves the configuration of SURB balancing for the given Session.
5896    ///
5897    /// Returns an error if the Session with the given `id` does not exist.
5898    pub fn get_surb_balancer_config(&self, id: &SessionId) -> errors::Result<Option<SurbBalancerConfig>> {
5899        match self.sessions.get(id) {
5900            Some(session) => Ok(Some(session.surb_mgmt.as_ref())
5901                .filter(|c| !c.is_disabled())
5902                .map(|d| d.as_config())),
5903            None => Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into()),
5904        }
5905    }

5907    /// Gets estimations produced/received and consumed SURBs by the Session.
5908    ///
5909    /// For an outgoing Session (Entry) the pair is the number of SURBs sent (by us) and used (by the Exit).
5910    /// For an incoming Session (Exit) the pair is the number of SURBs received (from Entry) and used (by us).
5911    ///
5912    /// Returns an error if the Session with the given `id` does not exist.
5913    pub fn get_surb_level_estimates(&self, id: &SessionId) -> errors::Result<(u64, u64)> {
5914        match self.sessions.get(id) {
5915            Some(session) => Ok((
5916                session
5917                    .surb_estimator
5918                    .produced
5919                    .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
5920                session
5921                    .surb_estimator
5922                    .consumed
5923                    .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
5924            )),
5925            None => Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into()),
5926        }
5927    }
5928
5929    /// Forwards a PIX protocol observation to the Session's supervisor.
5930    ///
5931    /// The manager no longer interprets these. Deciding what an early-recovery signal or a failed
5932    /// share means for a Session's lifecycle needs the whole picture — which SSAs are in flight,
5933    /// what phase each is in, how much service has been consumed — and that lives in the supervisor.
5934    ///
5935    /// A `NonExistingSession` error is expected traffic rather than a fault: acknowledgements
5936    /// outlive their Session by up to the reconstructor's ack window, so events for a just-closed
5937    /// Session are routine. Callers distinguish it for exactly that reason.
5938    pub async fn dispatch_pix_event(&self, event: HoprSessionInPixEvent) -> errors::Result<()> {
5939        // Copied rather than borrowed, so the match below can move the event's payload out.
5940        let session_id = *event.pseudonym();
5941        let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) else {
5942            debug!(%session_id, "pix event for a session that is no longer registered");
5943            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
5944        };
5945
5946        let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get() else {
5947            // Entry side, or a Session that negotiated no PIX: nothing supervises it, so there is
5948            // nothing an observation could act on.
5949            trace!(%session_id, "pix event on a session without a supervisor");
5950            return Ok(());
5951        };
5952
5953        // Progress is the one input whose rate is set by traffic rather than by lifecycle
5954        // transitions, so it is delivered without backpressure — awaiting channel capacity here
5955        // would put the supervisor's scheduling latency on the acknowledgement path. Safe by
5956        // construction rather than by tolerance: snapshots carry absolute counters and the state
5957        // machine keeps the maximum it has seen, so a dropped one is indistinguishable from a late
5958        // one, and the next one supersedes it.
5959        if let HoprSessionInPixEvent::RecoveryProgress(progress) = event {
5960            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5961            telemetry::set_pix_recovery_progress(&session_id, progress.useful_shares, progress.target_useful_shares);
5962
5963            if !supervisor.try_send_progress(progress) {
5964                trace!(%session_id, "dropped a pix progress snapshot on a full supervisor channel");
5965            }
5966            return Ok(());
5967        }
5968
5969        let sent = match event {
5970            HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaAlmostRecovered(ssa_id) => {
5971                supervisor.send_event(SessionPixEvent::AlmostRecovered(ssa_id)).await
5972            }
5973            HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id) => {
5974                supervisor.send_event(SessionPixEvent::Recovered(ssa_id)).await
5975            }
5976            HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
5977                ssa_id,
5978                observed_total,
5979                peer,
5980            } => {
5981                supervisor
5982                    .send_event(SessionPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
5983                        ssa_id,
5984                        observed_total,
5985                        peer,
5986                    })
5987                    .await
5988            }
5989            HoprSessionInPixEvent::RecoveryProgress(_) => unreachable!("handled above"),
5990        };
5991
5992        if sent.is_err() {
5993            error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor is no longer accepting events");
5994        }
5995
5996        Ok(())
5997    }
5998
5999    /// Sets how many SURBs of `session`, held in the counterparty's store, are invalid: their return
6000    /// path runs through a relayer judged dead on any hop. Also their share of what it was handed, so the
6001    /// balancer replaces them. `false` if there is no such Session.
6002    pub fn set_invalid_surbs(&self, session: &SessionId, count: u64, share: f64) -> bool {
6003        self.sessions
6004            .get(session)
6005            .map(|slot| slot.surb_mgmt.set_invalid_surbs(count, share))
6006            .is_some()
6007    }
6008
6009    /// Whether an `SsaRequest` for `session_id` names SSA state this node holds or is making.
6010    ///
6011    /// Only the Exit asks for SSA commitments, and only of its own Entry: a Session this node holds
6012    /// as an outgoing (`Forward`) slot, or one this node is still initiating (`pending_outgoing`).
6013    /// An Exit-side (`Return`) slot never legitimately receives one, so a request naming one is
6014    /// refused.
6015    ///
6016    /// Lives on [`Self::start_message_is_for_local_state`] only. [`Self::handle_ssa_request`]
6017    /// re-checks the two cheap halves of it (slot present, or initiation pending) as a backstop, but
6018    /// deliberately not the variant — see there.
6019    fn ssa_request_names_local_state(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> bool {
6020        self.pending_outgoing.contains_key(session_id)
6021            || self
6022                .sessions
6023                .get(session_id)
6024                .is_some_and(|slot| matches!(slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. }))
6025    }
6026
6027    /// Whether a Start-protocol message names Session state this node actually holds.
6028    ///
6029    /// Start messages share one bounded worker pool, and several handlers park a worker on state a
6030    /// bogus message will never have — `handle_ssa_request` waits up to a second for a Session slot
6031    /// a random pseudonym never gets. Deciding admission here, where the session lookup is already
6032    /// being done, keeps those messages off the pool entirely.
6033    fn start_message_is_for_local_state(&self, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym, msg: &HoprStartProtocol) -> bool {
6034        match msg {
6035            // Creates the state the other arms are checked against.
6036            HoprStartProtocol::StartSession(_) => true,
6037
6038            // Per-Session control traffic. The pseudonym a Start message arrives under is the
6039            // Session's own pseudonym on both sides, so a mismatch names someone else's Session.
6040            HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(m) => m.session_id == *pseudonym && self.sessions.contains_key(&m.session_id),
6041            HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(m) => m.session_id == *pseudonym && self.sessions.contains_key(&m.session_id),
6042
6043            // Only the Exit asks for SSA commitments, and only of its own Entry: an outgoing
6044            // (Forward) Session, or one this node is still initiating. An Exit-side (Return) slot
6045            // never legitimately receives one.
6046            HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(m) => {
6047                m.session_id == *pseudonym && self.ssa_request_names_local_state(&m.session_id)
6048            }
6049
6050            // Both are replies to something this node sent: an initiation named by challenge, or —
6051            // for `SessionError` only — a post-establishment error naming a registered Session by
6052            // its id.
6053            HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(est) => self.session_initiations.contains_key(&est.orig_challenge),
6054            HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(err) => match err.identifier {
6055                ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(challenge) => self.session_initiations.contains_key(&challenge),
6056                ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(id) => id == *pseudonym && self.sessions.contains_key(&id),
6057            },
6058        }
6059    }
6060
6061    /// Tells `session` that its counterparty dropped every SURB it held, because the session's SURB
6062    /// generation advanced: the counterparty clears its store on the first batch of the new one.
6063    ///
6064    /// The balancer restarts its level estimate from empty and paces the refill, instead of reading
6065    /// back the level the counterparty last reported. `false` if there is no such Session.
6066    pub fn on_counterparty_surbs_wiped(&self, session: &SessionId) -> bool {
6067        self.sessions
6068            .get(session)
6069            .map(|slot| slot.surb_mgmt.on_counterparty_wiped())
6070            .is_some()
6071    }
6072
6073    /// The main method to be called whenever data are received.
6074    ///
6075    /// It tries to recognize the message and correctly dispatches either
6076    /// the Session protocol or Start protocol messages.
6077    ///
6078    /// If the data are not recognized, they are returned as [`DispatchResult::Unrelated`].
6079    pub fn dispatch_message(
6080        &self,
6081        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
6082        in_data: ApplicationDataIn,
6083    ) -> errors::Result<DispatchResult> {
6084        if in_data.data.application_tag == HoprStartProtocol::START_PROTOCOL_MESSAGE_TAG {
6085            // Start-protocol traffic bypasses `session_rx`, but an Exit → Entry message still
6086            // consumed one return SURB and unlocked one PIX share. Count it on outgoing Sessions
6087            // before anything else: the decode and the admission filter below can both drop the
6088            // message, and a packet that is dropped here has already spent its return SURB, so the
6089            // credit must not depend on it being decodable or admitted. Incoming Sessions receive
6090            // this traffic from the Entry over the forward path and must not be credited.
6091            if let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&pseudonym)
6092                && matches!(&session_slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. })
6093            {
6094                session_slot
6095                    .returned_packets
6096                    .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6097
6098                // The only place the Exit's SURB supply can be heard from a quiet Session. The
6099                // conversion below takes `in_data.data` and drops the packet info with it, so by the
6100                // time `handle_keep_alive` runs the signals are gone -- and keep-alives are all a
6101                // Session that has stopped exchanging data still sends.
6102                session_slot
6103                    .surb_mgmt
6104                    .observe_counterparty_signals(in_data.packet_info.signals_from_sender);
6105            }
6106
6107            // What the packet did to the SURB store, taken before the decode below consumes the data
6108            // it is counted from; see [`SurbsStored`]. An incoming Session books it here, where every
6109            // kind of Start message passes, and before the decode and the admission filter below can drop
6110            // the message: the pipeline stored the SURBs before this ran, so they are in the ring whether
6111            // or not the message is handled. The opening `StartSession` finds no Session yet; the Start
6112            // protocol task books it once the Session exists, and only what was not booked here goes
6113            // along: an opening repeated for a Session that already exists is booked here, and must not
6114            // be booked again when the task refuses it, or a wipe it reports is subtracted twice.
6115            let stored = SurbsStored::of(&in_data);
6116            let booked = self
6117                .sessions
6118                .get(&pseudonym)
6119                .is_some_and(|session_slot| book_start_message_surbs(&session_slot, &pseudonym, stored));
6120            let unbooked = if booked { SurbsStored::default() } else { stored };
6121
6122            // Decode once, then decide locally whether anything on this node could handle it.
6123            // Without this check a peer spraying Start messages for pseudonyms it invented occupies
6124            // the shared Start-protocol worker pool — several handlers park a worker on state such
6125            // a message never has — and the bounded queue then fills, dropping every message behind
6126            // it.
6127            let msg = HoprStartProtocol::try_from(in_data.data)?;
6128
6129            if !self.start_message_is_for_local_state(&pseudonym, &msg) {
6130                // Quiet on purpose: a peer spraying Start messages for pseudonyms we never issued
6131                // must not be able to fill the log any more than it can fill the handler pool.
6132                trace!(%pseudonym, "dropping Start protocol message that names no local session");
6133                crate::counters::SESSION_STALE_START_MESSAGES.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6134                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6135                METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_stale_start"], 1);
6136                return Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage));
6137            }
6138
6139            // This is a Start protocol message, so we send it to the handler, with the packet info
6140            // and what the packet did to the SURB store.
6141            trace!("dispatching Start protocol message");
6142            if let Some(start_protocol_tx) = self.start_protocol_tx.get() {
6143                start_protocol_tx
6144                    .try_send((pseudonym, msg, in_data.packet_info, unbooked))
6145                    .map_err(|error| {
6146                        crate::counters::START_PROTOCOL_SEND_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6147                        error!(%error, "failed to send Start protocol message to processing task");
6148                        SessionManagerError::other(error)
6149                    })?;
6150            } else {
6151                return Err(SessionManagerError::NotStarted.into());
6152            }
6153
6154            #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6155            METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["processed"], 1);
6156
6157            return Ok(DispatchResult::Processed);
6158        } else if in_data.data.application_tag == SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG {
6159            // This is traffic that belongs to one of the Sessions
6160            let session_id = pseudonym;
6161
6162            // How often a sustained inbox-full condition is allowed to log. Backpressure can
6163            // affect every packet on the hot path, so warning per drop would reproduce exactly
6164            // the ERROR spam this dispatch was rewritten to avoid — warn once per interval instead.
6165            const SESSION_INBOX_FULL_WARN_INTERVAL: usize = 256;
6166
6167            return if let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
6168                trace!(%session_id, "received data for a registered session");
6169
6170                // Recorded here rather than once the Session reads the packet, because the send
6171                // below can drop it for local backpressure and the reader would never see it. What
6172                // the counterparty says about its own SURB supply is the override on the organic
6173                // SURB gate, so losing it to a full inbox would leave production shut off on an
6174                // estimate the counterparty has just contradicted.
6175                if matches!(&session_slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. }) {
6176                    session_slot
6177                        .surb_mgmt
6178                        .observe_counterparty_signals(in_data.packet_info.signals_from_sender);
6179                }
6180
6181                match session_slot.session_tx.try_send(in_data) {
6182                    Ok(_) => {
6183                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6184                        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["processed"], 1);
6185
6186                        Ok(DispatchResult::Processed)
6187                    }
6188                    // Benign teardown race: the slot is still registered but its data sink was
6189                    // dropped. Quiet on purpose — see [`DropReason`].
6190                    Err(crossfire::TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => {
6191                        trace!(%session_id, "dropping data for a session whose sink has closed");
6192                        crate::counters::SESSION_INBOX_CLOSED_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6193                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6194                        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_sink_closed"], 1);
6195                        Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::SinkClosed))
6196                    }
6197                    // Genuine backpressure: the reader is not keeping up. Rate-limited so a
6198                    // sustained overload cannot become per-packet log spam.
6199                    Err(crossfire::TrySendError::Full(_)) => {
6200                        let prev =
6201                            crate::counters::SESSION_INBOX_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6202                        if prev.is_multiple_of(SESSION_INBOX_FULL_WARN_INTERVAL) {
6203                            warn!(%session_id, total_inbox_full_drops = prev + 1, "session inbox full, dropping data (backpressure)");
6204                        }
6205                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6206                        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_sink_full"], 1);
6207                        Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::SinkFull))
6208                    }
6209                }
6210            } else {
6211                // Fully deregistered session: packets still in flight for a torn-down session.
6212                // Quiet — see [`DropReason::Unregistered`].
6213                trace!(%session_id, "dropping data for an unregistered session");
6214                crate::counters::SESSION_UNKNOWN_DATA_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6215                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6216                METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_unregistered"], 1);
6217                Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::Unregistered))
6218            };
6219        }
6220
6221        trace!(tag = %in_data.data.application_tag, "received data not associated with session protocol or any existing session");
6222
6223        crate::counters::SESSION_UNRELATED_DATA_DISPATCHES.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6224
6225        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6226        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["unrelated"], 1);
6227
6228        Ok(DispatchResult::Unrelated(in_data))
6229    }

6231    /// Pre-populates the sessions cache with a session slot for benchmarking.
6232    ///
6233    /// Intended for benchmarks that need a session to exist before calling
6234    /// [`SessionManager::dispatch_message`].
6235    ///
6236    /// Requires the `"benchmark"` feature (or a test build).
6237    #[cfg(any(feature = "benchmark", test))]
6238    pub fn pre_populate_session(&self, session_id: SessionId, routing_opts: DestinationRouting) {
6239        let (session_tx, _) =
6240            crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(self.cfg.session_forward_capacity);
6241        let slot = SessionSlot {
6242            session_tx,
6243            routing_opts,
6244            abort_handles: Default::default(),
6245            surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default()),
6246            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
6247            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
6248            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
6249            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
6250            pix_fill: Default::default(),
6251            returned_packets: Default::default(),
6252            // Never PIX, so there is no reconstructor state to charge for.
6253            cycle_budget: None,
6254            admission_token: Default::default(),
6255            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
6256        };
6257        self.sessions.insert(session_id, slot);
6258        self.slot_allocated
6259            .lock()
6260            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
6261            .remove(&session_id);
6262    }

6299
6300    /// Charges `params`' worth of reconstructor state against the node-wide budget.
6301    ///
6302    /// Returns `None` if the node has already committed to as much as
6303    /// [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::max_live_cycle_bytes`] allows — the caller must then refuse the
6304    /// Session, because nothing later in establishment can give the memory back.
6305    ///
6306    /// A CAS loop rather than an unconditional `fetch_add` with a rollback: an add that is
6307    /// provisionally over the ceiling is briefly visible to every concurrent initiation, and with
6308    /// enough of them arriving at once the budget would appear exhausted to Sessions that do fit.
6309    fn reserve_cycle_budget(&self, params: &PixParams, ssas_per_request: usize) -> Option<Arc<CycleBudgetReservation>> {
6310        let bytes = cycle_budget_for(params, ssas_per_request);
6311        let ceiling = self.cfg.pix_config.max_live_cycle_bytes;
6312
6313        self.live_cycle_bytes
6314            .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |held| {
6315                held.checked_add(bytes).filter(|total| *total <= ceiling)
6316            })
6317            .ok()
6318            .map(|_| {
6319                // Reports only this reservation's own bytes, not an outstanding total. Initiations
6320                // are processed concurrently, so any total computed here can be published out of
6321                // order with another reservation's; the gauge adds instead, which commutes.
6322                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
6323                crate::telemetry::pix::record_cycle_bytes_reserved(bytes);
6324
6325                Arc::new(CycleBudgetReservation {
6326                    bytes,
6327                    outstanding: self.live_cycle_bytes.clone(),
6328                    released: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
6329                })
6330            })
6331    }
6332
6333    /// Asks the session server on what terms this Session may be admitted.
6334    ///
6335    /// Fails closed. A refusal, a server that does not answer in time, a full request channel and a
6336    /// dropped reply all end the Session here rather than falling back to the node's own terms:
6337    /// falling back would mean an overloaded or wedged server silently disables every rule the
6338    /// operator wrote, and the peer would be served on terms nobody chose.
6339    ///
6340    /// The two failure kinds are reported differently because they call for different responses. A
6341    /// server that answered `Err` has decided, and re-asking will not change the answer, so the peer
6342    /// is told [`StartErrorReason::TargetNotAdmitted`]. Everything else is this node being unable to
6343    /// ask right now, which is transient, so the peer is told [`StartErrorReason::Busy`] and may
6344    /// retry.
6345    ///
6346    /// A node with no session server has nobody to ask, and admits on its own terms.
6347    async fn request_admission(
6348        &self,
6349        session_id: SessionId,
6350        req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
6351        offered: Option<PixParams>,
6352    ) -> Result<SessionAdmissionDecision, StartErrorReason> {
6353        let Some(admission_tx) = self.admission_tx.get() else {
6354            return Ok(SessionAdmissionDecision::default());
6355        };
6356
6357        let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = oneshot::channel();
6358        // The capability bits travel as the peer sent them; the offer travels decoded, since the
6359        // wire encoding is this crate's to read and the server has no business unpacking it.
6360        let request = SessionAdmissionRequest::new(session_id, req.target.clone(), req.capabilities.0.bits());
6361        let request = match offered {
6362            Some(params) => request.with_offer(OfferedIncentivization::new(
6363                params.polys_per_ssa(),
6364                params.shares_per_poly(),
6365                params.surplus_shares(),
6366                pix_params_to_quota(&params),
6367            )),
6368            None => request,
6369        };
6370
6371        // `try_send` rather than an awaited send: waiting for room in the queue would hold this
6372        // initiation past the peer's own timeout, and the queue being full is exactly the condition
6373        // the bound exists to report.
6374        if let Err(error) = admission_tx.lock().try_send((request, reply_tx)) {
6375            warn!(
6376                %session_id,
6377                %error,
6378                "cannot ask the session server to admit this session; refusing it as busy"
6379            );
6380            return Err(StartErrorReason::Busy);
6381        }
6382
6383        match reply_rx
6384            .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(self.cfg.session_admission_timeout))
6385            .await
6386        {
6387            Ok(Ok(Ok(decision))) => Ok(decision),
6388            Ok(Ok(Err(error))) => {
6389                debug!(%session_id, %error, "the session server refused this session's target");
6390                Err(StartErrorReason::TargetNotAdmitted)
6391            }
6392            // The server dropped the reply without answering, which is a bug in it rather than a
6393            // decision, so it is reported as transient like the timeout it resembles.
6394            Ok(Err(_)) => {
6395                error!(
6396                    %session_id,
6397                    "the session server dropped an admission request without answering it"
6398                );
6399                Err(StartErrorReason::Busy)
6400            }
6401            Err(_) => {
6402                warn!(
6403                    %session_id,
6404                    timeout = ?self.cfg.session_admission_timeout,
6405                    "the session server did not decide in time; refusing the session as busy"
6406                );
6407                Err(StartErrorReason::Busy)
6408            }
6409        }
6410    }
6411
6412    /// Checks the offer against the terms this Session was admitted on.
6413    ///
6414    /// Judged against `policy` — the node's configuration as narrowed by the session server's
6415    /// decision for this Session — rather than against the node's configuration directly, which is
6416    /// what makes the accepted quota a property of the target as well as of the node.
6417    ///
6418    /// `offered` is what [`decode_pix_offer`] read, so this is only the
6419    /// policy question; the wire has already been judged.
6420    ///
6421    /// Returns the validated parameters and selected SSA batch size, or `None` if the offer cannot
6422    /// satisfy that policy.
6423    fn check_pix_params(
6424        &self,
6425        challenge: StartChallenge,
6426        offered: Option<PixParams>,
6427        policy: &EffectivePixAdmission,
6428    ) -> Option<(PixParams, usize)> {
6429        if let Some(params) = offered {
6430            let quota_per_ssa = pix_params_to_quota(&params);
6431            let ssas_per_request = policy.ssa_batch_size_for_quota(quota_per_ssa);
6432            let accepted_quota = ssas_per_request.and_then(|batch_size| quota_per_ssa.checked_mul(batch_size as u64));
6433            debug!(
6434                challenge,
6435                %params,
6436                acceptable_range = ?policy.quota_range,
6437                node_range = ?self.cfg.pix_config.quota_range,
6438                dynamic_batches = policy.allow_dynamic_ssa_batches,
6439                configured_max_ssas_per_request = policy.ssas_per_request,
6440                selected_ssas_per_request = ?ssas_per_request,
6441                offered_quota_mb_per_ssa = quota_per_ssa as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0),
6442                accepted_quota_mb = ?accepted_quota.map(|quota| quota as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0)),
6443                "client offered PIX SSA quota"
6444            );
6445
6446            // A window narrowed to nothing means the session server's rule and this node's envelope
6447            // do not overlap, which is a misconfiguration rather than a peer offering badly: no
6448            // offer whatsoever could have been accepted, so it is worth saying out loud once per
6449            // Session rather than leaving it to look like a rejected client.
6450            if ssas_per_request.is_none() && policy.quota_range.is_empty() {
6451                warn!(
6452                    challenge,
6453                    admitted_range = ?policy.quota_range,
6454                    node_range = ?self.cfg.pix_config.quota_range,
6455                    "the admitted quota range for this target is empty, so no offer can be accepted"
6456                );
6457            }
6458
6459            ssas_per_request.map(|batch_size| (params, batch_size))
6460        } else if policy.enforce_pix {
6461            // Client didn't offer PIX, but PIX is enforced
6462            None
6463        } else {
6464            // Client didn't offer PIX, and PIX is not enforced, so set default values
6465            // which are not going to be used.
6466            Some((DEFAULT_PIX_PARAMS, 1))
6467        }
6468    }
6469
6470    /// Refuses a PIX offer whose initiation packet carried a SURB with a direct (0-hop) return path.
6471    ///
6472    /// A PIX share is decrypted with the acknowledgement of the return path's first relayer, and a
6473    /// direct return path has none, so the Entry mints such SURBs share-less and the Session could never
6474    /// make PIX progress (RFC-0012, Appendix 2). A conforming Entry refuses to offer PIX over one in
6475    /// `new_session`; without this check, a non-conforming one would be served until the commitment
6476    /// deadline closed the Session as `CommitmentTimeout`, a reason that names the clock rather than
6477    /// the fault.
6478    ///
6479    /// The hop count is the SURB creator's word (its declared Proof-of-Relay chain length), so this
6480    /// turns a misconfigured Entry away early rather than bounding a malicious one — the egress gate
6481    /// does that. Only the initiation packet is inspected: a conforming Entry keeps its return-path
6482    /// hop count for the lifetime of the Session. A node with no PIX support lets the offer through, so
6483    /// `handle_incoming_session_initiation` refuses it for that more fundamental reason.
6484    ///
6485    /// Returns `true` if the offer was refused and a `SessionError` was sent.
6486    async fn refuse_pix_over_direct_return_path(
6487        &self,
6488        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
6489        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
6490        min_return_path_hops: Option<u8>,
6491    ) -> errors::Result<bool> {
6492        if !session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX)
6493            || min_return_path_hops != Some(0)
6494            || self.pix_toolbox.get().is_none()
6495        {
6496            return Ok(false);
6497        }
6498
6499        error!(
6500            challenge = session_req.challenge,
6501            "client offered PIX over a direct return path"
6502        );
6503        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
6504        let reason = StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams;
6505        let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6506            identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6507            reason,
6508        });
6509        PixAdmissionRejection::DirectReturnPath.record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6510        send_via_msg_sender(
6511            &mut msg_sender,
6512            DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()),
6513            data,
6514            "session error due to a PIX offer over a direct return path",
6515        )
6516        .await?;
6517
6518        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6519        METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
6520        Ok(true)
6521    }
6522
6523    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, session_req))]
6524    async fn handle_incoming_session_initiation(
6525        &self,
6526        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
6527        session_req: StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
6528    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
6529        trace!(challenge = session_req.challenge, "received session initiation request");
6530
6531        debug!("got new session request, searching for a free session slot");
6532
6533        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
6534
6535        // Reply routing uses SURBs only with the pseudonym of this Session's ID
6536        let reply_routing = DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into());
6537
6538        // Reject UsePIX if this node is not configured with a PixToolbox
6539        // (e.g. relay nodes that do not participate in PIX processing).
6540        if self.pix_toolbox.get().is_none() && session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX) {
6541            error!(
6542                challenge = session_req.challenge,
6543                "client offered PIX but this node has no PIX support installed"
6544            );
6545            let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6546                identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6547                reason: StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
6548            });
6549            // Counted before the send, not after: the refusal has already happened, and
6550            // `send_via_msg_sender` can fail to encode, fail to send, or time out. Counting
6551            // afterwards would drop exactly the refusals that a struggling node makes most.
6552            PixAdmissionRejection::NoPixSupport.record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6553            send_via_msg_sender(
6554                &mut msg_sender,
6555                reply_routing,
6556                data,
6557                "session error due to missing PIX support",
6558            )
6559            .await?;
6560            return Ok(());
6561        }
6562
6563        // Ask whoever runs the session server on what terms this target may be served, before
6564        // anything is allocated for the Session. This is the only place the target can influence
6565        // admission: the transport cannot read a sealed target, and by the time the server sees the
6566        // established Session the terms have already been fixed.
6567        // Read the offer before anyone is asked about it: an offer this node cannot read, or whose
6568        // curve it does not share, is refused without a round trip to the session server, and the
6569        // server is told what was offered rather than having to unpack the wire itself.
6570        let offered = match decode_pix_offer(&session_req) {
6571            Ok(offered) => offered,
6572            Err(reason) => {
6573                error!(
6574                    challenge = session_req.challenge,
6575                    "client offered unacceptable PIX parameters"
6576                );
6577                let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6578                    identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6579                    reason,
6580                });
6581                PixAdmissionRejection::UnacceptableParams.record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6582                send_via_msg_sender(
6583                    &mut msg_sender,
6584                    reply_routing,
6585                    data,
6586                    "session error message due to unacceptable PIX parameters",
6587                )
6588                .await?;
6589
6590                // Left after the send, unlike the line above: this one counts errors *sent*, so a
6591                // send that never happened is correctly not one of them.
6592                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6593                METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
6594                return Ok(());
6595            }
6596        };
6597
6598        let session_id: SessionId = pseudonym;
6599        let admission = match self.request_admission(session_id, &session_req, offered).await {
6600            Ok(decision) => decision,
6601            Err(reason) => {
6602                let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6603                    identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6604                    reason,
6605                });
6606                // `request_admission` distinguishes these two on purpose — a refused target will not
6607                // be served however the request is phrased, while `Busy` is this node being unable
6608                // to ask right now and is worth retrying — so the aggregate keeps them apart too.
6609                match reason {
6610                    StartErrorReason::TargetNotAdmitted => PixAdmissionRejection::TargetPolicy,
6611                    _ => PixAdmissionRejection::Busy,
6612                }
6613                .record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6614                send_via_msg_sender(
6615                    &mut msg_sender,
6616                    reply_routing,
6617                    data,
6618                    "session error due to a refused admission",
6619                )
6620                .await?;
6621
6622                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6623                METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
6624                return Ok(());
6625            }
6626        };
6627        let pix_policy = self.cfg.pix_config.effective_for(&admission);
6628
6629        // Verify the offer against the terms this Session was admitted on.
6630        let Some((client_params, ssas_per_request)) =
6631            self.check_pix_params(session_req.challenge, offered, &pix_policy)
6632        else {
6633            error!(
6634                challenge = session_req.challenge,
6635                "client offered unacceptable PIX parameters"
6636            );
6637
6638            // Notify the sender that the session could not be established
6639            let reason = StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams;
6640            let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6641                identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6642                reason,
6643            });
6644            PixAdmissionRejection::UnacceptableParams.record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6645            send_via_msg_sender(
6646                &mut msg_sender,
6647                reply_routing,
6648                data,
6649                "session error message due to unacceptable PIX parameters",
6650            )
6651            .await?;
6652
6653            #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6654            METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
6655            return Ok(());
6656        };
6657
6658        info!(params = %client_params, ssas_per_request, "client offered acceptable PIX parameters");
6659
6660        // Charge this Session's reconstructor state against the node-wide budget before anything is
6661        // allocated for it. Only a PIX Session holds cycle state, so only a PIX Session is charged —
6662        // `check_pix_params` hands back nominal parameters for a peer that offered none, and
6663        // reserving on those would bill Sessions that never reconstruct anything.
6664        //
6665        // Refused here rather than at the successor request, which is the other place the ceiling
6666        // could be applied: by then the Entry has funded a cycle and refusing costs it that deposit,
6667        // whereas a Session refused now is one the peer can retry elsewhere at no charge.
6668        let cycle_budget = if session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX) {
6669            let Some(reservation) = self.reserve_cycle_budget(&client_params, ssas_per_request) else {
6670                warn!(
6671                    challenge = session_req.challenge,
6672                    requested = cycle_budget_for(&client_params, ssas_per_request),
6673                    outstanding = self.live_cycle_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
6674                    ceiling = self.cfg.pix_config.max_live_cycle_bytes,
6675                    "refusing a PIX session: the node's live reconstructor-cycle budget is exhausted"
6676                );
6677
6678                let reason = StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable;
6679                let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6680                    identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6681                    reason,
6682                });
6683                // The refusal this whole aggregate exists to separate from the one below. Both are
6684                // `NoSlotsAvailable` on the wire, but this one says the node is healthy and full of
6685                // reconstructor state, and the other says it is at its Session limit.
6686                PixAdmissionRejection::LiveCycleCapacity.record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6687                send_via_msg_sender(
6688                    &mut msg_sender,
6689                    reply_routing,
6690                    data,
6691                    "session error message due to an exhausted live-cycle budget",
6692                )
6693                .await?;
6694
6695                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6696                METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
6697                return Ok(());
6698            };
6699            Some(reservation)
6700        } else {
6701            None
6702        };
6703
6704        let (new_session_notifier, close_session_notifier) = self
6705            .session_notifiers
6706            .get()
6707            .cloned()
6708            .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
6709
6710        // Use constant application tag for all sessions
6711        self.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
6712
6713        let (session_tx, session_rx) =
6714            crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(self.cfg.session_forward_capacity);
6715        let (session_rx, session_rx_ah) = hopr_utils::runtime::DropAbortable::new(session_rx.into_stream());
6716
6717        let slot = SessionSlot {
6718            session_tx,
6719            routing_opts: reply_routing.clone(),
6720            abort_handles: Default::default(),
6721            surb_mgmt: Default::default(),
6722            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
6723            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
6724            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
6725            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
6726            pix_fill: Default::default(),
6727            returned_packets: Default::default(),
6728            cycle_budget,
6729            admission_token: Default::default(),
6730            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
6731        };
6732        slot.abort_handles.lock().insert(SessionHandles::Ingress, session_rx_ah);
6733
6734        // Insert the slot and get a guard. Any failure from here on rolls the slot
6735        // back, otherwise it would block this pseudonym until idle eviction. The atomic
6736        // insert (inside the helper) also prevents a TOCTOU race, so only one concurrent
6737        // request can claim the slot for a given pseudonym.
6738        let Some(mut slot_guard) = self.allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone()) else {
6739            // No slots available for this pseudonym
6740            error!("no slots available for this pseudonym");
6741            let reason = StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable;
6742            let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
6743                identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
6744                reason,
6745            });
6746
6747            PixAdmissionRejection::NoSessionSlot.record_if_pix(session_req.capabilities.0);
6748            send_via_msg_sender(
6749                &mut msg_sender,
6750                reply_routing.clone(),
6751                data,
6752                "session error message due to lack of slots",
6753            )
6754            .await?;
6755
6756            #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
6757            METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
6758
6759            return Ok(());
6760        };
6761
6762        debug!(?session_req, "assigned a new session");
6763
6764        // Stand the supervisor up before the `HoprSession` is constructed, so the egress adapters
6765        // below see a populated gate. Installing it afterwards would leave a window in which packets
6766        // are served ungated — small, but exactly the window an unfunded Entry would aim for.
6767        //
6768        // Its first `RequestSsa` action is deliberately *not* carried out here: the action driver
6769        // spawned after publication does it, which is what keeps `SessionEstablished` ahead of
6770        // `SsaRequest` on the wire.
6771        let pix: Option<ActionRx> = if self.pix_toolbox.get().is_some()
6772            && session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX)
6773        {
6774            // We use the same dimensions the client offered.
6775            slot.current_ssa_state
6776                .set(SessionSsaState::new(client_params))
6777                .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("session pix state must be uninitialized")))?;
6778
6779            let supervisor_config = SupervisorConfig {
6780                ssas_per_request,
6781                ..self.cfg.pix_config.supervisor_config()
6782            };
6783            let (handle, action_rx) =
6784                spawn_supervisor_worker(supervisor_config, client_params, session_id, std::time::Instant::now());
6785
6786            let _ = slot.pix_egress_gate.set(handle.gate.clone());
6787            let _ = slot.pix_supervisor.set(handle);
