6788            Some(action_rx)
6789        } else {
6790            None
6791        };
6792
6793        // The SURB buffer target the Entry asked for, resolved once for both branches below.
6794        //
6795        // The Session request carries a "hint" as additional data telling what the Session initiator
6796        // has configured as its target buffer size in the Balancer. The lower 32 bits of the options
6797        // word contain the SURB target; its upper 32 bits carry PIX parameters and must be masked out.
6798        //
6799        // Resolved even for an Entry that announces none (a `NoRateControl` one, or a rate-controlled one
6800        // without a SURB balancer), and on the `NoRateControl` branch, which runs no balancer: the Exit's
6801        // keep-alive stream derives its fill SURB reserve from this figure, and the fallback below — the
6802        // same one a rate-controlled Exit's balancer runs at — is the only estimate of the buffer there is.
6803        //
6804        // That fallback serves the balancer and the fill reserve only. It is not what the SURB ring is
6805        // sized from when nothing was announced: see `ring_surb_target` below.
6806        let surb_target = initiation_options(session_req.additional_data) as u32;
6807        let announced_surb_target = {
6808            if surb_target > 0 {
6809                (surb_target as u64).min(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64)
6810            } else {
6811                self.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate as u64
6812                    * self
6813                        .cfg
6814                        .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
6815                        .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
6816                        .as_secs()
6817            }
6818        };
6819
6820        // The target this Session's SURB ring is sized from: the one the Entry announced, or, when it
6821        // announced none, the largest this node allows (`maximum_surb_buffer_size`).
6822        //
6823        // Decided from the raw figure on the wire and not from `announced_surb_target`, which is
6824        // clamped and has already fallen back when nothing was announced.
6825        //
6826        // The fallback is a balancer-rate estimate (`initial_return_session_egress_rate` times the
6827        // minimum buffer duration, 50 at the defaults), not a buffer anyone asked for, and the store
6828        // turns it into a ring of 75. An Entry that runs no balancer announces nothing at establishment
6829        // (a `NoRateControl` one, or a rate-controlled one without `surb_management`; an Entry that
6830        // predates that announced the fallback itself, which cannot be told from a real target of 50),
6831        // and it sends no keep-alives to announce a target later either, so nothing would ever widen
6832        // that ring: a Session that bursts replies finds its SURBs evicted past the 75th, and the
6833        // replies without one. The ring is a ceiling and not a reservation (it
6834        // allocates with occupancy, see `SurbStoreConfig::rb_capacity`), so a large one costs at most
6835        // what it has held: its storage grows with the SURBs stored and never shrinks below that
6836        // high-water mark, but is not taken up front. And any Entry can have the same ring by
6837        // announcing the maximum target, so a smaller one for an Entry that announces nothing protects
6838        // nothing here; it only starves the Entries that cannot announce one, such as a Session opened
6839        // without `surb_management`. The transport sets the maximum to two thirds of
6840        // `rb_capacity`, which the store's headroom, at its default of 50 %, turns into a ring of
6841        // `rb_capacity` (to within a SURB of integer rounding).
6842        let ring_surb_target = if surb_target > 0 {
6843            announced_surb_target
6844        } else {
6845            self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64
6846        };
6847
6848        let closure_notifier = Box::new(move |session_id: SessionId, reason: ClosureReason| {
6849            if let Err(error) = close_session_notifier.try_send((session_id, reason)) {
6850                error!(%session_id, %error, %reason, "failed to notify session closure");
6851            }
6852        });
6853
6854        let session = if !session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::NoRateControl) {
6855            // Because of SURB scarcity, control the egress rate of incoming sessions
6856            let egress_rate_control =
6857                RateController::new(self.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate, Duration::from_secs(1));
6858
6859            let target_surb_buffer_size = announced_surb_target;
6860
6861            let surb_estimator_tx = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
6862            let surb_estimator_rx = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
6863            // Resolved once, here, rather than per packet: the gate was installed before this point,
6864            // so the egress path never has to look inside the `OnceLock` again.
6865            let egress_gate = slot.pix_egress_gate.get().cloned();
6866            let session = HoprSession::new(
6867                session_id,
6868                reply_routing.clone(),
6869                session_config(&self.cfg, session_req.capabilities.into()),
6870                (
6871                    // Sent packets = SURB consumption estimate. Data is held back once the stock is down
6872                    // to the reserve for the keep-alives, but only after the Entry's first keep-alive has
6873                    // shown that a balancer on its side acts on what the Exit reports, and only if the
6874                    // Exit runs a keep-alive stream to hold it for (see `spawn_exit_keep_alive` below). An
6875                    // Entry without a balancer runs this branch too, and what it announces says nothing
6876                    // either way: it announces no target, or the balancer-rate fallback if it predates
6877                    // that. The `NoRateControl` branch below has no such reserve.
6878                    exit_data_egress(
6879                        msg_sender.clone().sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
6880                        session_id,
6881                        surb_estimator_tx,
6882                        slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
6883                        egress_gate,
6884                        self.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period.is_some() || pix.is_some(),
6885                    )
6886                    .rate_limit_with_controller(&egress_rate_control)
6887                    .buffer((2 * target_surb_buffer_size) as usize),
6888                    // Received packets = SURB retrieval estimate. Session data packets only: the
6889                    // SURBs of a Start message, a keep-alive among them, are booked by
6890                    // `book_start_message_surbs`, from `dispatch_message`.
6891                    session_rx.inspect(move |data| {
6892                        // SURBs saved into the store, and older ones the full store evicted to make room.
6893                        let produced = data.num_surbs_with_msg() as u64;
6894                        let evicted = data.packet_info.num_evicted_surbs as u64;
6895                        account_incoming_surbs(&surb_estimator_rx, produced, evicted);
6896                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
6897                        telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(&session_id, produced);
6898                    }),
6899                ),
6900                Some(closure_notifier),
6901            )?;
6902
6903            // The SURB balancer will start intervening by rate-limiting the
6904            // egress of the Session, once the estimated number of SURBs drops below
6905            // the target defined here. Otherwise, the maximum egress is allowed.
6906            let balancer_config = SurbBalancerConfig {
6907                target_surb_buffer_size,
6908                // At maximum egress, the SURB buffer drains in `minimum_surb_buffer_duration` seconds
6909                max_surbs_per_sec: target_surb_buffer_size / self.cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.as_secs(),
6910                // No SURB decay at the Exit, since we know almost exactly how many SURBs
6911                // were received
6912                surb_decay: None,
6913            };
6914
6915            slot.surb_mgmt.update(&balancer_config);
6916            slot.surb_mgmt
6917                .set_counterparty_buffer_capacity(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64);
6918
6919            // Spawn the SURB balancer only once we know we have registered the
6920            // abort handle with the pre-allocated Session slot
6921            debug!(%session_id, ?balancer_config ,"spawning exit SURB balancer");
6922            let balancer = SurbBalancer::new(
6923                session_id,
6924                SimpleBalancerController::default(),
6925                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
6926                SurbControllerWithCorrection(egress_rate_control, 1), // 1 SURB per egress packet
6927                slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
6928            );
6929
6930            // Assign the SURB balancer and abort handles to the already allocated Session slot
6931            let (_, balancer_abort_handle) = balancer.start_control_loop(self.cfg.balancer_sampling_interval);
6932            slot.abort_handles
6933                .lock()
6934                .insert(SessionHandles::Balancer, balancer_abort_handle);
6935
6936            // Reports the SURB buffer level towards the Entry, and — on a PIX Session — carries the
6937            // Exit's own fill.
6938            self.spawn_exit_keep_alive(
6939                session_id,
6940                &slot,
6941                msg_sender.clone(),
6942                pix.is_some(),
6943                announced_surb_target,
6944            );
6945
6946            session
6947        } else {
6948            // `NoRateControl`: no SURB balancer, but the PIX gate still applies. A Session that
6949            // opts out of rate control is exactly the one that could drain the most service before
6950            // funding, so leaving this path ungated would make the predeposit budget optional.
6951            let egress_gate = slot.pix_egress_gate.get().cloned();
6952            let surb_estimator_tx = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
6953            let surb_estimator_rx = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
6954            let session = HoprSession::new(
6955                session_id,
6956                reply_routing.clone(),
6957                session_config(&self.cfg, session_req.capabilities.into()),
6958                (
6959                    msg_sender.clone().sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other).with(
6960                        move |(routing, data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
6961                            // Counted here too, though nothing on this branch balances anything. The
6962                            // estimate is what the fill reserve is measured against, and a reserve
6963                            // measured against a counter that only ever counts in one direction is a
6964                            // reserve that either never binds or never releases. `NoRateControl` is
6965                            // also the branch that can drain SURBs fastest, so it is the one where
6966                            // that matters most.
6967                            let data = count_return_packet_surb(&surb_estimator_tx, data);
6968                            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
6969                            telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
6970                            acquire_egress_permit(egress_gate.clone(), routing, data)
6971                        },
6972                    ),
6973                    session_rx.inspect(move |data| {
6974                        // SURBs saved into the store, and older ones the full store evicted to make room.
6975                        let produced = data.num_surbs_with_msg() as u64;
6976                        let evicted = data.packet_info.num_evicted_surbs as u64;
6977                        account_incoming_surbs(&surb_estimator_rx, produced, evicted);
6978                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
6979                        telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(&session_id, produced);
6980                    }),
6981                ),
6982                Some(closure_notifier),
6983            )?;
6984
6985            self.spawn_exit_keep_alive(
6986                session_id,
6987                &slot,
6988                msg_sender.clone(),
6989                pix.is_some(),
6990                announced_surb_target,
6991            );
6992
6993            session
6994        };
6995
6996        // Extract useful information about the session from the Start protocol message
6997        let incoming_session = IncomingSession {
6998            id: session_id,
6999            session,
7000            target: session_req.target,
7001        };
7002
7003        // Notify that a new incoming session has been created. Lock the sink and send
7004        // directly into it, so no extra forwarding task between channels is needed.
7005        match async {
7006            let mut guard = new_session_notifier.lock().await;
7007            guard.send(incoming_session).await
7008        }
7009        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT))
7010        .await
7011        {
7012            Err(_) => {
7013                error!(%session_id, "timeout to notify about new incoming session");
7014                return Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout);
7015            }
7016            Ok(Err(error)) => {
7017                error!(%session_id, %error, "failed to notify about new incoming session");
7018                return Err(SessionManagerError::other(error).into());
7019            }
7020            _ => {}
7021        };
7022
7023        trace!(?session_id, "session notification sent");
7024
7025        // Notify the sender that the session has been established.
7026        // Set our peer ID in the session ID sent back to them.
7027        let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(StartEstablished {
7028            orig_challenge: session_req.challenge,
7029            session_id,
7030        });
7031
7032        send_via_msg_sender(
7033            &mut msg_sender,
7034            reply_routing.clone(),
7035            data,
7036            "session establishment message",
7037        )
7038        .await?;
7039
7040        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
7041        initialize_session_telemetry(
7042            session_id,
7043            &self.cfg,
7044            session_req.capabilities.0,
7045            Some(&slot.surb_estimator),
7046            Some(&slot.surb_mgmt),
7047        );
7048
7049        // The session is published, so the supervisor's actions can now be carried out. The first of
7050        // them is the initial `RequestSsa`, which is why this runs after `SessionEstablished` has
7051        // gone out: the Entry must see the two in that order.
7052        if let Some(action_rx) = pix {
7053            let driver = self.spawn_pix_action_driver(session_id, &slot, action_rx, reply_routing.clone());
7054            slot.abort_handles
7055                .lock()
7056                .insert(SessionHandles::PixActionDriver, driver);
7057        }
7058
7059        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
7060        METRIC_NUM_ESTABLISHED_SESSIONS.increment();
7061
7062        // `ring_surb_target` — the buffer the Entry asked for, or the largest this node allows when it
7063        // asked for none — is what the store sizes the admitted ring off. It is live only from its
7064        // resolution at the top of this function, which is why the admit rides on `commit` rather than
7065        // on slot allocation. See where it is resolved for why an Entry that announced nothing is not
7066        // given the balancer's fallback figure, on both branches.
7067        commit_slot_guard(
7068            &mut slot_guard,
7069            &self.sessions,
7070            session_id,
7071            self.surb_admission.clone(),
7072            ring_surb_target as usize,
7073        );
7074
7075        Ok(())
7076    }
7077
7078    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, est))]
7079    async fn handle_session_established(&self, est: StartEstablished<SessionId>) -> errors::Result<()> {
7080        debug!(
7081            session_id = ?est.session_id,
7082            "received session establishment confirmation"
7083        );
7084        let challenge = est.orig_challenge;
7085        let session_id = est.session_id;
7086
7087        if let Some(tx_est) = self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge) {
7088            if let Err(error) = tx_est.try_send(Ok(est)) {
7089                error!(%challenge, %session_id, %error, "failed to send session establishment confirmation");
7090                return Err(SessionManagerError::other(error).into());
7091            }
7092            debug!(?session_id, challenge, "session establishment complete");
7093        } else {
7094            error!(%session_id, challenge, "unknown session establishment attempt or expired");
7095        }
7096        Ok(())
7097    }
7098
7099    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self))]
7100    async fn handle_session_error(
7101        &self,
7102        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
7103        error_type: StartErrorType<SessionId>,
7104    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
7105        let reason = error_type.reason;
7106        match error_type.identifier {
7107            ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(challenge) => {
7108                trace!(%challenge, error = ?error_type.reason, "session initiation error received");
7109                if let Some(tx_est) = self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge) {
7110                    if let Err(error) = tx_est.try_send(Err(error_type)) {
7111                        error!(%error, "could not send session error message");
7112                        return Err(SessionManagerError::other(error).into());
7113                    }
7114                    error!(%challenge, "session establishment error received");
7115                } else {
7116                    error!(
7117                        %challenge,
7118                        "session establishment attempt expired before error could be delivered"
7119                    );
7120                }
7121            }
7122            ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(session_id) => {
7123                if session_id != pseudonym {
7124                    debug!(%pseudonym, %session_id, "dropping session error naming a different session");
7125                    return Ok(());
7126                }
7127                error!(
7128                    %session_id, %reason,
7129                    "received post-establishment session error — closing session"
7130                );
7131                // Best-effort close; the session may have already been removed.
7132                self.close_session(&session_id);
7133            }
7134        }
7135
7136        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
7137        METRIC_RECEIVED_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
7138
7139        Ok(())
7140    }
7141
7142    /// Handles a keep-alive.
7143    ///
7144    /// On an incoming Session (the Exit) a keep-alive from the Entry is also a delivery of SURBs, booked
7145    /// with those of every other Start message in [`dispatch_message`](Self::dispatch_message); see
7146    /// [`book_start_message_surbs`].
7147    #[tracing::instrument(level = "trace", skip(self, msg))]
7148    async fn handle_keep_alive(
7149        &self,
7150        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
7151        msg: KeepAliveMessage<SessionId>,
7152    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
7153        // The pseudonym a Start message arrives under is the Session's own pseudonym on both sides,
7154        // so a mismatch means the sender is naming someone else's Session. Pseudonyms are 80 random
7155        // bits, so this only matters on a leak — which is exactly when it matters.
7156        if msg.session_id != pseudonym {
7157            debug!(%pseudonym, session_id = %msg.session_id, "dropping keep-alive naming a different session");
7158            return Ok(());
7159        }
7160
7161        let session_id = msg.session_id;
7162        if let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
7163            trace!(?session_id, "received keep-alive message");
7164            match &session_slot.routing_opts {
7165                // Session is outgoing - keep-alive was received from the Exit
7166                DestinationRouting::Forward { .. } => {
7167                    if msg.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState) && !session_slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled() {
7168                        // Record the reported level and let it infer the counterparty's real store
7169                        // capacity from a plateau. Every report is fed in, including one that repeats
7170                        // the last value -- a level that stops rising while we are still minting is
7171                        // exactly the plateau signal, so this must not dedup equal reports.
7172                        let changed = session_slot.surb_mgmt.buffer_level() != msg.additional_data;
7173                        session_slot.surb_mgmt.observe_reported_level(msg.additional_data);
7174                        if changed {
7175                            debug!(%session_id, surb_level = msg.additional_data, "keep-alive updated SURB buffer size from the Exit");
7176                        }
7177                    }
7178
7179                    // Increase the number of consumed SURBs in the estimator
7180                    session_slot
7181                        .surb_estimator
7182                        .consumed
7183                        .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
7184                    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
7185                    telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
7186                }
7187                // Session is incoming - keep-alive was received from the Entry
7188                DestinationRouting::Return(_) => {
7189                    // Only an Entry's SURB balancer sends keep-alives of its own accord: from now on the
7190                    // Exit's data can be held back for its keep-alive reserve, which this Entry will
7191                    // refill, and the Exit's SURB-level reports can go out, since this Entry has a
7192                    // balancer to read them (see `PixFillControl::admit`).
7193                    //
7194                    // Not a manual ping, though: an Entry without a balancer pings by hand through
7195                    // `ping_session` too, and would otherwise be taken for one that has. The mark is the
7196                    // only way to tell the two apart, as a balancer that does not announce its target
7197                    // sends its keep-alives unflagged (`surb_target_notify` off). The SURBs a ping
7198                    // carries are booked all the same, with those of every Start message
7199                    // (`book_start_message_surbs`). An Entry that predates the mark sends its pings
7200                    // unflagged, and is taken for a balancer as it always was.
7201                    if !msg.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing) {
7202                        session_slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
7203                    }
7204
7205                    // Allow updating SURB balancer target based on the received Keep-Alive message.
7206                    //
7207                    // Clamped exactly as establishment clamps it, and for every use below. The value
7208                    // is a peer's claim: the balancer's set-point and the ring's ceiling are two
7209                    // views of one figure, and letting an over-announcing Entry set them apart would
7210                    // have the Exit aim at a buffer the ring can never hold.
7211                    //
7212                    // A `NoRateControl` Session runs no balancer on this side, so there is no
7213                    // set-point to move (its target is never set). Its ring is the same bounded
7214                    // store, though, sized at establishment from the target the Entry announced then.
7215                    // A Session whose Entry announced nothing was given the full ring at that point
7216                    // (see `ring_surb_target` in `handle_incoming_session_initiation`), so there is nothing left to
7217                    // widen; the raise matters for one that announced a target at establishment and
7218                    // has since raised it, for the same reason as for any other
7219                    // (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739). With no set-point to compare against, a raise is
7220                    // whatever exceeds the largest figure already recorded on the slot; the ring
7221                    // only ever widens, so a repeated announcement changes nothing.
7222                    let announced = msg.additional_data.min(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64);
7223                    let balanced = !session_slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled();
7224                    if msg.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget)
7225                        && announced > 0
7226                        && if balanced {
7227                            session_slot.surb_mgmt.controller_bounds().target() != announced
7228                        } else {
7229                            session_slot
7230                                .peek_raised_surb_target()
7231                                .is_none_or(|raised| announced as usize > raised)
7232                        }
7233                    {
7234                        if balanced {
7235                            // Update the target buffer size as sent to us from the Entry
7236                            session_slot
7237                                .surb_mgmt
7238                                .target_surb_buffer_size
7239                                .store(announced, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
7240                            // Update maximum SURBs per second based on the new target
7241                            session_slot.surb_mgmt.max_surbs_per_sec.store(
7242                                announced / self.cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.as_secs(),
7243                                std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed,
7244                            );
7245                        }
7246
7247                        // The store sized this Session's ring once, off the target announced at
7248                        // establishment. A target raised afterwards must widen it, or every SURB
7249                        // minted toward the new one is evicted on arrival — under PIX, together with
7250                        // the share it carried. See `SurbAdmissionControl::raise_target`.
7251                        //
7252                        // Recorded on the slot before the call as well: the Exit answers
7253                        // `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so this can arrive before the ring
7254                        // exists. The commit sizes the ring from the recorded figure; once the
7255                        // admission exists, the raise widens it on the spot.
7256                        session_slot.note_raised_surb_target(announced as usize);
7257                        if let Some(admission) = self.surb_admission.get() {
7258                            admission.raise_target(
7259                                &session_id,
7260                                session_slot.peek_admission_token(),
7261                                announced as usize,
7262                            );
7263                        }
7264
7265                        if balanced {
7266                            debug!(%session_id, target_surb_buffer_size = announced, "keep-alive updated SURB balancer target buffer size from the Entry");
7267                        } else {
7268                            debug!(%session_id, target_surb_buffer_size = announced, "keep-alive target recorded for the SURB ring of a session without a balancer");
7269                        }
7270                    }
7271                }
7272            }
7273        } else {
7274            debug!(%session_id, "received keep-alive request for an unknown session");
7275        }
7276
7277        Ok(())
7278    }
7279
7280    /// Handled by the Exit, when Entry replies with PIX commitment
7281    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, msg))]
7282    async fn handle_ssa_commit(
7283        &self,
7284        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
7285        msg: SsaClientCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixCommitmentProof>,
7286    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
7287        let Some(pix_toolbox) = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned() else {
7288            return Err(SessionManagerError::UnsupportedMessage.into());
7289        };
7290
7291        let session_id = msg.session_id;
7292
7293        if pseudonym != session_id {
7294            error!(%pseudonym, %msg.session_id, "received SSA client commitment for a different session");
7295            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
7296        }
7297
7298        let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) else {
7299            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
7300        };
7301
7302        // See if we haven't received an SSA commitment for a Session that we did not register as PIX-capable
7303        let Some(ssa_state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() else {
7304            return Err(SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!("no SSA state for session {session_id}")).into());
7305        };
7306        let quota_per_ssa = ssa_state.quota_per_ssa();
7307
7308        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, msg.ssa_index);
7309
7310        // Decode the accompanying proof of knowledge, if the message carries one. A malformed proof
7311        // is rejected here rather than being passed on as absent, so that it cannot be mistaken for
7312        // a peer that simply did not send one.
7313        let commitment_proof = msg
7314            .commitment_proof
7315            .map(|proof| proof.try_into_pix_proof())
7316            .transpose()
7317            .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
7318
7319        // Insert the newly received coefficients into the SSA Reconstructor
7320        let pix_toolbox_clone = pix_toolbox.clone();
7321        let ssa_client_commitment_state = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
7322            move || {
7323                pix_toolbox_clone
7324                    .share_processor
7325                    .insert_coefficient_commitments(
7326                        ssa_id,
7327                        msg.coefficient_index,
7328                        commitment_proof,
7329                        msg.coefficient_commitments.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, v.0)),
7330                    )
7331                    .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)
7332            },
7333            "ssa commitment reconstructor",
7334        )
7335        .await
7336        .map_err(|_| {
7337            SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!(
7338                "failed to insert SSA coefficients into the SSA reconstructor"
7339            ))
7340        })??;
7341
7342        // A verifiable commitment is what starts the deposit clock, so tell the supervisor before
7343        // the observer below can report anything against it.
7344        //
7345        // An *incomplete* one is reported too, and per message: that is what arms the supervisor's
7346        // re-request timer and keeps pushing it out while the burst is still arriving, so it fires
7347        // only once delivery has actually stalled. It is also the only evidence that the Entry
7348        // answered at all, which is what separates a cycle worth re-asking for from one where
7349        // nothing was ever delivered and there is no scope to name.
7350        if let Some(supervisor) = session_slot.pix_supervisor.get() {
7351            let event = if ssa_client_commitment_state.is_verifiable {
7352                SessionPixEvent::CommitmentVerified(ssa_id)
7353            } else {
7354                SessionPixEvent::CommitmentProgress(ssa_id)
7355            };
7356            if supervisor.send_event(event).await.is_err() {
7357                error!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "pix supervisor is no longer accepting events");
7358            }
7359        }
7360
7361        if ssa_client_commitment_state.deposit_address_first_encountered
7362            && let Some(deposit_address) = ssa_client_commitment_state.ssa_deposit_address
7363        {
7364            // Inside the guard on purpose: every other `SsaCommit` of a cycle takes the other branch,
7365            // so allocating this before the `if` built and dropped a channel per message.
7366            let (deposit_done_tx, deposit_done_rx) =
7367                futures::channel::mpsc::channel::<(PixAddressId, hopr_api::HoprBalance)>(10);
7368            // Report deposits for as long as they arrive rather than waiting for the first one and
7369            // stopping: the pool may report more than once for a cycle, and a first message carrying
7370            // a zero balance asserts nothing, so the one that funds the cycle need not be the first.
7371            // The supervisor owns the deadline, so the observer carries none — a timeout here would
7372            // have been a second authority racing the first.
7373            let supervisor = session_slot.pix_supervisor.get().cloned();
7374            session_slot.abort_handles.lock().insert(
7375                SessionHandles::PixDepositObserver(ssa_id.ssa_index().get()),
7376                hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
7377                    let Some(supervisor) = supervisor else {
7378                        // No supervisor: a Session that negotiated PIX always has one, so this is
7379                        // only reachable if it died between the check above and here.
7380                        return;
7381                    };
7382                    let mut confirmations = deposit_done_rx.filter(|(evt_id, _)| {
7383                        futures::future::ready(
7384                            evt_id.ssa_index() == ssa_id.ssa_index() && &evt_id.session_id() == ssa_id.pseudonym(),
7385                        )
7386                    });
7387                    while let Some((_, amount)) = confirmations.next().await {
7388                        info!(%session_id, %ssa_id, %amount, "ssa deposit confirmed");
7389                        if supervisor
7390                            .send_event(SessionPixEvent::DepositConfirmed { ssa_id, amount })
7391                            .await
7392                            .is_err()
7393                        {
7394                            return;
7395                        }
7396                    }
7397                    // The upper layer dropped the sender without ever confirming, so no deposit is
7398                    // coming. Saying so is better than letting the supervisor wait out its deadline.
7399                    warn!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "deposit channel closed without confirmation");
7400                    let _ = supervisor
7401                        .send_event(SessionPixEvent::DepositObserverClosed(ssa_id))
7402                        .await;
7403                }),
7404            );
7405
7406            // Notify upstream that deposit is needed
7407            pix_toolbox
7408                .pix_events
7409                .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(
7410                    AgreedSsaQuota {
7411                        ssa_id,
7412                        deposit_address,
7413                        quota_per_ssa,
7414                        // Handed back to the pool that produced it, now that the address it pays for
7415                        // is known. Consumed here: this branch is reached once per cycle.
7416                        deposit_data: ssa_state.take_sent_deposit_data(&session_id, ssa_id.ssa_index()),
7417                    },
7418                    deposit_done_tx,
7419                ))
7420                .map_err(|_| {
7421                    SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("failed to send pix event for needed deposit"))
7422                })?;
7423            info!(%ssa_id, %deposit_address, quota_per_ssa, "retrieved first client SSA commitment and deposit address");
7424        }
7425
7426        Ok(())
7427    }
7428
7429    /// Tells the Exit that its [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`] was refused, and tears down this half
7430    /// of the Session.
7431    ///
7432    /// Without the notice the refusal is invisible to the Exit, and it has no way to recover from it.
7433    /// Its supervisor registered an Exit commitment per requested index and armed each cycle's
7434    /// commitment deadline the moment the request went out; it will never receive an `SsaCommit`, and
7435    /// nothing can make it re-ask, because a new `RequestSsa` only comes from share-recovery events and
7436    /// no shares exist for a cycle the Entry never committed to. So it serves the Session
7437    /// unincentivized for the whole batch-scaled `max_ssa_delivery_time` and then closes it as
7438    /// `CommitmentTimeout` — a reason that names the clock rather than the refusal, on the one node
7439    /// whose operator can act on it.
7440    ///
7441    /// Closing this half too is what stops the Entry sitting on a Session that can never make PIX
7442    /// progress: a refusal is terminal either way, since the Exit re-derives every request from state
7443    /// that cannot drift within a Session, so a later one would be refused identically. Left alone the
7444    /// slot would survive until the idle timeout.
7445    ///
7446    /// That holds for the refusals that come through here — parameters, the batch cap, an undecodable
7447    /// commitment and lost generator state. It does *not* hold for the successor gate, whose two
7448    /// refusals (early, under-served) and the stale-index drop are `NotAdmitted` and never reach this
7449    /// function: they depend on how far the predecessor has been served, which changes, and the
7450    /// Exit's supervisor re-sends its unanswered successor request while that generation is still
7451    /// being served. Closing on one of those would end a Session over a shortfall that the next
7452    /// re-send repairs.
7453    ///
7454    /// No new capability is handed to an attacker by closing on a refusal: an `SsaRequest` only reaches
7455    /// here with `pseudonym == session_id`, and relayers never see that pseudonym — a relayer can garble
7456    /// a packet in transit but not forge one for this Session — so only the Exit can produce one, and
7457    /// the Exit can already close the Session whenever it likes.
7458    async fn refuse_ssa_request(&self, session_id: SessionId, routing: DestinationRouting) {
7459        self.notify_session_error(
7460            session_id,
7461            routing,
7462            StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
7463            "session error due to a refused SSA request",
7464        )
7465        .await;
7466
7467        if self.close_session(&session_id) {
7468            error!(%session_id, "closed session after refusing the Exit's SSA request");
7469        }
7470    }
7471
7472    /// Handled by the Entry, when the Exit says it never received parts of a commitment this node
7473    /// already published.
7474    ///
7475    /// Re-sends the named polynomial commitments and nothing else. Emits no
7476    /// [`ReadyToDeposit`](HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit): the deposit address of a cycle is
7477    /// fixed when it is first committed, and the caller was told it then, so announcing it again
7478    /// would invite a second deposit against one quota.
7479    ///
7480    /// That holds for a cycle whose publication completed. For one whose publication was cut short —
7481    /// the transport failed part-way through its burst, or between its burst and the announcement — the
7482    /// caller was *not* told, and the scoped parts would hand the Exit a complete commitment for a
7483    /// cycle nobody was asked to fund. Such a cycle is answered instead by resuming the publication of
7484    /// the batch it belongs to: whole bursts and the owed `ReadyToDeposit`s, in ascending order, each
7485    /// published by whoever claims it (see [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`]) so that a deposit is
7486    /// announced once however many requests arrive. The cycles of the request that were not cut short
7487    /// are answered with their scoped parts as before. This is reached only when the Exit asks, so it
7488    /// is the answer for a burst that got part of the way out: a cycle with no message out, or one
7489    /// whose burst was whole and only its announcement failed, prompts no request and is not covered
7490    /// (see [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`]). A resumption the transport cuts short again is the
7491    /// non-fatal `NotAdmitted`.
7492    ///
7493    /// A failure here is reported to the caller of the Start-message dispatcher and otherwise
7494    /// dropped. It is deliberately not [`refuse_ssa_request`](Self::refuse_ssa_request), which closes
7495    /// the Session: an Exit that asks for a cycle this node cannot serve is asking for something
7496    /// already lost, and its own commitment deadline ends the Session either way — whereas closing on
7497    /// a request that merely raced our own state would throw away a Session that was about to work.
7498    ///
7499    /// Two separate bounds keep this from being a packet-amplification lever, because one request may
7500    /// name a whole cycle's polynomials and the answer to that is the entire commitment burst again.
7501    /// The generator bounds how often it answers for *one* cycle
7502    /// ([`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS)); this
7503    /// function bounds how many cycles one request may set going. Neither stands in for the other —
7504    /// the first bounds repeats, the second bounds breadth.
7505    async fn handle_ssa_recommit(
7506        &self,
7507        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
7508        session_slot: &SessionSlot,
7509        msg: SsaServerCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixDepositPayload>,
7510    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
7511        // The wire bounds the *runs* a request carries, not the number of cycles they are spread
7512        // over — one run of 8 bytes can name a whole cycle — so without this a single packet names
7513        // every retained cycle and is answered with a full commitment burst for each. The generator's
7514        // per-cycle attempt cap does not bound that: it bounds repeats of one cycle, not breadth
7515        // across cycles.
7516        //
7517        // The same cap as the new-SSA path, so repairing a batch can never cost more than committing
7518        // to it did, and the Exit's own requests name a single cycle. Dropped rather than refused
7519        // with `refuse_ssa_request`: the peer is already inside its own commitment deadline and
7520        // learns nothing from a refusal it does not learn from that, and replying at all would hand
7521        // back some of the amplification the request was reaching for.
7522        let max_ssas_per_request = self.cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request;
7523        if msg.missing.len() > max_ssas_per_request {
7524            return Err(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
7525                "Exit asked for retransmissions across {} SSA cycles in a single request, at most \
7526                 {max_ssas_per_request} allowed",
7527                msg.missing.len()
7528            ))
7529            .into());
7530        }
7531
7532        let pix_toolbox = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
7533        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
7534        let session_id = msg.session_id;
7535
7536        // Cycles named here whose publication never completed. Decided before anything is sent, and
7537        // answered once for all of them: resuming publishes every member that is owed, not only the
7538        // ones this request names, and the ones it names are then not also answered with a scoped
7539        // re-send — their whole burst has just gone out, and a second answer would spend another of
7540        // the cycle's retransmissions on parts the Exit now has.
7541        let cut_short: Vec<SsaIndex> = session_slot
7542            .current_ssa_state
7543            .get()
7544            .map(|state| {
7545                state
7546                    .unpublished_indices()
7547                    .into_iter()
7548                    .filter(|ssa_index| msg.missing.contains_key(ssa_index))
7549                    .collect()
7550            })
7551            .unwrap_or_default();
7552
7553        // A resumption's failure is kept rather than returned at once. The cycles of this request
7554        // that were published in full are repairs of their own, and a resumption the transport cut
7555        // short is no reason to make them wait a whole re-request interval. It is reported once they
7556        // have been sent.
7557        let resumed = match session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() {
7558            Some(ssa_state) if !cut_short.is_empty() => {
7559                tracing::info!(%session_id, ?cut_short, "a re-request names cycles whose publication was cut short — resuming it");
7560                resume_publication(
7561                    session_id,
7562                    pseudonym,
7563                    &session_slot.routing_opts,
7564                    ssa_state,
7565                    &pix_toolbox,
7566                    &mut msg_sender,
7567                )
7568                .await
7569            }
7570            _ => Ok(()),
7571        };
7572
7573        for (ssa_index, runs) in msg.missing {
7574            if cut_short.contains(&ssa_index) {
7575                continue;
7576            }
7577
7578            // Rebuilt from the bytes that went out the first time, so the peer's already-filled slots
7579            // see a re-delivery rather than a contradiction.
7580            let pix_toolbox_clone = pix_toolbox.clone();
7581            let commitment = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
7582                move || pix_toolbox_clone.share_generator.recommit(&pseudonym, ssa_index, runs),
7583                "client_ssa_recommitment",
7584            )
7585            .await
7586            .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?
7587            .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)?;
7588
7589            let commitment_msgs =
7590                SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, commitment).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
7591            let num_messages = commitment_msgs.len();
7592
7593            for commitment_msg in commitment_msgs {
7594                send_via_msg_sender(
7595                    &mut msg_sender,
7596                    session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
7597                    HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(commitment_msg),
7598                    "re-sent client SSA commitment message",
7599                )
7600                .await?;
7601            }
7602
7603            info!(%session_id, %ssa_index, num_messages, "re-sent the requested SSA commitment parts");
7604        }
7605
7606        resumed
7607    }
7608
7609    /// Handled by the Entry, when the Exit sends PIX initiation request
7610    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, msg))]
7611    async fn handle_ssa_request(
7612        &self,
7613        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
7614        msg: SsaServerCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixDepositPayload>,
7615    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
7616        let Some(pix_toolbox) = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned() else {
7617            return Err(SessionManagerError::UnsupportedMessage.into());
7618        };
7619
7620        if pseudonym != msg.session_id {
7621            error!(%pseudonym, %msg.session_id, "received SSA server commitment for a different session");
7622            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
7623        }
7624
7625        // Deliberately narrower than the dispatch filter's `SsaRequest` arm
7626        // (`ssa_request_names_local_state`), which additionally requires the slot to be an outgoing
7627        // (`Forward`) one: a compliant peer never sends an `SsaRequest` to an Exit-side (Return)
7628        // slot, so dispatch drops that case outright, and re-checking the variant here would only
7629        // re-decide what dispatch already decided on the same in-memory state. This guard is the
7630        // backstop for the state changing between the two — a message that sat queued long enough
7631        // for the session it names to close, or for a `pending_outgoing` initiation to be removed —
7632        // and for callers that bypass dispatch entirely. Refusing here rather than after the wait
7633        // below is what kept a flood of bogus requests from parking the shared handler pool.
7634        if self.sessions.get(&msg.session_id).is_none() && !self.pending_outgoing.contains_key(&msg.session_id) {
7635            trace!(session_id = %msg.session_id, "refusing an SSA request for a session this node does not hold");
7636            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
7637        }
7638
7639        // The SsaRequest can arrive before new_session() or handle_incoming_session_initiation
7640        // has finished allocating the session slot, since both SessionEstablished and SsaRequest
7641        // are sent by the Exit back-to-back and processed concurrently by the Start protocol handler.
7642        // Instead of busy-looping, await the allocation notification for this specific SessionId.
7643        let session_slot = {
7644            use std::collections::hash_map::Entry;
7645            let session_id = msg.session_id;
7646            let waiter_deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
7647            loop {
7648                if Instant::now() >= waiter_deadline {
7649                    debug!(%session_id, "session slot waiter deadline exceeded");
7650                    return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
7651                }
7652                // Optimistic cache check
7653                if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
7654                    break slot;
7655                }
7656
7657                // Register a waiter under the lock, then recheck the cache to avoid the
7658                // TOCTOU race between the initial cache check and waiter registration.
7659                let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel::<()>();
7660                {
7661                    let mut map = self.slot_allocated.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
7662                    // Recheck while holding the lock: the slot may have been inserted
7663                    // between the optimistic check and now. If so, don't register.
7664                    if self.sessions.get(&session_id).is_some() {
7665                        drop(map);
7666                        continue;
7667                    }
7668
7669                    // At most one request per Session waits here; any other is refused at once, for
7670                    // the reason `ssa_request_locks` below is only `try_lock`ed. The dispatch filter
7671                    // admits every request naming a pending initiation, and each one waiting here
7672                    // parks a shared Start handler — so whoever holds SURBs for the pseudonym could
7673                    // occupy all of them before the slot exists. A conforming Exit sends only its
7674                    // opening request before then; a retransmission names commitments that only an
7675                    // existing slot can have sent.
7676                    let waiters = map.entry(session_id).or_default();
7677                    if waiters.iter().any(|w| !w.is_canceled()) {
7678                        return Err(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
7679                            "an SSA request for {session_id} is already waiting for its session slot"
7680                        ))
7681                        .into());
7682                    }
7683                    waiters.push(tx);
7684                }
7685
7686                let timeout = futures_time::time::Duration::from(Duration::from_millis(1000));
7687                match rx.timeout(timeout).await {
7688                    Ok(Ok(())) => {
7689                        // Notified — recheck the cache
7690                        continue;
7691                    }
7692                    _ => {
7693                        // Timeout or the sender was dropped (cancelled). Clean up our
7694                        // waiter entry to avoid unbounded accumulation in the map.
7695                        let mut map = self.slot_allocated.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
7696                        if let Entry::Occupied(mut e) = map.entry(session_id) {
7697                            e.get_mut().retain(|w| !w.is_canceled());
7698                            if e.get().is_empty() {
7699                                e.remove();
7700                            }
7701                        }
7702                        drop(map);
7703
7704                        // Final cache recheck before giving up — the slot might have
7705                        // been inserted while we were cleaning up.
7706                        if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
7707                            break slot;
7708                        }
7709
7710                        debug!(%session_id, "session slot not found after awaiting allocation");
7711                        return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
7712                    }
7713                }
7714            }
7715        };
7716
7717        debug!(
7718            num_server_commitments = msg.commitments.len(),
7719            "received Exit SSA commitments"
7720        );
7721
7722        // Cap how many SSAs a single request may ask us to commit to.
7723        //
7724        // The wire format alone permits `MAX_SSAS_PER_REQUEST` (27) commitments per message, and
7725        // every accepted entry costs a full `new_ssa_commitment` (hundreds of thousands of EC
7726        // commitments) plus thousands of outbound `SsaCommit` packets, and emits its own
7727        // `ReadyToDeposit` — i.e. its own on-chain deposit. Without a cap, a single packet from a
7728        // misbehaving Exit amplifies into minutes of Entry CPU, a large packet burst, and up to 27
7729        // simultaneous deposits bounded only by the per-deposit allocation limit.
7730        //
7731        // Rejecting the whole message rather than the surplus is deliberate: a truncated batch would
7732        // leave the Exit holding reconstructor cycles for indices it will never receive commitments
7733        // for, which its own kill switch then has to clean up.
7734        let max_ssas_per_request = self.cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request;
7735        if msg.commitments.len() > max_ssas_per_request {
7736            let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
7737                "Exit requested {} SSA commitments in a single request, at most {max_ssas_per_request} allowed",
7738                msg.commitments.len()
7739            ));
7740            self.refuse_ssa_request(msg.session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone())
7741                .await;
7742            return Err(error.into());
7743        }
7744
7745        let Some(ssa_state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() else {
7746            return Err(
7747                SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!("no SSA state for session {}", msg.session_id)).into(),
7748            );
7749        };
7750        let our_params = ssa_state.params;
7751
7752        // The Entry enforces that the Exit's SSA parameters match exactly the ones we offered in the
7753        // Session Initiation message.  Negotiation (accepting an Exit-chosen quota within our
7754        // bounds) is not implemented, so any mismatch is rejected.
7755        //
7756        // The whole quadruple is compared rather than the scalar quota it implies.  Quota equality
7757        // was once argued to be sufficient — the Exit does not pick the dimensions independently, so
7758        // a matching product implied matching `(polys, shares)` from any Exit running unmodified
7759        // code.  The quota now prices three of the four, so it is no longer blind to the surplus,
7760        // but it is still a product: it cannot tell `polys x threshold` from a transposition of the
7761        // two, and those are not interchangeable to the protocol.  Comparing the params is both
7762        // stricter and simpler, and costs nothing now that all four travel together.
7763        //
7764        // The fourth, the curve suite, is why the Entry needs no separate curve check of its own:
7765        // the Exit refused a foreign suite before it sent this message, and an Exit that echoed a
7766        // different one back than the Entry offered fails right here.
7767        //
7768        // Malformed params never reach this comparison as a mismatch: `dimensions()` fails first,
7769        // and that failure takes the same refusal path, so the Exit is told either way rather than
7770        // being left waiting on a dropped packet.
7771        let server_params = match msg.dimensions() {
7772            Ok(params) => params,
7773            Err(error) => {
7774                self.refuse_ssa_request(msg.session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone())
7775                    .await;
7776                return Err(
7777                    SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!("Exit sent malformed PIX parameters: {error}")).into(),
7778                );
7779            }
7780        };
7781        if our_params != server_params {
7782            let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
7783                "Exit sent unacceptable PIX parameters {server_params} (ours are {our_params})"
7784            ));
7785            self.refuse_ssa_request(msg.session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone())
7786                .await;
7787            return Err(error.into());
7788        }
7789        // A request naming missing commitment parts asks for nothing new — see
7790        // `SsaServerCommitmentMessage` — and none of what follows may run for it.
7791        //
7792        // That placement is the whole safety argument for reusing this message. The successor gate
7793        // below would refuse an index that is *already* being served, which is every index a
7794        // retransmission can name; the served-packet gate prices service against a batch nobody is
7795        // asking for; and `new_ssa_commitment` rejects an index at or below the watermark, which
7796        // again is every index this can name. Above this line is what a retransmission does need:
7797        // the pseudonym check, the session slot, and the parameter comparison.
7798        if !msg.missing.is_empty() {
7799            return self.handle_ssa_recommit(pseudonym, &session_slot, msg).await;
7800        }
7801
7802        let quota_per_ssa = pix_params_to_quota(&our_params);
7803
7804        // Everything from here to the end of the batch is serialised per pseudonym. Start messages run
7805        // under `for_each_concurrent`, so the successor gate below would otherwise be read by several
7806        // requests before any of them advanced it, and every one would pass. See `ssa_request_locks`.
7807        //
7808        // Taken without waiting. A request that finds the lock held is one the Exit is going to send
7809        // again — a repeat of the batch being committed right now, or a request racing it — and
7810        // queueing behind the holder would park a `for_each_concurrent` slot for as long as that
7811        // holder runs: the near-miss wait below, or generating a commitment (a fraction of a second per
7812        // cycle at the deployed dimensions, longer for wide dimensions or a full batch). The
7813        // Exit re-sends an unanswered request every few seconds, so a queue of them would be a lever
7814        // on exactly those slots. Dropping it costs nothing: either the holder admits the batch and the
7815        // repeat is moot, or it does not and the repeat is the next attempt.
7816        //
7817        // Kept after the recommit branch, which needs no serialisation and must stay reachable while
7818        // the commitment it repairs is still being published. And kept after the slot waiter above:
7819        // `ssa_request_locks` is uncapped, so taking it any earlier would let a request naming a
7820        // pseudonym with no Session create an entry, for as long as the cache's idle timer holds it.
7821        let request_lock = self
7822            .ssa_request_locks
7823            .get_with(pseudonym, async { Arc::new(futures::lock::Mutex::new(())) })
7824            .await;
7825        let Some(_request_guard) = request_lock.try_lock_owned() else {
7826            let error =
7827                SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!("another SSA request for {pseudonym} is being processed"));
7828            tracing::debug!(session_id = %msg.session_id, %error, "dropped an SSA request that found the request lock held");
7829            return Err(error.into());
7830        };
7831
7832        // A request that asks for what has already been committed to. It comes first under the lock,
7833        // before either half of the successor gate, because neither half has anything to say about it.
7834        //
7835        // Two things look the same from the watermark and are not. A *repeat* names the batch this
7836        // Session committed to last: the Exit re-sends an unanswered successor request until a part of
7837        // every member's commitment reaches it, so once one is admitted the re-sends already in flight
7838        // arrive at an Entry that has nothing left to do for them. For a batch that was published in
7839        // full they succeed without effect — no second burst, no second `ReadyToDeposit`, and above all
7840        // no second deposit. That holds while they arrive within `SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE` of the batch
7841        // last going out. A repeat that arrives later was sent after the bursts should have reached the
7842        // Exit, so one of them was lost after the transport took it. Every announced member's burst
7843        // then goes out again, still with no `ReadyToDeposit`. A batch whose publication was cut short
7844        // is the other exception: members still owed are published now, whole, and the repeat succeeds
7845        // only if that did (see `SessionSsaState::unpublished`); otherwise it is a non-fatal refusal
7846        // and the Exit's next re-send tries again. A *stale* request names indices at or below the
7847        // watermark that are not that batch; it is dropped, and is not `refuse_ssa_request`, since it
7848        // can be nothing worse than an Exit that lost track of what it asked for, which its own
7849        // deadlines already end. The one other way to have committed past the batch last recorded is
7850        // a batch that moved the generator and then failed to stage, and that failure ends the
7851        // Session instead (see phase two below).
7852        //
7853        // The opening batch has no watermark and passes this untouched.
7854        let first_asked = msg.commitments.keys().next().copied();
7855        if let Some(first) = first_asked
7856            && let Some(watermark) = ssa_state.committed_watermark()
7857            && first <= watermark
7858        {
7859            if ssa_state.last_committed_first() == Some(first) {
7860                if !ssa_state.unpublished_indices().is_empty() {
7861                    tracing::info!(
7862                        session_id = %msg.session_id, %first, %watermark,
7863                        "a repeat of an SSA request whose publication was cut short — resuming it"
7864                    );
7865                    let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
7866                    return resume_publication(
7867                        msg.session_id,
7868                        pseudonym,
7869                        &session_slot.routing_opts,
7870                        ssa_state,
7871                        &pix_toolbox,
7872                        &mut msg_sender,
7873                    )
7874                    .await;
7875                }
7876
7877                let lost = ssa_state.claim_republication(Instant::now(), SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE);
7878                if lost.is_empty() {
7879                    tracing::debug!(
7880                        session_id = %msg.session_id, %first, %watermark,
7881                        "ignored a repeat of an SSA request this Session already committed to"
7882                    );
7883                    return Ok(());
7884                }
7885
7886                tracing::info!(
7887                    session_id = %msg.session_id, %first, %watermark, members = ?lost,
7888                    "a repeat of an SSA request long after it was published — re-sending its commitments"
7889                );
7890                let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
7891                return republish_commitments(
7892                    msg.session_id,
7893                    pseudonym,
7894                    &session_slot.routing_opts,
7895                    ssa_state,
7896                    &pix_toolbox,
7897                    &mut msg_sender,
7898                    lost,
7899                )
7900                .await;
7901            }
7902
7903            let error = SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
7904                "Exit asked for SSAs from {first}, at or below the committed {watermark}, and the batch last \
7905                 committed to starts at {:?}",
7906                ssa_state.last_committed_first()
7907            ));
7908            SsaRefusal::Stale.log(
7909                ssa_state.note_refusal(first_asked, SsaRefusal::Stale),
7910                &msg.session_id,
7911                &error,
7912            );
7913            return Err(error.into());
7914        }
7915
7916        // Successor gate, the Entry's half of the one in `SessionPixSupervisor`. A correct Exit asks
7917        // for the next batch when the *last* cycle of the current one is nearly recovered, by which
7918        // point we have long been emitting that cycle's shares. An Exit that asks earlier is asking
7919        // for deposits it cannot have earned, so nothing here commits and nothing is deposited.
7920        //
7921        // Two conditions, and the second is what the first alone cannot give. Emission must have
7922        // reached the last committed cycle — which, with the window clamped to one cycle, means every
7923        // earlier one is exhausted — *and* it must be far enough into that cycle. Checking only the
7924        // index admitted a successor batch on the last cycle's very first share, i.e. ~0 % of the way
7925        // through the batch rather than the ~79 % at which a conforming Exit asks. That is nearly a
7926        // whole cycle of unearned deposits, on a gate whose entire purpose is to prevent them.
7927        //
7928        // The boundary is derived rather than guessed — see `min_emission_for_early_recovery`, which
7929        // accounts for the Exit counting *polynomials* and for emission running in lockstep windows
7930        // that spend their whole surplus before the next window starts. A flat fraction of the cycle
7931        // gets this badly wrong in the unsafe direction: 0.85 over the 3.47× surplus factor is 24.5 %,
7932        // against a true boundary of 78.6 % at the deployed dimensions.
7933        //
7934        // Being early is refused rather than fatal, and deliberately not via `refuse_ssa_request`,
7935        // which closes the Session: that message is dropped as `NotAdmitted` and the Session left
7936        // running. A correct Exit never lands there. One that does is not told, but it is not lost
7937        // either: the Exit's supervisor sends an unanswered successor request again every
7938        // `ssa_request_resend_interval` while the batch before it is still being served, so the same
7939        // request is admitted as soon as emission has caught up, and an Exit that never sends it again
7940        // has its own deadline for the cycles it already allocated. Either way nothing is paid for
7941        // before it is earned. Lost generator state is the one arm that *is* fatal, for the reason
7942        // given at it.
7943        //
7944        // First index rather than each: `commitments` is a `BTreeMap`, so the lowest index leads, and
7945        // checking it before the loop is also what stops a batch that fails partway from having
7946        // already emitted `ReadyToDeposit` for its earlier members.
7947        //
7948        // Computed at the protocol floor rather than at our own reconstructor's threshold. The value
7949        // that decides when a correct Exit asks is *its* setting, which does not travel on the wire;
7950        // gating on ours refused a peer configured lower, silently — two valid configurations that
7951        // could not talk, and which the Exit's re-sends only turn from fatal into a stream of refusals
7952        // until emission catches up. See `MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD`, which every Exit is held to by
7953        // `validate_pix_supervision` and which is therefore the earliest any conforming peer can ask.
7954        let min_emitted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
7955            &our_params,
7956            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
7957        );
7958        match pix_toolbox.share_generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym) {
7959            Some(progress) if !progress.is_serving_last_committed() || progress.front_emitted < min_emitted => {
7960                let error = SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
7961                    "Exit asked for SSAs from {first_asked:?} while emission has reached {:?} ({} of {min_emitted} \
7962                     shares needed for an early-recovery signal) of the batch committed up to {}",
7963                    progress.highest_emitted, progress.front_emitted, progress.last_committed
7964                ));
7965                SsaRefusal::Early.log(
7966                    ssa_state.note_refusal(first_asked, SsaRefusal::Early),
7967                    &msg.session_id,
7968                    &error,
7969                );
7970                return Err(error.into());
7971            }
7972            // No generator state, but this Session has committed before: the entry was discarded
7973            // under us and the gate above has nothing left to measure.
7974            //
7975            // Absent state is otherwise the ordinary opening batch, which is why the gate treats it as
7976            // admissible — and that is the whole of the hole this closes. The generator keeps its
7977            // per-pseudonym entry in a cache with an idle retention, refreshed by share *emission*; a
7978            // Session kept alive on KeepAlives alone while the Entry sends nothing outlives it. An Exit
7979            // that arranges exactly that gets the successor gate deleted rather than merely relaxed —
7980            // no emission boundary, and no monotonic index either, since the discarded entry took the
7981            // high-watermark with it — and can then farm a fresh deposit per retention period.
7982            //
7983            // Terminal rather than a dropped message. The polynomials for the committed cycles went
7984            // with the entry, so `next_share` yields nothing and no share of them will ever be emitted:
7985            // whatever the Exit deposited against them is already unrecoverable and this half of the
7986            // Session can make no further PIX progress. Refusing quietly would leave the Exit to
7987            // discover that by timing out on commitments we have decided never to send.
7988            None if session_slot
7989                .current_ssa_state
7990                .get()
7991                .and_then(SessionSsaState::committed_watermark)
7992                .is_some() =>
7993            {
7994                let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
7995                    "generator state for {pseudonym} was discarded while the Session was live; the cycles committed \
7996                     up to {:?} can no longer be served",
7997                    session_slot
7998                        .current_ssa_state
7999                        .get()
8000                        .and_then(SessionSsaState::committed_watermark)
8001                ));
8002                warn!(session_id = %msg.session_id, %error, "refused an SSA request against lost generator state");
8003                self.refuse_ssa_request(msg.session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone())
8004                    .await;
8005                return Err(error.into());
8006            }
8007            _ => {}
8008        }
8009
8010        // Second half of the successor gate, and the one that measures the Exit rather than us.
8011        //
8012        // Emission above is this node's own work: it counts shares handed to the local packet
8013        // pipeline by `create_surb_for_path`, a consumption that is not even rolled back when the
8014        // rest of the packet build fails. An Exit that requests, is funded, and then returns nothing
8015        // still walks that counter forward for as long as we keep sending, so on its own it prices
8016        // deposits against work we did to ourselves.
8017        //
8018        // What is checked here is service that actually arrived. A share is encrypted with the first
8019        // relayer's challenge solution and rides a return SURB, so the Exit can only decrypt it by
8020        // *using* that SURB — one returned packet is one SURB consumed is one share unlocked. The
8021        // Exit cannot inflate this without unlocking exactly as many shares, which advances the
8022        // recovery it is claiming to have made. Nothing it reports is trusted.
8023        //
8024        // Skipped before the first commitment: the opening batch is the one nothing has been paid
8025        // for yet, and there is no service to have been rendered against it.
8026        if let Some(state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get()
8027            && let Some(watermark) = state.committed_watermark()
8028        {
8029            let shares_per_cycle = our_params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * our_params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
8030            let target = (watermark.get() as u64 - 1) * shares_per_cycle + min_emitted;
8031
8032            // Discounted, because the Exit unlocks a share when the *first relayer* acknowledges,
8033            // which is upstream of us: every packet lost after that point is progress it legitimately
8034            // has and we cannot see. Demanding the undiscounted figure would refuse conforming Exits
8035            // on any lossy path.
8036            //
8037            // By the loss a cycle actually survives, not by the surplus ratio `s/(t+s)` this used to
8038            // take. The ratio is break-even — the loss at which a polynomial receives `t` shares on
8039            // average — and a cycle needs every polynomial to clear it, so at break-even it fails. At
8040            // the deployed `4096 × (32 + 79)` the ratio is 71.2 % against a tolerance of 50.3 % — a
8041            // cycle losing 71.2 % of its shares does not recover — and discounting by it put the bar
8042            // at 23.9 % of a cycle's packets, below even the 111 424 shares a lossless Exit must have
8043            // unlocked to reach its early-recovery point. The tolerance puts the mean at 41.3 %; the bound
8044            // below sets the bar at 41.0 %.
8045            //
8046            // The discount is also what an Exit can withhold for as long as it likes and still have
8047            // every next deposit funded — one whose first return relayer is its own acknowledges each
8048            // packet, unlocking the share, and drops it. So it is the design tolerance and no more:
8049            // the loss the negotiated surplus carries at the 99 % target `default_surplus_for` sizes
8050            // it to. That is the tolerance the *Entry* bought, as insurance against the return
8051            // relayers it picked — one expecting unreliable relayers buys more surplus and thereby
8052            // loosens its own gate. How strict the gate is follows from that choice; it is not a knob
8053            // of its own, and the Exit, which judges an offer by its quota alone, does not set it.
8054            //
8055            // Not at the mean of what an Exit losing that much returns, though, but well below it. One
8056            // losing exactly the tolerance downstream of its first return relayer still unlocks every
8057            // share and asks at the lossless boundary, and the packets of it that reach us are
8058            // `Binomial(target, 1 − L)`: short of their mean half the time, and at the deployed split
8059            // one time in five by more than the near-miss window below — refused at once, and left to
8060            // the Exit's next re-send to retry rather than to the Session's deadline.
8061            // `SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS` standard deviations under the mean make that negligible
8062            // for a fraction of a percent more that an Exit can withhold. The deviation is the same
8063            // binomial's, so the bound still follows the split the Entry chose; a split without
8064            // surplus is demanded its whole target.
8065            let required = successor_required_packets(target, our_params.tolerated_share_loss());
8066
8067            let served = |slot: &SessionSlot| {
8068                state.served_since_first_commit(slot.returned_packets.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed))
8069            };
8070            let mut observed = served(&session_slot);
8071
8072            if observed < required {
8073                // A conforming Exit asks the instant its reconstructor crosses the threshold, and the
8074                // request travels the same mixed path as the packets that earned it — so it can
8075                // overtake the last few of them. Refusing that is not free even though the Exit
8076                // re-sends: the next one is an interval away (`ssa_request_resend_interval`, the
