8077                // Exit's setting, 3 s by default), and on a path that is merely a few packets behind
8078                // it would have been admitted at once. A short wait costs nothing and saves the
8079                // interval.
8080                //
8081                // Entered only for a near miss, and that is what keeps the wait from being a lever:
8082                // this handler runs under a bounded `for_each_concurrent` and holds the
8083                // per-pseudonym request lock, so an Exit must already have returned all but one
8084                // emission window of what it owes to occupy either. Anything further out is refused
8085                // on the spot, at no cost to us.
8086                //
8087                // One window rather than a fraction of `required`: it is the unit emission advances
8088                // in, so a shortfall below it is genuinely in-flight, and a percentage would round to
8089                // zero at exactly the small dimensions where this matters most.
8090                let near_miss = observed > 0 && required - observed <= hopr_protocol_pix::SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64;
8091                if near_miss {
8092                    let deadline = Instant::now() + SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT;
8093                    while observed < required && Instant::now() < deadline {
8094                        hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_POLL).await;
8095                        observed = served(&session_slot);
8096                    }
8097                }
8098            }
8099
8100            if observed < required {
8101                let error = SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
8102                    "Exit asked for SSAs having returned {observed} of the {required} packets its batch committed up \
8103                     to {watermark} has been paid for"
8104                ));
8105                SsaRefusal::UnderServed.log(
8106                    ssa_state.note_refusal(first_asked, SsaRefusal::UnderServed),
8107                    &msg.session_id,
8108                    &error,
8109                );
8110                return Err(error.into());
8111            }
8112        }
8113
8114        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
8115        let session_id = msg.session_id;
8116
8117        // The server can theoretically send multiple SSA commitments asking us to make the equal
8118        // number of client commitments and deposits, and the batch is all-or-nothing: either every
8119        // member gets a commitment and a `ReadyToDeposit`, or none does.
8120        //
8121        // Hence three phases rather than one loop. Interleaving them meant a batch whose *second*
8122        // exit commitment failed to decode had already sent the first member's `SsaCommit` burst and
8123        // emitted its `ReadyToDeposit` — an on-chain deposit instruction — before the failure was
8124        // reached. The Exit, whose own request was rejected as a whole, has no cycle to spend it on.
8125        //
8126        // The server is authoritative in giving the ssa_index; the client only verifies that it is
8127        // strictly monotonic. That monotonicity is enforced inside `new_ssa_commitment` in phase two,
8128        // which rejects any `ssa_index` that is `<=` the last one generated for this pseudonym with
8129        // `PixError::InvalidInput` (see `SsaShareGenerator::new_ssa_commitment`). Because that call
8130        // happens in a phase before anything is published, a stale, duplicate, or out-of-order
8131        // `SsaRequest` cannot cause a deposit — the whole message is rejected first. The
8132        // per-pseudonym baseline lives in the generator's `polynomials` cache (30-min idle TTL,
8133        // refreshed on every use), so it persists for the life of an active session. Gaps (an index
8134        // strictly greater than the last, but not the immediate successor) are allowed by design,
8135        // since the Exit may advance by more than one SSA at a time.
8136
8137        // Phase 1 — validate. Decoding is the only step that consumes attacker-supplied bytes:
8138        // `try_into_pix_group` decompresses the point and rejects anything outside the prime-order
8139        // subgroup. Doing every one of them up front is what makes a malformed later member cost
8140        // nothing, and it is cheap relative to phase two.
8141        // Taken out before the loop consumes `msg.commitments`, and drained as the loop goes: an SSA
8142        // is committed to once, so its deposit data is needed once.
8143        let mut deposit_payloads = msg.deposit_data;
8144
8145        let mut validated = Vec::with_capacity(msg.commitments.len());
8146        for (ssa_index, exit_commitment) in msg.commitments {
8147            trace!(ssa_index, "received Exit SSA commitment");
8148            match exit_commitment.try_into_pix_group() {
8149                Ok(point) => validated.push((ssa_index, point)),
8150                Err(error) => {
8151                    // Terminal, like every other unacceptable-parameter case here. A peer that cannot
8152                    // produce a valid group element is not going to produce one on a retry, and the
8153                    // Exit would otherwise wait out `max_ssa_delivery_time` on commitments that are
8154                    // never coming.
8155                    let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
8156                        "Exit sent an undecodable SSA commitment for index {ssa_index}: {error}"
8157                    ));
8158                    self.refuse_ssa_request(session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone())
8159                        .await;
8160                    return Err(error.into());
8161                }
8162            }
8163        }
8164
8165        // Phase 2 — stage. Generates every client commitment and derives every deposit address,
8166        // publishing none of them. This is the expensive phase, and it still mutates the generator:
8167        // `new_ssa_commitment` appends to the per-pseudonym polynomial queue. Failing here therefore
8168        // leaves queued polynomials the Exit never learns of — wasted work rather than a leaked
8169        // deposit instruction, and the generator's own monotonic index keeps them from being mistaken
8170        // for a later cycle's. That same index makes a failure after the first member was generated
8171        // the end of the Session, below.
8172        let watermark_before = ssa_state.committed_watermark();
8173        let mut staged: Vec<(AgreedSsaQuota, CommitmentBurst)> = Vec::with_capacity(validated.len());
8174        let staging: errors::Result<()> = async {
8175            for (ssa_index, exit_point) in validated {
8176                // Use the global `pix_toolbox.share_generator` to generate the client
8177                // commitment. The generator is shared with the packet pipeline's
8178                // `next_share`, so polynomials created here will be used when the
8179                // pipeline embeds PIX shares into return-path SURBs.
8180                //
8181                // The generator dimension (polys × threshold) must match what the
8182                // Exit's reconstructor expects — both are set from the session's
8183                // negotiated PIX params (pix_global_config on Entry → SsaRequest
8184                // params on Exit).  If the client sends commitments that exceed the
8185                // Exit's expected dimensions, the Exit rejects them as InvalidInput.
8186                let pix_toolbox_clone = pix_toolbox.clone();
8187                let client_commitment = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
8188                    move || {
8189                        pix_toolbox_clone
8190                            .share_generator
8191                            .new_ssa_commitment(&pseudonym, ssa_index)
8192                    },
8193                    "client_ssa_commitment",
8194                )
8195                .await
8196                .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?
8197                .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)?;
8198
8199                // The generator has been advanced for this index, so the Session records it now rather
8200                // than after the publish phase. Recording it early is the safe direction: the watermark
8201                // only ever makes the successor gate stricter, and a batch abandoned between here and
8202                // publication has still moved the generator.
8203                if let Some(state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() {
8204                    state.note_committed(
8205                        ssa_index,
8206                        session_slot.returned_packets.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
8207                    );
8208                }
8209
8210                // Construct the full SSA by adding the client and exit commitments, getting the deposit address
8211                let full_ssa = client_commitment.ssa_commitment + exit_point;
8212                let deposit_address = HoprPixSpec::group_to_deposit_address(full_ssa).ok_or(
8213                    SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("failed to convert SSA to deposit address")),
8214                )?;
8215
8216                // Split the SSA client commitment into Start protocol commitment messages
8217                let commitment_msgs = SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, client_commitment)
8218                    .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
8219                debug!(%ssa_index, count = commitment_msgs.len(), "generated client SSA commitment messages");
8220
8221                // What `ReadyToDeposit` will say, fixed here with the address. Kept whole so that a
8222                // publication that is cut short can still announce it later: nothing about it can be
8223                // derived again once this request is gone, the deposit data least of all.
8224                let quota = AgreedSsaQuota {
8225                    ssa_id: SsaId::new(pseudonym, ssa_index),
8226                    deposit_address,
8227                    quota_per_ssa,
8228                    // Rebuilt rather than carried: the `id` is not on the wire, because this message
8229                    // already says which Session and which SSA these bytes belong to.
8230                    deposit_data: PixDepositData {
8231                        id: PixAddressId::new(&pseudonym, ssa_index),
8232                        data: deposit_payloads
8233                            .remove(&ssa_index)
8234                            .map(|payload| payload.0)
8235                            .unwrap_or_default(),
8236                    },
8237                };
8238                staged.push((quota, commitment_msgs));
8239            }
8240            Ok(())
8241        }
8242        .await;
8243        if let Err(error) = staging {
8244            // Nothing generated yet means nothing moved, and the Exit's next re-send tries the whole
8245            // batch again. Once a member has been generated, though, the batch can never be committed.
8246            // The generator refuses that member's index for good, so every re-send of this request
8247            // would be dropped as stale until the Exit's deadline closed the Session,
8248            // and meanwhile the polynomials it queued would go on to be emitted for a cycle whose
8249            // commitment the Exit never receives. Terminal, like lost generator state, and for the
8250            // same reason: this half of the Session can make no further PIX progress.
8251            if ssa_state.committed_watermark() != watermark_before {
8252                tracing::error!(
8253                    %session_id, %error,
8254                    "staging an admitted SSA batch failed after part of it was generated; it can never be committed"
8255                );
8256                self.refuse_ssa_request(session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone())
8257                    .await;
8258            }
8259            return Err(error);
8260        }
8261
8262        // Recorded once phase two has staged the whole request, and before anything is published: a
8263        // burst that then fails to send has still moved the generator, and the re-sends of this request
8264        // must be recognised as repeats of it. See `SessionSsaState::last_committed_first`. The same
8265        // moment records every member as owed its publication, which is what lets a repeat finish the
8266        // job when phase three is cut short.
8267        ssa_state.stage_unpublished(staged.iter().map(|(quota, _)| quota.clone()));
8268        if let Some((quota, _)) = staged.first() {
8269            ssa_state.note_committed_first(quota.ssa_id.ssa_index());
8270        }
8271
8272        // Phase 3 — publish. Nothing below can fail on the *content* of the request; only the
8273        // transport can, and under ordinary backpressure it does: a send gives up after
8274        // `EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT`. A failed send does not fail the Session. The member being published
8275        // goes back to the owed set and a non-fatal `NotAdmitted` is returned, logged once at `warn!`;
8276        // members after it were never claimed and stay owed too. What happens next is up to the Exit,
8277        // which has two ways to ask again: its automatic repeat of this request, sent only while some
8278        // member of the batch has reported nothing and the batch is behind the front, and its scoped
8279        // re-request for a member whose commitment began to arrive, which works wherever the batch
8280        // stands and resumes every owed member, not only the one named, but only when the member it
8281        // names is itself still owed, because its own burst was cut part-way. Two cases are therefore
8282        // not recovered. A member of which no message went out, whose batch holds the front (the
8283        // opening batch always does), is resumed only as a side effect of a re-request for an earlier
8284        // member of the same batch that is itself still owed. And a member whose whole burst went out
8285        // but whose `ReadyToDeposit` could not be queued prompts no request at all, since the Exit
8286        // already holds its complete commitment. In both the Exit's own deadline ends the cycle, and
8287        // nothing is stranded for that member because nothing was announced for it. See
8288        // `SessionSsaState::unpublished` and `resume_publication`.
8289        for (staged_quota, burst) in staged {
8290            // Claimed just before its burst, so that nobody else can publish this member while this
8291            // call is doing so, and so that only the claimant announces it.
8292            let ssa_index = staged_quota.ssa_id.ssa_index();
8293            let Some(claim) = ssa_state.claim_unpublished(ssa_index) else {
8294                tracing::debug!(%ssa_index, "another task is already publishing this SSA's commitment");
8295                continue;
8296            };
8297
8298            match publish_commitment(
8299                &pix_toolbox,
8300                &mut msg_sender,
8301                &session_slot.routing_opts,
8302                burst,
8303                &claim.quota,
8304                "client SSA commitment message",
8305            )
8306            .await
8307            {
8308                Ok(()) => ssa_state.complete_publication(claim, Instant::now()),
8309                Err(error) => return Err(publication_cut_short(session_id, ssa_state, claim, &error)),
8310            }
8311        }
8312
8313        trace!(quota_per_ssa, "Exit commitment message has been fully processed");
8314        Ok(())
8315    }
8316}

8339    /// A [`PixToolbox`] whose deposit-data requests are answered, for tests that do not read the
8340    /// PIX event stream themselves.
8341    ///
8342    /// An Exit cannot send an `SsaRequest` without the pool answering, so a test that only needs the
8343    /// request to *happen* would otherwise be asserting against `MissingDepositData`.
8344    fn pix_toolbox_with_pool(
8345        generator: Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
8346        reconstructor: Arc<SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>>,
8347    ) -> PixToolbox {
8348        let (toolbox, events) = PixToolbox::new(generator, reconstructor);
8349        // The answering task owns `events`, and lives until the toolbox is dropped. The forwarded
8350        // stream is discarded: these tests do not read PIX events.
8351        drop(crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(events, |_| Vec::new()));
8352        toolbox
8353    }

8383    #[test]

8403    /// The head-of-line bound must reach a session that cannot recover a missing frame, and must
8404    /// not reach one that can.
8405    ///
8406    /// Both halves matter. Without the first, a session with no retransmission holds every frame
8407    /// behind a gap for the full frame timeout, waiting for something that is never coming —
8408    /// measured on a cluster as 98.5 % of bytes arriving over the wire and 0.60 % reaching the
8409    /// application. Without the second, a session that *would* have retransmitted the gap instead
8410    /// abandons it, turning recoverable frames into loss.
8411    #[test]
8412    fn session_config_should_bound_the_gap_only_without_retransmission() {
8413        assert_eq!(
8414            SessionManagerConfig::default().max_frames_behind_gap,
8415            Some(256),
8416            "the default must bound the gap, or the stall stays in place unless opted out of"
8417        );
8418
8419        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
8420            max_frames_behind_gap: Some(8),
8421            ..Default::default()
8422        };
8423
8424        for reliable in [Capability::RetransmissionAck, Capability::RetransmissionNack] {
8425            assert_eq!(
8426                session_config(&cfg, reliable.into()).max_frames_behind_gap,
8427                None,
8428                "{reliable:?} can recover the gap, so the wait is productive and must be left alone"
8429            );
8430        }
8431
8432        for unreliable in [Capabilities::empty(), Capability::Segmentation.into()] {
8433            assert_eq!(
8434                session_config(&cfg, unreliable).max_frames_behind_gap,
8435                Some(8),
8436                "without retransmission the gap must be bounded"
8437            );
8438        }
8439    }

8441    /// The right value tracks throughput x latency spread, which is a property of the *session*,
8442    /// not of the node: a bulk data session and a control session on the same node have entirely
8443    /// different reordering depths. A caller that knows its own traffic must be able to say so.
8444    #[test]
8445    fn a_session_should_be_able_to_override_the_nodes_gap_bound() {
8446        let node = SessionManagerConfig {
8447            max_frames_behind_gap: Some(256),
8448            ..Default::default()
8449        };
8450
8451        assert_eq!(
8452            session_config_with(&node, Capabilities::empty(), Some(16)).max_frames_behind_gap,
8453            Some(16),
8454            "the session's own value must win over the node default"
8455        );
8456        assert_eq!(
8457            session_config_with(&node, Capabilities::empty(), None).max_frames_behind_gap,
8458            Some(256),
8459            "saying nothing must inherit the node default"
8460        );
8461        assert_eq!(
8462            session_config_with(&node, Capabilities::empty(), Some(0)).max_frames_behind_gap,
8463            None,
8464            "zero disables the bound for this session, matching the env knob's semantics"
8465        );
8466    }

8468    /// A per-session override must not be able to re-enable the bound where waiting is productive.

8470    fn a_session_override_should_not_reach_a_session_that_can_retransmit() {
8471        let node = SessionManagerConfig::default();
8472        assert_eq!(
8473            session_config_with(&node, Capability::RetransmissionAck.into(), Some(4)).max_frames_behind_gap,
8474            None,
8475            "retransmission can recover the gap, so no caller should be able to cut the wait short"
8476        );

8502    /// Balancer state with the given target sitting at the given level.
8503    fn gate_state(target: u64, buffer_level: u64) -> BalancerStateValues {
8504        let state = BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
8505            target_surb_buffer_size: target,
8506            ..Default::default()
8507        });
8508        state
8509            .buffer_level
8510            .store(buffer_level, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
8511        state
8512    }

8514    /// A packet short enough to have room for a SURB. `max_surbs_with_message` is
8515    /// `(PAYLOAD_SIZE - len) / SURB_SIZE`, so anything past roughly half the payload already caps
8516    /// itself at zero and would make the assertions below pass for the wrong reason.
8517    fn small_outgoing_packet() -> anyhow::Result<ApplicationDataOut> {
8518        let data = ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG, b"short")?);
8519        anyhow::ensure!(
8520            data.estimate_surbs_with_msg() >= 1,
8521            "fixture must have room for a SURB, otherwise the cap is not what is being measured"
8522        );
8523        Ok(data)
8524    }
8525
8526    /// `account_incoming_surbs` must keep the estimator's held count (`saturating_diff`) equal to
8527    /// what a bounded store of capacity `CAP` would actually hold across a fill-past-capacity-then-drain
8528    /// sequence. The eviction term is what makes the held count fall back to zero once the overflow is
8529    /// drained -- and so what stops the keep-alive report and the PIX fill reserve from reading a level
8530    /// that never falls.
8531    #[test]
8532    fn account_incoming_surbs_tracks_a_bounded_store_through_overflow_and_drain() {
8533        const CAP: u64 = 100;
8534        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
8535        let mut occupancy: u64 = 0;
8536
8537        let mut receive = |batch: u64| {
8538            let evicted = (occupancy + batch).saturating_sub(CAP);
8539            occupancy = (occupancy + batch).min(CAP);
8540            account_incoming_surbs(&estimator, batch, evicted);
8541        };
8542
8543        for _ in 0..5 {
8544            receive(40);
8545        }
8546        assert_eq!(occupancy, CAP, "the model store is full");
8547        assert_eq!(
8548            estimator.saturating_diff(),
8549            CAP,
8550            "held count tracks a full store, not the {}-SURB total received",
8551            5 * 40
8552        );
8553
8554        for _ in 0..CAP {
8555            estimator.consumed.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
8556            occupancy -= 1;
8557        }
8558        assert_eq!(occupancy, 0, "the model store is empty");
8559        assert_eq!(
8560            estimator.saturating_diff(),
8561            0,
8562            "held count returns to zero after the drain; the evicted surplus is not counted as held"
8563        );
8564    }
8565
8566    /// The gate primitive itself mints whenever the level is below the effective target. A level
8567    /// short of target with no capacity inferred yet still mints -- the stop for a smaller-than-target
8568    /// store comes from inferring its capacity over successive reports (see
8569    /// `a_plateau_below_target_infers_the_counterparty_capacity` in `balancer/controller.rs`), which
8570    /// lowers the effective target rather than changing this primitive.
8571    #[test]
8572    fn organic_minting_continues_below_target_without_an_inferred_capacity() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
8573        const EXIT_CAPACITY: u64 = 500;
8574        const ENTRY_TARGET: u64 = 2_000;
8575
8576        let mut data = small_outgoing_packet()?;
8577        cap_organic_surbs(&mut data, 1, &gate_state(ENTRY_TARGET, EXIT_CAPACITY));
8578
8579        assert_eq!(Some(1), data.packet_info.map(|i| i.max_surbs_in_packet));
8580        assert_eq!(
8581            1,
8582            data.estimate_surbs_with_msg(),
8583            "below the effective target with no inferred capacity, the Entry mints"
8584        );
8585        Ok(())
8586    }

8588    #[test]
8589    fn cap_organic_surbs_should_zero_the_packet_once_the_counterparty_is_at_target() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
8590        let mut data = small_outgoing_packet()?;
8591        cap_organic_surbs(&mut data, 1, &gate_state(100, 200));
8592
8593        assert_eq!(Some(0), data.packet_info.map(|i| i.max_surbs_in_packet));
8594        assert_eq!(
8595            0,

8751    /// The Exit's balancer is not paced at its start. It holds the SURBs the Entry sends and paces the
8752    /// Exit's own egress; the fill of an empty counterparty is the Entry's to pace, and the Exit's
8753    /// incoming-session path is not where that is armed.
8754    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
8755    async fn an_exit_balancer_is_not_paced_at_start() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
8756        for (offer, balancing, why) in [
8757            (no_pix_offer(), true, "a rate-controlled session"),
8758            (
8759                StartInitiation {
8760                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl),
8761                    ..no_pix_offer()
8762                },
8763                false,
8764                "a session that opts out of rate control",
8765            ),

8767            let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
8768                started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, None)?;

8772            {

8777                assert_eq!(
8778                    balancing,

8783                    !slot.surb_mgmt.refill_pacing_active(),

8788            sender.close_channel();

8795    trait SendMsg {
8796        async fn send_message(
8797            &self,
8798            routing: DestinationRouting,
8799            data: ApplicationDataOut,
8800        ) -> crate::errors::Result<()>;

8803    mockall::mock! {
8804        MsgSender {}
8805        impl SendMsg for MsgSender {
8806            fn send_message<'a, 'b>(&'a self, routing: DestinationRouting, data: ApplicationDataOut)
8807            -> BoxFuture<'b, crate::errors::Result<()>> where 'a: 'b, Self: Sync + 'b;
8808        }

8810
8811    fn mock_packet_planning(
8812        sender: MockMsgSender,
8813    ) -> (
8814        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
8815        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
8816    ) {
8817        let (tx, rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
8818        let handle = tokio::task::spawn(async move {
8819            pin_mut!(rx);
8820            while let Some((routing, data)) = rx.next().await {
8821                sender.send_message(routing, data).await?;
8822            }
8823            Ok(())
8824        });
8825        (tx, handle)
8826    }

8828    /// What the packet pipeline reports for a keep-alive the Entry sent: it carried every SURB that fits
8829    /// beside the message. The Exit books those, and the mock transports that stand in for the pipeline
8830    /// have to say how many there were, as a real packet does.
8831    fn keep_alive_packet_info(data: &ApplicationData) -> IncomingPacketInfo {
8832        IncomingPacketInfo {
8833            num_saved_surbs: hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPacket::max_surbs_with_message(data.total_len()),
8834            ..Default::default()
8835        }
8836    }

8838    fn msg_type(data: &ApplicationDataOut, expected: StartProtocolDiscriminants) -> bool {

8840            .map(|d| StartProtocolDiscriminants::from(d) == expected)
8841            .unwrap_or(false)
8842    }

8844    fn start_msg_match(data: &ApplicationDataOut, msg: impl Fn(HoprStartProtocol) -> bool) -> bool {
8845        HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
8846            .map(msg)
8847            .unwrap_or(false)

8850    /// Waits (bounded) until the manager reports no active sessions.
8851    ///
8852    /// The session-slot rollback runs on a spawned task, so its effect is observed
8853    /// asynchronously; this polls [`SessionManager::active_sessions`] until it drains.
8854    async fn wait_for_no_active_sessions(
8855        mgr: &SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
8856    ) -> bool {
8857        for _ in 0..50 {
8858            if mgr.active_sessions().is_empty() {
8859                return true;
8860            }
8861            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
8862        }
8863        mgr.active_sessions().is_empty()
8864    }
8865
8866    const SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY: usize = 10000;
8867
8868    /// Waits (bounded) until `admission` has recorded at least `count` retires of `pseudonym`.
8869    ///
8870    /// The retire is deferred past the SURB-resolution window by [`release_session_slot`], and the
8871    /// teardown that asks for it does not always run on the test's own task — the slot-guard rollback
8872    /// removes the slot on a spawned task, and the cache's eviction listener runs on moka's
8873    /// maintenance thread — so a test that counts immediately after triggering a teardown would race
8874    /// it twice over. Polling keeps the test honest about the ordering it actually asserts (retire
8875    /// happens, and after the admit) without sleeping a fixed delay in every test that touches the
8876    /// seam. `surb_retire_grace`'s one-second margin is what bounds the wait below the ten-second
8877    /// ceiling even when a test keeps the default `surb_resolution_wait`.
8878    async fn wait_for_retire(admission: &RecordingAdmission, pseudonym: &SessionId, count: usize) -> usize {
8879        for _ in 0..200 {
8880            let retired = admission.retired(pseudonym);
8881            if retired >= count {
8882                return retired;
8883            }
8884            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
8885        }
8886        admission.retired(pseudonym)
8887    }

8889    /// A return packet the Exit counted as consumed, and routing resolution then dropped for want of a
8890    /// SURB, spent nothing. Its refund counts the SURB as given back in the estimator that counted it,
8891    /// on a counter of its own rather than one fewer consumed: the balancer reads the counters as deltas
8892    /// between samples and rejects a snapshot in which one of them went down. The held count takes the
8893    /// SURB back; the balancer's delta does not (see `a_refund_should_not_raise_the_balancer_level`).
8894    #[test]
8895    fn a_counted_return_packet_should_give_its_surb_back_to_the_estimator_that_counted_it() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
8896        use crate::balancer::{SimpleSurbFlowEstimator, SurbFlowEstimator};
8897
8898        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
8899        estimator.produced.fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
8900        let data = count_return_packet_surb(&estimator, small_outgoing_packet()?);
8901        assert!(data.surb_refund.is_counted(), "a counted packet carries its refund");
8902        assert_eq!(9, estimator.saturating_diff(), "counted as it was handed on");
8903
8904        let before = SimpleSurbFlowEstimator::from(&estimator);
8905        data.surb_refund.give_back();
8906        assert_eq!(
8907            10,
8908            estimator.saturating_diff(),
8909            "the starved packet's SURB is back in the held count"
8910        );
8911        assert_eq!(
8912            Some(0),
8913            SimpleSurbFlowEstimator::from(&estimator).estimated_surb_buffer_change(&before),
8914            "every counter still grows, and the balancer's delta leaves the refund out"
8915        );
8916        Ok(())
8917    }

8980    /// Verifies that a self-initiated session is rejected with `SessionManagerError::Loopback`.
8981    ///
8982    /// ## Steps
8983    /// 1. Alice's manager is started with a mock transport that delivers messages back to itself.
8984    /// 2. Alice initiates a session toward `bob_peer`; the mock routes her `StartSession` back to her own manager
8985    ///    (simulating a network loopback).
8986    /// 3. Alice's manager processes `StartSession` as incoming, auto-responds with `SessionEstablished`, and the mock
8987    ///    delivers it back to complete the handshake.
8988    /// 4. `new_session` returns `Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Loopback))`.
8989    /// 5. Exactly one active session is present — the incoming slot accepted from the self-delivered `StartSession`.
8990    ///    The rejection fires after slot insertion, not before.
8991    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
8992    async fn session_manager_should_not_allow_loopback_sessions() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
8993        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
8994        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
8995
8996        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
8997
8998        let mut sequence = mockall::Sequence::new();
8999        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
9000
9001        // Alice sends the StartSession message
9002        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
9003        alice_transport
9004            .expect_send_message()
9005            .once()
9006            .in_sequence(&mut sequence)
9007            .withf(move |peer, data| {
9008                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
9009                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
9010            })
9011            .returning(move |_, data| {
9012                // But the message is again processed by Alice due to Loopback
9013                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
9014                Box::pin(async move {
9015                    alice_mgr_clone
9016                        .dispatch_message(
9017                            alice_pseudonym,
9018                            ApplicationDataIn {
9019                                data: data.data,
9020                                packet_info: Default::default(),
9021                            },
9022                        )
9023                        ?;
9024                    Ok(())
9025                })
9026            });
9027
9028        // Alice sends the SessionEstablished message (as Bob)
9029        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
9030        alice_transport
9031            .expect_send_message()
9032            .once()
9033            .in_sequence(&mut sequence)
9034            .withf(move |peer, data| {
9035                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished)
9036                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == alice_pseudonym)
9037            })
9038            .returning(move |_, data| {
9039                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
9040
9041                Box::pin(async move {
9042                    alice_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
9043                        alice_pseudonym,
9044                        ApplicationDataIn {
9045                            data: data.data,
9046                            packet_info: Default::default(),
9047                        },
9048                    )?;
9049                    Ok(())
9050                })
9051            });
9052
9053        // Start Alice
9054        let (new_session_tx_alice, new_session_rx_alice) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
9055        let (alice_sender, alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
9056        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_alice, None, None)?;
9057        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
9058
9059        let alice_session = alice_mgr
9060            .new_session(
9061                bob_peer,
9062                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9063                SessionClientConfig {
9064                    capabilities: None.into(),
9065                    pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
9066                    surb_management: None,
9067                    ..Default::default()
9068                },
9069            )
9070            .await;
9071
9072        println!("{alice_session:?}");
9073        assert!(matches!(
9074            alice_session,
9075            Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Loopback))
9076        ));
9077        // There is one session in the manager, which is the incoming one that Alice's manager
9078        // accepted when it received the StartSession message from itself.
9079        assert_eq!(alice_mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1);
9080
9081        drop(new_session_rx_alice);
9082
9083        // Cleanup: close sender and await handle
9084        alice_sender.close_channel();
9085        alice_handle.await??;
9086
9087        Ok(())
9088    }
9089
9090    /// A failed initiation must leave no `pending_outgoing` marker behind: the marker is what lets
9091    /// an `SsaRequest` for the pseudonym wait for a slot at dispatch, and a marker outliving its
9092    /// attempt would park a handler on a Session that never arrives — one per leaked attempt, for
9093    /// as long as the entry's TTL. The marker was once cleared by hand on each failure path and
9094    /// keyed by the peer-supplied `session_id`; the guard that replaces it removes it keyed by the
9095    /// pseudonym it was inserted under, on every path.
9096    ///
9097    /// ## Steps
9098    /// 1. The transport swallows the `StartSession` message, so the initiation is never answered and times out (the
9099    ///    deterministic failure path; a loopback needs a live manager for it to bounce off).
9100    /// 2. `new_session` under a fixed pseudonym fails with `Timeout`.
9101    /// 3. An `SsaRequest` naming that pseudonym must be dropped as stale at dispatch — no marker left to admit it.
9102    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
9103    async fn a_failed_session_initiation_must_leave_no_pending_outgoing_marker() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9104        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
9105
9106        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
9107            initiation_timeout_base: Duration::from_millis(100),
9108            ..Default::default()
9109        };
9110        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(cfg);
9111
9112        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
9113        // Swallow the StartSession: the initiation times out.
9114        alice_transport
9115            .expect_send_message()
9116            .once()
9117            .withf(move |peer, data| {
9118                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
9119                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
9120            })
9121            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
9122
9123        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
9124        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
9125        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
9126        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
9127
9128        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
9129        let result = alice_mgr
9130            .new_session(
9131                bob_peer,
9132                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9133                SessionClientConfig {
9134                    capabilities: None.into(),
9135                    pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
9136                    surb_management: None,
9137                    ..Default::default()
9138                },
9139            )
9140            .await;
9141        assert!(
9142            matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)),
9143            "the fixture must actually fail the initiation, got {result:?}"
9144        );
9145
9146        // With no marker left, the same request a fast Exit could have raced ahead of is refused at
9147        // dispatch instead of parking a handler on a slot that will never exist.
9148        let refused = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
9149        assert!(
9150            matches!(refused, DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage)),
9151            "an SsaRequest for a failed initiation's pseudonym must be stale, got {refused:?}"
9152        );
9153
9154        Ok(())
9155    }

9157    /// A second initiation for a pseudonym already claimed by one in flight must be refused, not
9158    /// silently overwrite the first one's `pending_outgoing` reservation.
9159    ///
9160    /// `moka`'s `insert` overwrites an existing entry, so the claim the first initiation holds used
9161    /// to be a single shared marker: whichever attempt finished first removed it while the other
9162    /// was still awaiting establishment, and an `SsaRequest` for that Session then failed the
9163    /// dispatch filter and was dropped as `StaleStartMessage` — a false negative, the exact class
9164    /// of miss the filter must not have. `new_session` therefore claims the name atomically and
9165    /// refuses the overlap.
9166    ///
9167    /// ## Steps
9168    /// 1. Alice's transport swallows the first `StartSession` (expectation `.once()`), so that initiation stays in
9169    ///    flight; its `pending_outgoing` marker is held by its guard.
9170    /// 2. A second `new_session` under the SAME pseudonym must fail with `Unacceptable` — and must not have sent
9171    ///    anything (the refusal happens before the send).
9172    /// 3. The refusal must not have consumed a challenge slot: `session_initiations.entry_count()` stays at 1, the
9173    ///    first attempt's reservation.
9174    /// 4. The first initiation still owns the marker (its `SsaRequest` dispatches as in flight), and then times out
9175    ///    cleanly, leaving no marker and no challenge reservation behind.
9176    ///
9177    /// Sequential rather than `tokio::join!`-concurrent: the property pinned is that the *second*
9178    /// call sees the first one's live claim, which is what the atomic compute serialises — running
9179    /// them concurrently would only randomise which call is "first" without strengthening the
9180    /// assertion, while the in-flight fixture (swallowed send) requires the first call to be
9181    /// parked in its await for the second to observe the claim.
9182    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
9183    async fn a_second_initiation_for_a_pending_pseudonym_must_be_refused_without_consuming_a_challenge_slot()
9184    -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9185        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
9186
9187        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
9188            initiation_timeout_base: Duration::from_millis(100),
9189            ..Default::default()
9190        };
9191        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(cfg);
9192
9193        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
9194        // Swallow the FIRST StartSession only: that initiation stays in flight holding its claim.
9195        // The refused attempt must never reach the transport, so `.once()` also pins that.
9196        alice_transport
9197            .expect_send_message()
9198            .once()
9199            .withf(move |peer, data| {
9200                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
9201                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
9202            })
9203            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
9204
9205        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
9206        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
9207        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
9208        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
9209
9210        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
9211        let client_cfg = SessionClientConfig {
9212            capabilities: None.into(),
9213            pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
9214            surb_management: None,
9215            ..Default::default()
9216        };
9217
9218        // Park the first initiation in flight: the transport swallowed its StartSession, so it
9219        // holds both its challenge reservation and its pending-outgoing claim for the whole of
9220        // this call's initiation timeout.
9221        let in_flight = alice_mgr.new_session(
9222            bob_peer,
9223            SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9224            client_cfg.clone(),
9225        );
9226        futures::pin_mut!(in_flight);
9227
9228        // Poll the in-flight attempt exactly once, which runs it up to its first await: the claim
9229        // (and the challenge reservation) are taken before the send, so a single pending poll is
9230        // enough to make the overlap observable — no sleeps, and no runtime-dependent ordering.
9231        assert!(
9232            futures::poll!(in_flight.as_mut()).is_pending(),
9233            "fixture: the swallowed StartSession must leave the initiation pending"
9234        );
9235
9236        // The first attempt's claim is live: an SsaRequest naming the pseudonym is admitted at
9237        // dispatch as belonging to an initiation this node is still making (it goes to the handler
9238        // pool rather than being dropped as stale).
9239        let admitted = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
9240        assert!(
9241            matches!(admitted, DispatchResult::Processed),
9242            "an SsaRequest for the in-flight initiation must be admitted, got {admitted:?}"
9243        );
9244
9245        let before = {
9246            // moka defers the write op: without this the count is read before the insertion lands.
9247            alice_mgr.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
9248            alice_mgr.session_initiations.entry_count()
9249        };
9250        assert_eq!(
9251            before, 1,
9252            "fixture: the in-flight initiation must hold exactly one challenge reservation"
9253        );
9254
9255        // The overlap: the same pseudonym, still pending. Must be refused, not allowed to
9256        // overwrite the first attempt's reservation.
9257        let refused = alice_mgr
9258            .new_session(
9259                bob_peer,
9260                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9261                client_cfg,
9262            )
9263            .await;
9264        assert!(
9265            matches!(
9266                refused,
9267                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
9268            ),
9269            "a second initiation under a pending pseudonym must be refused as Unacceptable, got {refused:?}"
9270        );
9271
9272        // The refusal happened after the challenge reservation but before the send, and released
9273        // its own reservation: exactly the in-flight one remains, none consumed by the refusal.
9274        alice_mgr.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
9275        let after = alice_mgr.session_initiations.entry_count();
9276        assert_eq!(
9277            after, before,
9278            "the refused attempt must not consume a challenge slot (before: {before}, after: {after})"
9279        );
9280        assert_eq!(
9281            alice_mgr.num_active_sessions(),
9282            0,
9283            "neither attempt may have allocated a session slot"
9284        );
9285
9286        // The first initiation is unaffected by the refusal and still owns the claim.
9287        let still_admitted = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
9288        assert!(
9289            matches!(still_admitted, DispatchResult::Processed),
9290            "the refusal must not have cleared the in-flight initiation's claim, got {still_admitted:?}"
9291        );
9292
9293        // The in-flight initiation then times out cleanly: no marker, no challenge reservation.
9294        let timed_out = in_flight.await;
9295        assert!(
9296            matches!(timed_out, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)),
9297            "the first initiation must still fail on its own timeout, got {timed_out:?}"
9298        );
9299        assert_eq!(
9300            {
9301                alice_mgr.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
9302                alice_mgr.session_initiations.entry_count()
9303            },
9304            0,
9305            "the timed-out initiation must release its challenge reservation"
9306        );
9307        let stale = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
9308        assert!(
9309            matches!(stale, DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage)),
9310            "after the timeout, the pseudonym's marker must be gone, got {stale:?}"
9311        );
9312
9313        Ok(())
9314    }

9316    /// Verifies that a session initiation returns `TransportSessionError::Timeout` when the peer
9317    /// never processes or responds to the `StartSession` message.
9318    ///
9319    /// ## Steps
9320    /// 1. Alice's manager is configured with `initiation_timeout_base: 100ms`. Bob's manager is started but its mock
9321    ///    transport silently swallows all messages (never dispatches to the manager).
9322    /// 2. Alice calls `new_session`; her `StartSession` is captured by the mock and silently discarded.
9323    /// 3. The 100ms timeout expires; `new_session` returns `Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)`.
9324    /// 4. `num_active_sessions` is 0, confirming no orphaned slot was left in the cache.
9325    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
9326    async fn session_manager_should_timeout_new_session_attempt_when_no_response() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9327        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();

9329        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {

9339        let bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
9340
9341        // Alice sends the StartSession message, but Bob does not handle it

9343            .expect_send_message()
9344            .once()
9345            .in_sequence(&mut sequence)
9346            .withf(move |peer, data| {
9347                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
9348                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
9349            })
9350            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
9351
9352        // Start Alice
9353        let (new_session_tx_alice, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
9354        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);

9360        let (bob_sender, _bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
9361        bob_mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_bob, None, None)?;
9362        assert!(bob_mgr.is_started());
9363
9364        let result = alice_mgr
9365            .new_session(
9366                bob_peer,
9367                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9368                SessionClientConfig {

9370                    pseudonym: None,
9371                    surb_management: None,

9373                },

9383    /// Verifies that a failed incoming session establishment does not register any telemetry.
9384    ///
9385    /// ## Steps
9386    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is started with the `telemetry` feature enabled.
9387    /// 2. The new-session notification channel's receiver is dropped immediately, so notifying about a new incoming
9388    ///    session will fail.

9390    ///    notifying about the new session fails (receiver is gone).
9391    /// 4. `wait_for_no_active_sessions` polls until there are no active sessions, confirming the partially-inserted
9392    ///    slot was rolled back.
9393    /// 5. `num_active_sessions` is 0, proving the rollback prevented any telemetry registration for the failed session.
9394    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9395    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
9396    async fn failed_incoming_session_establishment_does_not_register_telemetry() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9397        let mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
9398
9399        let transport = MockMsgSender::new();
9400        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
9401        drop(new_session_rx);
9402        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
9403        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
9404        assert!(mgr.is_started());
9405
9406        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
9407        let result = mgr
9408            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
9409                pseudonym,
9410                StartInitiation {
9411                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
9412                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9413                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capabilities::empty()),
9414                    additional_data: 0,
9415                },
9416            )
9417            .await;
9418
9419        assert!(result.is_err());
9420
9421        // The slot inserted before the failure must be rolled back, so it neither
9422        // counts towards `maximum_sessions` nor registers any telemetry.
9423        assert!(
9424            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
9425            "the partially established session slot was not rolled back"
9426        );
9427        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
9428
9429        // Cleanup: close sender and await handle
9430        sender.close_channel();
9431        _handle.await??;
9432
9433        Ok(())
9434    }

9436    /// Verifies that a session slot is rolled back if session setup fails after the slot is inserted.
9437    ///
9438    /// ## Steps
9439    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is started; the new-session notification channel's receiver is dropped, so notifying about
9440    ///    a new incoming session will fail.
9441    /// 2. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with a random pseudonym. The slot is inserted into the cache
9442    ///    first, then notifying about the new session fails (because the receiver is gone).
9443    /// 3. The call returns an error, and `wait_for_no_active_sessions` confirms the slot was removed.
9444    /// 4. `num_active_sessions` is 0, proving the rollback removed the slot and freed the pseudonym.
9445    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
9446    async fn session_manager_should_roll_back_slot_when_incoming_session_setup_fails() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9447        let mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
9448
9449        // Drop the receiver so that notifying about the new incoming session fails
9450        // *after* the session slot has already been inserted into the cache.
9451        let transport = MockMsgSender::new();
9452        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
9453        drop(new_session_rx);
9454        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
9455        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
9456        assert!(mgr.is_started());
9457
9458        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
9459
9460        // The setup fails after the slot is inserted (notifying about the new
9461        // incoming session errors out because the receiver is gone), so the slot
9462        // must be rolled back instead of lingering until idle eviction.
9463        let result = mgr
9464            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
9465                pseudonym,
9466                StartInitiation {
9467                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
9468                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9469                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
9470                    additional_data: 0,
9471                },
9472            )
9473            .await;
9474        assert!(result.is_err());
9475
9476        // An empty active-session set proves the slot was removed and, since
9477        // sessions are keyed by pseudonym, that the pseudonym is free again.
9478        assert!(
9479            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
9480            "the partially established session slot was not rolled back"
9481        );
9482
9483        // Cleanup
9484        sender.close_channel();
9485        handle.await??;
9486
9487        Ok(())
9488    }

9490    /// Collects everything that arrives on `rx` during `window`, returning once it elapses.
9491    async fn originated_during(
9492        rx: &mut futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
9493        window: Duration,
9494    ) -> Vec<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> {
9495        let mut collected = Vec::new();
9496        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + window;
9497        while let Ok(Some(item)) = timeout(
9498            deadline.saturating_duration_since(tokio::time::Instant::now()),
9499            rx.next(),
9500        )
9501        .await
9502        {
9503            collected.push(item);
9504        }
9505        collected
9506    }
9507
9508    /// The manager floors the keep-alive period at [`MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD`], so this
9509    /// is as fast as an Exit keep-alive can be made to run, and it sets the pace of these tests.
9510    const KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD: Duration = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
9511
9512    type RecordingManager = SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>;
9513    type Originated = futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>;
9514
9515    /// Brings up an Exit-side session and returns once its keep-alive stream is observably running.
9516    ///
9517    /// The "observably running" part is load-bearing for every caller: `nothing was originated` is
9518    /// equally true of a stream that stopped and one that never started, so a test that does not
9519    /// first establish the stream is alive proves nothing when it later sees silence.
9520    ///
9521    /// The Exit's level report goes only to an Entry that has shown it refills, and only while the
9522    /// Exit holds a SURB to send it on (see [`PixFillControl::admit`]). Nothing here runs an Entry, so
9523    /// the fixture stands in for both: the Session is marked as refilled and given a stock of SURBs
9524    /// to report from, which is what an Entry's first keep-alive would have done.
9525    async fn exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
9526        cfg: SessionManagerConfig,
9527        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
9528    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
9529        RecordingManager,
9530        Originated,
9531        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
9532        HoprPseudonym,
9533    )> {
9534        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
9535            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
9536            ..cfg
9537        });
9538
9539        if let Some(admission) = admission {
9540            assert!(
9541                mgr.set_surb_admission(admission),
9542                "a freshly constructed fixture manager must accept the SURB admission seam"
9543            );
9544        }
9545
9546        let (msg_tx, mut msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
9547        // Returned rather than dropped: a second establishment on the same manager — the
9548        // pseudonym-reuse test — would otherwise fail its notification and roll back.
9549        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
9550        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
9551
9552        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
9553        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
9554            pseudonym,
9555            StartInitiation {
9556                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
9557                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9558                // Empty capabilities keep rate control on, which is what spawns the balancer and
9559                // the keep-alive stream. `NoRateControl` would skip both and make this vacuous.
9560                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capabilities::empty()),
9561                additional_data: 0,
9562            },
9563        )
9564        .await?;
9565
9566        // The reports are one SURB each; this outlasts every test that uses the fixture many times over.
9567        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
9568        slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
9569        slot.surb_estimator
9570            .produced
9571            .fetch_add(1_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9572        drop(slot);
9573
9574        let observed = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 2 + Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
9575        let keep_alives = observed
9576            .iter()
9577            .filter(|(routing, data)| {
9578                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::KeepAlive)
9579                    && matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if p == &pseudonym)
9580            })
9581            .count();
9582        anyhow::ensure!(
9583            keep_alives > 0,
9584            "no return-routed keep-alive was originated, so this test cannot tell a stopped stream from one that \
9585             never ran; {} message(s) were observed in total",
9586            observed.len()
9587        );
9588
9589        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, new_session_rx, pseudonym))
9590    }
9591
9592    /// How long the level reports of an Exit Session are watched: three notification periods, and half a
9593    /// second over so that the third report is not decided by a scheduling tick.
9594    const REPORT_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_millis(3_500);
9595
9596    /// SURBs the simulated Entry delivers. A keep-alive only carries as many as fit beside it, so the
9597    /// number the Exit ends up counting is read back from its estimate rather than assumed.
9598    const ENTRY_SURBS: usize = 3;
9599
9600    /// An Entry as the Exit has come to know it by the time its level reports are watched.
9601    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
9602    enum SimulatedEntry {
9603        /// An Entry whose SURB balancer is running: its keep-alives refill the Exit and carry `surbs`
9604        /// SURBs. `target_notify` says whether they announce its target (`BalancerTarget`) or not.
9605        Balancing { target_notify: bool, surbs: usize },
9606        /// An Entry with no SURB balancer: it sends no keep-alive, and its `surbs` SURBs arrived with
9607        /// data.
9608        WithoutBalancer { surbs: usize },
9609        /// An Entry with no SURB balancer that pings by hand (`ping_session`): its only keep-alives are
9610        /// marked as manual pings, and each carries `surbs` SURBs, as a real one does.
9611        PingingByHand { surbs: usize },
9612    }
9613
9614    /// What the Exit's level reports are expected to do.
9615    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
9616    enum Expect {
9617        /// They flow.
9618        Reports,
9619        /// They do not, until the Entry turns into a reader (a keep-alive carrying SURBs arrives).
9620        /// Silence alone proves nothing: a stream that never ran is as quiet, so the case then shows
9621        /// the reports start.
9622        SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
9623    }
9624
9625    /// A non-PIX Exit Session on a manager with the level reports on, with the Entry's announcement
9626    /// under the caller's control.
9627    ///
9628    /// `announced_target` is what the Entry puts in `StartInitiation::additional_data`.
9629    async fn exit_session_reporting_levels(
9630        capabilities: Capabilities,
9631        announced_target: u64,
9632    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
9633        RecordingManager,
9634        Originated,
9635        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
9636        HoprPseudonym,
9637    )> {
9638        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
9639            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
9640            ..Default::default()
9641        });
9642        let (msg_tx, msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
9643        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
9644        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
9645
9646        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
9647        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
9648            pseudonym,
9649            StartInitiation {
9650                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
9651                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
9652                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities),
9653                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(announced_target),
9654            },
9655        )
9656        .await?;
9657
9658        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, new_session_rx, pseudonym))
9659    }
9660
9661    /// Waits (bounded) until the Exit has handled a keep-alive from the Entry. The manager's Start
9662    /// protocol task does that after `dispatch_message` returns.
9663    async fn wait_for_counterparty_refills(mgr: &RecordingManager, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9664        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
9665            loop {
9666                if mgr
9667                    .sessions
9668                    .get(pseudonym)
9669                    .is_some_and(|slot| slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills())
9670                {
9671                    break;
9672                }
9673                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
9674            }
9675        })
9676        .await
9677        .context("the Exit never handled the Entry's keep-alive")
9678    }
9679
9680    /// The levels carried by the Exit's return-routed keep-alives for `pseudonym` over `window`, in the
9681    /// order they were sent.
9682    async fn level_reports_during(rx: &mut Originated, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, window: Duration) -> Vec<u64> {
9683        originated_during(rx, window)
9684            .await
9685            .iter()
9686            .filter(|(routing, _)| matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == pseudonym))
9687            .filter_map(|(_, data)| {
9688                match HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text).ok()? {
9689                    StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka) if ka.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState) => {
9690                        Some(ka.additional_data)
9691                    }
9692                    _ => None,
9693                }
9694            })
9695            .collect()
9696    }
9697
9698    /// Makes `entry` known to the Exit Session of `pseudonym`, and returns the SURBs the Exit counts.
9699    async fn show_exit_its_entry(
9700        mgr: &RecordingManager,
9701        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
9702        entry: SimulatedEntry,
9703    ) -> anyhow::Result<u64> {
9704        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
9705        match entry {
9706            SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify, surbs } => {
9707                let flags: KeepAliveFlags = if target_notify {
9708                    KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into()
9709                } else {
9710                    None.into()
9711                };
9712                dispatch_entry_keep_alive(mgr, pseudonym, flags, surbs, 0)?;
9713                wait_for_counterparty_refills(mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
9714            }
9715            SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs } => {
9716                // Its SURBs arrive with data, which books them like this and tells the Exit nothing
9717                // about a balancer.
9718                slot.surb_estimator
9719                    .produced
9720                    .fetch_add(surbs as u64, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9721                assert!(
9722                    !slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
9723                    "fixture: an Entry without a balancer has sent no keep-alive"
9724                );
9725            }
9726            SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs } => {
9727                // The Exit books the SURBs the ping carried, as with every Start message, but is told
9728                // nothing about a balancer.
9729                dispatch_entry_keep_alive(mgr, pseudonym, KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing.into(), surbs, 0)?;
9730            }
9731        }
9732        Ok(slot.surb_estimator.saturating_diff())
9733    }
9734
9735    /// The Exit's SURB-level reports follow what the Exit has seen of its Entry, for every kind of
9736    /// Session and every kind of Entry.
9737    ///
9738    /// A report spends one of the Session's SURBs, so it is sent only to an Entry that has shown it
9739    /// refills (any keep-alive from its balancer, whether or not it announces its target, but not a manual ping) and
9740    /// only while the Exit holds a SURB to send it on. What it says depends on whether the Exit runs a balancer:
9741    /// the balancer's level on a rate-controlled Session, the Exit's own count of its SURBs on a
9742    /// `NoRateControl` one, which has none.
9743    ///
9744    /// What the Entry announced when the Session was established decides nothing: the target is a
9745    /// figure the peer picks, and an Entry that announces one can still run no balancer
9746    /// (`d_entry_announcing_without_balancer`), or announce none and run one
9747    /// (`c_balancing_entry`, `c_balancing_entry_without_target_notify`).
9748    ///
9749    /// The cases that expect silence then let the Entry read, and want the reports to start: a stream
9750    /// that never ran would be as quiet.
9751    ///
9752    /// An Entry that only pings by hand (`a_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand`, `d_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand`)
9753    /// runs no balancer, though it sends keep-alives, and each of them brings SURBs. The mark on its pings
9754    /// is all that tells it from a balancing one, and the Exit stays quiet for it.
9755    #[rstest]
9756    #[case::a_balancing_entry(
9757        Capabilities::empty(),
9758        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9759        64,
9760        Expect::Reports
9761    )]
9762    #[case::a_balancing_entry_without_target_notify(
9763        Capabilities::empty(),
9764        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: false, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9765        64,
9766        Expect::Reports
9767    )]
9768    #[case::b_entry_without_balancer(
9769        Capabilities::empty(),
9770        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9771        64,
9772        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9773    )]
9774    #[case::c_balancing_entry(
9775        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9776        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9777        0,
9778        Expect::Reports
9779    )]
9780    #[case::c_balancing_entry_without_target_notify(
9781        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9782        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: false, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9783        0,
9784        Expect::Reports
9785    )]
9786    #[case::c_balancing_entry_announcing(
9787        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9788        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9789        64,
9790        Expect::Reports
9791    )]
9792    #[case::d_entry_without_balancer(
9793        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9794        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9795        0,
9796        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9797    )]
9798    #[case::d_entry_announcing_without_balancer(
9799        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9800        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9801        64,
9802        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9803    )]
9804    #[case::a_balancing_entry_empty_store(
9805        Capabilities::empty(),
9806        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: 0 },
9807        64,
9808        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9809    )]
9810    #[case::c_balancing_entry_empty_store(
9811        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9812        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: 0 },
9813        0,
9814        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9815    )]
9816    #[case::a_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand(
9817        Capabilities::empty(),
9818        SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9819        64,
9820        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9821    )]
9822    #[case::d_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand(
9823        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
9824        SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
9825        0,
9826        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads
9827    )]
9828    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
9829    async fn exit_level_reports_follow_the_entry(
9830        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
9831        #[case] entry: SimulatedEntry,
9832        #[case] announced: u64,
9833        #[case] expect: Expect,
9834    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
9835        let rate_controlled = !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl);
9836        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) =
9837            exit_session_reporting_levels(capabilities, announced).await?;
9838        let held = show_exit_its_entry(&mgr, pseudonym, entry).await?;
9839
9840        let levels = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, REPORT_WINDOW).await;
9841        match expect {
9842            Expect::Reports => {
9843                anyhow::ensure!(
9844                    held > 0,
9845                    "fixture: the Entry must have delivered SURBs for a report to be sent on"
9846                );
9847                anyhow::ensure!(
9848                    !levels.is_empty(),
9849                    "{entry:?} holds {held} SURB(s) of the Exit and refills it, yet no level report arrived over \
9850                     {REPORT_WINDOW:?}"
9851                );
9852                if rate_controlled {
9853                    // The Exit's balancer is running and the report is its level.
9854                    assert!(
9855                        levels.iter().all(|level| (1..=held).contains(level)),
9856                        "a rate-controlled Session reports its balancer's level, which is within 1..={held}: \
9857                         {levels:?}"
9858                    );
9859                } else {
9860                    // No balancer: the report is the Exit's own count, and every report spent one.
9861                    assert_eq!(
9862                        Some(held),
9863                        levels.first().copied(),
9864                        "a NoRateControl Session reports the SURBs it holds, not its balancer's unwritten zero: \
9865                         {levels:?}"
9866                    );
9867                    assert!(
9868                        levels.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[1] <= pair[0]),
9869                        "each report spent a SURB, so the count it carries cannot rise: {levels:?}"
9870                    );
9871                }
9872            }
9873            Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads => {
9874                assert!(
9875                    levels.is_empty(),
9876                    "{entry:?} gives the Exit no reason to report, yet it sent {} report(s) {levels:?}",
9877                    levels.len()
9878                );
9879
9880                if matches!(entry, SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { .. }) {
9881                    // Handled by now, over a window of several periods, so this is not just a ping
9882                    // that has yet to be looked at.
9883                    assert!(
9884                        !mgr.sessions
9885                            .get(&pseudonym)
9886                            .context("the session slot must exist")?
9887                            .surb_mgmt
9888                            .counterparty_refills(),
9889                        "a manual ping must not be taken for a sign that the Entry runs a balancer"
9890                    );
9891                }
9892
9893                // The Entry becomes a reader: a balancing one's keep-alive, carrying SURBs.
9894                dispatch_entry_keep_alive(&mgr, pseudonym, KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(), ENTRY_SURBS, 0)?;
9895                wait_for_counterparty_refills(&mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
9896
9897                let levels = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, REPORT_WINDOW).await;
9898                assert!(
9899                    !levels.is_empty(),
9900                    "the silence was the gate and not a dead stream: once the Entry refills the Exit and delivers \
9901                     SURBs, the reports must start, and none arrived over {REPORT_WINDOW:?}"
9902                );
9903            }
9904        }
9905
9906        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
9907        Ok(())
9908    }
9909
9910    /// Asserts `mgr` originates nothing further for `pseudonym`.
9911    ///
9912    /// Packets already handed to the sender before the closure are in flight rather than newly
9913    /// originated, so they are drained first and only what appears afterwards counts.
9914    async fn assert_no_further_origination(rx: &mut Originated, closure: &str) {
9915        let _in_flight = originated_during(rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
9916
9917        let window = KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 3;
9918        let after = originated_during(rx, window).await;
9919        assert!(
9920            after.is_empty(),
9921            "an Exit session closed by {closure} originated {} further packet(s) over {window:?} — each one is \
9922             return-routed to a pseudonym whose SURBs are gone, and one such packet is enough to stall all \
9923             origination on the node",
9924            after.len()
9925        );
9926    }
9927
9928    /// Records the `admit`/`retire` calls the manager makes, in order.
9929    ///
9930    /// Deliberately not mockall: the seam is two one-word methods on a trait whose implementations
9931    /// the tests assert about *sequentially* (admit must precede the retire that ends the Session),
9932    /// and a plain log the test can filter is easier to read than expectations wired against a
9933    /// sequence that cross-thread `Drop` validation cannot order anyway. The log is `Arc<Mutex<Vec>>`
9934    /// for the same reason the manager's own fields are: `admit` runs on whatever task commits the
9935    /// Session and `retire` on whatever task tears it down.
9936    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
9937    struct RecordingAdmission {
9938        events: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(String, SessionId)>>>,
9939        /// The tokens `admit` minted, in call order.
9940        ///
9941        /// Kept separate from the retires so each list answers one question: what admissions were
