9942        /// distinguished, and what a teardown actually presented. One combined list cannot — a
9943        /// retire's token would read as a mint, so a regression that presented the wrong token would
9944        /// hide behind the admit that also wrote the list.
9945        admit_tokens: Arc<Mutex<Vec<AdmissionToken>>>,
9946        /// The tokens `retire` presented, in call order.
9947        retire_tokens: Arc<Mutex<Vec<AdmissionToken>>>,
9948        /// The tokens `raise_target` presented, in call order.
9949        raise_tokens: Arc<Mutex<Vec<AdmissionToken>>>,
9950        /// The `expected_surbs` each `admit` was called with, in call order.
9951        admit_targets: Arc<Mutex<Vec<usize>>>,
9952        /// Mints the tokens `admit` returns, so each admission of a pseudonym is distinguishable —
9953        /// the property the token guard below pins.
9954        token_counter: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
9955    }
9956
9957    impl RecordingAdmission {
9958        fn admitted(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> usize {
9959            self.events
9960                .lock()
9961                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
9962                .iter()
9963                .filter(|(event, id)| event == "admit" && id == session_id)
9964                .count()
9965        }
9966
9967        fn retired(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> usize {
9968            self.events
9969                .lock()
9970                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
9971                .iter()
9972                .filter(|(event, id)| event == "retire" && id == session_id)
9973                .count()
9974        }
9975
9976        fn retire_precedes_admit(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> bool {
9977            let events = self.events.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
9978            match (
9979                events.iter().position(|(e, id)| e == "retire" && id == session_id),
9980                events.iter().position(|(e, id)| e == "admit" && id == session_id),
9981            ) {
9982                (Some(retired_at), Some(admitted_at)) => retired_at < admitted_at,
9983                _ => false,
9984            }
9985        }
9986
9987        /// The full `admit`/`retire` sequence recorded for `session_id`, in order.
9988        ///
9989        /// Counting admits and retires separately is not enough once a pseudonym can be reused: the
9990        /// property the store depends on is the *interleaving* — the teardown's retire must land
9991        /// between the two admits of a Session that was closed and re-established on the same
9992        /// pseudonym — and only the order of the log shows that.
9993        fn sequence(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> Vec<String> {
9994            self.events
9995                .lock()
9996                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
9997                .iter()
9998                .filter(|(_, id)| id == session_id)
9999                .map(|(event, _)| event.clone())
10000                .collect()
10001        }
10002
10003        /// Every token minted by an `admit` of this mock, in call order.
10004        ///
10005        /// Admissions of the same pseudonym must be distinguishable — that is what lets a deferred
10006        /// retire name the admission it belongs to rather than "whatever is admitted now".
10007        fn minted_tokens(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionToken> {
10008            self.admit_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
10009        }
10010
10011        /// The tokens presented by retires, in call order.
10012        fn retire_tokens(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionToken> {
10013            self.retire_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
10014        }
10015
10016        /// The `expected_surbs` each `admit` was called with, in call order.
10017        fn admitted_targets(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
10018            self.admit_targets.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
10019        }
10020
10021        /// The tokens presented by `raise_target`, in call order.
10022        fn raise_tokens(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionToken> {
10023            self.raise_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
10024        }
10025
10026        /// The targets `raise_target` was called with, in call order.
10027        fn raised_targets(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
10028            self.events
10029                .lock()
10030                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
10031                .iter()
10032                .filter_map(|(event, _)| event.strip_prefix("raise_target:")?.parse().ok())
10033                .collect()
10034        }
10035    }
10036
10037    impl SurbAdmissionControl for RecordingAdmission {
10038        fn admit(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId, expected_surbs: usize) -> AdmissionToken {
10039            self.events
10040                .lock()
10041                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
10042                .push(("admit".into(), *pseudonym));
10043            self.admit_targets
10044                .lock()
10045                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
10046                .push(expected_surbs);
10047            // `expected_surbs` is only observable here, so assert the contract inline rather than
10048            // thread a second channel out of the mock: a manager that admitted with a zero target
10049            // would defeat the store's sizing, so it is worth catching at the one point it happens.
10050            assert!(
10051                expected_surbs <= MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS,
10052                "admit was called with a target of {expected_surbs}, which no configuration in this crate produces"
10053            );
10054            // Distinct per admit, mirroring what the store does: the guard test below relies on a
10055            // stale retire never matching a successor's admission.
10056            let token =
10057                AdmissionToken::from_raw(self.token_counter.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) + 1);
10058            self.admit_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(token);
10059            token
10060        }
10061
10062        fn retire(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId, token: AdmissionToken) {
10063            self.events
10064                .lock()
10065                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
10066                .push(("retire".into(), *pseudonym));
10067            self.retire_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(token);
10068        }
10069
10070        fn raise_target(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId, token: AdmissionToken, expected_surbs: usize) {
10071            // Recorded with the target, since a raise that names the wrong ring is only visible from
10072            // both halves at once.
10073            self.events
10074                .lock()
10075                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
10076                .push((format!("raise_target:{expected_surbs}"), *pseudonym));
10077            self.raise_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(token);
10078        }
10079    }
10080
10081    /// Upper bound the recording mock asserts `admit` targets against. Matches the manager config
10082    /// the fixtures below run with, which is the only place a target comes from.
10083    const MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS: usize = 10_000;
10084
10085    /// An Exit session must originate nothing once it has been closed explicitly.
10086    ///
10087    /// The Exit's keep-alive stream is a `repeat_with` on a rate limiter: it produces a
10088    /// return-routed packet every period regardless of whether a SURB exists to carry it. That is
10089    /// fine while the initiator is present and replenishing, and it is the *supply* side of the
10090    /// `london-01` outage once the initiator is gone — every such packet is one the routing
10091    /// resolution stage can never resolve, and one unresolvable packet there stalls all origination
10092    /// on the node (see `hopr_transport::path::resolve`).
10093    ///
10094    /// Teardown is therefore the only thing standing between a departed initiator and an unbounded
10095    /// supply of unresolvable packets, which is why each closure path has to be shown to stop the
10096    /// stream rather than merely drop the slot.
10097    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10098    async fn an_exit_session_should_originate_nothing_after_an_explicit_close() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10099        // Default idle timeout (180 s), so eviction cannot confound what the explicit close proves.
10100        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) =
10101            exit_session_originating_keep_alives(Default::default(), None).await?;
10102
10103        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
10104
10105        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "an explicit close").await;
10106        Ok(())
10107    }
10108
10109    /// An Exit session must originate nothing once it has been evicted for being idle.
10110    ///
10111    /// This is the path that matters most for a departed initiator: nobody closes that session, so
10112    /// idle eviction is what ends it, and eviction runs through a Moka listener rather than the
10113    /// explicit close path. A keep-alive stream that survives eviction would go on originating
10114    /// unresolvable return packets with no session left to account for them.
10115    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10116    async fn an_exit_session_should_originate_nothing_after_idle_eviction() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10117        let idle_timeout = KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 3;
10118        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, _) = exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
10119            SessionManagerConfig {
10120                idle_timeout,
10121                ..Default::default()
10122            },
10123            None,
10124        )
10125        .await?;
10126
10127        // Moka evicts lazily, so drive its maintenance rather than waiting for the manager's own
10128        // (jittered, multi-second) eviction tick: this makes the eviction prompt and deterministic.
10129        for _ in 0..50 {
10130            mgr.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
10131            if mgr.active_sessions().is_empty() {
10132                break;
10133            }
10134            tokio::time::sleep(idle_timeout / 10).await;
10135        }
10136        assert!(
10137            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
10138            "the idle session was never evicted, so this test cannot say anything about eviction"
10139        );
10140
10141        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "idle eviction").await;
10142        Ok(())
10143    }
10144
10145    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
10146    // PIX fill — the Exit's own keep-alives
10147    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
10148
10149    /// A [`PixFillControl`] over a random pseudonym, an empty SURB estimate, and an Entry that has
10150    /// shown it refills.
10151    ///
10152    /// `reserve` is the *effective* reserve, as [`effective_surb_reserve`] would have derived it —
10153    /// these tests are about what `admit` does with one, not about where it came from. Against an
10154    /// estimate that starts empty, any `reserve` above zero refuses fill outright, which is what makes
10155    /// admission a usable assertion that a packet was classified as the notification: a test that
10156    /// wants one admitted gives the estimate a SURB, because the notification is not sent on none.
10157    fn fill_control(notify_period: Option<Duration>, reserve: u64) -> PixFillControl {
10158        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
10159        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
10160        fill_control_for(notify_period, reserve, surb_mgmt)
10161    }
10162
10163    /// [`fill_control`] over a balancer state the caller holds on to, so a test can decide when, if
10164    /// ever, the Entry is shown to refill.
10165    fn fill_control_for(
10166        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
10167        reserve: u64,
10168        surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
10169    ) -> PixFillControl {
10170        PixFillControl::new(
10171            HoprPseudonym::random(),
10172            RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1)),
10173            notify_period,
10174            reserve,
10175            Default::default(),
10176            surb_mgmt,
10177        )
10178    }
10179
10180    /// The `surb_starved` gauge moves on the edges, and a control dropped mid-stall returns it.
10181    ///
10182    /// Per refused packet would measure how hard the stream retried rather than how long the
10183    /// Session was starved, and a control that went away while withholding would leave the count
10184    /// standing for the life of the process.
10185    #[test]
10186    fn the_surb_starved_gauge_counts_stalls_and_is_returned_on_drop() {
10187        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
10188
10189        probe::reset();
10190        let control = fill_control(None, 10);
10191        let now = Instant::now();
10192
10193        // The estimator starts empty, so every one of these is below the reserve of ten.
10194        for _ in 0..3 {
10195            assert!(!control.admit_at(now), "fill must be withheld below the reserve");
10196        }
10197        assert_eq!(
10198            1,
10199            probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"),
10200            "three refusals are one stall, not three"
10201        );
10202
10203        // Enough SURBs arrive to clear the reserve.
10204        control
10205            .estimator
10206            .produced
10207            .fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10208        assert!(control.admit_at(now));
10209        assert_eq!(0, probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"));
10210
10211        // And a control dropped while withholding returns its own.
10212        control
10213            .estimator
10214            .consumed
10215            .fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10216        assert!(!control.admit_at(now));
10217        assert_eq!(1, probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"));
10218        drop(control);
10219        assert_eq!(
10220            0,
10221            probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"),
10222            "a session that dies mid-stall must not leave the gauge standing"
10223        );
10224    }
10225
10226    /// The fill reserve reads the estimator's held count, which must not stay inflated by evicted
10227    /// SURBs. After an overflow drains, the real store is empty, yet a raw `produced - consumed` would
10228    /// still read far above the reserve and admit fill into an empty buffer -- the exact failure the
10229    /// reserve exists to prevent (a return packet that finds no SURB stalls every packet the node
10230    /// originates). With evictions counted, the held count is what the store holds, so fill is withheld.
10231    #[test]
10232    fn the_fill_reserve_is_not_defeated_by_a_post_overflow_estimate() {
10233        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
10234
10235        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
10236        let control = fill_control(None, RESERVE);
10237        let now = Instant::now();
10238
10239        // Post-overflow-drain: 1000 SURBs arrived, the full store evicted 900 of them, and the 100 it
10240        // actually held were all spent. The store is empty; `produced - consumed` alone reads 900.
10241        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(1000, Ordering::Relaxed);
10242        control.estimator.evicted.fetch_add(900, Ordering::Relaxed);
10243        control.estimator.consumed.fetch_add(100, Ordering::Relaxed);
10244
10245        assert_eq!(0, control.drainable_surbs(), "an empty store has nothing to drain");
10246        assert!(
10247            !control.admit_at(now),
10248            "fill must be withheld: the real held count is below the reserve"
10249        );
10250    }
10251
10252    /// One stream, two producers, and the faster of them wins.
10253    ///
10254    /// The SURB-level notification and PIX fill are the same packet sent for different reasons, so
10255    /// running two streams of them would double the Exit's return traffic to say the same thing
10256    /// twice. What has to be preserved is the floor: turning fill off must leave the notification
10257    /// running, and a Session with no notification configured must still be fillable — that second
10258    /// case is the deployment's own test fixtures, which pin `surb_balance_notify_period: None`.
10259    #[test]
10260    fn the_exit_keep_alive_rate_is_the_faster_of_its_two_producers() {
10261        let notify = Duration::from_secs(60);
10262        let control = fill_control(Some(notify), 1);
10263
10264        assert_eq!(
10265            FillRate::ZERO,
10266            control.effective_rate(),
10267            "nothing runs before the notification's initial delay has elapsed"
10268        );
10269
10270        control.start_notify();
10271        assert_eq!(FillRate::once_per(notify), control.effective_rate());
10272
10273        control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
10274        assert_eq!(
10275            FillRate::per_second(10),
10276            control.effective_rate(),
10277            "fill above the notification rate must take over"
10278        );
10279
10280        control.set_fill(FillRate::once_per(Duration::from_secs(600)));
10281        assert_eq!(
10282            FillRate::once_per(notify),
10283            control.effective_rate(),
10284            "fill below the notification rate must not slow it down"
10285        );
10286
10287        control.set_fill(FillRate::ZERO);
10288        assert_eq!(
10289            FillRate::once_per(notify),
10290            control.effective_rate(),
10291            "a Session that has stopped filling still reports its SURB level"
10292        );
10293
10294        // And the other way round: no notification configured, so fill is the only producer.
10295        let fill_only = fill_control(None, 1);
10296        fill_only.start_notify();
10297        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, fill_only.effective_rate());
10298        fill_only.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(4));
10299        assert_eq!(FillRate::per_second(4), fill_only.effective_rate());
10300        fill_only.set_fill(FillRate::ZERO);
10301        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, fill_only.effective_rate());
10302    }
10303
10304    /// Fill yields to the Session's own SURB reserve; the SURB-level notification does not, though it
10305    /// still needs a SURB to be sent on.
10306    ///
10307    /// The asymmetry is the whole rule. A return packet that finds no SURB is not dropped — the
10308    /// routing resolver holds it, and every packet this node originates behind it, for the whole of
10309    /// `surb_resolution_wait`. So an Exit that filled a cycle down to its last SURB would stall the
10310    /// Session it was filling for, and every other Session on the node with it. The notification is
10311    /// exempt from the reserve because it is the message that *asks* for more SURBs: refusing to send
10312    /// it when SURBs are scarce is refusing to ask for the thing that is scarce. With none at all, it
10313    /// is the same packet that finds no SURB, and it is withheld like one.
10314    #[test]
10315    fn fill_withholds_below_the_surb_reserve_while_the_level_notification_does_not() {
10316        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
10317        let control = fill_control(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), RESERVE);
10318        control.start_notify();
10319
10320        assert!(
10321            !control.admit(),
10322            "the level notification has no SURB to be sent on, and must not wait out the resolver for one"
10323        );
10324
10325        // One SURB, 99 short of the reserve: enough for the notification, which the reserve does not
10326        // bind, and the first packet is it.
10327        control
10328            .estimator
10329            .produced
10330            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10331        assert!(control.admit(), "the level notification must go out below the reserve");
10332        // The notification period is an hour, so everything after it is fill — and there is too little
10333        // to spend.
10334        assert!(!control.admit(), "fill must not spend a SURB the Session does not have");
10335
10336        control
10337            .estimator
10338            .produced
10339            .fetch_add(RESERVE - 2, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10340        assert!(!control.admit(), "one short of the reserve is still short");
10341
10342        control
10343            .estimator
10344            .produced
10345            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10346        assert!(control.admit(), "at the reserve, fill may spend");
10347
10348        // Consumption counted elsewhere walks the estimate back below the reserve.
10349        control
10350            .estimator
10351            .consumed
10352            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10353        assert!(!control.admit());
10354    }
10355
10356    /// Exactly one caller may take a Session into its drain, and doing so silences the notification.
10357    ///
10358    /// `begin_surb_drain` is reached from the operator's close, the closure notifier and
10359    /// `handle_session_error` independently, so two closes can both read [`is_draining`] as false and
10360    /// race for the same drain. The transition is what settles it: the winner is the one caller that
10361    /// tells the supervisor the Session closed, and the loser is answered as though it had arrived
10362    /// afterwards. Were the check and the write separate, both would start a drain and the supervisor
10363    /// would be told twice about one close.
10364    ///
10365    /// [`is_draining`]: PixFillControl::is_draining
10366    #[test]
10367    fn only_one_caller_can_take_a_session_into_its_drain() {
10368        let notify = Duration::from_secs(60);
10369        // A reserve of two over a stock of one, so that fill is refused and a notification, which the
10370        // reserve does not bind, would not be: only the drain can be what refuses the last packet.
10371        let control = fill_control(Some(notify), 2);
10372        control
10373            .estimator
10374            .produced
10375            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10376        control.start_notify();
10377        assert_eq!(FillRate::once_per(notify), control.effective_rate());
10378
10379        assert!(control.enter_drain(), "the first caller takes the drain");
10380        assert!(control.is_draining());
10381        assert!(
10382            !control.enter_drain(),
10383            "a concurrent close must lose the transition rather than start a second drain"
10384        );
10385        assert!(control.is_draining(), "losing the transition must not clear the drain");
10386
10387        assert_eq!(
10388            FillRate::ZERO,
10389            control.effective_rate(),
10390            "a draining stream runs at the fill rate alone, and nothing is filling it"
10391        );
10392        assert!(
10393            !control.admit(),
10394            "the notification is the one packet exempt from the reserve, and a drain silences it"
10395        );
10396
10397        // Nor can the one-shot delay task, which holds a clone of this control, turn it back on.
10398        control.start_notify();
10399        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, control.effective_rate());
10400    }
10401
10402    /// The SURB-level notification is classified by when it was *due*, not by when the scheduler got
10403    /// round to releasing it.
10404    ///
10405    /// The rate limiter that releases these packets does not hit the period exactly: it sleeps in
10406    /// chunks of `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK`, re-reads its controller on each wake, and rounds a rate into an
10407    /// integer packet count. Compared against the period exactly, a period the controller rounds
10408    /// short by a microsecond would classify every other notification as fill — and, below the
10409    /// reserve, drop it. That is the message that *asks* for the SURBs whose absence caused the drop,
10410    /// and it runs on every Exit Session with a notification period configured, PIX or not.
10411    ///
10412    /// The reserve here is the instrument: the estimator holds one SURB against a reserve of a hundred,
10413    /// so a packet the rule classifies as fill is refused and a packet it classifies as the
10414    /// notification is admitted. Admission is therefore the assertion that it was not counted as fill.
10415    #[test]
10416    fn a_level_notification_released_a_shade_early_is_still_the_notification() {
10417        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
10418        // Two seconds, so the slack is `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK` rather than half the period, and the two
10419        // bounds are distinguishable.
10420        let period = Duration::from_secs(2);
10421        let control = fill_control(Some(period), RESERVE);
10422        // One SURB to send the notification on, far short of the reserve: the notification is not sent
10423        // on none.
10424        control
10425            .estimator
10426            .produced
10427            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10428        control.start_notify();
10429
10430        let t0 = Instant::now();
10431        assert!(
10432            control.admit_at(t0),
10433            "the first packet is the notification, below the reserve"
10434        );
10435
10436        // A shade under the period — the shape a rate rounded down by a microsecond produces.
10437        let early = t0 + period - Duration::from_micros(1);
10438        assert!(
10439            control.admit_at(early),
10440            "a notification released a microsecond early must not be reclassified as fill and dropped"
10441        );
10442
10443        // And it is the notification rather than a free pass: the next packet is measured from when
10444        // this one actually went out, so everything inside the following period is fill.
10445        assert!(
10446            !control.admit_at(early + Duration::from_millis(1)),
10447            "the packet after the notification is fill, and there is nothing to spend"
10448        );
10449        assert!(
10450            !control.admit_at(early + period - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK - Duration::from_millis(1)),
10451            "a packet inside the slack window is still fill"
10452        );
10453
10454        // The slack window opens `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK` before the period is up, and not earlier.
10455        assert!(
10456            control.admit_at(early + period - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK),
10457            "at the edge of the slack window the packet is the notification again"
10458        );
10459
10460        // A period short enough that `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK` would swallow it keeps half of itself.
10461        let short = Duration::from_millis(200);
10462        let control = fill_control(Some(short), RESERVE);
10463        control
10464            .estimator
10465            .produced
10466            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10467        control.start_notify();
10468        let t0 = Instant::now();
10469        assert!(control.admit_at(t0));
10470        assert!(
10471            !control.admit_at(t0 + short / 2 - Duration::from_millis(1)),
10472            "the slack is capped at half the period, so it cannot widen a short period away to nothing"
10473        );
10474        assert!(control.admit_at(t0 + short / 2));
10475    }
10476
10477    /// The level notification goes only to an Entry that has shown it refills.
10478    ///
10479    /// A report spends one of the Session's own SURBs. An Entry without a SURB balancer acts on no
10480    /// report, so every one sent to it spends a SURB to say nothing, and it is the Entry that has least
10481    /// to give the Exit back (gnosis_vpn#748). What the Exit has seen of it, and not what it announced,
10482    /// is the evidence: the announced target is a figure the peer picks.
10483    ///
10484    /// The withheld notification keeps its slot, so that the next packet to ask is the notification once the Entry is
10485    /// heard.
10486    #[test]
10487    fn a_level_notification_waits_for_an_entry_that_refills() {
10488        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
10489        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
10490        let control = fill_control_for(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), RESERVE, surb_mgmt.clone());
10491        control.start_notify();
10492        // SURBs to send it on, short of the reserve: this is not about the SURBs.
10493        control
10494            .estimator
10495            .produced
10496            .fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10497
10498        let now = Instant::now();
10499        assert!(
10500            !control.admit_at(now),
10501            "an Entry that has not been heard to refill has nobody reading the report"
10502        );
10503        assert!(!control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(1)));
10504
10505        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
10506        assert!(
10507            control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(2)),
10508            "the withheld notification keeps its slot: the next packet to ask goes out as the notification"
10509        );
10510        assert!(
10511            !control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(3)),
10512            "and it was the notification: the packet after it is fill, below the reserve"
10513        );
10514    }
10515
10516    /// The level notification is not sent on a SURB the Session does not have.
10517    ///
10518    /// A return packet that finds none is held by the routing resolver for the whole of
10519    /// `surb_resolution_wait`, and every packet this node originates with it. The decision reads the
10520    /// estimate, so SURBs that were spent do not count.
10521    #[test]
10522    fn a_level_notification_waits_for_a_surb_to_send_it_on() {
10523        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
10524
10525        let period = Duration::from_secs(3600);
10526        let control = fill_control(Some(period), 100);
10527        control.start_notify();
10528
10529        let now = Instant::now();
10530        assert!(
10531            !control.admit_at(now),
10532            "an empty estimate has no SURB to send the notification on"
10533        );
10534
10535        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(2, Relaxed);
10536        assert!(control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(1)));
10537
10538        // A period on, the two SURBs have been spent.
10539        control.estimator.consumed.fetch_add(2, Relaxed);
10540        assert!(
10541            !control.admit_at(now + period),
10542            "SURBs already spent are not SURBs to send on"
10543        );
10544
10545        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
10546        assert!(
10547            control.admit_at(now + period + Duration::from_millis(1)),
10548            "the notification keeps its slot until there is a SURB for it"
10549        );
10550    }
10551
10552    /// A notification that is due and withheld is not let through as fill.
10553    ///
10554    /// The packet is the same either way, and a withheld notification would otherwise fall through to
10555    /// the reserve check. Above the reserve that check admits, so a Session with no Entry reading its
10556    /// reports would send one every period, labelled as fill. While a fill is running, the packet is
10557    /// fill and meets the reserve like any other, but it is not counted as the notification.
10558    #[test]
10559    fn a_withheld_level_notification_is_not_let_through_as_fill() {
10560        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
10561        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
10562        let control = fill_control_for(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), RESERVE, surb_mgmt.clone());
10563        control.start_notify();
10564        // Far above the reserve, so a packet classified as fill would be admitted.
10565        control
10566            .estimator
10567            .produced
10568            .fetch_add(10 * RESERVE, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10569
10570        let now = Instant::now();
10571        for n in 0..3 {
10572            assert!(
10573                !control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(n)),
10574                "with no fill running there is nothing for a withheld notification to be mistaken for"
10575            );
10576        }
10577        assert!(
10578            control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_none(),
10579            "a withheld notification has not been sent, and keeps its slot"
10580        );
10581
10582        control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
10583        assert!(
10584            control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(3)),
10585            "while a fill runs the packet is fill, and the estimate is above the reserve"
10586        );
10587        assert!(
10588            control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_none(),
10589            "fill that took the notification's slot did not send the notification"
10590        );
10591
10592        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
10593        assert!(control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(4)));
10594        assert!(
10595            control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_some(),
10596            "once the Entry is heard the notification is sent in its own right"
10597        );
10598    }
10599
10600    /// The reserve is a ceiling on a figure derived from the buffer the *Entry* asked for.
10601    ///
10602    /// The configured value is an absolute SURB count, while the buffer it is compared against is
10603    /// sized by the peer. Left absolute, a PIX Session whose Entry targets fewer SURBs than the
10604    /// reserve could never be filled at all — every fill packet withheld, the funded cycle stranded on
10605    /// `max_recovery_time`, and nothing in the logs but a backoff.
10606    #[test]
10607    fn the_fill_surb_reserve_is_capped_at_a_quarter_of_the_entrys_announced_buffer() {
10608        // The shipped reserve against the worked profile's buffer: the configured value binds and the
10609        // derivation is inert, which is what keeps this from quietly weakening production.
10610        assert_eq!(500, effective_surb_reserve(500, 7_000));
10611        // Exactly four times the reserve is the point at which the two agree.
10612        assert_eq!(500, effective_surb_reserve(500, 2_000));
10613
10614        // Below that, the Entry's buffer is what decides. The cluster fixtures' 64-SURB target is the
10615        // case this exists for.
10616        assert_eq!(16, effective_surb_reserve(500, 64));
10617        assert_eq!(12, effective_surb_reserve(500, 50));
10618
10619        // Never zero: an Entry announcing a buffer of three would otherwise let fill spend the
10620        // Session's last SURB, which is the one failure the reserve exists to prevent.
10621        assert_eq!(1, effective_surb_reserve(500, 3));
10622        assert_eq!(1, effective_surb_reserve(500, 0));
10623        assert_eq!(1, effective_surb_reserve(0, 7_000));
10624    }
10625
10626    /// Test dimensions whose cycle is large enough to need a visible fill rate.
10627    ///
10628    /// [`small_pix_params`] is six packets, which any deadline covers at the heartbeat; these are
10629    /// three hundred, which against the fixture's 40 s recovery budget needs about eleven packets a
10630    /// second — far enough above the one-per-second notification for the two to be told apart.
10631    fn fill_pix_params() -> PixParams {
10632        PixParams::try_new(100, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE).expect("test dimensions must be valid")
10633    }
10634
10635    /// Brings up an Exit-side PIX Session, funds its first cycle, and returns once it is recovering.
10636    ///
10637    /// The Entry half is not simulated: the supervisor is a state machine, and driving it through
10638    /// `SsaRequestSent`, `CommitmentVerified` and `DepositConfirmed` puts its cycle in exactly the
10639    /// state a real commitment and deposit would — which is the state fill is planned from. What is
10640    /// real here is everything downstream of that: the action driver, the rate controller, the
10641    /// admission predicate and the stream.
10642    async fn recovering_exit_pix_session(
10643        capabilities: Capabilities,
10644        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
10645        fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig,
10646        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
10647    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RecordingManager, Originated, HoprPseudonym)> {
10648        let params = fill_pix_params();
10649        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
10650            surb_balance_notify_period: notify_period,
10651            // The admission tests over this fixture wait out the deferred retire; a short window
10652            // keeps them fast without changing the seam they exercise.
10653            surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
10654            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
10655                quota_range: 0..=pix_params_to_quota(&params),
10656                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
10657                    // As short as a legal pair gets: the idle deadline must clear the reconstructor's
10658                    // 30 s acknowledgement window, and the hard deadline must exceed the idle one.
10659                    // That is what makes the required fill rate — a whole cycle over 75 % of 40 s,
10660                    // about eleven packets a second — observable inside a test-length window.
10661                    max_recovery_idle: Duration::from_secs(31),
10662                    max_recovery_time: Duration::from_secs(40),
10663                    fill,
10664                    ..Default::default()
10665                },
10666                ..Default::default()
10667            },
10668            ..Default::default()
10669        });
10670
10671        if let Some(admission) = admission {
10672            assert!(
10673                mgr.set_surb_admission(admission),
10674                "a freshly constructed fixture manager must accept the SURB admission seam"
10675            );
10676        }
10677
10678        let (msg_tx, msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
10679        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
10680        mgr.start(
10681            msg_tx,
10682            new_session_tx,
10683            Some(pix_toolbox_with_pool(
10684                Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
10685                    polynomials_per_ssa: params.polys_per_ssa(),
10686                    threshold: params.shares_per_poly(),
10687                    surplus_shares: params.surplus_shares(),
10688                })),
10689                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
10690            )),
10691            None,
10692        )?;
10693
10694        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
10695        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
10696            pseudonym,
10697            StartInitiation {
10698                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
10699                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
10700                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities | Capability::UsePIX),
10701                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0)),
10702            },
10703        )
10704        .await?;
10705
10706        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
10707        let supervisor = slot
10708            .pix_supervisor
10709            .get()
10710            .context("an Exit-side PIX session must have a supervisor")?;
10711
10712        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("index one is non-zero"));
10713        for event in [
10714            SessionPixEvent::SsaRequestSent(ssa_id),
10715            SessionPixEvent::CommitmentVerified(ssa_id),
10716            SessionPixEvent::DepositConfirmed {
10717                ssa_id,
10718                amount: hopr_api::HoprBalance::new_base(1000),
10719            },
10720        ] {
10721            supervisor
10722                .send_event(event)
10723                .await
10724                .map_err(|()| anyhow::anyhow!("the supervisor stopped accepting events"))?;
10725        }
10726
10727        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, pseudonym))
10728    }
10729
10730    /// Counts the return-routed keep-alives `mgr` originated for `pseudonym` during `window`.
10731    async fn keep_alives_during(rx: &mut Originated, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, window: Duration) -> usize {
10732        originated_during(rx, window)
10733            .await
10734            .iter()
10735            .filter(|(routing, data)| {
10736                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::KeepAlive)
10737                    && matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == pseudonym)
10738            })
10739            .count()
10740    }
10741
10742    /// A funded, idle PIX Session must be filled by the Exit at the rate its own deadline needs.
10743    ///
10744    /// This is the mechanism end to end on one node: the supervisor plans a rate, the action driver
10745    /// applies it to the shared keep-alive controller, the admission predicate lets the packets past,
10746    /// and they come out return-routed to the Entry. The floor asserted is deliberately the
10747    /// *notification* rate rather than the planned one — a regression that leaves the stream running
10748    /// at one packet a second is exactly the failure this exists to prevent, and it looks like
10749    /// success to any assertion that only checks the stream is alive.
10750    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10751    async fn a_funded_idle_pix_session_is_filled_by_the_exit() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10752        let notify = Duration::from_secs(1);
10753        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
10754            Capabilities::empty(),
10755            Some(notify),
10756            // Draining off, so the trailing close below still means "the stream stopped at once".
10757            // What a drain does instead is the subject of the tests further down.
10758            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
10759                min_surb_reserve: 1,
10760                drain_after_close: false,
10761                ..Default::default()
10762            },
10763            None,
10764        )
10765        .await?;
10766
10767        // SURBs to spend, so the reserve is not what this test is measuring.
10768        mgr.sessions
10769            .get(&pseudonym)
10770            .context("the session slot must exist")?
10771            .surb_estimator
10772            .produced
10773            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10774
10775        // One sampling interval for the planner, then a window long enough that the notification
10776        // alone could not account for what is counted.
10777        let _ramp = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
10778        let window = Duration::from_millis(1500);
10779        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
10780
10781        // Counted against the rate the notification is *promoted* at rather than against the period,
10782        // for the reason `admit_at` documents: the classification window is one slack shorter than the
10783        // period, so a notification-only stream produces rather more than `window / period` packets.
10784        // Taking the period at face value here would set the floor too low and let a stream that had
10785        // stopped filling pass.
10786        let promote_every = notify - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(notify / 2);
10787        let notify_only = (window.as_secs_f64() / promote_every.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as usize;
10788        assert!(
10789            observed > notify_only,
10790            "a funded idle cycle produced {observed} keep-alive(s) over {window:?}, which the {notify:?} SURB-level \
10791             notification alone could have produced ({notify_only}, one every {promote_every:?})"
10792        );
10793
10794        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
10795        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "an explicit close of a filling PIX session").await;
10796        Ok(())
10797    }
10798
10799    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
10800    // Draining a closed PIX Session
10801    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
10802
10803    /// A funded, filling Exit PIX Session whose SURB estimate covers the rest of its cycle.
10804    ///
10805    /// The 100 000 is not decoration: it is the estimate `begin_surb_drain` nets the reserve out of
10806    /// and hands the supervisor, and against [`fill_pix_params`]' 300-packet cycle it is what makes a
10807    /// drain admissible at all. The ramp is waited out for the reason
10808    /// [`exit_session_originating_keep_alives`] gives — silence after a close says nothing unless the
10809    /// stream was observably running before it.
10810    async fn drainable_exit_pix_session(
10811        notify_period: Duration,
10812        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
10813    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RecordingManager, Originated, HoprPseudonym)> {
10814        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
10815            Capabilities::empty(),
10816            Some(notify_period),
10817            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
10818                min_surb_reserve: 1,
10819                ..Default::default()
10820            },
10821            admission,
10822        )
10823        .await?;
10824
10825        mgr.sessions
10826            .get(&pseudonym)
10827            .context("the session slot must exist")?
10828            .surb_estimator
10829            .produced
10830            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10831
10832        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
10833        anyhow::ensure!(
10834            observed > 0,
10835            "the fixture's keep-alive stream never ran, so nothing below can tell a drain from a Session that was \
10836             silent all along"
10837        );
10838        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, pseudonym))
10839    }
10840
10841    /// A closed PIX Session goes on originating until the cycle it was paid for recovers.
10842    ///
10843    /// The deposit is stranded rather than refunded if the cycle does not complete, so a close that
10844    /// tore the stream down while the Exit still held enough SURBs to finish would throw away money
10845    /// both sides have already paid. What must *not* happen is the mirror image of that: origination
10846    /// continuing past the point it is buying anything. So the recovery is delivered and the slot has
10847    /// to be gone, and the stream silent, on the other side of it.
10848    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10849    async fn a_closed_pix_session_keeps_originating_until_its_cycle_recovers() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10850        let notify = Duration::from_secs(1);
10851        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = drainable_exit_pix_session(notify, None).await?;
10852
10853        assert!(
10854            mgr.close_session(&pseudonym),
10855            "a close that starts a drain is still a close that was handled"
10856        );
10857        assert!(
10858            mgr.active_sessions().contains(&pseudonym),
10859            "the slot must survive the close — the drain runs out of it, and the supervisor's own teardown is what \
10860             removes it"
10861        );
10862
10863        // The SURB-level notification is switched off for the whole drain, so every packet counted
10864        // here is fill. The bar is nevertheless the notification-only figure, which keeps this
10865        // comparable with `a_funded_idle_pix_session_is_filled_by_the_exit` above.
10866        let window = Duration::from_millis(1500);
10867        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
10868        let promote_every = notify - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(notify / 2);
10869        let notify_only = (window.as_secs_f64() / promote_every.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as usize;
10870        assert!(
10871            observed > notify_only,
10872            "a closed session with a full SURB buffer originated {observed} keep-alive(s) over {window:?}, which is \
10873             no more than the {notify_only} its (now silenced) notification would have accounted for"
10874        );
10875
10876        // Recovery is the end of the drain: there is nothing left to work for, so the Session must go.
10877        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("index one is non-zero"));
10878        mgr.dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id))
10879            .await?;
10880        assert!(
10881            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
10882            "a recovered cycle must end the drain and tear the Session down"
10883        );
10884        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "a completed SURB drain").await;
10885        Ok(())
10886    }
10887
10888    /// A closed PIX Session with too few SURBs to finish is torn down as it always was.
10889    ///
10890    /// A hundred SURBs against [`fill_pix_params`]' 300-packet cycle: enough for the manager to offer
10891    /// the close to the supervisor, and not enough for the supervisor to take it. That is the
10892    /// arithmetic under test — draining on a buffer that runs out partway is strictly worse than not
10893    /// draining at all, since the SURBs are spent down to the reserve, the cycle recovers nothing,
10894    /// and every packet past the last useful one is return-routed on behalf of a Session that is gone.
10895    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10896    async fn a_closed_pix_session_without_enough_surbs_originates_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10897        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
10898            Capabilities::empty(),
10899            Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),
10900            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
10901                min_surb_reserve: 1,
10902                ..Default::default()
10903            },
10904            None,
10905        )
10906        .await?;
10907
10908        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
10909        slot.surb_estimator
10910            .produced
10911            .fetch_add(100, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10912        // An Entry that has been heard, so that the notification is one of the packets that shows the
10913        // stream running before the close, as it was before it was held for a reader. It does not
10914        // depend on the supervisor's first plan, which fill does.
10915        slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
10916        drop(slot);
10917        anyhow::ensure!(
10918            keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await > 0,
10919            "the stream must be running before the close for its absence afterwards to mean anything"
10920        );
10921
10922        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
10923        assert!(
10924            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
10925            "a drain the supervisor refuses must still tear the Session down"
10926        );
10927        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "a close with too few SURBs to drain").await;
10928        Ok(())
10929    }
10930
10931    /// With `drain_after_close` off, every close path is what it was before draining existed.
10932    ///
10933    /// Including the part an operator would notice first: the slot is gone by the time
10934    /// `close_session` returns, rather than one channel hop later once the supervisor has answered.
10935    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10936    async fn a_closed_pix_session_with_draining_disabled_originates_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10937        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
10938            Capabilities::empty(),
10939            Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
10940            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
10941                min_surb_reserve: 1,
10942                drain_after_close: false,
10943                ..Default::default()
10944            },
10945            None,
10946        )
10947        .await?;
10948
10949        mgr.sessions
10950            .get(&pseudonym)
10951            .context("the session slot must exist")?
10952            .surb_estimator
10953            .produced
10954            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10955        anyhow::ensure!(
10956            keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await > 0,
10957            "the fixture's keep-alive stream never ran"
10958        );
10959
10960        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
10961        assert!(
10962            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
10963            "with draining disabled the slot must be gone by the time the close returns"
10964        );
10965        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "an explicit close with draining disabled").await;
10966        Ok(())
10967    }
10968
10969    /// Closing a draining Session a second time forces the teardown.
10970    ///
10971    /// The drain is the Exit's decision, taken on the operator's behalf, and this is the operator's
10972    /// way to overrule it: a second `SessionManager::close_session` — or a peer `SessionError`, which
10973    /// arrives on the same path — stops the origination immediately rather than waiting out a cycle.
10974    /// The end-of-stream a close of our own ingress produces is deliberately *not* on this path; it
10975    /// carries `WriteClosed`/`EmptyRead` and is absorbed.
10976    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
10977    async fn a_second_close_of_a_draining_session_tears_it_down() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
10978        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = drainable_exit_pix_session(Duration::from_secs(1), None).await?;
10979
10980        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the first close starts the drain");
10981        assert!(
10982            mgr.active_sessions().contains(&pseudonym),
10983            "the drain must be running for the second close to have anything to overrule"
10984        );
10985
10986        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the second close must find the session");
10987        assert!(
10988            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
10989            "a second explicit close must remove the slot rather than let the drain run on"
10990        );
10991        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "a second explicit close of a draining session").await;
10992        Ok(())
10993    }
10994
10995    /// The same Session, with an Entry that reads its reports but supplies too few SURBs to fill with,
10996    /// must fall back to its SURB-level notification. Both kinds of Session do: the Exit's rule is the
10997    /// same with a balancer running (`rate_controlled`) and without one (`no_rate_control`).
10998    ///
10999    /// "No SURBs to spend" means below the reserve, which is the point at which fill stops: a few SURBs
11000    /// are still held, which is what the notification is sent on. A Session whose Entry has stopped
11001    /// supplying SURBs is the one case where filling harder is actively harmful: the packets cannot be
11002    /// routed, and an unroutable origination holds up every packet the node sends. What must survive is
11003    /// the notification, because it is the message that asks for the SURBs whose absence caused the
11004    /// backoff.
11005    #[rstest]
11006    #[case::rate_controlled(Capabilities::empty())]
11007    #[case::no_rate_control(Capability::NoRateControl.into())]
11008    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11009    async fn fill_backs_off_to_the_notification_when_the_entry_supplies_no_surbs(
11010        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
11011    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11012        // At `MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD`, so it survives the clamp `SessionManager::new`
11013        // applies. A shorter value would be raised to this one anyway, and the bound below would then
11014        // be computed from a period that is not the one in effect.
11015        let notify = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
11016        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
11017            capabilities,
11018            Some(notify),
11019            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
11020                min_surb_reserve: 500,
11021                ..Default::default()
11022            },
11023            None,
11024        )
11025        .await?;
11026        assert_eq!(
11027            Some(notify),
11028            mgr.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period,
11029            "the fixture's notification period must be the one the manager actually runs"
11030        );
11031
11032        // A balancing Entry has been heard, and it delivered a few SURBs: more than none, short of the
11033        // reserve. The reserve is the effective one, which the Entry's announced buffer lowers.
11034        dispatch_entry_keep_alive(&mgr, pseudonym, KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(), 1, 0)?;
11035        wait_for_counterparty_refills(&mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
11036        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
11037        slot.surb_estimator
11038            .produced
11039            .fetch_add(6, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11040        let reserve = slot
11041            .pix_fill
11042            .get()
11043            .context("a PIX session has a fill control")?
11044            .min_surb_reserve;
11045        let held = slot.surb_estimator.saturating_diff();
11046        anyhow::ensure!(
11047            0 < held && held < reserve,
11048            "fixture: the Exit must hold some SURBs, but fewer than its reserve of {reserve}; it holds {held}"
11049        );
11050
11051        let _ramp = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
11052        let window = Duration::from_millis(1500);
11053        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
11054
11055        // A notification is promoted every `period - min(MAX_WAIT_CHUNK, period / 2)`, not every
11056        // period: `admit_at` opens the window a slack early so the classification does not rest on the
11057        // rate limiter's scheduling latency. The ceiling has to be computed from that shorter interval,
11058        // or a stream doing exactly what this test permits would be read as filling.
11059        let promote_every = notify - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(notify / 2);
11060        let notify_only = (window.as_secs_f64() / promote_every.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as usize;
11061        assert!(
11062            observed > 0,
11063            "the SURB-level notification must survive the backoff — it is what asks for the SURBs"
11064        );
11065        assert!(
11066            observed <= notify_only + 1,
11067            "with no SURBs to spend the Exit originated {observed} keep-alive(s) over {window:?}, against the \
11068             {notify_only} its notification alone accounts for at one every {promote_every:?}"
11069        );
11070
11071        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
11072        Ok(())
11073    }
11074
11075    /// An Exit that has not been heard to read its reports originates nothing while it is below its
11076    /// SURB reserve, not even the notification.
11077    ///
11078    /// The other half of the rule above. With no balancer on the Entry's side the notification has no
11079    /// reader, and fill, which the reserve holds back, is the only thing the Session is entitled to
11080    /// send. Both kinds of Session behave alike. Silence alone proves nothing, so the stock is then
11081    /// raised above the reserve and fill must flow: the stream was gated, not dead.
11082    #[rstest]
11083    #[case::rate_controlled(Capabilities::empty())]
11084    #[case::no_rate_control(Capability::NoRateControl.into())]
11085    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11086    async fn a_pix_session_without_a_reader_below_its_reserve_originates_nothing(
11087        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
11088    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11089        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
11090            capabilities,
11091            Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),
11092            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
11093                min_surb_reserve: 500,
11094                ..Default::default()
11095            },
11096            None,
11097        )
11098        .await?;
11099
11100        // Its SURBs arrived with data, and it has sent no keep-alive: no balancer to read a report.
11101        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
11102        slot.surb_estimator
11103            .produced
11104            .fetch_add(6, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11105        let reserve = slot
11106            .pix_fill
11107            .get()
11108            .context("a PIX session has a fill control")?
11109            .min_surb_reserve;
11110        anyhow::ensure!(
11111            6 < reserve && !slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
11112            "fixture: below the reserve of {reserve}, with an Entry that has not been heard"
11113        );
11114
11115        // Long enough for the supervisor's first plan and for several periods of the notification.
11116        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(3_500)).await;
11117        assert_eq!(
11118            0, observed,
11119            "with nobody reading the reports and too few SURBs to fill with, the Exit originated {observed} \
11120             keep-alive(s)"
11121        );
11122
11123        slot.surb_estimator
11124            .produced
11125            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11126        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(2_000)).await;
11127        assert!(
11128            observed > 0,
11129            "the silence was the SURB reserve and not a dead stream: above it, fill must flow"
11130        );
11131
11132        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
11133        Ok(())
11134    }
11135
11136    /// A `NoRateControl` PIX Session must still have a SURB level estimate, or its reserve is a lie.
11137    ///
11138    /// That branch runs no balancer, and until now it wired no estimator either: `produced` and
11139    /// `consumed` both stayed at zero for the life of the Session. A reserve measured against that
11140    /// counter would refuse every fill packet forever — which is the branch that can drain SURBs
11141    /// fastest, so it is the one where getting it wrong costs most.
11142    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11143    async fn a_no_rate_control_pix_session_still_estimates_its_surb_level() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11144        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
11145            Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
11146            Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
11147            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
11148                min_surb_reserve: 1,
11149                ..Default::default()
11150            },
11151            None,
11152        )
11153        .await?;
11154
11155        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
11156        slot.surb_estimator
11157            .produced
11158            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11159
11160        let _ = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
11161
11162        assert!(
11163            slot.surb_estimator.consumed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) > 0,
11164            "a NoRateControl Session that has sent keep-alives must have counted them as consumed SURBs"
11165        );
11166
11167        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
11168        Ok(())
11169    }
11170
11171    /// An established Session must be admitted exactly once, and a teardown must retire it exactly
11172    /// once — while a SURB drain must retire nothing.
11173    ///
11174    /// This is the seam the SURB store's admission control hangs off (hoprnet#8515). Three properties
11175    /// are load-bearing and none is observable from the store alone:
11176    ///
11177    /// * **admit at establishment, not at allocation.** `handle_incoming_session_initiation` inserts the slot long
11178    ///   before the Start handshake completes; admitting there would put an unauthenticated peer into the store's
11179    ///   admitted class. Only the commit at the end of the Exit's establishment path counts, so the count below being
11180    ///   exactly one after the Session is live — and the fixture's keep-alives proving the Session really was
11181    ///   established, not merely allocated — is the security property itself.
11182    /// * **retire at every teardown.** The explicit close is the one teardown path a test can drive deterministically;
11183    ///   the eviction listener and the PIX-failure path funnel through the same `release_session_slot` this exercises.
11184    /// * **no retire on drain.** `begin_surb_drain` deliberately keeps the slot so the drain can spend the Session's
11185    ///   remaining SURBs; retiring there would size the store for a Session that is still spending. The close below
11186    ///   starts a drain (the fixture funds the buffer), and the retire count staying at zero while the drain runs is
11187    ///   what proves the drain path left the seam alone. The supervisor's own teardown of the drained Session then
11188    ///   supplies the single retire.
11189    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11190    async fn an_established_session_is_admitted_once_retired_once_and_drain_retires_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11191        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
11192        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) =
11193            drainable_exit_pix_session(Duration::from_secs(1), Some(Arc::new(admission.clone()))).await?;
11194
11195        assert_eq!(
11196            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
11197            1,
11198            "an established Session must be admitted exactly once, at commit"
11199        );
11200        assert_eq!(
11201            admission.retired(&pseudonym),
11202            0,
11203            "nothing before the close may retire an established Session"
11204        );
11205
11206        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
11207
11208        // The close starts a drain, so the slot survives it on purpose — and so must the admission.
11209        assert!(
11210            mgr.active_sessions().contains(&pseudonym),
11211            "the drain fixture's close must have started a drain for the assertions below to mean anything"
11212        );
11213        assert_eq!(
11214            admission.retired(&pseudonym),
11215            0,
11216            "a close answered by a SURB drain must not retire the Session — the drain still spends its SURBs"
11217        );
11218        assert!(
11219            !admission.retire_precedes_admit(&pseudonym),
11220            "no retire may be recorded before the Session's own admit"
11221        );
11222
11223        // End the drain the way the supervisor does, and let its teardown run: the retire belongs to
11224        // *that* path, not to the close that started the drain.
11225        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("index one is non-zero"));
11226        mgr.dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id))
11227            .await?;
11228        assert!(
11229            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
11230            "a recovered cycle must end the drain and tear the Session down"
11231        );
11232        assert_eq!(
11233            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
11234            1,
11235            "the drain's teardown must retire the Session exactly once"
11236        );
11237
11238        // Drain the packets the teardown is still holding so the fixture's sender task finishes.
11239        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
11240        Ok(())
11241    }
11242
11243    /// A Session whose establishment fails after the slot is inserted must never be admitted.
11244    ///
11245    /// The rollback path is the one place an unestablished peer comes closest to the admitted class:
11246    /// the slot exists, the pseudonym is set, and only the failed notification stands between it and
11247    /// the commit. The admit riding on `commit` — rather than on allocation — is what keeps it out,
11248    /// and the retired count of one is the rollback's own no-op retire flowing through the same seam
11249    /// as every teardown (idempotent against a pseudonym that was never admitted, but recorded here
11250    /// so the path is visibly wired rather than merely harmless).
11251    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11252    async fn a_rolled_back_session_is_never_admitted() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11253        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
11254        // Short grace: the rollback's retire is deferred, and the default window would make this
11255        // test wait out the library default in real time for no added coverage.
11256        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
11257            surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
11258            ..Default::default()
11259        });
11260        mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone()));
11261
11262        // Drop the receiver so that notifying about the new incoming session fails *after* the slot
11263        // has already been inserted — the same fixture the rollback test above uses.
11264        let transport = MockMsgSender::new();
11265        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
11266        drop(new_session_rx);
11267        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
11268        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
11269
11270        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
11271        let result = mgr
11272            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
11273                pseudonym,
11274                StartInitiation {
11275                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
11276                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
11277                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
11278                    additional_data: 0,
11279                },
11280            )
11281            .await;
11282        assert!(
11283            result.is_err(),
11284            "the fixture's dropped notification channel must fail the establishment"
11285        );
11286
11287        assert!(
11288            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
11289            "the partially established session slot was not rolled back"
11290        );
11291        assert_eq!(
11292            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
11293            0,
11294            "a Session that never committed must never be admitted — admission happens at commit, not at slot \
11295             allocation, and this is the peer the distinction exists to keep out"
11296        );
11297        assert_eq!(
11298            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
11299            1,
11300            "the rollback must run the retire through the same seam as every teardown"
11301        );
11302
11303        sender.close_channel();
11304        handle.await??;
11305        Ok(())
11306    }
