11308    /// A teardown on a reused pseudonym must present *its own* admission's token, not the successor's.
11309    ///
11310    /// The pseudonym is client-chosen (`SessionClientConfig::pseudonym`) and freely reusable, so
11311    /// "close Session A, open Session B on the same pseudonym" is a real sequence, not an exotic
11312    /// one. A's retire is deliberately deferred past the packet pipeline's SURB-resolution window —
11313    /// A's own return-routed notification needs its ring while the resolution stage looks it up — so
11314    /// it lands *after* B's commit, and an unconditional retire would invalidate B's already-admitted
11315    /// ring: B would go on inserting its SURBs into the 16-cap un-admitted quarantine and never
11316    /// recover, with nothing logged anywhere.
11317    ///
11318    /// The deferral is guarded by the token: `admit` returns one naming its admission, the teardown
11319    /// threads that token to its retire, and the store honours a retire only while its token still
11320    /// names the pseudonym's current admission. This test pins the manager half of that — the
11321    /// successor's admit is real and distinguished, and A's retire presents A's token rather than B's
11322    /// (the failure a teardown re-looking-up the slot under the pseudonym would produce). The store's
11323    /// own matching is pinned by `a_stale_retire_must_not_clobber_a_successor_admissions_ring` over in
11324    /// `hopr-protocol-hopr`, which is where the matching lives.
11325    ///
11326    /// The grace is shortened through `surb_resolution_wait` so the deferral is exercised without
11327    /// waiting out the library default in real time.
11328    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11329    async fn a_reused_pseudonym_keeps_the_successor_ring_when_the_stale_retire_fires() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11330        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
11331        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
11332            SessionManagerConfig {
11333                surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
11334                ..Default::default()
11335            },
11336            Some(Arc::new(admission.clone())),
11337        )
11338        .await?;
11339
11340        assert_eq!(
11341            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
11342            1,
11343            "the first Session must be established for the reuse below to mean anything"
11344        );
11345
11346        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
11347
11348        // Re-establish on the same pseudonym, the way a client reusing its configured pseudonym
11349        // would. The initiation runs the same handshake the first one did, so the second admit
11350        // comes from the same commit point.
11351        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
11352            pseudonym,
11353            StartInitiation {
11354                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
11355                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
11356                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capabilities::empty()),
11357                additional_data: 0,
11358            },
11359        )
11360        .await?;
11361
11362        // The successor's admit is in the log, and A's retire is deferred: the interleaving below is
11363        // the one the grace produces — B's admit first, A's retire after — which is exactly the case
11364        // the token makes safe. Waiting the retire out before asserting keeps the order pinned rather
11365        // than assumed.
11366        assert_eq!(
11367            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
11368            1,
11369            "the first teardown's retire must still be paid — deferred past the SURB-resolution window, never \
11370             suppressed"
11371        );
11372        assert_eq!(
11373            admission.sequence(&pseudonym),
11374            vec!["admit", "admit", "retire"]
11375                .into_iter()
11376                .map(String::from)
11377                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
11378            "the successor must be admitted before A's deferred retire fires — the case the token exists for"
11379        );
11380
11381        let minted = admission.minted_tokens();
11382        assert_eq!(
11383            minted.len(),
11384            2,
11385            "two Sessions on one pseudonym must mint two admissions"
11386        );
11387        assert_ne!(
11388            minted[0], minted[1],
11389            "the two admissions must carry distinct tokens, or no retire could tell them apart"
11390        );
11391        assert_eq!(
11392            admission.retire_tokens(),
11393            vec![minted[0]],
11394            "A's retire must present A's token and not B's — a teardown that re-looked-up the slot under the \
11395             pseudonym would present B's and invalidate the live ring"
11396        );
11397
11398        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
11399        Ok(())
11400    }
11401
11402    /// A stale teardown token must not retire a successor Session's admission.
11403    ///
11404    /// This is the manager side of the token guard the deferred retire leans on. The first Session's
11405    /// teardown captures its own token; a successor is then admitted on the same client-chosen
11406    /// pseudonym before that token is presented. The seam is wired so the teardown of a Session can
11407    /// only ever present the token its own `commit` obtained — the slot carries the token `commit`
11408    /// stamped into it, not whatever the teardown could otherwise reach for — which is the property
11409    /// this pins. The store's matching of token against admission is pinned over in
11410    /// `hopr-protocol-hopr`, which is where the matching lives.
11411    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11412    async fn a_teardown_presents_the_token_of_the_session_it_is_tearing_down() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11413        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
11414        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
11415            SessionManagerConfig {
11416                // Shortened so the deferred retire is exercised without waiting out the library
11417                // default in real time.
11418                surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
11419                ..Default::default()
11420            },
11421            Some(Arc::new(admission.clone())),
11422        )
11423        .await?;
11424
11425        assert_eq!(
11426            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
11427            1,
11428            "the first Session must be established for the token threading below to mean anything"
11429        );
11430        let first_token = admission
11431            .minted_tokens()
11432            .first()
11433            .copied()
11434            .ok_or(anyhow!("the first Session's commit must have minted a token"))?;
11435
11436        // Close the first Session: its teardown captures the token its own commit obtained and
11437        // schedules the retire with it. The token is read from the slot the teardown removes, so
11438        // what reaches the retire is that Session's, never a successor's.
11439        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
11440
11441        // The deferred retire carries the first admission's token, which the mock records; a
11442        // successor admitted in the meantime — as the reuse test above establishes — would then be
11443        // immune to it by construction, since the tokens differ. The retire must still be paid.
11444        assert_eq!(
11445            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
11446            1,
11447            "the teardown must present a token to the store — an unsuppressed retire is the contract, and the store's \
11448             matching is what makes the stale case safe"
11449        );
11450        let presented = admission
11451            .retire_tokens()
11452            .last()
11453            .copied()
11454            .ok_or(anyhow!("the teardown must have presented a token to the store"))?;
11455        assert_eq!(
11456            presented, first_token,
11457            "the teardown must present the token its own Session's commit obtained, not a successor's — a successor \
11458             admitted in the deferred-retire window would otherwise be invalidated"
11459        );
11460        assert!(
11461            !admission.retire_precedes_admit(&pseudonym),
11462            "no retire may be recorded before the Session's own admit"
11463        );
11464
11465        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
11466        Ok(())
11467    }
11468
11469    /// Verifies that established sessions exchange `KeepAlive` messages driven by the SURB balancer,
11470    /// that config updates propagate via keep-alives, and that SURB usage statistics are collected.
11471    ///
11472    /// ## Steps
11473    /// 1. Alice's manager is started with no `PixToolbox` and a `SurbBalancerConfig` with `target_surb_buffer_size:
11474    ///    100`. Bob's manager is configured with a 500ms `surb_balance_notify_period`. Alice's first fill is paced, a
11475    ///    fifth of the target a second, and a session is ready at a quarter of the target, so it is ready after 1.25 s
11476    ///    of fill plus up to a sampling tick (1.5 s measured), and not before 0.8 s, which an unpaced fill at this
11477    ///    test's ceiling would beat; Alice's balancer is seen to have armed the pacing, and Bob's not.
11478    /// 2. Alice initiates a session with the balancer config and PIX quota set; the `StartSession` /
11479    ///    `SessionEstablished` handshake completes via mock transports.
11480    /// 3. Both managers report the same `target_surb_buffer_size` via `get_surb_balancer_config` (confirmed from both
11481    ///    Alice and Bob's perspective).
11482    /// 4. A 1500ms sleep allows the SURB balancer's periodic keep-alive timer to fire multiple times.
11483    /// 5. `update_surb_balancer_config` is called to raise the target to 200. After another 1500ms, Bob's manager
11484    ///    reflects the updated target via `get_surb_balancer_config`, confirming keep-alives communicated the change.
11485    ///    That is with Alice's `surb_target_notify` on (`target_notify`). With it off, Alice's keep-alives carry no
11486    ///    `BalancerTarget` flag and no target, and Bob keeps the one announced at establishment.
11487    /// 6. `get_surb_level_estimates` is called on both sides; both report positive sent/received/used counts,
11488    ///    confirming the balancer collected SURB statistics.
11489    /// 7. Alice closes the session; `ping_session` returns `NonExistingSession` after a short wait.
11490    ///
11491    /// Bob's level reports are required in both cases, and are the end-to-end proof that the Exit sends them to
11492    /// an Entry it knows to be balancing by its keep-alives, whether or not those announce its target.
11493    ///
11494    /// The mock transports hand Alice's keep-alives to Bob with the packet info the pipeline would give
11495    /// them (`keep_alive_packet_info`): the SURBs the packet carried. Bob books those, not the message's
11496    /// declared maximum, so a mock that reported none would leave him with no received SURBs.
11497    #[rstest]
11498    #[case::target_notify_on(true)]
11499    #[case::target_notify_off(false)]
11500    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11501    async fn session_manager_should_send_keep_alives_via_surb_balancer(
11502        #[case] target_notify: bool,
11503    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11504        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
11505        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
11506
11507        let bob_cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
11508            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_millis(500)),
11509            ..Default::default()
11510        };
11511        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
11512            surb_target_notify: target_notify,
11513            ..Default::default()
11514        });
11515        let bob_mgr = SessionManager::new(bob_cfg.clone());
11516
11517        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
11518        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
11519
11520        // What Alice's keep-alives said: their flags and their additional data, in the order sent.
11521        let alice_keep_alives: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<(KeepAliveFlags, u64)>>> = Default::default();
11522
11523        // The SURBs a keep-alive actually carried, as the wire would report them. Alice's keep-alives
11524        // are the only SURB source in this fixture, so the Exit's estimate has to be built from these
11525        // packet infos rather than from `max_surbs()` alone.
11526        let surbs_carried = |data: &ApplicationDataOut| -> IncomingPacketInfo {
11527            let carried = HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
11528                .map(|msg| match msg {
11529                    StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka) => ka.max_surbs().unwrap_or_default(),
11530                    _ => 0,
11531                })
11532                .unwrap_or_default();
11533            IncomingPacketInfo {
11534                num_saved_surbs: carried,
11535                ..Default::default()
11536            }
11537        };
11538
11539        // Alice sends the StartSession message
11540        let mut open_sequence = mockall::Sequence::new();
11541        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
11542        alice_transport
11543            .expect_send_message()
11544            .once()
11545            .in_sequence(&mut open_sequence)
11546            .withf(move |peer, data| {
11547                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
11548                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
11549            })
11550            .returning(move |_, data| {
11551                let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
11552                Box::pin(async move {
11553                    let packet_info = surbs_carried(&data);
11554                    bob_mgr_clone
11555                        .dispatch_message(
11556                            alice_pseudonym,
11557                            ApplicationDataIn {
11558                                data: data.data,
11559                                packet_info,
11560                            },
11561                        )
11562                        ?;
11563                    Ok(())
11564                })
11565            });
11566
11567        // Bob sends the SessionEstablished message
11568        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
11569        bob_transport
11570            .expect_send_message()
11571            .once()
11572            .in_sequence(&mut open_sequence)
11573            .withf(move |peer, data| {
11574                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished)
11575                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == alice_pseudonym)
11576            })
11577            .returning(move |_, data| {
11578                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
11579                Box::pin(async move {
11580                    alice_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
11581                        alice_pseudonym,
11582                        ApplicationDataIn {
11583                            data: data.data,
11584                            packet_info: Default::default(),
11585                        },
11586                    )?;
11587                    Ok(())
11588                })
11589            });
11590
11591        // Large enough for the paced first fill (a fifth of the target per second) to have delivered
11592        // something by Bob's first level report, 500 ms in; the mock accepts only reports above zero.
11593        const INITIAL_BALANCER_TARGET: u64 = 100;
11594
11595        const NEXT_BALANCER_TARGET: u64 = 200;
11596
11597        // Alice sends KeepAlive messages from her balancer, which Bob receives. What they say is
11598        // recorded rather than matched here: with `surb_target_notify` on they announce the balancer
11599        // target (the initial one, then the updated one), and with it off they say nothing, and either
11600        // way they are the evidence to Bob that Alice balances.
11601        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
11602        let alice_keep_alives_clone = alice_keep_alives.clone();
11603        alice_transport
11604            .expect_send_message()
11605            .times(1..)
11606            //.in_sequence(&mut sequence)
11607            .withf(move |peer, data| {
11608                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::KeepAlive)
11609                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
11610            })
11611            .returning(move |_, data| {
11612                let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
11613                let alice_keep_alives_clone = alice_keep_alives_clone.clone();
11614                Box::pin(async move {
11615                    if let Ok(StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka)) =
11616                        HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
11617                    {
11618                        alice_keep_alives_clone.lock().push((ka.flags, ka.additional_data));
11619                    }
11620                    bob_mgr_clone
11621                        .dispatch_message(
11622                            alice_pseudonym,
11623                            ApplicationDataIn {
11624                                packet_info: keep_alive_packet_info(&data.data),
11625                                data: data.data,
11626                            },
11627                        )
11628                        ?;
11629                    Ok(())
11630                })
11631            });
11632
11633        // Bob sends at least 1 Keep Alive back reporting its SURB estimate
11634        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
11635        bob_transport
11636            .expect_send_message()
11637            .times(1..)
11638            //.in_sequence(&mut open_sequence)
11639            .withf(move |peer, data| {
11640                start_msg_match(data, |msg| matches!(msg, StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka) if ka.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState) && ka.additional_data > 0))
11641                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == alice_pseudonym)
11642            })
11643            .returning(move |_, data| {
11644                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
11645                Box::pin(async move {
11646                    alice_mgr_clone
11647                        .dispatch_message(
11648                            alice_pseudonym,
11649                            ApplicationDataIn {
11650                                data: data.data,
11651                                packet_info: Default::default(),
11652                            },
11653                        )
11654                        ?;
11655                    Ok(())
11656                })
11657            });
11658
11659        // Alice sends the terminating segment to close the Session
11660        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
11661        alice_transport
11662            .expect_send_message()
11663            .once()
11664            //.in_sequence(&mut sequence)
11665            .withf(move |peer, data| {
11666                hopr_protocol_session::types::SessionMessage::<{ ApplicationData::PAYLOAD_SIZE }>::try_from(
11667                    data.data.plain_text.as_ref(),
11668                )
11669                .ok()
11670                .and_then(|m| m.try_as_segment())
11671                .map(|s| s.is_terminating())
11672                .unwrap_or(false)
11673                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
11674            })
11675            .returning(move |_, data| {
11676                let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
11677                Box::pin(async move {
11678                    let packet_info = surbs_carried(&data);
11679                    bob_mgr_clone
11680                        .dispatch_message(
11681                            alice_pseudonym,
11682                            ApplicationDataIn {
11683                                data: data.data,
11684                                packet_info,
11685                            },
11686                        )
11687                        ?;
11688                    Ok(())
11689                })
11690            });
11691
11692        let mut ahs = Vec::new();
11693
11694        // Start Alice
11695        let (new_session_tx_alice, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
11696        let (alice_sender, alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
11697        ahs.extend(alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_alice, None, None)?);
11698        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
11699
11700        // Start Bob
11701        let (new_session_tx_bob, new_session_rx_bob) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
11702        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
11703        ahs.extend(bob_mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_bob, None, None)?);
11704        assert!(bob_mgr.is_started());
11705
11706        let target = SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?);
11707
11708        let balancer_cfg = SurbBalancerConfig {
11709            target_surb_buffer_size: INITIAL_BALANCER_TARGET,
11710            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
11711            ..Default::default()
11712        };
11713
11714        pin_mut!(new_session_rx_bob);
11715        // The first fill is paced, so readiness (a quarter of the target) takes 1.25 s of fill whatever the
11716        // target, plus up to a sampling tick (1.5 s measured); the open is given 4 s. Alice's slot exists
11717        // from before the readiness wait, and the first thing seen of it is whether
11718        // her balancer, the Entry's, armed the pacing of the first fill.
11719        let alice_slot_seen = async {
11720            loop {
11721                if let Some(slot) = alice_mgr.sessions.get(&alice_pseudonym) {
11722                    break slot.surb_mgmt.refill_pacing_active();
11723                }
11724                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
11725            }
11726        };
11727        let opened_at = Instant::now();
11728        let (alice_session, bob_session, alice_first_fill_paced) = timeout(
11729            Duration::from_secs(4),
11730            futures::future::join3(
11731                alice_mgr.new_session(
11732                    bob_peer,
11733                    SessionTarget::TcpStream(target.clone()),
11734                    SessionClientConfig {
11735                        pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
11736                        capabilities: Capability::Segmentation.into(),
11737                        surb_management: Some(balancer_cfg),
11738                        ..Default::default()
11739                    },
11740                ),
11741                new_session_rx_bob.next(),
11742                alice_slot_seen,
11743            ),
11744        )
11745        .await?;
11746        let opening = opened_at.elapsed();
11747
11748        let mut alice_session = alice_session?;
11749        let bob_session = bob_session.ok_or(anyhow!("bob must get an incoming session"))?;
11750        // A quarter of a target of 100 at 20 SURBs a second is 1.25 s; the ceiling of this test, 100 a
11751        // second, would have been ready in about a quarter of that.
11752        assert!(
11753            opening >= Duration::from_millis(800),
11754            "a paced first fill cannot make the session ready this fast, it took {opening:?}"
11755        );
11756        assert!(
11757            alice_first_fill_paced,
11758            "the Entry's balancer must pace its first fill like the refill after a wipe"
11759        );
11760        assert!(
11761            !bob_mgr
11762                .sessions
11763                .get(bob_session.session.id())
11764                .ok_or(anyhow!("bob must hold the session slot"))?
11765                .surb_mgmt
11766                .refill_pacing_active(),
11767            "the Exit's balancer does not pace anything at its start"
11768        );
11769
11770        assert!(matches!(bob_session.target, SessionTarget::TcpStream(host) if host == target));
11771
11772        assert_eq!(
11773            Some(balancer_cfg),
11774            alice_mgr.get_surb_balancer_config(alice_session.id())?
11775        );
11776
11777        // The organic SURB gate, on the real slot rather than a hand-built state. Two things it must
11778        // get right, both of which would deadlock a Session if inverted.
11779        {
11780            let alice_slot = alice_mgr
11781                .sessions
11782                .get(alice_session.id())
11783                .ok_or(anyhow!("alice must hold the session slot"))?;
11784
11785            // At cold start the gate must be open: readiness only waits for a quarter of the target, so a
11786            // gate that closed at or below that would stop the very production it is waiting on.
11787            assert_eq!(
11788                1,
11789                alice_slot.surb_mgmt.organic_surbs_per_packet(),
11790                "a freshly opened session must still produce organic SURBs"
11791            );
11792
11793            // And it must stay open on the counterparty's word, whatever the local estimate says.
11794            alice_slot
11795                .surb_mgmt
11796                .observe_counterparty_signals(PacketSignal::OutOfSurbs.into());
11797            alice_slot
11798                .surb_mgmt
11799                .buffer_level
11800                .store(u64::MAX, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11801            assert_eq!(
11802                1,
11803                alice_slot.surb_mgmt.organic_surbs_per_packet(),
11804                "a counterparty out of SURBs must override any local estimate"
11805            );
11806
11807            // Leave the slot as it was found; the balancer loop keeps running below.
11808            alice_slot
11809                .surb_mgmt
11810                .observe_counterparty_signals(PacketSignals::default());
11811            alice_slot
11812                .surb_mgmt
11813                .buffer_level
11814                .store(0, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11815        }
11816
11817        let remote_cfg = bob_mgr
11818            .get_surb_balancer_config(bob_session.session.id())?
11819            .ok_or(anyhow!("no remote config at bob"))?;
11820        assert_eq!(remote_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size, balancer_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size);
11821        assert_eq!(
11822            remote_cfg.max_surbs_per_sec,
11823            remote_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size
11824                / bob_cfg
11825                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
11826                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
11827                    .as_secs()
11828        );
11829
11830        // Let the Surb balancer send enough KeepAlive messages
11831        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
11832
11833        let new_balancer_cfg = SurbBalancerConfig {
11834            target_surb_buffer_size: NEXT_BALANCER_TARGET,
11835            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
11836            ..Default::default()
11837        };
11838
11839        // Update to a higher target
11840        alice_mgr.update_surb_balancer_config(alice_session.id(), new_balancer_cfg)?;
11841
11842        // Let the Surb balancer send enough KeepAlive messages
11843        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
11844
11845        // Bob knows about the updated target only if Alice announces it.
11846        let remote_cfg = bob_mgr
11847            .get_surb_balancer_config(bob_session.session.id())?
11848            .ok_or(anyhow!("no remote config at bob"))?;
11849        let expected_remote_target = if target_notify {
11850            new_balancer_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size
11851        } else {
11852            balancer_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size
11853        };
11854        assert_eq!(
11855            remote_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size, expected_remote_target,
11856            "Bob learns the raised target exactly when Alice's keep-alives announce it"
11857        );
11858        assert_eq!(
11859            remote_cfg.max_surbs_per_sec,
11860            expected_remote_target / bob_cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.as_secs()
11861        );
11862
11863        // Alice's keep-alives carry `BalancerTarget` with her target exactly when she announces it.
11864        let said = alice_keep_alives.lock().clone();
11865        assert!(!said.is_empty(), "Alice's balancer must have sent keep-alives");
11866        if target_notify {
11867            assert!(
11868                said.iter()
11869                    .all(|(flags, _)| flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget)),
11870                "every keep-alive of an announcing Entry names her target: {said:?}"
11871            );
11872            for target in [INITIAL_BALANCER_TARGET, NEXT_BALANCER_TARGET] {
11873                assert!(
11874                    said.iter().any(|(_, announced)| *announced == target),
11875                    "no keep-alive announced the target {target}: {said:?}"
11876                );
11877            }
11878        } else {
11879            assert!(
11880                said.iter()
11881                    .all(|(flags, announced)| flags.is_empty() && *announced == 0),
11882                "with `surb_target_notify` off the keep-alives carry no flag and no target: {said:?}"
11883            );
11884        }
11885
11886        let (alice_surb_sent, alice_surb_used) = alice_mgr.get_surb_level_estimates(alice_session.id())?;
11887        let (bob_surb_recv, bob_surb_used) = bob_mgr.get_surb_level_estimates(bob_session.session.id())?;
11888
11889        alice_session.close().await?;
11890
11891        assert!(alice_surb_sent > 0, "alice must've sent surbs");
11892        assert!(bob_surb_recv > 0, "bob must've received surbs");
11893        assert!(
11894            bob_surb_recv <= alice_surb_sent,
11895            "bob cannot receive more surbs than alice sent"
11896        );
11897
11898        assert!(alice_surb_used > 0, "alice must see bob used surbs");
11899        assert!(bob_surb_used > 0, "bob must've used surbs");
11900        assert!(
11901            alice_surb_used <= bob_surb_used,
11902            "alice cannot see bob used more surbs than bob actually used"
11903        );
11904
11905        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
11906        assert!(matches!(
11907            alice_mgr.ping_session(alice_session.id()).await,
11908            Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession))
11909        ));
11910
11911        futures::stream::iter(ahs)
11912            .for_each(|ah| async move { ah.abort() })
11913            .await;
11914
11915        // Cleanup: close senders and await handles
11916        alice_sender.close_channel();
11917        bob_sender.close_channel();
11918        alice_handle.await??;
11919        bob_handle.await??;
11920
11921        Ok(())
11922    }

11924    /// Verifies that a second incoming session initiation for the same pseudonym is handled gracefully
11925    /// (returns `Ok`) without creating a duplicate session slot.
11926    ///
11927    /// ## Steps
11928    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is started with a mock transport that accepts two outbound messages.
11929    /// 2. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with pseudonym `X` — succeeds; exactly one active session is
11930    ///    confirmed.
11931    /// 3. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called again with the same pseudonym `X`. The manager detects the
11932    ///    conflict and handles it internally by sending a `SessionError` to the peer.
11933    /// 4. The call still returns `Ok` (error is handled internally); `num_active_sessions` remains 1 with only the
11934    ///    original pseudonym present.
11935    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
11936    async fn session_manager_should_reject_duplicate_session_for_same_pseudonym() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
11937        use hopr_utils::network_types::prelude::SealedHost;
11938
11939        let bob_mgr: SessionManager<futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
11940            SessionManager::new(Default::default());
11941
11942        // Start the manager (required for handling incoming sessions)
11943        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
11944        transport
11945            .expect_send_message()
11946            .times(2)
11947            .returning(|_, _| futures::future::ok(()).boxed());
11948
11949        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
11950        // Spawn a task to receive new session notifications
11951        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
11952            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
11953            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {
11954                // Just drain the channel
11955            }
11956        });
11957        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
11958        bob_mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
11959        assert!(bob_mgr.is_started());
11960
11961        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
11962
11963        // First session initiation - should succeed
11964        let result = bob_mgr
11965            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
11966                pseudonym,
11967                StartInitiation {
11968                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
11969                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
11970                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
11971                    additional_data: 0,
11972                },
11973            )
11974            .await;
11975
11976        assert!(result.is_ok(), "first session initiation should succeed");
11977
11978        // Verify one session exists
11979        let active = bob_mgr.active_sessions();
11980        assert_eq!(active.len(), 1, "should have exactly one active session");
11981        assert_eq!(bob_mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1);
11982
11983        // Second session initiation with same pseudonym - should be handled gracefully
11984        // (returns Ok but sends SessionError to the requester)
11985        let result = bob_mgr
11986            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
11987                pseudonym,
11988                StartInitiation {
11989                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
11990                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
11991                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
11992                    additional_data: 0,
11993                },
11994            )
11995            .await;
11996
11997        // The second initiation returns Ok but handles the duplicate by sending SessionError
11998        assert!(
11999            result.is_ok(),
12000            "second session initiation should return Ok (error is handled internally)"
12001        );
12002
12003        // Verify still only one session exists
12004        let active = bob_mgr.active_sessions();
12005        assert_eq!(active.len(), 1, "should still have exactly one active session");
12006        assert_eq!(bob_mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1);
12007
12008        // Cleanup: close sender and await handle
12009        sender.close_channel();
12010        _handle.await??;
12011
12012        Ok(())
12013    }

12194    /// Verifies the `HoprStartProtocol::SessionError` match arm (line 689) in the
12195    /// `session_start_protocol_processor` task by calling `handle_session_error` directly.
12196    ///
12197    /// When a `SessionError` message is delivered while a `new_session` call is awaiting,
12198    /// `handle_session_error` retrieves the pending challenge from `session_initiations`,
12199    /// sends the error down the channel, and `new_session` propagates it as `Rejected`.
12200    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12201    async fn handle_session_error_propagates_peer_rejection_to_pending_new_session() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12202        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
12203            SessionManager::new(Default::default());
12204
12205        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
12206        // new_session sends StartSession (succeeds), then waits for SessionEstablished.
12207        // We inject the error before it arrives.
12208        transport
12209            .expect_send_message()
12210            .returning(|_, _| futures::future::ok(()).boxed());
12211
12212        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
12213        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
12214            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
12215            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
12216        });
12217        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
12218        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
12219        assert!(mgr.is_started());
12220
12221        // Spawn new_session so it is blocked waiting for the session establishment response.
12222        let mgr_clone = mgr.clone();
12223        let peer_address: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
12224        let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
12225            mgr_clone
12226                .new_session(
12227                    peer_address,
12228                    SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
12229                    SessionClientConfig {
12230                        surb_management: None,
12231                        ..Default::default()
12232                    },
12233                )
12234                .await
12235        });
12236
12237        // Give new_session time to insert the challenge into session_initiations.
12238        let challenge = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
12239            loop {
12240                if let Some((ch, _)) = mgr.session_initiations.iter().next() {
12241                    break *ch;
12242                }
12243                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
12244            }
12245        })
12246        .await
12247        .context("new_session did not insert a challenge into session_initiations")?;
12248
12249        // Inject the SessionError with the matching challenge before SessionEstablished arrives.
12250        let error_type = StartErrorType {
12251            identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(challenge),
12252            reason: StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable,
12253        };
12254        // The error is challenge-identified, so the handler ignores the sender's pseudonym on this
12255        // arm; `new_session` picks a random one, and none is captured here.
12256        mgr.handle_session_error(HoprPseudonym::random(), error_type).await?;
12257
12258        // new_session must propagate the error as Rejected.
12259        let result = handle.await?;
12260        match result {
12261            Ok(_session) => panic!("expected rejection error, got session"),
12262            Err(e) => {
12263                assert!(matches!(
12264                    e,
12265                    TransportSessionError::Rejected(StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable)
12266                ));
12267            }
12268        }
12269
12270        sender.close_channel();
12271        _handle.await??;
12272        Ok(())
12273    }
12274
12275    /// Verifies that an incoming session initiation is rejected (handled internally) when the
12276    /// manager already has `maximum_sessions` active sessions.
12277    ///
12278    /// ## Steps
12279    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is configured with `maximum_sessions: 1`.
12280    /// 2. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with pseudonym `X1` — succeeds; one active session confirmed.
12281    /// 3. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with pseudonym `X2` — the manager detects it is at capacity
12282    ///    and handles the conflict internally (sends `SessionError` to peer).
12283    /// 4. The call returns `Ok` (handled internally); `num_active_sessions` remains 1, with only `X1` present — `X2`
12284    ///    was rejected without creating a slot.
12285    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12286    async fn session_manager_should_reject_new_session_when_max_sessions_reached() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12287        use hopr_utils::network_types::prelude::SealedHost;
12288
12289        // Create manager with max 1 session
12290        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
12291            maximum_sessions: 1,
12292            ..Default::default()
12293        };
12294        let mgr: SessionManager<futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
12295            SessionManager::new(cfg);
12296
12297        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
12298        transport
12299            .expect_send_message()
12300            .times(2)
12301            .returning(|_, _| futures::future::ok(()).boxed());
12302
12303        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
12304        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
12305            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
12306            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
12307        });
12308        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
12309        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
12310        assert!(mgr.is_started());
12311
12312        // First session - should succeed
12313        let pseudonym1 = HoprPseudonym::random();
12314        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
12315            pseudonym1,
12316            StartInitiation {
12317                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
12318                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
12319                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
12320                additional_data: 0,
12321            },
12322        )
12323        .await?;
12324
12325        // Verify one session exists
12326        assert_eq!(mgr.active_sessions().len(), 1);
12327        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1);
12328
12329        // Second session - should fail with TooManySessions
12330        let pseudonym2 = HoprPseudonym::random();
12331        let _result = mgr
12332            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
12333                pseudonym2,
12334                StartInitiation {
12335                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
12336                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
12337                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
12338                    additional_data: 0,
12339                },
12340            )
12341            .await;
12342
12343        // The error is handled internally (sends SessionError), so result is Ok
12344        // But we can verify no new session was added
12345        assert_eq!(mgr.active_sessions().len(), 1);
12346        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1);
12347
12348        // Cleanup: close sender and await handle
12349        sender.close_channel();
12350        _handle.await??;
12351
12352        Ok(())
12353    }

12355    /// The node refuses a PIX Session it has no reconstructor memory left for, and does so before
12356    /// allocating anything.
12357    ///
12358    /// This is the bound `maximum_sessions` cannot express: a session slot is one slot whatever the
12359    /// peer offered, while the reconstructor state behind it is set by the peer's dimensions. Here
12360    /// `maximum_sessions` is wide open and the budget is exactly one Session's worth, so nothing but
12361    /// the budget can be doing the refusing.
12362    ///
12363    /// Refused, not queued: nothing later in establishment can give the memory back, and the peer is
12364    /// free to retry against another Exit.
12365    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12366    async fn a_pix_session_over_the_live_cycle_budget_is_refused() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12367        use hopr_utils::network_types::prelude::SealedHost;
12368
12369        // Four shares has only one legal dimension split: 2 polynomials at threshold 2. Using no
12370        // surplus makes this offer the worst-case reservation at its exact quota, so the configured
12371        // budget can honestly admit the whole range while still fitting exactly one such Session.
12372        let params = PixParams::try_new(2, 2, 0, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
12373        let quota = pix_params_to_quota(&params);
12374        let one_session = cycle_budget_for(&params, DEFAULT_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST);
12375        assert_eq!(one_session, max_cycle_budget_for_quota(quota, 1));
12376
12377        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
12378            SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
12379                maximum_sessions: 100,
12380                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
12381                    quota_range: quota..=quota,
12382                    // Room for exactly one Session at these dimensions.
12383                    max_live_cycle_bytes: one_session,
12384                    ..Default::default()
12385                },
12386                ..Default::default()
12387            });
12388
12389        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
12390            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
12391            threshold: 2,
12392            surplus_shares: 0,
12393        };
12394        let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events_rx) = PixToolbox::new(
12395            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
12396            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
12397        );
12398
12399        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
12400        transport
12401            .expect_send_message()
12402            .returning(|_, _| futures::future::ok(()).boxed());
12403        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
12404        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
12405        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
12406            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
12407            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
12408        });
12409        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
12410
12411        let offer = |pseudonym| {
12412            (
12413                pseudonym,
12414                StartInitiation {
12415                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
12416                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
12417                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
12418                    additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0)),
12419                },
12420            )
12421        };
12422
12423        let (p1, req1) = offer(HoprPseudonym::random());
12424        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(p1, req1).await?;
12425        assert_eq!(1, mgr.num_active_sessions(), "the first PIX session must be admitted");
12426        assert_eq!(
12427            one_session,
12428            mgr.live_cycle_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
12429            "and must have charged exactly one session's worth"
12430        );
12431
12432        // The budget is spent, so this one is refused — handled internally as a `SessionError`,
12433        // hence `Ok` with no new slot.
12434        let (p2, req2) = offer(HoprPseudonym::random());
12435        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(p2, req2).await?;
12436        assert_eq!(
12437            1,
12438            mgr.num_active_sessions(),
12439            "a session over the live-cycle budget must not be admitted"
12440        );
12441        assert_eq!(
12442            one_session,
12443            mgr.live_cycle_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
12444            "and a refused session must not leave a reservation behind"
12445        );
12446
12447        // Closing the admitted session returns its share, and the next request fits again.
12448        assert!(mgr.close_session(&p1));
12449        assert_eq!(
12450            0,
12451            mgr.live_cycle_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
12452            "closing a session must return its reservation"
12453        );
12454
12455        let (p3, req3) = offer(HoprPseudonym::random());
12456        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(p3, req3).await?;
12457        assert_eq!(
12458            1,
12459            mgr.num_active_sessions(),
12460            "the freed budget must admit the next session"
12461        );
12462
12463        sender.close_channel();
12464        _handle.await??;
12465        Ok(())
12466    }
12467
12468    /// A Session is charged for the dimensions its *peer* offered, not for this node's defaults.
12469    ///
12470    /// The Exit accepts a range of dimensions, and the reconstructor state behind them differs by
12471    /// more than an order of magnitude across it. Charging a flat figure would either refuse small
12472    /// Sessions that fit easily or admit large ones that do not.
12473    #[test]
12474    fn the_live_cycle_reservation_scales_with_the_offered_dimensions() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12475        let small = PixParams::try_new(1024, 64, 16, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
12476        let large = PixParams::try_new(8192, 64, 16, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
12477
12478        assert_eq!(
12479            8 * cycle_budget_for(&small, 1),
12480            cycle_budget_for(&large, 1),
12481            "eight times the polynomials must cost eight times the budget"
12482        );
12483        assert_eq!(
12484            3 * cycle_budget_for(&large, 1),
12485            cycle_budget_for(&large, 3),
12486            "and a batch of three must cost three times a batch of one"
12487        );
12488
12489        // The pipelining factor is in there once, and only once: a batch may have one successor
12490        // outstanding, not one per member.
12491        assert_eq!(
12492            MAX_OVERLAPPING_BATCHES * hopr_protocol_pix::peak_cycle_bytes::<HoprPixSpec>(&large),
12493            cycle_budget_for(&large, 1)
12494        );
12495
12496        // The clamp matches the one `SessionManager::new` applies, so a config that never went
12497        // through it cannot understate its own reservation.
12498        assert_eq!(cycle_budget_for(&large, 1), cycle_budget_for(&large, 0));
12499        assert_eq!(
12500            cycle_budget_for(&large, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE),
12501            cycle_budget_for(&large, usize::MAX)
12502        );
12503
12504        Ok(())
12505    }

12507    /// Runs an admission handler against `mgr`'s request channel for the duration of one test.
12508    ///
12509    /// Mirrors what `hopr-lib` spawns beside the session server, minus the concurrency: these tests
12510    /// drive one initiation at a time.
12511    fn spawn_admission_handler(
12512        handler: impl Fn(SessionAdmissionRequest) -> Result<SessionAdmissionDecision, String> + Send + 'static,
12513    ) -> (SessionAdmissionSink, tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>) {
12514        let (tx, mut rx) =
12515            futures::channel::mpsc::channel::<(SessionAdmissionRequest, crate::types::SessionAdmissionReply)>(4);
12516        let handle = tokio::task::spawn(async move {
12517            while let Some((request, reply)) = rx.next().await {
12518                let _ = reply.send(handler(request));
12519            }
12520        });
12521        (tx, handle)
12522    }
12523
12524    /// What [`started_manager_admitting_small_params`] hands back: the manager, its message sender
12525    /// and the task draining it, the first `SessionError` it replies with, and the incoming-session
12526    /// receiver — which the test must hold, since an admitted Session is published on it and a
12527    /// dropped receiver would turn every success into a send failure.
12528    type AdmissionFixture = (
12529        SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
12530        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
12531        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
12532        oneshot::Receiver<StartErrorType<SessionId>>,
12533        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
12534    );
12535
12536    /// A started manager that accepts an Entry offering [`small_pix_params`], with `admission`
12537    /// installed as its session server, so that any refusal is attributable to the decision rather
12538    /// than to the dimensions or to a missing toolbox.
12539    fn started_manager_admitting_small_params(
12540        quota_range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<SsaQuota>,
12541        enforce_pix: bool,
12542        admission: Option<SessionAdmissionSink>,
12543    ) -> anyhow::Result<AdmissionFixture> {
12544        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
12545
12546        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
12547            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
12548                enforce_pix,
12549                quota_range,
12550                ..Default::default()
12551            },
12552            session_admission_timeout: Duration::from_millis(200),
12553            ..Default::default()
12554        });
12555
12556        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
12557            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
12558                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
12559                threshold: 2,
12560                surplus_shares: TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES,
12561            })
12562            .into(),
12563            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
12564        );
12565
12566        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
12567        let (err_tx, err_rx) = oneshot::channel();
12568        let err_tx = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(err_tx)));
12569        transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
12570            let err_tx = err_tx.clone();
12571            Box::pin(async move {
12572                if let Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(err)) =
12573                    HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
12574                    && let Some(tx) = err_tx.lock().unwrap().take()
12575                {
12576                    let _ = tx.send(err);
12577                }
12578                Ok(())
12579            })
12580        });
12581
12582        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
12583        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
12584        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), admission)?;
12585
12586        Ok((mgr, sender, handle, err_rx, new_session_rx))
12587    }

12589    /// An Entry offering [`small_pix_params`], i.e. an offer the fixture's node accepts.
12590    fn pix_offer() -> StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities> {
12591        StartInitiation {
12592            challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
12593            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain(
12594                "127.0.0.1:80".parse().expect("test target must parse"),
12595            )),
12596            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::UsePIX),
12597            additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
12598        }
12599    }
12600
12601    /// The same target from an Entry that offered no incentivization at all.
12602    fn no_pix_offer() -> StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities> {
12603        StartInitiation {
12604            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::Segmentation.into()),
12605            additional_data: 0,
12606            ..pix_offer()
12607        }
12608    }
12609
12610    /// The quota an Entry offering [`small_pix_params`] asks for.
12611    fn small_params_quota() -> SsaQuota {
12612        pix_params_to_quota(&small_pix_params())
12613    }
12614
12615    /// A node's configured window is an envelope, not a default: a decision may take less of it, but
12616    /// asking for more of it than was configured — and validated, and preallocated against — leaves
12617    /// the envelope's own bounds in place.
12618    #[test]
12619    fn an_admission_decision_narrows_the_configured_quota_window_and_never_widens_it() {
12620        let cfg = IncomingSessionPixConfig {
12621            quota_range: 100..=200,
12622            ..Default::default()
12623        };
12624
12625        let narrowed = cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_pix_quota_range(120..=180));
12626        assert_eq!(narrowed.quota_range, 120..=180);
12627
12628        let widened = cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_pix_quota_range(1..=1000));
12629        assert_eq!(widened.quota_range, 100..=200, "neither bound may leave the envelope");
12630
12631        let one_end = cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_pix_quota_range(150..=u64::MAX));
12632        assert_eq!(one_end.quota_range, 150..=200, "an open end leaves that bound alone");
12633
12634        let disjoint = cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_pix_quota_range(500..=600));
12635        assert!(
12636            disjoint.quota_range.is_empty(),
12637            "a rule that does not overlap the envelope admits nothing, rather than silently picking one"
12638        );
12639    }
12640
12641    /// Unlike the quota window, `enforce_pix` is coupled to nothing validated at startup, so a
12642    /// decision simply replaces it — in either direction.
12643    #[test]
12644    fn an_admission_decision_overrides_enforce_pix_in_both_directions() {
12645        let strict = IncomingSessionPixConfig {
12646            enforce_pix: true,
12647            ..Default::default()
12648        };
12649        let lax = IncomingSessionPixConfig {
12650            enforce_pix: false,
12651            ..Default::default()
12652        };
12653
12654        assert!(strict.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default()).enforce_pix);
12655        assert!(
12656            !strict
12657                .effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_enforce_pix(false))
12658                .enforce_pix
12659        );
12660        assert!(!lax.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default()).enforce_pix);
12661        assert!(
12662            lax.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_enforce_pix(true))
12663                .enforce_pix
12664        );
12665    }

12667    /// Runs an initiation through the same two steps admission does — read the offer off the wire,
12668    /// then judge it against the node's own terms. `None` is a refusal from either.
12669    fn decode_and_check(
12670        mgr: &SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
12671        req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
12672    ) -> Option<(PixParams, usize)> {
12673        let policy = mgr.cfg.pix_config.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default());
12674        decode_pix_offer(req)
12675            .ok()
12676            .and_then(|offered| mgr.check_pix_params(req.challenge, offered, &policy))
12677    }
12678
12679    /// The offer must reach the session server decoded, and the capability bits verbatim.
12680    ///
12681    /// Without it the server can only price a target blind: it names a window with no idea whether
12682    /// the peer is anywhere near it, and cannot hold a *dimension* to a floor, since the quota is
12683    /// their product and the same product admits many splits.
12684    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12685    async fn the_admission_request_carries_the_decoded_offer_and_capability_bits() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12686        let (seen_tx, seen_rx) = oneshot::channel();
12687        let seen_tx = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(seen_tx)));
12688        let (admission, handler) = spawn_admission_handler(move |request| {
12689            if let Some(tx) = seen_tx.lock().unwrap().take() {
12690                let _ = tx.send((request.capabilities, request.offered));
12691            }
12692            Ok(SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
12693        });
12694        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
12695            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, Some(admission))?;
12696
12697        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(HoprPseudonym::random(), pix_offer())
12698            .await?;
12699
12700        let (capabilities, offered) = seen_rx.await.context("admission was never asked")?;
12701        let offered = offered.context("an offer was made, so one must have been reported")?;
12702
12703        let params = small_pix_params();
12704        assert_eq!(offered.parts_per_ssa, params.polys_per_ssa());
12705        assert_eq!(offered.shares_per_part, params.shares_per_poly());
12706        assert_eq!(
12707            offered.surplus_shares,
12708            params.surplus_shares(),
12709            "the surplus is priced in, so a server judging the quota needs it"
12710        );
12711        assert_eq!(offered.quota_per_ssa, small_params_quota());
12712        assert_eq!(
12713            capabilities,
12714            pix_offer().capabilities.0.bits(),
12715            "the capability bits travel as the peer sent them"
12716        );
12717
12718        sender.close_channel();
12719        transport.await??;
12720        handler.abort();
12721        Ok(())
12722    }
12723
12724    /// A peer offering nothing must be reported as offering nothing, not as offering zero: the two
12725    /// are different answers, and only one of them means "this Session is free if you allow it".
12726    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12727    async fn a_peer_offering_no_incentivization_reports_no_offer() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12728        let (seen_tx, seen_rx) = oneshot::channel();
12729        let seen_tx = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(seen_tx)));
12730        let (admission, handler) = spawn_admission_handler(move |request| {
12731            if let Some(tx) = seen_tx.lock().unwrap().take() {
12732                let _ = tx.send(request.offered);
12733            }
12734            Ok(SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
12735        });
12736        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
12737            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, Some(admission))?;
12738
12739        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(HoprPseudonym::random(), no_pix_offer())
12740            .await?;
12741
12742        assert!(
12743            seen_rx.await.context("admission was never asked")?.is_none(),
12744            "no offer must read as no offer"
12745        );
12746
12747        sender.close_channel();
12748        transport.await??;
12749        handler.abort();
12750        Ok(())
12751    }

12753    /// An offer this node cannot read is refused before the session server is troubled with it: no
12754    /// decision could rescue it, and the round trip would be spent to reach the same answer.
12755    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12756    async fn an_unreadable_offer_is_refused_without_asking_the_session_server() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12757        let asked = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
12758        let asked_by_handler = asked.clone();
12759        let (admission, handler) = spawn_admission_handler(move |_| {
12760            asked_by_handler.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
12761            Ok(SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
12762        });
12763        let (mgr, sender, transport, err_rx, _incoming) =
12764            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, Some(admission))?;
12765
12766        // Zero polynomials is outside the protocol range, so unpacking refuses it outright.
12767        let unreadable = StartInitiation {
12768            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(((LOCAL_PIX_SUITE as u64) << 62) | (128u64 << 40)),
12769            ..pix_offer()
12770        };
12771        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(HoprPseudonym::random(), unreadable)
12772            .await?;
12773
12774        let err = err_rx.await.context("send_message was never called")?;
12775        assert_eq!(err.reason, StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams);
12776        assert_eq!(
12777            asked.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
12778            0,
12779            "an offer that cannot be read must not cost an admission round trip"
12780        );
12781        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
12782
12783        sender.close_channel();
12784        transport.await??;
12785        handler.abort();
12786        Ok(())
12787    }

12789    /// The feature itself: one Exit, one Entry offering the same thing, two targets, two answers.
12790    ///
12791    /// Every other test here fixes the decision and varies the offer; this one fixes the offer and
12792    /// varies the target, which is the only thing #8376 actually asks for.
12793    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12794    async fn two_targets_on_one_exit_are_admitted_on_different_terms() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12795        let free_target = SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("10.0.0.1:80".parse()?));
12796        let paid_target = SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("10.0.0.2:80".parse()?));
12797
12798        let free_for = free_target.clone();
12799        let (admission, handler) = spawn_admission_handler(move |request| {
12800            Ok(if request.target == free_for {
12801                SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_enforce_pix(false)
12802            } else {
12803                SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_enforce_pix(true)
12804            })
12805        });
12806
12807        // The node demands PIX; only the rule for `free_target` waives it.
12808        let (mgr, sender, transport, err_rx, _incoming) =
12809            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), true, Some(admission))?;
12810
12811        // Same Entry offer both times — no PIX at all.
12812        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
12813            HoprPseudonym::random(),
12814            StartInitiation {
12815                target: free_target,
12816                ..no_pix_offer()
12817            },
12818        )
12819        .await?;
12820        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1, "the waived target must be served");
12821
12822        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
12823            HoprPseudonym::random(),
12824            StartInitiation {
12825                target: paid_target,
12826                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE + 1,
12827                ..no_pix_offer()
12828            },
12829        )
12830        .await?;
12831        assert_eq!(
12832            mgr.num_active_sessions(),
12833            1,
12834            "the second target must be refused, leaving only the first session"
12835        );
12836
12837        let err = err_rx.await.context("send_message was never called")?;
12838        assert_eq!(err.reason, StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams);
12839        assert_eq!(
12840            err.identifier,
12841            ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(MIN_CHALLENGE + 1),
12842            "the refusal must name the second initiation, not the admitted first"
12843        );
12844
12845        sender.close_channel();
12846        transport.await??;
12847        handler.abort();
12848        Ok(())
12849    }

12851    /// A queue with no reader is the third transient failure, beside the timeout and the dropped
12852    /// reply. It is `Busy` for the same reason: nothing about the target was decided.
12853    ///
12854    /// Reachable only because every request goes through one shared sender — sending through a
12855    /// fresh clone would hand each call its own guaranteed slot and the queue would never be full.
12856    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
12857    async fn a_full_admission_queue_refuses_the_session_as_busy() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12858        // No receiver task at all, so nothing is ever drained. `_rx` is held rather than dropped:
12859        // a closed channel is a different failure from a full one.
12860        let (admission, _rx) =
12861            futures::channel::mpsc::channel::<(SessionAdmissionRequest, crate::types::SessionAdmissionReply)>(0);
12862
12863        let (mgr, sender, transport, err_rx, _incoming) =
12864            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, Some(admission))?;
12865
12866        // The first request takes the sender's guaranteed slot; the second finds the queue full.
12867        for challenge in [MIN_CHALLENGE, MIN_CHALLENGE + 1] {
12868            mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
12869                HoprPseudonym::random(),
12870                StartInitiation {
12871                    challenge,
12872                    ..pix_offer()
12873                },
12874            )
12875            .await?;
12876        }
12877
12878        let err = err_rx.await.context("send_message was never called")?;
12879        assert_eq!(err.reason, StartErrorReason::Busy);
12880        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
12881
12882        sender.close_channel();
12883        transport.await??;
12884        Ok(())
12885    }

12919    /// Narrowing does not only accept or reject — with dynamic batching it moves the batch the Exit
12920    /// asks for, which is what the Entry pays per deposit round trip.
12921    #[test]
12922    fn a_narrowed_window_can_change_the_selected_batch_size() {
12923        let cfg = IncomingSessionPixConfig {
12924            quota_range: 100..=400,
12925            supervision: SupervisorConfig {
12926                ssas_per_request: 4,
12927                allow_dynamic_ssa_batches: true,
12928                ..Default::default()
12929            },
12930            ..Default::default()
12931        };
12932
12933        // The node's own window accepts a single SSA of 100.
12934        assert_eq!(
12935            cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
12936                .ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100),
12937            Some(1)
12938        );
12939
12940        // Narrowed to a floor of 250, the smallest batch that reaches it is three.
12941        assert_eq!(
12942            cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_pix_quota_range(250..=400))
12943                .ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100),
12944            Some(3)
12945        );
12946
12947        // Narrowed to a window every multiple of the offer jumps over — three total 300 and four
12948        // total 400, with nothing in between — so no batch fits and the Session is refused.
12949        assert_eq!(
12950            cfg.effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default().with_pix_quota_range(310..=390))
12951                .ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100),
12952            None
12953        );
12954    }

13277        assert!(
13278            err_rx.await.is_err(),
13279            "no SessionError may be sent for an admitted session"
13280        );
13281        Ok(())
13282    }

13284    /// The request the session server is handed must name the target it is being asked about, or the
13285    /// hook cannot do the one job it exists for.
13286    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13287    async fn the_admission_request_carries_the_session_target() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13288        let (seen_tx, seen_rx) = oneshot::channel();
13289        let seen_tx = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(seen_tx)));
13290        let (admission, handler) = spawn_admission_handler(move |request| {
13291            if let Some(tx) = seen_tx.lock().unwrap().take() {
13292                let _ = tx.send((request.session_id, request.target.clone()));
13293            }
13294            Ok(SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
13295        });
13296        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
13297            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, Some(admission))?;
13298
13299        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
13300        let offer = pix_offer();
13301        let expected_target = offer.target.clone();
13302        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(pseudonym, offer).await?;
13303
13304        let (seen_id, seen_target) = seen_rx.await.context("admission was never asked")?;
13305        assert_eq!(seen_target, expected_target);
13306        assert_eq!(seen_id, pseudonym, "the request must name the session it would become");
13307
13308        sender.close_channel();
13309        transport.await??;
13310        handler.abort();
13311        Ok(())
13312    }

13331    /// Dynamic admission chooses the least expensive batch that brings the Entry's total offer into
13332    /// the accepted range. A cap is still a cap: it may leave the offer unsatisfiable, and checked
13333    /// multiplication must make an overflowing candidate a refusal rather than a wrapped match.
13334    #[test]
13335    fn dynamic_ssa_batches_choose_the_smallest_satisfying_batch() {
13336        // Through `effective_for` with an empty decision, which is the no-session-server path and
13337        // so yields exactly the node's configured policy.
13338        let config = |quota_range, ssas_per_request| {
13339            IncomingSessionPixConfig {
13340                quota_range,
13341                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
13342                    ssas_per_request,
13343                    allow_dynamic_ssa_batches: true,
13344                    ..Default::default()
13345                },
13346                ..Default::default()
13347            }
13348            .effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
13349        };
13350
13351        assert_eq!(Some(1), config(100..=350, 4).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100));
13352        assert_eq!(Some(3), config(250..=350, 4).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100));
13353        assert_eq!(None, config(250..=350, 2).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100));
13354        assert_eq!(
13355            None,
13356            config(150..=175, 4).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100),
13357            "the first multiple jumps over the range and every later one is larger"
13358        );
13359        assert_eq!(None, config(100..=350, 4).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(400));
13360        assert_eq!(
13361            None,
13362            config(u64::MAX..=u64::MAX, 2).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(u64::MAX / 2 + 1),
13363            "an overflowing batch quota must not wrap into the accepted range"
13364        );
13365    }
13366
13367    /// Disabling dynamic admission restores both halves of the old contract: only the per-SSA quota
13368    /// is compared with `quota_range`, and an accepted offer uses the configured batch exactly.
13369    #[test]
13370    fn disabling_dynamic_ssa_batches_preserves_fixed_batch_admission() {
13371        let fixed = |quota_range| {
13372            IncomingSessionPixConfig {
13373                quota_range,
13374                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
13375                    ssas_per_request: 3,
13376                    allow_dynamic_ssa_batches: false,
13377                    ..Default::default()
13378                },
13379                ..Default::default()
13380            }
13381            .effective_for(&SessionAdmissionDecision::default())
13382        };
13383
13384        assert_eq!(
13385            None,
13386            fixed(250..=350).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100),
13387            "fixed mode must not rescue a sub-range SSA even when three of them total 300"
13388        );
13389        assert_eq!(
13390            Some(3),
13391            fixed(100..=100).ssa_batch_size_for_quota(100),
13392            "an individually accepted SSA must retain the configured exact batch"
13393        );
13394    }

13396    /// Admission reserves against the batch it selected for this Session, not the configured dynamic
13397    /// ceiling. Otherwise a ceiling of nine would charge every already-satisfactory one-SSA offer as
13398    /// nine and silently divide the number of Sessions the Exit can admit.
13399    #[test]
13400    fn live_cycle_reservation_uses_the_selected_batch_size() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13401        let params = small_pix_params();

13405            SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {

13410                        ..Default::default()
13411                    },
13412                    ..Default::default()
13413                },
13414                ..Default::default()
13415            });

13419            .context("the selected batch should fit exactly")?;

13421        drop(reservation);
