15196    /// A raised `BalancerTarget` must reach the SURB store, so the Session's ring grows with it, on a
15197    /// `NoRateControl` Session as much as on a rate-controlled one.
15198    ///
15199    /// The ring is sized once at establishment from the target then announced. The gnosis_vpn client
15200    /// opens at a ping tier and announces its main tier seconds later (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739); an
15201    /// Exit that only updates the balancer's set-point leaves the ring at the ping tier, and every
15202    /// SURB minted toward the main one is evicted on arrival — losing the PIX share each carried.
15203    /// A `NoRateControl` Session has no set-point to move (`no_rate_control`: its balancer state stays
15204    /// disabled), yet its ring is the same store and has the same need, when its Entry announced a
15205    /// target at establishment for the ring to be sized from. One that announced none starts with the
15206    /// full ring, which leaves nothing to widen
15207    /// (`the_admitted_ring_follows_the_announced_target_or_takes_the_ceiling`).
15208    ///
15209    /// Only a keep-alive that carries `BalancerTarget` raises anything. An Entry whose
15210    /// `surb_target_notify` is off sends its keep-alives without it, and the Exit then learns of no
15211    /// raise (`*_without_target_notify`).
15212    ///
15213    /// The token matters as much as the call: the store widens only the admission the token names,
15214    /// and a raise under a successor's pseudonym must not touch its ring.
15215    #[rstest]
15216    #[case::rate_controlled(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 688, true)]
15217    #[case::no_rate_control(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 688, true)]
15218    #[case::rate_controlled_without_target_notify(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 688, false)]
15219    #[case::no_rate_control_without_target_notify(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 688, false)]
15220    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15221    async fn a_raised_balancer_target_must_widen_the_sessions_ring(
15222        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
15223        #[case] announced: u64,
15224        #[case] target_notify: bool,
15225    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15226        let rate_controlled = !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl);
15227        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
15228        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
15229            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, None)?;
15230        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
15231
15232        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15233        // The ping tier the Session is admitted with — the low 32 bits of the options word are the
15234        // announced SURB target, which is what the Exit sizes the ring from.
15235        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
15236            pseudonym,
15237            StartInitiation {
15238                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities),
15239                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(announced),
15240                ..no_pix_offer()
15241            },
15242        )
15243        .await?;
15244        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
15245        assert_eq!(
15246            !rate_controlled,
15247            slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled(),
15248            "fixture: only a rate-controlled Exit runs a balancer"
15249        );
15250
15251        // The Entry's main tier, announced seconds later.
15252        let raised = 6_887_usize;
15253        let flags: KeepAliveFlags = if target_notify {
15254            KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into()
15255        } else {
15256            None.into()
15257        };
15258        let keep_alive = KeepAliveMessage::<SessionId> {
15259            session_id: pseudonym,
15260            flags,
15261            additional_data: raised as u64,
15262        };
15263
15264        if target_notify {
15265            mgr.dispatch_message(
15266                pseudonym,
15267                ApplicationDataIn {
15268                    data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(keep_alive.clone()).try_into()?,
15269                    packet_info: Default::default(),
15270                },
15271            )?;
15272
15273            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
15274                loop {
15275                    if !admission.raised_targets().is_empty() {
15276                        break;
15277                    }
15278                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
15279                }
15280            })
15281            .await
15282            .context("the raised target never reached the SURB store")?;
15283
15284            assert_eq!(
15285                vec![raised],
15286                admission.raised_targets(),
15287                "the announced target, not the one the Session was admitted with, is what the ring is widened to"
15288            );
15289            assert_eq!(
15290                admission.minted_tokens(),
15291                admission.raise_tokens(),
15292                "the raise must name the admission the Session holds, or the store widens nothing"
15293            );
15294
15295            // The Entry repeats the announcement on every keep-alive. Handled here and not dispatched,
15296            // so that it is known to be done when the count is read.
15297            mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive).await?;
15298            assert_eq!(
15299                1,
15300                admission.raised_targets().len(),
15301                "an announcement that raises nothing further must not ask the store again"
15302            );
15303
15304            assert_eq!(
15305                !rate_controlled,
15306                slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled(),
15307                "a raise must not switch on a balancer the Session does not run"
15308            );
15309            if rate_controlled {
15310                assert_eq!(
15311                    raised as u64,
15312                    slot.surb_mgmt.controller_bounds().target(),
15313                    "a rate-controlled Exit follows the Entry's target with its balancer too"
15314                );
15315            }
15316        } else {
15317            // Handled here and not dispatched: nothing happens that could be waited for, and the
15318            // refills flag is set before the raise is decided, so it could not say the handler is done.
15319            mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive).await?;
15320            assert!(
15321                slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
15322                "the keep-alive must have been handled, or its silence proves nothing"
15323            );
15324            assert!(
15325                admission.raised_targets().is_empty(),
15326                "a keep-alive that announces no target raises no ring, whatever value it carries; got {:?}",
15327                admission.raised_targets()
15328            );
15329            if rate_controlled {
15330                assert_eq!(
15331                    announced,
15332                    slot.surb_mgmt.controller_bounds().target(),
15333                    "nor does it move the balancer's target"
15334                );
15335            }
15336        }
15337
15338        sender.close_channel();
15339        transport.await??;
15340        Ok(())
15341    }
15342
15343    /// A keep-alive shows the Exit that its Entry refills it, unless the Entry sent it as a manual ping.
15344    ///
15345    /// An Entry without a SURB balancer can ping a Session by hand (`ping_session`), and that keep-alive
15346    /// brings SURBs like any other. Taken for a balancer's, it would make the Exit send the Entry level
15347    /// reports nothing reads, each at the cost of a reply SURB, and on a rate-controlled Session hold its
15348    /// data at the keep-alive reserve. The mark on the ping is the only way to tell it from a balancer
15349    /// that keeps `surb_target_notify` off, whose keep-alives carry no flag either.
15350    ///
15351    /// Each keep-alive is handled directly, so that the answer is known to be final once it is read. The
15352    /// level reports it decides are covered through the real dispatch by `exit_level_reports_follow_the_entry`.
15353    #[rstest]
15354    #[case::a_manual_ping(KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing.into(), false)]
15355    #[case::a_balancer_announcing_its_target(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(), true)]
15356    #[case::a_balancer_not_announcing_its_target_or_an_older_entrys_ping(None.into(), true)]
15357    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15358    async fn a_keep_alive_shows_the_entry_refills_unless_it_is_a_manual_ping(
15359        #[case] flags: KeepAliveFlags,
15360        #[case] latched: bool,
15361    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15362        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15363        let (mgr, _estimator) = exit_slot_for_keep_alives(pseudonym);
15364        let (new_session_tx, _new_sessions) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
15365        let (mock_sender, _sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
15366        let _ahs = mgr.start(mock_sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15367
15368        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
15369        assert!(
15370            !slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
15371            "fixture: nothing has shown the Exit that its Entry refills it"
15372        );
15373
15374        mgr.handle_keep_alive(
15375            pseudonym,
15376            KeepAliveMessage::<SessionId> {
15377                session_id: pseudonym,
15378                flags,
15379                additional_data: 0,
15380            },
15381        )
15382        .await?;
15383
15384        assert_eq!(
15385            latched,
15386            slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
15387            "a keep-alive with flags {flags:?} {} that the Entry refills the Exit",
15388            if latched { "must show" } else { "must not show" }
15389        );
15390        Ok(())
15391    }

15393    /// `ping_session` marks its keep-alive as a manual ping, and it is no bigger than any other.
15394    ///
15395    /// The mark is what stops an Exit from taking the ping of an Entry without a balancer for the sign
15396    /// of a balancer (`a_keep_alive_shows_the_entry_refills_unless_it_is_a_manual_ping`). It must not
15397    /// change how many SURBs the ping can carry, which is what a manual ping is used for.
15398    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15399    async fn ping_session_sends_a_keep_alive_marked_as_a_manual_ping() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15400        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15401        let (mgr, _estimator) = exit_slot_for_keep_alives(pseudonym);
15402        let (new_session_tx, _new_sessions) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
15403        let (mock_sender, mut sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
15404        let _ahs = mgr.start(mock_sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15405
15406        mgr.ping_session(&pseudonym).await?;
15407
15408        let (_, data) = timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sent.next())
15409            .await
15410            .context("the ping was never sent")?
15411            .context("the manager's sender closed")?;
15412        let StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ping) =
15413            HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)?
15414        else {
15415            anyhow::bail!("not a keep-alive");
15416        };
15417        assert_eq!(pseudonym, ping.session_id);
15418        assert_eq!(
15419            KeepAliveFlags::from(KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing),
15420            ping.flags,
15421            "the ping is marked as one, and as nothing a balancer sends"
15422        );
15423        assert_eq!(0, ping.additional_data);
15424
15425        let unmarked: ApplicationData = HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(pseudonym.into()).try_into()?;
15426        assert_eq!(
15427            unmarked.total_len(),
15428            data.data.total_len(),
15429            "the mark must not change how many SURBs fit beside the ping"
15430        );
15431        Ok(())
15432    }

15434    /// What an Entry with `capabilities` and, if it balances, a SURB balancer targeting `balancer_target`
15435    /// sends to open a Session: its `StartSession`, as the Exit would receive it.
15436    async fn entry_start_session(
15437        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
15438        capabilities: Capabilities,
15439        balancer_target: Option<u64>,
15440    ) -> anyhow::Result<ApplicationData> {
15441        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(Default::default());
15442        let (msg_tx, mut msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
15443        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
15444        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15445
15446        // Nobody answers, so the opening never completes: only the `StartSession` it sends is of interest.
15447        let opening = timeout(
15448            Duration::from_millis(500),
15449            mgr.new_session(
15450                (&ChainKeypair::random()).into(),
15451                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
15452                SessionClientConfig {
15453                    capabilities,
15454                    pseudonym: pseudonym.into(),
15455                    surb_management: balancer_target.map(|target_surb_buffer_size| SurbBalancerConfig {
15456                        target_surb_buffer_size,
15457                        max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
15458                        ..Default::default()
15459                    }),
15460                    ..Default::default()
15461                },
15462            ),
15463        )
15464        .await;
15465        anyhow::ensure!(
15466            opening.is_err(),
15467            "fixture: nobody answered, so the opening cannot have completed"
15468        );
15469
15470        originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::ZERO)
15471            .await
15472            .into_iter()
15473            .map(|(_, data)| data.data)
15474            .find(|data| {
15475                matches!(
15476                    HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.application_tag, &data.plain_text),
15477                    Ok(StartProtocol::StartSession(_))
15478                )
15479            })
15480            .context("the Entry must have sent a StartSession")
15481    }

15483    /// The SURB target an Entry announces is the one it balances toward, and none otherwise.
15484    ///
15485    /// An Entry that runs no SURB balancer (`surb_management` unset, as for a hoprd `responseBuffer`
15486    /// below two packets) used to announce the balancer-rate fallback on the rate-controlled branch (50 at
15487    /// the defaults), which the Exit cannot tell from a real target of 50. It admitted a ring of 75 for
15488    /// it, and nothing widened that ring. A zero lets the Exit tell, and give such a Session the full ring
15489    /// (`an_exit_gives_an_entry_without_a_balancer_the_full_ring`). A `NoRateControl` Entry announces
15490    /// nothing either way, whether or not it runs a balancer.
15491    ///
15492    /// Only the lower 32 bits of the options word are the SURB target; its upper half carries the PIX
15493    /// parameters, which these cases do not use and the assertion would not look at anyway.
15494    #[rstest]
15495    #[case::rate_controlled_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), Some(300), 300)]
15496    #[case::rate_controlled_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), None, 0)]
15497    #[case::no_rate_control_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, Some(300), 0)]
15498    #[case::no_rate_control_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, None, 0)]
15499    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15500    async fn the_entry_announces_the_target_it_balances_toward_and_none_otherwise(
15501        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
15502        #[case] balancer_target: Option<u64>,
15503        #[case] expected: u32,
15504    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15505        let start = entry_start_session(HoprPseudonym::random(), capabilities, balancer_target).await?;
15506        let Ok(StartProtocol::StartSession(initiation)) =
15507            HoprStartProtocol::decode(start.application_tag, &start.plain_text)
15508        else {
15509            anyhow::bail!("not a StartSession");
15510        };
15511
15512        assert_eq!(
15513            expected,
15514            initiation_options(initiation.additional_data) as u32,
15515            "the SURB target in the low 32 bits of the options word"
15516        );
15517        Ok(())
15518    }

15520    /// An Exit gives the Entry's own `StartSession` the ring and the balancer it should: the full ring
15521    /// when the Entry announced no target, its target otherwise, and for a rate-controlled Exit the
15522    /// balancer at the announced target, or at the Exit's own fallback when there was none.
15523    ///
15524    /// The end-to-end half of `the_entry_announces_the_target_it_balances_toward_and_none_otherwise`
15525    /// and of `the_admitted_ring_follows_the_announced_target_or_takes_the_ceiling`: a rate-controlled
15526    /// Entry without a balancer is the one whose announcement changed, and it is the case that was left
15527    /// with a ring of 75 SURBs.
15528    #[rstest]
15529    #[case::rate_controlled_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), Some(300), 300)]
15530    #[case::rate_controlled_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), None, 0)]
15531    #[case::no_rate_control_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, Some(300), 0)]
15532    #[case::no_rate_control_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, None, 0)]
15533    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15534    async fn an_exit_gives_an_entry_without_a_balancer_the_full_ring(
15535        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
15536        #[case] balancer_target: Option<u64>,
15537        #[case] announced: u32,
15538    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15539        let rate_controlled = !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl);
15540        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15541        let start = entry_start_session(pseudonym, capabilities, balancer_target).await?;
15542
15543        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
15544        let exit = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
15545            maximum_surb_buffer_size: RING_CEILING,
15546            ..Default::default()
15547        });
15548        assert!(exit.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
15549        let (msg_tx, _msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
15550        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
15551        exit.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15552
15553        exit.dispatch_message(
15554            pseudonym,
15555            ApplicationDataIn {
15556                data: start,
15557                packet_info: Default::default(),
15558            },
15559        )?;
15560        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
15561            while admission.admitted_targets().is_empty() {
15562                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
15563            }
15564        })
15565        .await
15566        .context("the Exit never admitted the Session")?;
15567
15568        assert_eq!(
15569            vec![if announced > 0 {
15570                announced as usize
15571            } else {
15572                RING_CEILING
15573            }],
15574            admission.admitted_targets(),
15575            "the ring is sized from what the Entry announced, or from the Exit's ceiling when it announced nothing"
15576        );
15577
15578        if rate_controlled {
15579            let fallback = exit.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate as u64
15580                * exit
15581                    .cfg
15582                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
15583                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
15584                    .as_secs();
15585            let balancer = exit
15586                .get_surb_balancer_config(&pseudonym)?
15587                .context("a rate-controlled Exit runs a balancer")?;
15588            assert_eq!(
15589                if announced > 0 { announced as u64 } else { fallback },
15590                balancer.target_surb_buffer_size,
15591                "the Exit's balancer follows the announced target, or runs at the Exit's own fallback when none was \
15592                 announced"
15593            );
15594        }
15595
15596        assert!(exit.close_session(&pseudonym));
15597        Ok(())
15598    }
15599
15600    /// The node's `maximum_surb_buffer_size` in the ring tests: well clear of the balancer's fallback
15601    /// (50) and of anything a test announces, and inside the bound the recording admission asserts.
15602    const RING_CEILING: usize = 4_000;
15603    const _: () = assert!(RING_CEILING <= MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS);
15604
15605    /// The SURB ring the Exit admits follows the target the Entry announced, and is the node's ceiling
15606    /// when the Entry announced none.
15607    ///
15608    /// Without an announcement the Exit used to pass the balancer's fallback figure (50 at the defaults)
15609    /// to the store, which turned it into a ring of 75. An Entry that runs no balancer announces
15610    /// nothing (see `the_entry_announces_the_target_it_balances_toward_and_none_otherwise`) and sends no
15611    /// keep-alive to raise a target later, so nothing widened that ring, and a burst of replies found
15612    /// its SURBs evicted past the 75th. The ring is a ceiling that allocates with
15613    /// occupancy, so the Session is given the largest one the node allows (`maximum_surb_buffer_size`)
15614    /// and pays for what it stores. This holds on both kinds of Session, because the ring is the same
15615    /// store whether or not the Exit runs a balancer.
15616    ///
15617    /// An announcement is still the Session's own figure, clamped to the ceiling, however small.
15618    #[rstest]
15619    #[case::rate_controlled_announcing_nothing(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 0, RING_CEILING)]
15620    #[case::no_rate_control_announcing_nothing(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 0, RING_CEILING)]
15621    #[case::rate_controlled_announcing_64(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 64, 64)]
15622    #[case::no_rate_control_announcing_64(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 64, 64)]
15623    #[case::rate_controlled_announcing_more_than_the_ceiling(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 9_999, RING_CEILING)]
15624    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15625    async fn the_admitted_ring_follows_the_announced_target_or_takes_the_ceiling(
15626        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
15627        #[case] announced: u64,
15628        #[case] expected: usize,
15629    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15630        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
15631        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
15632            maximum_surb_buffer_size: RING_CEILING,
15633            ..Default::default()
15634        });
15635        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
15636        // Held for the whole test: the establishment answer is sent through it.
15637        let (msg_tx, _msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
15638        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
15639        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15640
15641        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15642        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
15643            pseudonym,
15644            StartInitiation {
15645                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
15646                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
15647                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities),
15648                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(announced),
15649            },
15650        )
15651        .await?;
15652
15653        assert_eq!(
15654            vec![expected],
15655            admission.admitted_targets(),
15656            "the ring is sized from what the Entry announced ({announced}), or from the node's ceiling when it \
15657             announced nothing"
15658        );
15659
15660        // The ring takes the ceiling, but the balancer keeps the figure it always had when nothing was
15661        // announced (so does the fill reserve, which derives from the same one): the rate the Exit starts
15662        // at times the buffer duration it has to outlast, which is a different number from the ring's. A
15663        // NoRateControl Exit runs no balancer, so there is nothing to read there.
15664        if !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl) {
15665            let fallback = mgr.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate as u64
15666                * mgr
15667                    .cfg
15668                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
15669                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
15670                    .as_secs();
15671            anyhow::ensure!(
15672                fallback as usize != RING_CEILING,
15673                "fixture: the fallback must differ from the ring's ceiling for this to tell them apart"
15674            );
15675            let balancer = mgr
15676                .get_surb_balancer_config(&pseudonym)?
15677                .context("a rate-controlled Exit runs a balancer")?;
15678            let expected_target = if announced > 0 { expected as u64 } else { fallback };
15679            assert_eq!(
15680                expected_target, balancer.target_surb_buffer_size,
15681                "the balancer is given what the Entry announced, or the balancer-rate fallback ({fallback}) when it \
15682                 announced nothing, and never the ring's ceiling"
15683            );
15684        }
15685
15686        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
15687        Ok(())
15688    }
15689
15690    /// A keep-alive that arrives *before* the admission is committed must not claim the token cell.
15691    ///
15692    /// The Exit answers `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive can
15693    /// be processed in that window. Reading the cell the way a teardown does would initialize it with
15694    /// `NONE`, and the establishment's own `commit` would then fail its `set` — retiring the live
15695    /// admission and leaving the Session's SURBs in the quarantine, which is precisely the
15696    /// unadmitted-Session failure the seam exists to prevent (hoprnet#8515).
15697    ///
15698    /// Driven deterministically rather than by racing a real establishment: the slot is allocated
15699    /// and left uncommitted, the keep-alive is delivered while its token cell is still empty, and only
15700    /// then does the commit run — which is the ordering the Exit produces on the wire.
15701    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15702    async fn a_keep_alive_before_commit_must_not_claim_the_admission_token() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15703        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
15704        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15705        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
15706        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
15707
15708        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(MockMsgSender::new());
15709        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
15710        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15711
15712        // Uncommitted: the Session exists, but nothing has admitted it yet.
15713        let slot = unregistered_slot(pseudonym);
15714        let mut guard = mgr
15715            .allocate_session_slot(pseudonym, slot.clone())
15716            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
15717        assert_eq!(
15718            AdmissionToken::NONE,
15719            slot.peek_admission_token(),
15720            "fixture: the slot must start uncommitted"
15721        );
15722
15723        // The Entry's ramp announces while the cell is still empty.
15724        mgr.handle_keep_alive(
15725            pseudonym,
15726            KeepAliveMessage {
15727                session_id: pseudonym,
15728                flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
15729                additional_data: 256,
15730            },
15731        )
15732        .await
15733        .context("the keep-alive must be handled without error while uncommitted")?;
15734
15735        assert!(
15736            slot.admission_token.get().is_none(),
15737            "handling a keep-alive must not claim the cell, or the commit's own `set` would fail"
15738        );
15739
15740        // The establishment's commit runs next and must succeed — admitting at the announced target,
15741        // not retiring the admission it just made.
15742        guard.commit(Some(&slot), Some(&admission), 64);
15743
15744        let minted = admission.minted_tokens();
15745        assert_eq!(1, minted.len(), "the commit must admit exactly once");
15746        assert_eq!(
15747            Some(minted[0]),
15748            slot.admission_token.get().copied(),
15749            "the commit's token must land in the cell the keep-alive left untouched"
15750        );
15751        assert!(
15752            admission.retire_tokens().is_empty(),
15753            "a keep-alive racing the commit must leave it to succeed, not make it retire its own admission; retires \
15754             were {:?}",
15755            admission.retire_tokens()
15756        );
15757        assert_eq!(
15758            vec![256],
15759            admission.admitted_targets(),
15760            "the commit must size the ring from the target the keep-alive announced before it"
15761        );
15762
15763        handle.abort();
15764        Ok(())
15765    }
15766
15767    /// A target announced in the `SessionEstablished`-before-commit window must survive the commit.
15768    ///
15769    /// That window is real — the Exit answers before it commits — and the ring is sized once, at
15770    /// `commit`. A raise processed in it has no admission to widen yet, so the figure is recorded on
15771    /// the slot and the commit sizes the ring from the larger of it and establishment's target.
15772    /// Without that, an Entry that announces its main tier early gets a ping-tier ring, which is the
15773    /// gnosis_vpn shape (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739) reached one interleaving earlier.
15774    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15775    async fn a_target_announced_before_commit_must_survive_the_commit() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15776        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
15777        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
15778            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, None)?;
15779        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
15780
15781        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15782        let admitted_with = 688_u64;
15783        let raised = 6_887_usize;
15784
15785        // Establish and announce the main tier in one turn, so the announcement is queued behind the
15786        // establishment — it is processed by the same Start-protocol worker, and whether it lands
15787        // before or after `commit` is the scheduling detail this test must not depend on.
15788        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
15789            pseudonym,
15790            StartInitiation {
15791                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(admitted_with),
15792                ..no_pix_offer()
15793            },
15794        )
15795        .await?;
15796        mgr.dispatch_message(
15797            pseudonym,
15798            ApplicationDataIn {
15799                data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
15800                    session_id: pseudonym,
15801                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
15802                    additional_data: raised as u64,
15803                })
15804                .try_into()?,
15805                packet_info: Default::default(),
15806            },
15807        )?;
15808
15809        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
15810            loop {
15811                if admission.raised_targets().contains(&raised) {
15812                    break;
15813                }
15814                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
15815            }
15816        })
15817        .await
15818        .context("the announcement never reached the SURB store")?;
15819
15820        // Whether the raise widened a live admission or the commit sized the ring from it, the store
15821        // must have been told about the raised target and the Session must be admitted, not retired.
15822        assert!(
15823            admission.raised_targets().contains(&raised),
15824            "the commit must start from the recorded target when the raise preceded it, got {:?}",
15825            admission.raised_targets()
15826        );
15827        assert!(
15828            admission.retire_tokens().is_empty(),
15829            "the commit must not retire the admission the raise raced it into"
15830        );
15831
15832        sender.close_channel();
15833        transport.await??;
15834        Ok(())
15835    }
15836
15837    /// The Exit's SURB level must fall by what its store actually lost, not by what a keep-alive
15838    /// could have carried.
15839    ///
15840    /// Keep-alives are Start-protocol traffic, so they never pass through `session_rx`, which is
15841    /// where data packets book both the SURBs saved and the ones the full store evicted. Booking
15842    /// `max_surbs()` alone here counts every SURB a keep-alive *could* carry as if it had been
15843    /// retained: during a PIX fill (the gnosis_vpn report's ~30 keep-alives/s) the Exit reported
15844    /// 10,597–12,263 SURBs for a ring that could hold at most 1,032, and then spent against that
15845    /// figure until the ring was empty.
15846    ///
15847    /// Each keep-alive is booked once, by `dispatch_message`. The test lets the Start task handle both
15848    /// keep-alives before it reads, so a second booking there would show.
15849    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15850    async fn keep_alive_surbs_must_be_booked_with_their_evictions() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15851        let mgr: TestManager = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
15852        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(MockMsgSender::new());
15853        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
15854        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15855
15856        // The Exit side of a Session: it receives the Entry's keep-alives and books their SURBs.
15857        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15858        let _rx = mgr.pre_populate_session_with_receiver(pseudonym, DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()));
15859
15860        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("slot must exist")?;
15861        let estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
15862        drop(slot);
15863
15864        // A keep-alive with no SURBs of its own is not evidence that it retained any: the packet
15865        // info says both what arrived and what the full store dropped to make room.
15866        let keep_alive = |saved: usize, evicted: usize| -> anyhow::Result<ApplicationDataIn> {
15867            Ok(ApplicationDataIn {
15868                data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
15869                    session_id: pseudonym,
15870                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
15871                    additional_data: 1_000,
15872                })
15873                .try_into()?,
15874                packet_info: IncomingPacketInfo {
15875                    num_saved_surbs: saved,
15876                    num_evicted_surbs: evicted,
15877                    ..Default::default()
15878                },
15879            })
15880        };
15881
15882        // One keep-alive whose SURBs all landed, one whose SURBs were all evicted on arrival. Seven is all a
15883        // keep-alive can carry: eight SURBs fit in an empty packet, and the message takes one's room.
15884        mgr.dispatch_message(pseudonym, keep_alive(7, 0)?)?;
15885        mgr.dispatch_message(pseudonym, keep_alive(7, 7)?)?;
15886
15887        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
15888            loop {
15889                if estimator.estimate_surbs_produced() == 14 {
15890                    break;
15891                }
15892                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
15893            }
15894        })
15895        .await
15896        .context("the keep-alives never reached the estimator")?;
15897
15898        // A second booking would land after the wait above, once the Start task gets to the keep-alives.
15899        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
15900        assert_eq!(
15901            14,
15902            estimator.estimate_surbs_produced(),
15903            "each keep-alive must be booked once"
15904        );
15905        assert_eq!(
15906            7,
15907            estimator.saturating_diff(),
15908            "the level must be what the store kept, not the SURBs the keep-alives could have carried"
15909        );
15910
15911        handle.abort();
15912        Ok(())
15913    }
15914
15915    /// A keep-alive that carries no SURBs at all must book none.
15916    ///
15917    /// The bound `max_surbs()` is what the message *could* carry, and a keep-alive sent with
15918    /// `max_surbs_in_packet` of zero carries nothing. At the report's fill rate that bound alone
15919    /// inflated the Exit's level by several times the ring's whole capacity.
15920    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15921    async fn a_surbless_keep_alive_must_not_book_surbs() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15922        let mgr: TestManager = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
15923        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(MockMsgSender::new());
15924        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
15925        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15926
15927        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
15928        let _rx = mgr.pre_populate_session_with_receiver(pseudonym, DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()));
15929
15930        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("slot must exist")?;
15931        let estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
15932        drop(slot);
15933
15934        mgr.dispatch_message(
15935            pseudonym,
15936            ApplicationDataIn {
15937                data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
15938                    session_id: pseudonym,
15939                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
15940                    additional_data: 1_000,
15941                })
15942                .try_into()?,
15943                packet_info: Default::default(),
15944            },
15945        )?;
15946
15947        // Give the Start-protocol worker time to have run, then assert the absence rather than racing it.
15948        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
15949        assert_eq!(
15950            0,
15951            estimator.estimate_surbs_produced(),
15952            "a keep-alive with no SURBs must not be booked as carrying the packet's maximum"
15953        );
15954
15955        handle.abort();
15956        Ok(())
15957    }

15959    /// Verifies that a session is evicted after the `idle_timeout` fires, without needing an explicit close.
15960    ///
15961    /// ## Steps
15962    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is configured with `maximum_sessions: 1` and `idle_timeout: 100ms`.
15963    /// 2. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` creates one session — confirmed active.
15964    /// 3. The test sleeps 200ms (well past the 100ms timeout), then calls `sessions.run_pending_tasks()` to drive the
15965    ///    eviction timer.
15966    /// 4. `active_sessions` is empty, confirming the idle session was cleaned up without an explicit close call.
15967    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15968    async fn session_manager_should_evict_idle_session_and_call_close_callback() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15969        use hopr_utils::network_types::prelude::SealedHost;
15970
15971        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
15972            maximum_sessions: 1,
15973            idle_timeout: Duration::from_millis(100),
15974            ..Default::default()
15975        };
15976        let mgr: SessionManager<futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
15977            SessionManager::new(cfg);
15978
15979        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
15980        transport
15981            .expect_send_message()
15982            .times(1)
15983            .returning(|_, _| futures::future::ok(()).boxed());
15984
15985        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
15986        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
15987            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
15988            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
15989        });
15990        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
15991        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
15992        assert!(mgr.is_started());
15993
15994        // Create first session
15995        let pseudonym1 = HoprPseudonym::random();
15996        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
15997            pseudonym1,
15998            StartInitiation {
15999                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
16000                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
16001                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
16002                additional_data: 0,
16003            },
16004        )
16005        .await?;
16006
16007        // Verify first session exists
16008        assert_eq!(mgr.active_sessions().len(), 1);
16009
16010        // Wait for the session to expire (idle_timeout = 100ms)
16011        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
16012        mgr.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
16013
16014        // Verify session was evicted (cache should be empty now)
16015        assert_eq!(
16016            mgr.active_sessions().len(),
16017            0,
16018            "idle session should be evicted after timeout"
16019        );
16020
16021        Ok(())
16022    }

16112    /// Verifies that `new_session` rejects `UsePIX` when the return path has 0 intermediate hops.
16113    ///
16114    /// PIX shares are encrypted with the first relayer's ticket-challenge solution and carried
16115    /// in return-path SURBs. With 0 intermediate hops (a direct Exit→Entry SURB), there is no
16116    /// relayer to provide the challenge solution, so shares are never embedded — the ongoing
16117    /// PIX share delivery mechanism is dead and the Exit's quota is never replenished.
16118    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16119    async fn new_session_rejects_usepix_with_zero_return_hops() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16120        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
16121            SessionManager::new(Default::default());
16122
16123        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
16124        // The error happens before any message is sent, so expect_send_message should NOT fire.
16125        transport.expect_send_message().times(0);
16126
16127        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
16128        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
16129        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
16130        assert!(mgr.is_started());
16131
16132        let result = mgr
16133            .new_session(
16134                Address::from(&ChainKeypair::random()),
16135                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
16136                SessionClientConfig {
16137                    capabilities: Capability::UsePIX.into(),
16138                    surb_management: None,
16139                    forward_path_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(1.try_into()?),
16140                    return_path_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(0.try_into()?),
16141                    ..Default::default()
16142                },
16143            )
16144            .await;
16145
16146        let err = result.unwrap_err();
16147        let msg = format!("{err:?}");
16148        assert!(
16149            msg.contains("UsePIX requires at least 1 intermediate hop on the return path"),
16150            "expected return-path guard error, got: {msg}"
16151        );
16152
16153        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
16154        // No challenge slot was consumed because the validations run before insert_into_next_slot.
16155        assert_eq!(
16156            mgr.session_initiations.entry_count(),
16157            0,
16158            "session_initiations must remain empty when UsePIX is rejected"
16159        );
16160
16161        sender.close_channel();
16162        _handle.await??;
16163        Ok(())
16164    }

16228    /// The fill fractions must be range-checked before anything computes with them.
16229    ///
16230    /// This validator runs *before* `validate_pix_supervision` on both paths that reach it:
16231    /// `SessionManager::start` calls it first, and in `HoprProtocolConfig` it is a field validator
16232    /// while the other is a schema-level one. So it cannot assume the ranges have already been
16233    /// checked — and it feeds `finish_fraction` straight into `Duration::mul_f64`, which panics on a
16234    /// `NaN`, on a negative, and on a product the monotonic clock cannot hold. A single
16235    /// `finish_fraction: .nan` in a YAML file would therefore abort the node at load instead of being
16236    /// reported as the configuration error it is.
16237    ///
16238    /// The finite out-of-range values do not panic, which is why they are here too: they compute a
16239    /// floor that is wrong in the permissive direction, and nothing downstream ever says so.
16240    #[test]
16241    fn fill_fractions_are_rejected_before_the_ceiling_arithmetic_runs() {
16242        let with_fill = |fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig| IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16243            supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16244                fill,
16245                ..Default::default()
16246            },
16247            ..Default::default()
16248        };
16249
16250        for finish_fraction in [f64::NAN, -1.0, f64::INFINITY, 2.0] {
16251            let cfg = with_fill(crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
16252                finish_fraction,
16253                ..Default::default()
16254            });
16255            let outcome = validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&cfg, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE);
16256            assert!(
16257                matches!(&outcome, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(msg)) if msg.contains("fill.finish_fraction")),
16258                "a finish_fraction of {finish_fraction} must be refused rather than multiplied, got {outcome:?}"
16259            );
16260        }
16261
16262        for loss_margin in [f64::NAN, -0.5, 1.0] {
16263            let cfg = with_fill(crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
16264                loss_margin,
16265                ..Default::default()
16266            });
16267            let outcome = validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&cfg, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE);
16268            assert!(
16269                matches!(&outcome, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(msg)) if msg.contains("fill.loss_margin")),
16270                "a loss_margin of {loss_margin} must be refused, got {outcome:?}"
16271            );
16272        }
16273
16274        validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&IncomingSessionPixConfig::default(), MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE)
16275            .expect("the shipped defaults must still validate");
16276    }
16277
16278    /// A zero recovery deadline must be named as such on both fill paths, rather than reaching the
16279    /// fill arithmetic and being reported as an infinite rate requirement.
16280    #[test]
16281    fn a_zero_recovery_deadline_is_refused_as_zero_with_and_without_fill() {
16282        for enabled in [true, false] {
16283            let cfg = IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16284                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16285                    max_recovery_time: Duration::ZERO,
16286                    fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
16287                        enabled,
16288                        ..Default::default()
16289                    },
16290                    ..Default::default()
16291                },
16292                ..Default::default()
16293            };
16294            let outcome = validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&cfg, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE);
16295            assert!(
16296                matches!(&outcome, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(msg)) if msg.contains("max_recovery_time must be non-zero")),
16297                "with fill enabled = {enabled}, a zero deadline must be refused as zero, got {outcome:?}"
16298            );
16299        }
16300    }

16302    /// The fill heartbeat is clamped at *both* ends for a programmatically assembled config.
16303    ///
16304    /// The upper clamp is the one every other supervisor duration takes. The lower one is what stops
16305    /// a zero period, which `validate_pix_supervision` rejects and nothing in this crate calls: with
16306    /// it, `FillRate::as_packets_per_sec` reports zero for the heartbeat, so the planner's floor is
16307    /// zero, both heartbeat branches of `FillPlanner::bound` return a zero-period rate, and
16308    /// `PixFillControl::apply` hands `set_rate_per_unit(1, 1µs)` to the controller — which
16309    /// `RateController::MIN_DELAY` turns into 10 000 packets/s. The `max_rate` ceiling never sees it,
16310    /// so the one bound on this node's self-generated egress would be bypassed by the one field left
16311    /// unbounded below.
16312    #[test]
16313    fn programmatic_fill_heartbeat_is_clamped_to_a_positive_period() {
16314        let normalized = |heartbeat: Duration| {
16315            let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
16316                SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
16317                    pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16318                        supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16319                            fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
16320                                heartbeat,
16321                                ..Default::default()
16322                            },
16323                            ..Default::default()
16324                        },
16325                        ..Default::default()
16326                    },
16327                    ..Default::default()
16328                });
16329            mgr.cfg.pix_config.supervision.fill.heartbeat
16330        };
16331
16332        // The exact dual of the `max_rate` ceiling, so the two clamps cannot drift apart.
16333        let floor = Duration::from_secs(1) / crate::supervision::MAX_FILL_RATE;
16334        assert_eq!(
16335            floor,
16336            normalized(Duration::ZERO),
16337            "a zero heartbeat must be raised to the period of MAX_FILL_RATE"
16338        );
16339        assert_eq!(
16340            crate::supervision::MAX_SUPERVISOR_DURATION,
16341            normalized(Duration::MAX),
16342            "an unrepresentable heartbeat must be lowered to the same cap every other deadline takes"
16343        );
16344
16345        // Which is the property the clamp exists for: a rate the planner can divide by.
16346        assert!(
16347            FillRate::once_per(normalized(Duration::ZERO)).as_packets_per_sec() > 0.0,
16348            "the clamped heartbeat must be a rate the planner can compare against its ceiling"
16349        );
16350    }
16351
16352    /// Supervisor durations a programmatic caller supplies must be clamped, not trusted.
16353    ///
16354    /// `validate_pix_supervision` rejects these, but nothing in this crate calls `validate` — a
16355    /// `SessionManagerConfig` assembled in code reaches the supervisor exactly as written. And the
16356    /// failure is silent in the worst direction: `Instant::checked_add` returns `None` for a duration
16357    /// the monotonic clock cannot represent, and every phase reads an absent deadline as *no
16358    /// deadline*, so the over-large value disables the rule rather than relaxing it.
16359    ///
16360    /// The two batch-scaled deadlines are clamped by what is actually armed, so a batch of `n` leaves
16361    /// each of them at a cap `n` times smaller.
16362    #[test]
16363    fn programmatic_supervisor_durations_are_clamped_to_a_representable_deadline() {
16364        const BATCH: usize = 4;
16365        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
16366            SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
16367                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16368                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16369                        ssas_per_request: BATCH,
16370                        max_ssa_delivery_time: Duration::MAX,
16371                        max_deposit_wait: Duration::MAX,
16372                        max_recovery_idle: Duration::MAX,
16373                        max_recovery_time: Duration::MAX,
16374                        tombstone_retention_window: Duration::MAX,
16375                        ..Default::default()
16376                    },
16377                    ..Default::default()
16378                },
16379                ..Default::default()
16380            });
16381
16382        let sup = &mgr.cfg.pix_config.supervision;
16383        let cap = crate::supervision::MAX_SUPERVISOR_DURATION;
16384        let per_cycle_cap = cap / BATCH as u32;
16385
16386        assert_eq!(per_cycle_cap, sup.max_ssa_delivery_time);
16387        assert_eq!(per_cycle_cap, sup.max_deposit_wait);
16388        assert_eq!(cap, sup.max_recovery_time);
16389        assert_eq!(cap, sup.tombstone_retention_window);
16390
16391        // `max_recovery_idle` is bounded by something tighter than the clock: it must stay strictly
16392        // under the reconstructor's `unused_verifier_lifetime`, or the supervisor waits on a cycle
16393        // whose state was reclaimed long before. Normalized against the default reconstructor, which
16394        // is the one `SessionManager::new` can see; `start` re-checks against the installed one.
16395        let lifetime = hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig::default().unused_verifier_lifetime;
16396        assert!(
16397            sup.max_recovery_idle < lifetime,
16398            "clamped max_recovery_idle ({:?}) must stay under the reconstructor lifetime ({lifetime:?})",
16399            sup.max_recovery_idle
16400        );
16401        crate::supervision::validate_pix_supervision(sup, &hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig::default())
16402            .expect("a normalized config must satisfy every cross-component invariant, not only representability");
16403
16404        // Which is exactly the condition that makes every deadline representable.
16405        let now = std::time::Instant::now();
16406        for dur in [
16407            crate::supervision::scaled_deadline(sup.max_ssa_delivery_time, sup.ssas_per_request),
16408            crate::supervision::scaled_deadline(sup.max_deposit_wait, sup.ssas_per_request),
16409            sup.max_recovery_idle,
16410            sup.max_recovery_time,
16411            sup.tombstone_retention_window,
16412        ] {
16413            assert!(
16414                now.checked_add(dur).is_some(),
16415                "a clamped duration ({dur:?}) must still produce a deadline"
16416            );
16417        }
16418    }

16420    /// Normalizing against the default reconstructor is not enough when a caller installs a
16421    /// different one.
16422    ///
16423    /// `SessionManager::new` cannot see the reconstructor — it arrives with the toolbox at `start` —
16424    /// so its clamp can only assume the defaults. A caller pairing a shorter
16425    /// `unused_verifier_lifetime` with a supervisor config that was valid against the defaults gets
16426    /// a supervisor that outlives the state it is waiting on. That must be an error rather than a
16427    /// silent clamp: at `start` both halves were chosen deliberately, and overriding one of them
16428    /// would be answering a question the caller did not ask.
16429    #[test]
16430    fn start_rejects_a_supervisor_config_the_installed_reconstructor_cannot_support() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16431        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
16432
16433        // Valid against the defaults — 10 min sits well under the default 30 min lifetime — and
16434        // therefore untouched by the constructor's clamp.
16435        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
16436            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16437                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16438                    max_recovery_idle: Duration::from_secs(600),
16439                    ..Default::default()
16440                },
16441                ..Default::default()
16442            },
16443            ..Default::default()
16444        };
16445        crate::supervision::validate_pix_supervision(&cfg.pix_config.supervision, &SsaReconstructorConfig::default())
16446            .expect("the fixture must be valid against the default reconstructor");
16447
16448        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> = SessionManager::new(cfg);
16449
16450        // But the reconstructor actually installed reclaims a cycle after 60 s.
16451        let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
16452            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig::default()).into(),
16453            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig {
16454                unused_verifier_lifetime: Duration::from_secs(60),
16455                ..Default::default()
16456            })
16457            .into(),
16458        );
16459
16460        let (tx, _rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
16461        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
16462        let started = mgr.start(tx, new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None);
16463
16464        assert!(
16465            matches!(started, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(_))),
16466            "starting with a reconstructor that cannot support the supervisor config must fail, got {started:?}"
16467        );
16468
16469        Ok(())
16470    }

16472    /// A programmatically assembled manager must enforce the same incoming-PIX cross-field rules

16485                },
16486                "quota_range",
16487            ),
16488            (
16489                "recovery deadline below one accepted cycle",
16490                IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16491                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16492                        max_recovery_time: Duration::from_secs(1),
16493                        ..valid.supervision.clone()
16494                    },
16495                    ..valid.clone()
16496                },
16497                "max_recovery_time",
16498            ),
16499            (
16500                "live-cycle budget below one accepted cycle",
16501                IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16502                    max_live_cycle_bytes: widest - 1,
16503                    ..valid
16504                },
16505                "max_live_cycle_bytes",
16506            ),
16507        ];

16509        for (case, pix_config, expected_field) in invalid_configs {
16510            let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
16511                SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
16512                    pix_config,
16513                    ..Default::default()
16514                });
16515            let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
16516                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig::default()).into(),
16517                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
16518            );
16519            let (tx, _rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
16520            let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
16521
16522            match mgr.start(tx, new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None) {
16523                Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(message)) => assert!(
16524                    message.contains(expected_field),
16525                    "{case} should identify {expected_field}, got: {message}"
16526                ),
16527                Err(error) => anyhow::bail!("{case} returned the wrong error: {error}"),
16528                Ok(_) => anyhow::bail!("{case} was accepted"),
16529            }
16530        }
16531
16532        Ok(())
16533    }

16535    /// A rejected PIX configuration must not consume the manager's one-shot start state.
16536    ///
16537    /// Validation is fallible and happens before any worker is spawned, so callers must be able to
16538    /// correct the toolbox (or start without PIX) and retry the same manager. Otherwise `start`
16539    /// reports an ordinary configuration error while leaving `is_started() == false`, but the
16540    /// already-filled message-sender lock makes every retry fail with `AlreadyStarted`.
16541    ///
16542    /// On a runtime because the retry now gets far enough to spawn the manager's workers, which is
16543    /// the whole point — before the fix it returned `AlreadyStarted` before reaching them.
16544    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16545    async fn rejected_pix_start_does_not_poison_a_retry() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16546        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
16547
16548        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
16549            SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
16550                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16551                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
16552                        max_recovery_idle: Duration::from_secs(600),
16553                        ..Default::default()
16554                    },
16555                    ..Default::default()
16556                },
16557                ..Default::default()
16558            });
16559
16560        let (invalid_pix, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
16561            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig::default()).into(),
16562            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig {
16563                unused_verifier_lifetime: Duration::from_secs(60),
16564                ..Default::default()
16565            })
16566            .into(),
16567        );
16568        let (first_tx, _first_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
16569        let (first_notifier, _first_notifications) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
16570        assert!(matches!(
16571            mgr.start(first_tx, first_notifier, Some(invalid_pix), None),
16572            Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(_))
16573        ));
16574        assert!(
16575            !mgr.is_started(),
16576            "a rejected start must not report the manager as running"
16577        );
16578
16579        let (retry_tx, _retry_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
16580        let (retry_notifier, _retry_notifications) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
16581        let retry = mgr.start(retry_tx, retry_notifier, None, None);
16582        assert!(
16583            retry.is_ok(),
16584            "a configuration error must leave the manager retryable, got {retry:?}"
16585        );
16586
16587        Ok(())
16588    }

16936    /// Verifies that a session is closed on the very first `UnverifiableShares` PIX event.
16937    ///
16938    /// An event means a whole polynomial failed to open its commitment, which already dooms the
16939    /// cycle, so there is nothing to tolerate and nothing to configure. See
16940    /// `SessionPixSupervisor::on_unverifiable_shares` for the reasoning.
16941    ///
16942    /// ## Steps
16943    /// 1. Bob's manager is started with a `PixToolbox` and a PIX quota config. Alice's session initiation is processed
16944    ///    via `handle_incoming_session_initiation`.
16945    /// 2. One `UnverifiableShares` event is dispatched for the session's `SsaId`.
16946    /// 3. The session is closed: `active_sessions` is empty and `num_active_sessions` is 0, confirming the supervisor
16947    ///    closed it.
16948    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16949    async fn session_is_closed_on_the_first_unverifiable_share() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16950        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
16951        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
16952
16953        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
16954            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
16955            threshold: 2,
16956            surplus_shares: 1,
16957        };
16958
16959        let (pix_toolbox, _) = PixToolbox::new(
16960            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
16961            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
16962        );
16963
16964        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
16965            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
16966                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
16967                ..Default::default()
16968            },
16969            ..Default::default()
16970        });
16971
16972        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
16973        bob_transport
16974            .expect_send_message()
16975            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
16976        // handle_incoming_session_initiation sends SessionEstablished + SsaRequest.
16977        bob_transport
16978            .expect_send_message()
16979            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
16980
16981        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
16982        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
16983        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
16984            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
16985            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
16986        });
16987        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
16988
16989        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
16990
16991        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
16992            alice_pseudonym,
16993            StartInitiation {
16994                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
16995                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
16996                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
16997                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
16998            },
16999        )
17000        .await?;
17001
17002        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1, "the session must start out open");
17003
17004        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(alice_pseudonym, SsaIndex::MIN);
17005        mgr.dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
17006            ssa_id,
17007            observed_total: 1,
17008            peer: crate::supervision::test_peer(),
17009        })
17010        .await?;
17011
17012        // The supervisor decides, and its `Close` reaches the driver over a channel, so the close
17013        // is observed rather than assumed.
17014        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
17015            while mgr.num_active_sessions() > 0 {
17016                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
17017            }
17018        })
17019        .await
17020        .context("session must be closed by the first unverifiable share")?;
17021
17022        assert!(mgr.active_sessions().is_empty());
17023
17024        bob_sender.close_channel();
17025        bob_handle.await??;
17026        Ok(())
17027    }

17029    // Four tests lived here, all asserting how many `SsaRequest` messages an `SsaAlmostRecovered` or
17030    // `SsaRecovered` event produced: `exit_requests_new_ssa_after_almost_recovered_event`,
17031    // `exit_ignores_stale_ssa_almost_recovered_event`,
17032    // `exit_handles_concurrent_almost_and_full_recovery_for_same_ssa` and
17033    // `exit_requests_new_ssa_on_recovery_when_not_already_pipelined`.
17034    //
17035    // That decision is the supervisor's now, and each of them has a direct counterpart against the
17036    // state machine: `almost_recovered_while_recovering_requests_next_once`,
17037    // `almost_recovered_while_awaiting_deposit_defers_request`,
17038    // `recovered_with_prior_early_event_does_not_fallback` and
17039    // `recovered_without_prior_early_event_falls_back_to_request`. Reaching the same logic through
17040    // an event channel, an action channel and a spawned driver only added scheduling noise — and
17041    // three of the four asserted a pipelining that no longer happens on an unfunded SSA, which is
17042    // the deliberate change: the Exit does not commit to another SSA before the current one is paid
17043    // for.
17044    //
17045    // What those tests did cover that the state machine cannot is the wiring itself, in both
17046    // directions. Actions reaching the wire is `the_opening_ssa_request_follows_session_established`
17047    // below; events reaching the supervisor is `session_is_closed_on_the_first_unverifiable_share`.
17048
17049    /// Verifies that the supervisor's opening `RequestSsa` reaches the wire, and does so *after* the
17050    /// `SessionEstablished` that publishes the Session.
17051    ///
17052    /// The ordering is why the supervisor is spawned where it is. An `SsaRequest` arriving first
17053    /// would reference a Session the Entry has not been told exists.
17054    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17055    async fn the_opening_ssa_request_follows_session_established() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17056        use std::sync::Arc;
17057
17058        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
17059        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
17060
17061        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
17062            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
17063                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
17064                threshold: 2,
17065                surplus_shares: 1,
17066            })
17067            .into(),
17068            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
17069        );
17070
17071        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
17072            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
17073                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
17074                ..Default::default()
17075            },
17076            ..Default::default()
17077        });
17078
17079        // Records the kind of every outbound Start message, in order.
17080        let sent = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::<&'static str>::new()));
17081        let sent_clone = sent.clone();
17082        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
17083        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
17084            let sent_clone = sent_clone.clone();
17085            Box::pin(async move {
17086                match HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text) {
17087                    Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(_)) => sent_clone.lock().unwrap().push("established"),
17088                    Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(req)) => {
17089                        assert_eq!(
17090                            req.dimensions().expect("SsaRequest params must be in range"),
17091                            PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE).expect("valid"),
17092                            "SsaRequest must carry the negotiated dimensions, surplus included"
17093                        );
17094                        assert_eq!(
17095                            req.commitments.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
17096                            [SsaIndex::MIN],
17097                            "the opening request must commit to the first SSA index"
17098                        );
17099                        sent_clone.lock().unwrap().push("ssa_request");
17100                    }
17101                    _ => {}
17102                }
17103                Ok(())
17104            })
17105        });
17106
17107        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
17108        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
17109        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
17110            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
17111            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
17112        });
17113        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
17114
17115        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17116        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
17117            alice_pseudonym,
17118            StartInitiation {
17119                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
17120                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
17121                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
17122                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
17123            },
17124        )
17125        .await?;
17126
17127        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
17128            while sent.lock().unwrap().len() < 2 {
17129                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
17130            }
17131        })
17132        .await
17133        .context("the supervisor's opening SsaRequest never reached the wire")?;
17134
17135        assert_eq!(
17136            sent.lock().unwrap().as_slice(),
17137            ["established", "ssa_request"],
17138            "the Entry must learn the Session exists before it is asked to commit to an SSA"
17139        );
17140
17141        bob_sender.close_channel();
17142        bob_handle.await??;
17143        Ok(())
17144    }
