17146    /// A pool that does not supply deposit data must take the Session with it, and name itself.
17147    ///
17148    /// The data only ever travels in the `SsaRequest` that carries the commitments, so an Entry that
17149    /// needs it and does not get it cannot ask for it later — it would simply never deposit, and the
17150    /// Session would die on the Exit's own commitment deadline, blamed on the peer. Failing here
17151    /// costs one Session that was not going to work, and points at the local pool instead: the Entry
17152    /// is told with `UnacceptablePixParams` rather than the supervisor's generic `Unknown`, and this
17153    /// node records [`ClosureReason::MissingDepositData`] rather than `PixFailure`.
17154    ///
17155    /// The event stream is dropped rather than left unanswered, which reaches the same failure
17156    /// through the listener check instead of [`DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`] — the same error, the
17157    /// same close, three seconds sooner. What the collection itself does with a pool that answers
17158    /// badly is covered by the `request_deposit_data` tests below.
17159    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17160    async fn missing_deposit_data_closes_the_session_and_names_the_pool() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17161        use std::sync::Arc;
17162
17163        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
17164        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
17165
17166        // Deliberately *not* `pix_toolbox_with_pool`: nothing answers, which is the case under test.
17167        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
17168            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
17169                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
17170                threshold: 2,
17171                surplus_shares: 1,
17172            })
17173            .into(),
17174            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
17175        );
17176        drop(pix_events);
17177
17178        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
17179            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
17180                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
17181                ..Default::default()
17182            },
17183            ..Default::default()
17184        });
17185
17186        // Records the kind of every outbound Start message, with the reason of any SessionError.
17187        let sent = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
17188        let sent_clone = sent.clone();
17189        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
17190        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
17191            let sent_clone = sent_clone.clone();
17192            Box::pin(async move {
17193                match HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text) {
17194                    Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(_)) => {
17195                        sent_clone.lock().unwrap().push("established".into())
17196                    }
17197                    Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(_)) => sent_clone.lock().unwrap().push("ssa_request".into()),
17198                    Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(err)) => {
17199                        sent_clone.lock().unwrap().push(format!("error:{}", err.reason))
17200                    }
17201                    _ => {}
17202                }
17203                Ok(())
17204            })
17205        });
17206
17207        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
17208        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
17209        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
17210            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
17211            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
17212        });
17213        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
17214
17215        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17216        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
17217            alice_pseudonym,
17218            StartInitiation {
17219                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
17220                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
17221                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
17222                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
17223            },
17224        )
17225        .await?;
17226
17227        timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
17228            while mgr.num_active_sessions() > 0 {
17229                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
17230            }
17231        })
17232        .await
17233        .context("the Session must not survive a pool that cannot supply deposit data")?;
17234
17235        let sent = sent.lock().unwrap().clone();
17236        assert!(
17237            !sent.iter().any(|m| m == "ssa_request"),
17238            "no SsaRequest may go on the wire without the deposit data it has to carry, got {sent:?}"
17239        );
17240        assert!(
17241            sent.iter()
17242                .any(|m| m == &format!("error:{}", StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams)),
17243            "the Entry must be told with a reason that names the failure, got {sent:?}"
17244        );
17245
17246        bob_sender.close_channel();
17247        bob_handle.await??;
17248        Ok(())
17249    }

17251    // `pipelined_ssa_preserves_earlier_deposit_deadline` lived here. It asserted that
17252    // `PixKillSwitch(1)` and `PixKillSwitch(2)` were independent entries in the `AbortableList`,
17253    // which is no longer a thing the manager can observe: per-SSA deadlines belong to the
17254    // supervisor. The invariant moved with them, to
17255    // `supervision::supervisor::tests::pipelining_a_second_ssa_leaves_the_first_ones_deadlines_alone`,
17256    // where it can compare the deadline instants rather than just the presence of two handles.
17257
17258    /// Verifies that an explicit `close_session` leaves no reconstructor state behind for an SSA
17259    /// cycle that was still in flight.
17260    ///
17261    /// Retirement used to be an explicit sweep over every index the Session had ever used; it is
17262    /// now a consequence of aborting the action driver, which drops the guards it holds. This
17263    /// exercises one cycle because that is all a mock transport can get in flight — pipelining a
17264    /// second needs a funded first, and funding arrives from the chain. The multi-cycle case is
17265    /// covered where the guards are: `protocols/pix`'s guard tests and the supervisor's own suite.
17266    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17267    async fn close_session_retires_in_flight_ssa_cycles() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17268        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
17269            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
17270                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
17271                threshold: 2,
17272                surplus_shares: 1,
17273            })
17274            .into(),
17275            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
17276        );
17277        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
17278            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
17279                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
17280                ..Default::default()
17281            },
17282            ..Default::default()
17283        });
17284        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
17285        bob_transport
17286            .expect_send_message()
17287            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
17288        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
17289        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
17290        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
17291            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
17292            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
17293        });
17294        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
17295
17296        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17297        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
17298            alice_pseudonym,
17299            StartInitiation {
17300                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
17301                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
17302                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
17303                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
17304            },
17305        )
17306        .await?;
17307
17308        // Grab a reference to the reconstructor before close_session consumes the slot.
17309        let pix_toolbox_ref = mgr.pix_toolbox.get().unwrap().clone();
17310        let share_processor = pix_toolbox_ref.share_processor;
17311
17312        let ssa1 = SsaId::new(alice_pseudonym, SsaIndex::MIN);
17313
17314        // Precondition: the first cycle's builder exists, so the assertion below proves actual
17315        // retirement rather than the absence of a builder that was never created. The supervisor's
17316        // opening `RequestSsa` reaches the driver asynchronously, so this waits rather than assumes.
17317        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
17318            while !share_processor.contains_builder(&ssa1) {
17319                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
17320            }
17321        })
17322        .await
17323        .context("the opening SSA request never registered a builder")?;
17324
17325        mgr.close_session(&alice_pseudonym);
17326
17327        // Aborting the driver drops the `SsaCommitmentGuard`s it owns, which releases each SSA's
17328        // reconstructor state. The abort takes effect at the next scheduling point, hence the wait.
17329        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
17330            while share_processor.contains_builder(&ssa1) {
17331                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
17332            }
17333        })
17334        .await
17335        .context("close_session left the in-flight SSA's reconstructor state behind")?;
17336
17337        bob_sender.close_channel();
17338        bob_handle.await??;
17339        Ok(())
17340    }

17378        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
17379        bob_transport

17384            .expect_send_message()

17435    /// The default live-cycle budget must admit at least as many PIX Sessions as a node manages by
17436    /// default, or the Session limit stops being the first one reached and the documented default
17437    /// no longer holds.
17438    ///
17439    /// The per-Session figure is what admission reserves at the default batch of one, not the bare
17440    /// peak of one cycle: `cycle_budget_for` multiplies by `MAX_OVERLAPPING_BATCHES`.
17441    #[test]
17442    fn default_live_cycle_budget_admits_the_default_managed_session_count() {
17443        // Default of `maximum_managed_sessions` in `hopr-transport`'s `HoprProtocolConfig`, which is
17444        // not visible from this crate; keep in step with it.
17445        const DEFAULT_MANAGED_SESSIONS: u64 = 100;
17446
17447        let per_session = cycle_budget_for(&DEFAULT_PIX_PARAMS, 1);
17448        let budget = IncomingSessionPixConfig::default().max_live_cycle_bytes;
17449
17450        assert!(
17451            budget / per_session >= DEFAULT_MANAGED_SESSIONS,
17452            "a {budget}-byte budget at {per_session} bytes per Session admits {} Sessions, fewer than the \
17453             {DEFAULT_MANAGED_SESSIONS} a node manages by default",
17454            budget / per_session
17455        );
17456    }
17457
17458    /// The Entry must not admit a successor before a default Exit could possibly have produced its
17459    /// early-recovery request.
17460    ///
17461    /// Recovery is counted in completed polynomials, while emission is windowed. Every fully drained
17462    /// window before the one containing the 85% boundary has already emitted both threshold and
17463    /// surplus shares. Dividing 85% by the global surplus factor therefore underestimates the
17464    /// boundary. At the deployed split (`DEFAULT_PIX_PARAMS`, whose factor is 3.47x) the first
17465    /// possible early signal is about 83% through emission, not 24.5%; those figures belong to that
17466    /// split and move with it.
17467    ///
17468    /// The gate compares against `min_emission_for_early_recovery` directly, so this test recomputes
17469    /// the boundary independently — from the same first principles, but without calling the function
17470    /// under test — and checks the two agree. A shared helper would agree with itself.
17471    #[test]
17472    fn successor_gate_waits_until_default_early_recovery_can_be_reached() {
17473        let params = DEFAULT_PIX_PARAMS;
17474        let polys = params.polys_per_ssa() as u64;
17475        let threshold = params.shares_per_poly() as u64;
17476        let surplus = params.surplus_shares() as u64;
17477        let window = (hopr_protocol_pix::SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64).min(polys);
17478        // The floor, because that is what the gate is computed at — see
17479        // `MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD`. The default must not sit below it, or a stock Exit would
17480        // ask before a stock Entry admits.
17481        let early = hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD;
17482        assert!(
17483            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold >= early,
17484            "the shipped default must be admissible under the protocol floor it is gated against"
17485        );
17486        let needed = (early * polys as f64).ceil() as u64;
17487
17488        // `needed` lies in this window. Earlier windows are fully exhausted, including surplus;
17489        // inside this one, `threshold - 1` complete passes and `in_window` shares of the threshold
17490        // pass are the absolute minimum that can have been emitted before those polynomials recover.
17491        let prior_windows = (needed - 1) / window;
17492        let prior_polys = prior_windows * window;
17493        let current_width = window.min(polys - prior_polys);
17494        let in_window = needed - prior_polys;
17495        let minimum_emitted = prior_polys * (threshold + surplus) + (threshold - 1) * current_width + in_window;
17496        let minimum_fraction = minimum_emitted as f64 / (polys * (threshold + surplus)) as f64;
17497
17498        let gate = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(&params, early);
17499        assert_eq!(
17500            minimum_emitted,
17501            gate,
17502            "the successor gate opens at {} shares ({:.1}% of emission) against an independently derived earliest \
17503             honest request of {minimum_emitted} ({:.1}%); any shortfall permits a hostile Exit to solicit a deposit \
17504             before it is earned",
17505            gate,
17506            gate as f64 / (polys * (threshold + surplus)) as f64 * 100.0,
17507            minimum_fraction * 100.0,
17508        );
17509
17510        // And the estimate this replaced is demonstrably below it, so the test would have caught it.
17511        assert!(
17512            ((early / 1.5) * (polys * (threshold + surplus)) as f64) < gate as f64,
17513            "the surplus-factor estimate must sit below the real boundary"
17514        );
17515    }
17516
17517    /// Dimensions wide enough that the protocol floor and a stricter local threshold disagree.
17518    ///
17519    /// At `small_pix_params`' two polynomials, `ceil(0.85 x 2)` and `ceil(1.0 x 2)` are both 2, so
17520    /// every threshold in range produces the same boundary and a test built on them cannot tell which
17521    /// one the gate used. Eight separates them: 7 polynomials against 8.
17522    fn wide_pix_params() -> PixParams {
17523        PixParams::try_new(8, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE).expect("test dimensions must be valid")
17524    }
17525
17526    /// What a fixture's transport has been asked to put on the wire.
17527    #[derive(Default)]
17528    struct WireRecord {
17529        sent: parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<StartProtocolDiscriminants>>,
17530    }
17531
17532    impl WireRecord {
17533        /// How many Start messages of `kind` have been sent so far.
17534        fn count(&self, kind: StartProtocolDiscriminants) -> usize {
17535            self.sent.lock().iter().filter(|sent| **sent == kind).count()
17536        }
17537    }
17538
17539    /// Builds an Entry-side manager serving `params`, with the reconstructor at `early_threshold`.
17540    ///
17541    /// Returns the manager, its generator, and the PIX event stream, with one PIX Session already
17542    /// established for the returned pseudonym.
17543    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
17544    async fn entry_with_pix_session(
17545        params: PixParams,
17546        early_threshold: f64,
17547    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
17548        SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
17549        Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
17550        HoprPseudonym,
17551        impl futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin,
17552        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
17553        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
17554    )> {
17555        entry_with_recorded_pix_session(params, early_threshold, Arc::new(WireRecord::default())).await
17556    }
17557
17558    /// [`entry_with_pix_session`], whose transport also records what it is asked to send.
17559    ///
17560    /// For the tests whose subject is what the Entry did *not* put on the wire: a repeated request
17561    /// must emit neither a `ReadyToDeposit` nor a second `SsaCommit` burst, and only the transport
17562    /// can say the second part of that.
17563    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
17564    async fn entry_with_recorded_pix_session(
17565        params: PixParams,
17566        early_threshold: f64,
17567        wire: Arc<WireRecord>,
17568    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
17569        SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
17570        Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
17571        HoprPseudonym,
17572        impl futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin,
17573        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
17574        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
17575    )> {
17576        entry_with_wrapped_sender(params, early_threshold, wire, |sender| sender).await
17577    }
17578
17579    /// [`entry_with_recorded_pix_session`], whose manager sends through `wrap(sender)` instead of the
17580    /// plain channel sender.
17581    ///
17582    /// For the tests that need the Entry's transport to fail *selectively*: a channel sender can only
17583    /// fail by being closed, and it never recovers. The returned sender is the unwrapped one, so
17584    /// the test can still close the channel and join the forwarding task.
17585    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
17586    async fn entry_with_wrapped_sender<S>(
17587        params: PixParams,
17588        early_threshold: f64,
17589        wire: Arc<WireRecord>,
17590        wrap: impl FnOnce(UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>) -> S,
17591    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
17592        SessionManager<S>,
17593        Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
17594        HoprPseudonym,
17595        impl futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin,
17596        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
17597        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
17598    )>
17599    where
17600        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
17601        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
17602    {
17603        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
17604
17605        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
17606            polynomials_per_ssa: params.polys_per_ssa(),
17607            threshold: params.shares_per_poly(),
17608            surplus_shares: params.surplus_shares(),
17609        }));
17610        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
17611            generator.clone(),
17612            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig {
17613                early_recovery_threshold: early_threshold,
17614                ..Default::default()
17615            })
17616            .into(),
17617        );
17618        // This fixture's manager plays both halves, so its own Exit side opens a cycle and blocks on
17619        // the deposit pool. Answered on the way through, leaving the stream the caller reads — which
17620        // is the deposits — as it was.
17621        let pix_events = crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events, |_| Vec::new());
17622
17623        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
17624            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
17625                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
17626                ..Default::default()
17627            },
17628            ..Default::default()
17629        });
17630
17631        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
17632        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
17633            let wire = wire.clone();
17634            Box::pin(async move {
17635                let Ok(message) = HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text) else {
17636                    return Ok(());
17637                };
17638                wire.sent.lock().push(StartProtocolDiscriminants::from(message));
17639                Ok(())
17640            })
17641        });
17642        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
17643        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
17644        tokio::spawn(async move {
17645            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
17646            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
17647        });
17648        mgr.start(wrap(bob_sender.clone()), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
17649
17650        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17651        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
17652            pseudonym,
17653            StartInitiation {
17654                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
17655                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
17656                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
17657                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0)),
17658            },
17659        )
17660        .await?;
17661
17662        Ok((mgr, generator, pseudonym, pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle))
17663    }
17664
17665    /// One SSA commitment at `index`, from the identity element the Exit-side point is not checked
17666    /// against here.
17667    fn ssa_request_for(index: u32) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<SsaIndex, HoprPixGroupElement> {
17668        let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(
17669            hopr_protocol_pix::PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default()
17670                .to_bytes()
17671                .as_ref(),
17672        )
17673        .expect("identity element must be valid");
17674        std::collections::BTreeMap::from([(SsaIndex::new(index).expect("non-zero"), identity)])
17675    }
17676
17677    /// Drains whatever the PIX event stream has ready, counting the deposits among it.
17678    ///
17679    /// Only [`ReadyToDeposit`](HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit) is counted: an Exit sharing
17680    /// this stream also asks its pool for deposit data on it, and every caller here is asking how
17681    /// many cycles were opened, not how many messages went by.
17682    async fn drain_pix_events(events: &mut (dyn futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin)) -> usize {
17683        let mut seen = 0;
17684        // A bounded wait rather than `now_or_never`: these fixtures answer the Exit half's
17685        // deposit-data requests on a forwarding task, so an event that has already been produced may
17686        // not have crossed it yet. The wait is only paid once, when the stream has gone quiet.
17687        while let Ok(Some(event)) = timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), events.next()).await {
17688            if matches!(event, HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit(_)) {
17689                seen += 1;
17690            }
17691        }
17692        seen
17693    }
17694
17695    /// Credits `count` Exit → Entry packets to the Session, as its receive path would.
17696    ///
17697    /// These fixtures build their slot through `handle_incoming_session_initiation`, whose receive
17698    /// path counts the *outgoing* direction, so the Entry-side counter the successor gate reads has
17699    /// to be driven by hand. `returned_packets_are_counted_on_the_entry_receive_path` is what pins
17700    /// that a real Entry Session advances it; here it only has to move.
17701    fn credit_returned_packets<S>(mgr: &SessionManager<S>, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym, count: u64)
17702    where
17703        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
17704        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
17705    {
17706        mgr.sessions
17707            .get(pseudonym)
17708            .expect("session must exist")
17709            .returned_packets
17710            .fetch_add(count, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17711    }
17712
17713    /// Packets the successor gate requires before it will admit a batch beyond `watermark`.
17714    ///
17715    /// Mirrors `handle_ssa_request`'s boundary rather than calling it, so that a change to the
17716    /// boundary has to be restated here — a helper shared with the code under test would agree with
17717    /// itself whatever either of them did. The bar set below that boundary is
17718    /// [`successor_required_packets`] itself, which
17719    /// `the_successor_bar_is_a_lower_confidence_bound_on_honest_arrivals` pins against values computed
17720    /// independently.
17721    fn required_returned_packets(params: &PixParams, watermark: u32) -> u64 {
17722        let min_emitted =
17723            hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(params, hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD);
17724        let shares_per_cycle = params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
17725        let target = (watermark as u64 - 1) * shares_per_cycle + min_emitted;
17726        successor_required_packets(target, params.tolerated_share_loss())
17727    }
17728
17729    /// The successor gate must open at the protocol floor, not at the local reconstructor's threshold.
17730    ///
17731    /// The value that decides when a correct Exit asks for its next batch is the *peer's*
17732    /// `early_recovery_threshold`, and it does not travel on the wire. Deriving the boundary from the
17733    /// Entry's own copy meant two individually valid configurations could not communicate: an Exit
17734    /// configured lower sent its request before the gate opened and the Entry dropped it silently.
17735    /// Before the Exit re-sent an unanswered successor request that was fatal — the Session died on
17736    /// `max_ssa_delivery_time` waiting for a commitment that had been deliberately refused, visible on
17737    /// neither node as a configuration error. It is now a stream of refusals until emission catches
17738    /// up, which is why the boundary still has to be the floor's: a gate on the local value would
17739    /// refuse a conforming Exit for longer than it needs to.
17740    ///
17741    /// So the gate is computed at [`hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD`], which
17742    /// `validate_pix_supervision` holds every Exit to. This fixture puts the local reconstructor at
17743    /// `1.0` — the strictest end of the range — and asks at exactly the floor's boundary. A gate built
17744    /// on the local value wants one more share and refuses.
17745    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17746    async fn successor_gate_opens_at_the_protocol_floor_not_the_local_threshold() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17747        let params = wide_pix_params();
17748        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
17749            entry_with_pix_session(params, 1.0).await?;
17750
17751        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
17752            pseudonym,
17753            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
17754        )
17755        .await
17756        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
17757        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17758
17759        // Fully served, so that the emission boundary is the only thing this test can be measuring.
17760        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required_returned_packets(&params, 1));
17761
17762        let at_floor = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
17763            &params,
17764            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
17765        );
17766        let at_local = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(&params, 1.0);
17767        assert!(
17768            at_floor < at_local,
17769            "the fixture must separate the two boundaries, got {at_floor} and {at_local}"
17770        );
17771
17772        // One share short of the floor's boundary, the request is early under either reading.
17773        for sent in 1..at_floor as u32 {
17774            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
17775        }
17776        let err = mgr
17777            .handle_ssa_request(
17778                pseudonym,
17779                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
17780            )
17781            .await
17782            .expect_err("a request one share below the boundary must be refused");
17783        assert!(
17784            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
17785            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
17786        );
17787        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17788
17789        // On the boundary itself it is admitted — and would not be if the gate read the local 1.0.
17790        generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &at_floor.to_be_bytes())?;
17791        assert_eq!(
17792            at_floor,
17793            generator
17794                .emission_progress(&pseudonym)
17795                .expect("committed")
17796                .front_emitted,
17797            "the fixture must stand exactly on the floor's boundary"
17798        );
17799        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
17800            pseudonym,
17801            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
17802        )
17803        .await
17804        .context("a request at the protocol floor must be accepted whatever the local threshold is")?;
17805        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17806
17807        bob_sender.close_channel();
17808        bob_handle.await??;
17809        Ok(())
17810    }
17811
17812    /// A successor request arriving after the generator's state was discarded must be refused.
17813    ///
17814    /// The gate only applies where there is emission progress to measure, and absent progress is
17815    /// otherwise the ordinary opening batch. But the generator keeps its per-pseudonym state in a
17816    /// cache with an idle retention refreshed by share *emission*, so a Session kept alive while the
17817    /// Entry emits nothing outlives it — and the successor gate is then not relaxed but deleted, along
17818    /// with the monotonic index the discarded entry carried. An Exit that arranges that farms one
17819    /// unearned deposit per retention period, which is the exposure the gate exists to close.
17820    ///
17821    /// `forget` reaches the same state the retention would, deliberately: an evicted entry and an
17822    /// explicitly dropped one are indistinguishable from the outside, which is precisely why the fact
17823    /// that a batch *was* committed has to be held somewhere that lives as long as the Session.
17824    ///
17825    /// The opening request in this test is the other half of the property — absent state with nothing
17826    /// committed is still admitted, or no PIX Session could ever start.
17827    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17828    async fn an_ssa_request_against_discarded_generator_state_is_refused_and_closes_the_session() -> anyhow::Result<()>
17829    {
17830        let params = small_pix_params();
17831        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
17832            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
17833
17834        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
17835            pseudonym,
17836            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
17837        )
17838        .await
17839        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
17840        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17841        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions());
17842
17843        generator.forget(&pseudonym);
17844        assert!(
17845            generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).is_none(),
17846            "the fixture must reproduce the state an idle eviction leaves behind"
17847        );
17848
17849        let err = mgr
17850            .handle_ssa_request(
17851                pseudonym,
17852                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
17853            )
17854            .await
17855            .expect_err("a successor request against discarded generator state must be refused");
17856        assert!(
17857            matches!(
17858                err,
17859                TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_))
17860            ),
17861            "expected Unacceptable, got {err:?}"
17862        );
17863        assert_eq!(
17864            0,
17865            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
17866            "a refused request must not emit a single ReadyToDeposit"
17867        );
17868        assert!(
17869            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
17870            "the Entry can no longer emit shares for the cycles it committed to, so leaving the Session open only \
17871             makes the Exit wait out its commitment deadline"
17872        );
17873
17874        bob_sender.close_channel();
17875        bob_handle.await??;
17876        Ok(())
17877    }
17878
17879    /// Emission is not service: a successor must be refused until the Exit has returned data.
17880    ///
17881    /// This is H6, and it is the case the emission half of the gate cannot see. `emission_progress`
17882    /// counts shares this node handed to its own packet pipeline — a consumption `create_surb_for_path`
17883    /// does not even roll back when the rest of the packet build fails. An Exit that requests, is
17884    /// funded and then returns nothing still walks that counter forward for as long as the Entry keeps
17885    /// sending, so on its own it prices deposits against work the Entry did to itself.
17886    ///
17887    /// The fixture therefore satisfies the emission half completely and the returned half not at all.
17888    /// Before this gate existed the request below was admitted and a second deposit instruction went
17889    /// out for it.
17890    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17891    async fn entry_refuses_a_successor_the_exit_has_not_paid_for_with_returned_data() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17892        let params = wide_pix_params();
17893        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
17894            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
17895
17896        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
17897            pseudonym,
17898            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
17899        )
17900        .await
17901        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
17902        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17903
17904        // Emit the whole cycle: the emission half of the gate is now satisfied several times over,
17905        // and it is the only half that would have been consulted before.
17906        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
17907            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
17908        }
17909        let progress = generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).expect("committed");
17910        assert!(
17911            progress.is_serving_last_committed()
17912                && progress.front_emitted
17913                    >= hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
17914                        &params,
17915                        hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD
17916                    ),
17917            "the fixture must satisfy the emission half outright, or it is not testing the other one"
17918        );
17919
17920        let err = mgr
17921            .handle_ssa_request(
17922                pseudonym,
17923                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
17924            )
17925            .await
17926            .expect_err("a successor must not be funded before the Exit has returned anything");
17927        assert!(
17928            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
17929            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
17930        );
17931        assert_eq!(
17932            0,
17933            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
17934            "a refused successor must not emit a single ReadyToDeposit"
17935        );
17936        assert_eq!(
17937            vec![pseudonym],
17938            mgr.active_sessions(),
17939            "an under-served request is refused, not fatal — the Exit may still earn the batch it holds"
17940        );
17941
17942        // And the same request is admitted the moment the service exists.
17943        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required_returned_packets(&params, 1));
17944        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
17945            pseudonym,
17946            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
17947        )
17948        .await
17949        .context("a successor must be admitted once the Exit has returned what it owes")?;
17950        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17951
17952        bob_sender.close_channel();
17953        bob_handle.await??;
17954        Ok(())
17955    }
17956
17957    /// An Exit that has returned nothing is refused immediately, not held.
17958    ///
17959    /// The deferral below the boundary exists for reordering, and it holds a bounded
17960    /// `for_each_concurrent` slot and the per-pseudonym request lock while it runs. That is only safe
17961    /// because it is entered exclusively for a *near miss*: an Exit which has returned nothing at all
17962    /// must cost nothing at all to refuse, or "ask early and say nothing" becomes a way to park one of
17963    /// this node's Start-protocol slots per Session it holds.
17964    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17965    async fn an_unserved_successor_is_refused_without_waiting() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17966        let params = wide_pix_params();
17967        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
17968            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
17969
17970        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
17971            pseudonym,
17972            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
17973        )
17974        .await
17975        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
17976        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
17977
17978        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
17979            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
17980        }
17981
17982        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
17983        let err = mgr
17984            .handle_ssa_request(
17985                pseudonym,
17986                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
17987            )
17988            .await
17989            .expect_err("an unserved successor must be refused");
17990        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
17991
17992        assert!(
17993            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
17994            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
17995        );
17996        assert!(
17997            elapsed * 4 < SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT,
17998            "refusing an Exit that returned nothing took {elapsed:?}, which is within reach of the \
17999             {SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT:?} near-miss wait — it must not have entered it at all"
18000        );
18001
18002        bob_sender.close_channel();
18003        bob_handle.await??;
18004        Ok(())
18005    }
18006
18007    /// Before a Session's slot exists, at most one request for it waits for the slot; any other is
18008    /// refused at once rather than parking a second shared Start handler.
18009    ///
18010    /// The dispatch filter admits every request naming a pending initiation, and the wait comes
18011    /// before the request lock, so without this whoever holds SURBs for the pseudonym could occupy
18012    /// every handler for the length of the wait — the symptom the request lock closes once the slot
18013    /// exists.
18014    ///
18015    /// ## Steps
18016    /// 1. A pseudonym is pending as an outgoing initiation, and has no slot yet.
18017    /// 2. A first request waits for the slot.
18018    /// 3. A second request for the same pseudonym is refused as `Unacceptable` without waiting.
18019    /// 4. Control: the first was waiting, not refused — it gives up as `NonExistingSession` when no slot comes — and
18020    ///    once it has left, the next request waits too rather than being refused.
18021    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18022    async fn a_second_ssa_request_for_a_pending_session_is_refused_without_waiting_for_its_slot() -> anyhow::Result<()>
18023    {
18024        let params = wide_pix_params();
18025        let (mgr, _generator, _pseudonym, _pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
18026            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
18027
18028        let pending = HoprPseudonym::random();
18029        mgr.pending_outgoing.insert(pending, PendingOutgoingToken::next());
18030        let request = move || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pending, params, ssa_request_for(1), []);
18031        let is_waiting = || {
18032            mgr.slot_allocated
18033                .lock()
18034                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
18035                .get(&pending)
18036                .is_some_and(|waiters| waiters.iter().any(|w| !w.is_canceled()))
18037        };
18038
18039        let first = tokio::spawn({
18040            let mgr = mgr.clone();
18041            async move { mgr.handle_ssa_request(pending, request()).await }
18042        });
18043        timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
18044            while !is_waiting() {
18045                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
18046            }
18047        })
18048        .await
18049        .context("the first request must wait for the pending Session's slot")?;
18050
18051        let refused = timeout(Duration::from_millis(250), mgr.handle_ssa_request(pending, request()))
18052            .await
18053            .context("a second request must not wait for the slot as well")?;
18054        assert!(
18055            matches!(
18056                refused,
18057                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
18058            ),
18059            "expected Unacceptable, got {refused:?}"
18060        );
18061
18062        let first = first.await?;
18063        assert!(
18064            matches!(
18065                first,
18066                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession))
18067            ),
18068            "the first request must have waited and given up on the slot, got {first:?}"
18069        );
18070
18071        let next = mgr.handle_ssa_request(pending, request()).await;
18072        assert!(
18073            matches!(
18074                next,
18075                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession))
18076            ),
18077            "once the first request has left, the next one must wait rather than be refused, got {next:?}"
18078        );
18079
18080        bob_sender.close_channel();
18081        bob_handle.await??;
18082        Ok(())
18083    }
18084
18085    /// A request that arrives just ahead of the packets that earned it is waited for, not refused.
18086    ///
18087    /// A conforming Exit asks the instant its reconstructor crosses the threshold, and that request
18088    /// travels the same mixed path as the returned packets which unlocked the shares — so it can
18089    /// overtake the last few of them. Refusing it is not free, although the Exit re-sends: the next
18090    /// re-send is a whole `ssa_request_resend_interval` away, and a request that is only a few packets
18091    /// behind would have been admitted at once. The gate therefore absorbs the reordering rather than
18092    /// treating it as under-service.
18093    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18094    async fn a_near_miss_successor_waits_for_the_packets_still_in_flight() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18095        let params = wide_pix_params();
18096        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
18097            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
18098
18099        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18100            pseudonym,
18101            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
18102        )
18103        .await
18104        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
18105        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18106
18107        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
18108            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
18109        }
18110
18111        // One packet short: the request is in flight ahead of the last one that earned it.
18112        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
18113        assert!(required > 1, "the fixture needs room to be one short");
18114        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required - 1);
18115
18116        // The straggler lands while the request is already being evaluated.
18117        let mgr_clone = mgr.clone();
18118        let late = tokio::spawn(async move {
18119            tokio::time::sleep(SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_POLL).await;
18120            credit_returned_packets(&mgr_clone, &pseudonym, 1);
18121        });
18122
18123        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18124            pseudonym,
18125            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18126        )
18127        .await
18128        .context("a request one packet ahead of its own service must be waited for, not refused")?;
18129        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18130        late.await?;
18131
18132        bob_sender.close_channel();
18133        bob_handle.await??;
18134        Ok(())
18135    }
18136
18137    /// Service rendered before the first commitment does not pay for the first successor.
18138    ///
18139    /// Until a cycle is committed the generator holds no polynomials, so the SURBs going out carry no
18140    /// shares — and the Exit may legitimately be served up to `max_predeposit_packets` of them before
18141    /// any deposit exists. Crediting that prefix would let an Exit bank unpaid service against the
18142    /// first cycle it *is* paid for, which is the one window in a Session's life where the gate has no
18143    /// prior cycle to measure against.
18144    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18145    async fn service_returned_before_the_first_commitment_is_not_credited() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18146        let params = wide_pix_params();
18147        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
18148            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
18149
18150        // Generously served *before* anything is committed, and none of it may count.
18151        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
18152        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required * 10);
18153
18154        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18155            pseudonym,
18156            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
18157        )
18158        .await
18159        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
18160        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18161
18162        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
18163            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
18164        }
18165
18166        let err = mgr
18167            .handle_ssa_request(
18168                pseudonym,
18169                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18170            )
18171            .await
18172            .expect_err("pre-commitment service must not pay for the first successor");
18173        assert!(
18174            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
18175            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
18176        );
18177        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18178
18179        bob_sender.close_channel();
18180        bob_handle.await??;
18181        Ok(())
18182    }

18184    /// The boundary is discounted by the loss a cycle tolerates, not by the surplus ratio.
18185    ///
18186    /// The Exit unlocks a share when the *first relayer* acknowledges its returned packet, which is
18187    /// upstream of the Entry — so everything lost after that point is progress the Exit legitimately
18188    /// has and this node cannot observe, and demanding the undiscounted emission boundary would refuse
18189    /// conforming Exits on any lossy path. But the discount is also what an Exit can withhold for good
18190    /// and still be funded, so it may be no larger than the loss a cycle survives.
18191    ///
18192    /// The surplus ratio `s/(t+s)` is break-even, not survival. At the deployed split it discounted
18193    /// 71.2 % where a cycle tolerates 50.3 %, and put the bar at 23.9 % of a cycle — below the shares a
18194    /// lossless Exit has necessarily unlocked by the earliest point it may ask at all.
18195    ///
18196    /// The bar is then set [`SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS`] standard deviations below the mean an
18197    /// Exit at that loss returns, so that one losing exactly the tolerance is not refused for the
18198    /// variance of its own arrivals.
18199    ///
18200    /// Pinned at the deployed dimensions because the resulting fraction is not something a reader can
18201    /// check by inspection, and it is what decides when real money moves.
18202    #[test]
18203    fn the_successor_boundary_is_discounted_by_the_loss_a_cycle_tolerates() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18204        use crate::{DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA, DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY, DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES};
18205
18206        let params = PixParams::try_new(
18207            DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA,
18208            DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY,
18209            DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES,
18210            LOCAL_PIX_SUITE,
18211        )?;
18212        let cycle = params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
18213        assert_eq!(454_656, cycle);
18214
18215        let undiscounted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
18216            &params,
18217            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
18218        );
18219        assert_eq!(357_274, undiscounted);
18220
18221        // floor(μ − 4σ) for μ = 357 274 × (1 − L) = 177 606.89 and σ = √(357 274 · L · (1 − L)) =
18222        // 298.86, at L = 0.502 883 257 4… computed independently at 90 significant digits. (At a
18223        // window of 256 the boundary was 377 498 and the bar 186 431.)
18224        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
18225        assert_eq!(176_411, required);
18226
18227        let tolerated = params.tolerated_share_loss();
18228        let mean = undiscounted as f64 * (1.0 - tolerated);
18229        let deviation = (undiscounted as f64 * tolerated * (1.0 - tolerated)).sqrt();
18230        let bound = mean - SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * deviation;
18231        assert!(
18232            required as f64 <= bound && bound < required as f64 + 1.0,
18233            "the bar must be the mean arrivals at the tolerated loss less {SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS} of their \
18234             standard deviations, floored, and nothing else: {bound} against {required}"
18235        );
18236
18237        let fraction = required as f64 / cycle as f64;
18238        assert!(
18239            (0.387..0.389).contains(&fraction),
18240            "the deployed successor boundary must sit at ~38.8% of a cycle's returned packets, got {fraction}"
18241        );
18242
18243        // A lossless conforming Exit asks no earlier than `ceil(0.85 × 4096)` recovered polynomials,
18244        // each of which took `t` unlocked shares before any of its surplus. A bar below that funds the
18245        // next deposit on less delivered service than the useful shares the Exit is claiming to have
18246        // recovered from.
18247        let unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit =
18248            (hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD * DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA as f64).ceil() as u64
18249                * DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY as u64;
18250        assert_eq!(111_424, unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit);
18251        assert!(
18252            required >= unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit,
18253            "the successor boundary ({required}) must not sit below what a lossless Exit has unlocked when it may \
18254             first ask ({unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit})"
18255        );
18256
18257        // Each further cycle of a batch is demanded in full at the same discount, less only what the
18258        // margin grows by — and that grows with the square root of the target, so by less than the
18259        // margin a cycle would get on its own. The floor can move either end by one packet.
18260        let whole_first_cycle = required_returned_packets(&params, 2) - required;
18261        let discounted_cycle = cycle as f64 * (1.0 - tolerated);
18262        let lone_cycle_margin = SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * (cycle as f64 * tolerated * (1.0 - tolerated)).sqrt();
18263        assert!(
18264            (discounted_cycle - lone_cycle_margin - 1.0..=discounted_cycle + 1.0).contains(&(whole_first_cycle as f64)),
18265            "a batch of two must demand the first cycle's whole discounted worth, less under {lone_cycle_margin} of \
18266             margin, plus the second's boundary; got {whole_first_cycle} for the first cycle against \
18267             {discounted_cycle}"
18268        );
18269
18270        Ok(())
18271    }
18272
18273    /// The successor gate follows the surplus the Entry bought.
18274    ///
18275    /// The discount is the tolerance of the *negotiated* split, so an Entry that expects unreliable
18276    /// return relayers and buys more surplus loosens its own gate by exactly that much: how strict the
18277    /// gate is follows from the Entry's insurance choice rather than being a knob of its own. At
18278    /// `4096 × (2 + 102)` a cycle tolerates ~86 % share loss, and the bar falls to ~10.4 % of a cycle's
18279    /// packets against the deployed split's ~38.8 %.
18280    ///
18281    /// Driven through `handle_ssa_request` at the real dimensions rather than only through
18282    /// [`required_returned_packets`], because the property is that the gate reads the Session's own
18283    /// parameters — a mirror of its arithmetic cannot show that.
18284    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18285    async fn the_successor_gate_follows_the_surplus_the_entry_bought() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18286        let params = PixParams::try_new(4096, 2, 102, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
18287        let cycle = params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
18288        let undiscounted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
18289            &params,
18290            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
18291        );
18292
18293        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
18294        // floor(μ − 4σ) for μ = 320 410 × (1 − L) = 45 193.78 and σ = 197.03, at L = 0.858 950 169 2…
18295        // computed independently at 90 significant digits. (At a window of 256: 346 522 and 48 057.)
18296        assert_eq!(320_410, undiscounted);
18297        assert_eq!(44_405, required);
18298
18299        let fraction = required as f64 / cycle as f64;
18300        assert!(
18301            (0.103..0.105).contains(&fraction),
18302            "the successor boundary of 4096 x (2 + 102) must sit at ~10.4% of a cycle's returned packets, got \
18303             {fraction}"
18304        );
18305
18306        // And the gate itself, not only its mirror: with emission past the boundary, one emission
18307        // window short of `required` is refused outright — past the near-miss wait, so at once —
18308        // and the rest of it admits the successor.
18309        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
18310            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
18311        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18312            pseudonym,
18313            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
18314        )
18315        .await
18316        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
18317        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18318
18319        for sent in 1..=undiscounted as u32 {
18320            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
18321        }
18322
18323        let short = hopr_protocol_pix::SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64 + 1;
18324        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required - short);
18325        let err = mgr
18326            .handle_ssa_request(
18327                pseudonym,
18328                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18329            )
18330            .await
18331            .expect_err("a successor short of the bought tolerance's boundary must be refused");
18332        assert!(
18333            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
18334            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
18335        );
18336        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18337
18338        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, short);
18339        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18340            pseudonym,
18341            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18342        )
18343        .await
18344        .context("a successor at the bought tolerance's boundary must be admitted")?;
18345        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18346
18347        bob_sender.close_channel();
18348        bob_handle.await??;
18349        Ok(())
18350    }
18351
18352    /// A tiny boundary under a huge surplus must still demand one returned packet.
18353    ///
18354    /// At `128 × (2 + 255)` the early-recovery boundary is 237 packets against a tolerated loss of
18355    /// ~95 %: μ − 4σ is below one, and an unfloored bar of zero funds the successor on the Entry's
18356    /// own emission with nothing returned — the near-miss wait is skipped on zero observed packets, so
18357    /// nothing else would stop it.
18358    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18359    async fn the_successor_gate_demands_a_returned_packet_whatever_the_surplus() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18360        let params = PixParams::try_new(128, 2, 255, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
18361        let target = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
18362            &params,

18364        );

18368        let mean = target as f64 * (1.0 - tolerated);
18369        let deviation = (target as f64 * tolerated * (1.0 - tolerated)).sqrt();
18370        let raw_bound = mean - SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * deviation;
18371        assert!(
18372            raw_bound < 1.0,
18373            "the unfloored bound must be below one packet, got {raw_bound}"
18374        );
18375        assert_eq!(1, required_returned_packets(&params, 1));
18376
18377        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
18378            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
18379        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18380            pseudonym,
18381            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
18382        )
18383        .await
18384        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
18385        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18386
18387        for sent in 1..=target as u32 {
18388            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
18389        }
18390
18391        let err = mgr
18392            .handle_ssa_request(
18393                pseudonym,
18394                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18395            )
18396            .await
18397            .expect_err("a successor with no returned packet must be refused");
18398        assert!(
18399            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
18400            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
18401        );
18402        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18403
18404        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1);
18405        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18406            pseudonym,
18407            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18408        )
18409        .await
18410        .context("a successor with one returned packet must be admitted")?;
18411        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18412
18413        bob_sender.close_channel();
18414        bob_handle.await??;
18415        Ok(())
18416    }
