18418    /// The bar is a lower confidence bound on an honest Exit's arrivals, not their mean.
18419    ///
18420    /// Pinned against `floor(μ − 4σ)` computed outside this crate from independently computed
18421    /// tolerances: at the deployed split, at one an Entry distrusting its return relayers may buy, and
18422    /// at the derived `2048 × (64 + 123)`, where the mean refused an honest Exit. The ends are what tie
18423    /// the bound to the split — no surplus, no tolerance and so no slack; a tolerance near one asks
18424    /// for one packet rather than for a negative count or nothing.
18425    #[test]
18426    fn the_successor_bar_is_a_lower_confidence_bound_on_honest_arrivals() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18427        for target in [0, 1, 377_498, 1 << 40] {
18428            assert_eq!(
18429                target,
18430                successor_required_packets(target, 0.0),
18431                "a split tolerating no loss must be demanded its whole target"
18432            );
18433        }
18434
18435        // 100 × 0.01 − 4 × √(100 × 0.01 × 0.99) < 0: the margin outweighs the mean.
18436        // ... but never below one packet of a non-zero boundary, and a zero boundary stays zero.
18437        assert_eq!(1, successor_required_packets(100, 0.99));
18438        assert_eq!(1, successor_required_packets(377_498, 1.0));
18439        for loss in [0.0, 0.5, 0.99, 1.0] {
18440            assert_eq!(
18441                0,
18442                successor_required_packets(0, loss),
18443                "a zero boundary demands nothing at L = {loss}"
18444            );
18445        }
18446
18447        // The boundaries of the 512-polynomial emission window, pinned in the tests above. (At a
18448        // window of 256: 377 498 → 186 431, 346 522 → 48 057 and 303 565 → 150 641.)
18449        for (polys, threshold, surplus, target, required) in [
18450            (4096, 32, 79, 357_274, 176_411),
18451            (4096, 2, 102, 320_410, 44_405),
18452            (2048, 64, 123, 319_693, 158_674),
18453        ] {
18454            let params = PixParams::try_new(polys, threshold, surplus, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
18455            assert_eq!(
18456                required,
18457                successor_required_packets(target, params.tolerated_share_loss()),
18458                "{polys} x ({threshold} + {surplus}) must demand {required} of a {target}-packet boundary"
18459            );
18460        }
18461
18462        Ok(())
18463    }
18464
18465    /// An honest Exit losing the tolerated share fraction must not lose its Session to the variance
18466    /// of its own arrivals.
18467    ///
18468    /// Losses past the first return relayer cost the Exit nothing — the relayer has acknowledged, so
18469    /// the share is unlocked — and it asks at the lossless boundary with `Binomial(target, 1 − L)` of
18470    /// its packets having reached the Entry. A bar at their mean refused it about half the time, and
18471    /// at this split ~18 % of the time by more than the near-miss window, at once. The Exit's re-sends
18472    /// would since have caught the next one, but a bar that refuses a conforming Exit one time in five
18473    /// still costs it an interval of delay and a request per interval until its packets arrive.
18474    ///
18475    /// The draw is a reproduction of that at the surplus derived for `2048 × 64`: 159 028 of 319 693
18476    /// packets arrived, 777 short of the mean (an independent review's draw at the window of 256 was
18477    /// 391 short; the window is now twice as wide, so the fixture has to fall further short to be more
18478    /// than one window short).
18479    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18480    async fn an_honest_exit_at_the_tolerated_loss_is_not_refused_for_its_variance() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18481        use hopr_protocol_pix::{MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD, SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW, default_surplus_for};
18482
18483        // 319 693 independent fair bits: `sum(r.getrandbits(1) for _ in range(319_693))` with
18484        // `r = random.Random(60)`. (Seed 3 and 303 565 bits, 151 352 arrivals, at a window of 256.)
18485        const ARRIVED: u64 = 159_028;
18486
18487        let params = PixParams::try_new(2048, 64, default_surplus_for(2048, 64), LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
18488        assert_eq!(123, params.surplus_shares());
18489        assert!(
18490            IncomingSessionPixConfig::default()
18491                .quota_range
18492                .contains(&pix_params_to_quota(&params)),
18493            "the split must be one a default Exit accepts"
18494        );
18495
18496        let boundary = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(&params, MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD);
18497        assert_eq!(319_693, boundary);
18498
18499        // floor(μ − 4σ) for μ = 319 693 × (1 − L) = 159 805.20 and σ = 282.71, at
18500        // L = 0.500 129 201 488 385 6.
18501        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
18502        assert_eq!(158_674, required);
18503
18504        // What this pins: a bar at the mean would have refused the draw outright, never reaching the
18505        // near-miss wait, where the confidence bound admits it.
18506        let at_the_mean = (boundary as f64 * (1.0 - params.tolerated_share_loss())) as u64;
18507        assert_eq!(159_805, at_the_mean);
18508        assert!(
18509            ARRIVED + (SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64) < at_the_mean,
18510            "the draw must fall more than one emission window short of the mean, or a mean bar would have waited"
18511        );
18512        assert!(ARRIVED >= required, "the draw must clear the confidence bound");
18513
18514        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut events, sender, handle) =
18515            entry_with_pix_session(params, MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD).await?;
18516        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18517            pseudonym,
18518            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
18519        )
18520        .await?;
18521        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut events).await);
18522
18523        for n in 1..=boundary as u32 {
18524            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &n.to_be_bytes())?;
18525        }
18526
18527        // Every packet was acknowledged by the first relayer; the losses are downstream, so the Exit
18528        // asks at the boundary.
18529        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, ARRIVED);
18530        let result = mgr
18531            .handle_ssa_request(
18532                pseudonym,
18533                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18534            )
18535            .await;
18536
18537        sender.close_channel();
18538        handle.await??;
18539        result.context("honest Exit on a 50 % downstream-loss path lost its only successor request")?;
18540        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut events).await);
18541
18542        Ok(())
18543    }
18544
18545    /// A real Entry Session must advance the counter the successor gate reads.
18546    ///
18547    /// The gate's worst failure is not being too strict, it is being wired to a counter nothing
18548    /// feeds: that closes it permanently, and every PIX Session then dies on its second cycle with
18549    /// the Exit blaming its own commitment deadline. The other tests here drive
18550    /// `returned_packets` by hand, so none of them would notice.
18551    ///
18552    /// Deliberately built with `surb_management: None`. That is the branch which passed `session_rx`
18553    /// through untouched and left `surb_estimator` at its default — the one place where reusing the
18554    /// balancer's estimate instead of a counter of our own would have produced exactly that silent
18555    /// permanent closure.
18556    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18557    async fn returned_packets_are_counted_on_the_entry_receive_path() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18558        use hopr_protocol_start::StartProtocolDiscriminants;
18559
18560        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18561        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
18562
18563        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
18564        let bob_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
18565
18566        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
18567        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
18568
18569        // Alice → Bob, and Bob → Alice, with no filtering: the handshake is not what is under test.
18570        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
18571        alice_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
18572            let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
18573            Box::pin(async move {
18574                let _ = bob_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
18575                    alice_pseudonym,
18576                    ApplicationDataIn {
18577                        data: data.data,
18578                        packet_info: Default::default(),
18579                    },
18580                );
18581                Ok(())
18582            })
18583        });
18584        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
18585        bob_transport
18586            .expect_send_message()
18587            .withf(|_, data| msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished))
18588            .returning(move |_, data| {
18589                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
18590                Box::pin(async move {
18591                    alice_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
18592                        alice_pseudonym,
18593                        ApplicationDataIn {
18594                            data: data.data,
18595                            packet_info: Default::default(),
18596                        },
18597                    )?;
18598                    Ok(())
18599                })
18600            });
18601
18602        let (alice_sender, alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
18603        let (new_session_tx_alice, _alice_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
18604        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_alice, None, None)?;
18605
18606        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
18607        let (new_session_tx_bob, new_session_rx_bob) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
18608        bob_mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_bob, None, None)?;
18609        let _bob_notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
18610            pin_mut!(new_session_rx_bob);
18611            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx_bob.next().await {}
18612        });
18613
18614        let alice_session = alice_mgr
18615            .new_session(
18616                bob_peer,
18617                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
18618                SessionClientConfig {
18619                    pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
18620                    capabilities: None.into(),
18621                    surb_management: None,
18622                    ..Default::default()
18623                },
18624            )
18625            .await
18626            .context("the session must establish")?;
18627
18628        let counter = alice_mgr
18629            .sessions
18630            .get(&alice_pseudonym)
18631            .expect("alice must hold the session slot")
18632            .returned_packets;
18633        assert_eq!(
18634            0,
18635            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
18636            "nothing has come back yet"
18637        );
18638
18639        // Three packets arriving the way the Exit's return traffic does.
18640        for i in 0..3u8 {
18641            alice_mgr.dispatch_message(
18642                alice_pseudonym,
18643                ApplicationDataIn {
18644                    data: ApplicationData::new(SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG, &[i])?,
18645                    packet_info: Default::default(),
18646                },
18647            )?;
18648        }
18649
18650        // The count is taken as the Session drains its receiver, and the receiver is only polled by a
18651        // reader — which is exactly how it behaves in production, where the client is reading.
18652        let mut alice_session = alice_session;
18653        let mut buffer = [0u8; 16];
18654        for _ in 0..50 {
18655            if counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) >= 3 {
18656                break;
18657            }
18658            let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
18659                Duration::from_millis(20),
18660                futures::AsyncReadExt::read(&mut alice_session, &mut buffer),
18661            )
18662            .await;
18663        }
18664        assert_eq!(
18665            3,
18666            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
18667            "every Exit → Entry packet must be counted, or the successor gate can never open"
18668        );
18669
18670        drop(alice_session);
18671        alice_sender.close_channel();
18672        bob_sender.close_channel();
18673        let _ = alice_handle.await?;
18674        let _ = bob_handle.await?;
18675        Ok(())
18676    }
18677
18678    /// Re-points the fixture's slot at `Forward` routing, the way a real Entry's slot is built.
18679    ///
18680    /// [`entry_with_pix_session`] establishes through `handle_incoming_session_initiation` because
18681    /// that is the path which installs the PIX state the successor gate needs, and it stores the
18682    /// Exit's `Return` reply routing. The gate is an Entry-side rule, and the counter it reads is
18683    /// only credited on Sessions this node *initiated* — Start-protocol traffic on an incoming
18684    /// Session comes from the Entry over the forward path and must not be paid for. So the routing is
18685    /// what decides whether the keep-alives below are read as service arriving or as service being
18686    /// asked for, and the fixture has to be put on the side the rule is about.
18687    ///
18688    /// Re-inserting rather than mutating: the slot lives in a `moka` cache by value, and its routing
18689    /// is a plain field rather than a cell, because nothing in production ever changes it.
18690    fn make_session_outgoing<S>(mgr: &SessionManager<S>, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym, destination: Address)
18691    where
18692        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
18693        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
18694    {
18695        let mut slot = mgr.sessions.get(pseudonym).expect("session must exist");
18696        slot.routing_opts = DestinationRouting::Forward {
18697            destination: Box::new(destination.into()),
18698            pseudonym: Some(*pseudonym),
18699            forward_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(hopr_api::types::primitive::bounded::BoundedSize::MIN),
18700            return_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(hopr_api::types::primitive::bounded::BoundedSize::MIN).into(),
18701        };
18702        mgr.sessions.insert(*pseudonym, slot);
18703    }
18704
18705    /// A cycle served only by the Exit's keep-alives must still buy its successor.
18706    ///
18707    /// This is the property that lets the Exit finish a funded cycle whose application has fallen
18708    /// silent: it sends its own Exit → Entry keep-alives, each one consuming a return SURB and
18709    /// therefore unlocking one share, and the cycle completes on those alone. If they earned nothing
18710    /// at this gate the successor would be refused for as long as the Exit relied on them: the Exit's
18711    /// re-sends would be dropped as under-served until the cycle's emission ended, at which point the
18712    /// successor reaches the front, the re-sends stop, and the Session closes on `CommitmentTimeout`,
18713    /// naming a timer rather than the rule that fired.
18714    ///
18715    /// Driven through [`dispatch_message`](SessionManager::dispatch_message) with real encoded
18716    /// keep-alives rather than by touching the counter, because the credit lives on that path and
18717    /// nowhere else: the message never reaches `session_rx`, so the receive-path inspector that
18718    /// [`returned_packets_are_counted_on_the_entry_receive_path`] pins cannot cover for it.
18719    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18720    async fn keep_alives_alone_can_carry_a_cycle_to_its_successor() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18721        let params = wide_pix_params();
18722        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
18723            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
18724
18725        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18726            pseudonym,
18727            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
18728        )
18729        .await
18730        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
18731        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18732
18733        // Emission reaches the boundary, so service is the only thing left for the gate to weigh.
18734        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
18735            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
18736        }
18737
18738        make_session_outgoing(&mgr, &pseudonym, (&ChainKeypair::random()).into());
18739
18740        let counter = mgr
18741            .sessions
18742            .get(&pseudonym)
18743            .expect("session must exist")
18744            .returned_packets;
18745        assert_eq!(
18746            0,
18747            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
18748            "the fixture must start with nothing served"
18749        );
18750
18751        // Exactly what the gate demands, and every packet of it a keep-alive.
18752        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
18753        for level in 0..required {
18754            let keep_alive: ApplicationData = HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
18755                session_id: pseudonym,
18756                flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState.into(),
18757                additional_data: level,
18758            })
18759            .try_into()?;
18760            mgr.dispatch_message(
18761                pseudonym,
18762                ApplicationDataIn {
18763                    data: keep_alive,
18764                    packet_info: Default::default(),
18765                },
18766            )?;
18767        }
18768        assert_eq!(
18769            required,
18770            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
18771            "every keep-alive consumed a return SURB and must be credited as service"
18772        );
18773
18774        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18775            pseudonym,
18776            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
18777        )
18778        .await
18779        .context("a cycle served entirely by keep-alives must still buy its successor")?;
18780        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
18781
18782        bob_sender.close_channel();
18783        bob_handle.await??;
18784        Ok(())
18785    }
18786
18787    /// The Entry's half of the successor gate: a batch asked for before emission has reached the last
18788    /// cycle of the batch already committed must be refused, committing nothing and depositing
18789    /// nothing — and the Session must survive it.
18790    ///
18791    /// The Exit-side gate in `SessionPixSupervisor` means a correct peer never lands here. This is
18792    /// what makes a peer that *does* — an unpatched or hostile Exit answering every cycle's
18793    /// early-recovery signal with a fresh batch — cost the Entry nothing rather than one on-chain
18794    /// deposit per surplus request.
18795    ///
18796    /// Ordering across a batch is pinned where it lives, on the generator, by
18797    /// `emission_never_crosses_a_cycle_boundary_early` and
18798    /// `emission_progress_lags_the_commitment_index_across_a_batch`. What this test drives is the
18799    /// wiring and all three points of the gate: nothing emitted at all, emission having merely
18800    /// *reached* the last committed cycle, and emission far enough into it.
18801    ///
18802    /// The middle point is the regression. Admission used to be "emission has reached the last
18803    /// committed index", which becomes true on that cycle's very first share — so a successor batch
18804    /// was admitted ~0 % into the batch rather than the ~85 % at which a conforming Exit asks. See
18805    /// [`MIN_SUCCESSOR_EMISSION_FRACTION`].
18806    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18807    async fn entry_refuses_a_batch_asked_for_before_emission_reaches_the_current_one() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18808        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18809
18810        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
18811        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
18812
18813        const BATCH: u32 = 3;
18814
18815        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
18816            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
18817            threshold: 2,
18818            surplus_shares: 1,
18819        }));
18820        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
18821            generator.clone(),
18822            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
18823        );
18824        // This manager plays both halves, so its own Exit side opens a cycle and blocks on the
18825        // deposit pool. Answered on the way through; the deposits this test counts pass on unchanged.
18826        let mut pix_events = crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events, |_| Vec::new());
18827
18828        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
18829            max_ssas_per_ssa_request: BATCH as usize,
18830            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
18831                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
18832                ..Default::default()
18833            },
18834            ..Default::default()
18835        });
18836
18837        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
18838        bob_transport
18839            .expect_send_message()
18840            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
18841
18842        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
18843        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
18844        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
18845            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
18846            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
18847        });
18848        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
18849
18850        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18851        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
18852            pseudonym,
18853            StartInitiation {
18854                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
18855                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
18856                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
18857                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
18858            },
18859        )
18860        .await?;
18861
18862        let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
18863            .expect("identity element must be valid");
18864        let batch = |from: u32| {
18865            (from..from + BATCH)
18866                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
18867                .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>()
18868        };
18869
18870        // The opening batch is accepted: nothing is committed yet, so there is nothing to be early for.
18871        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18872            pseudonym,
18873            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(1), []),
18874        )
18875        .await
18876        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
18877        assert_eq!(
18878            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
18879            BATCH as usize,
18880            "the opening batch must yield one deposit address per SSA"
18881        );
18882
18883        // Fully served for the batch, so emission ordering is the only thing under test here. The
18884        // returned-data half of the gate has its own tests.
18885        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required_returned_packets(&small_pix_params(), BATCH));
18886
18887        // Asking again before a single share has gone out is a whole batch early.
18888        let err = mgr
18889            .handle_ssa_request(
18890                pseudonym,
18891                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(BATCH + 1), []),
18892            )
18893            .await
18894            .expect_err("a batch asked for before any share was emitted must be refused");
18895        assert!(
18896            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
18897            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
18898        );
18899        assert_eq!(
18900            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
18901            0,
18902            "a refused batch must not emit a single ReadyToDeposit"
18903        );
18904        assert_eq!(
18905            mgr.active_sessions(),
18906            vec![pseudonym],
18907            "refusing a request must not close the Session"
18908        );
18909
18910        // Emit until the last cycle of the batch has taken the front — but no further.
18911        let mut sent = 0u32;
18912        let mut emit_until = |pred: &dyn Fn(&hopr_protocol_pix::EmissionProgress) -> bool| -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18913            for _ in 0..1024 {
18914                if generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).as_ref().is_some_and(pred) {
18915                    return Ok(());
18916                }
18917                sent += 1;
18918                generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
18919            }
18920            anyhow::bail!("emission did not reach the expected point")
18921        };
18922        emit_until(&|p| p.is_serving_last_committed())?;
18923
18924        // The boundary the gate actually uses, recomputed from the same negotiated params.
18925        let min_emitted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
18926            &small_pix_params(),
18927            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
18928        );
18929
18930        // Reaching the last cycle is *not* enough, and this is the H2 regression. The index-only gate
18931        // this replaced admitted a successor batch right here — on the last cycle's first share, ~0 %
18932        // of the way through the batch — which is nearly a whole cycle of deposits the Exit has not
18933        // earned, on the one gate whose purpose is to prevent exactly that.
18934        let progress = generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).expect("committed");
18935        assert!(
18936            progress.front_emitted < min_emitted,
18937            "the test must stand at the start of the last cycle, got {} of {min_emitted}",
18938            progress.front_emitted
18939        );
18940        let err = mgr
18941            .handle_ssa_request(
18942                pseudonym,
18943                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(BATCH + 1), []),
18944            )
18945            .await
18946            .expect_err("reaching the last cycle must not by itself admit the next batch");
18947        assert!(
18948            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
18949            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
18950        );
18951        assert_eq!(
18952            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
18953            0,
18954            "a batch refused for being early must not emit a single ReadyToDeposit"
18955        );
18956
18957        // Far enough into that last cycle, the same batch is admitted.
18958        emit_until(&|p| p.front_emitted >= min_emitted)?;
18959        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
18960            pseudonym,
18961            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(BATCH + 1), []),
18962        )
18963        .await
18964        .context("a batch asked for on time must be accepted")?;
18965
18966        bob_sender.close_channel();
18967        bob_handle.await??;
18968        Ok(())
18969    }
18970
18971    /// How many `SsaCommit` messages the fixture's transport has been given, once that has stopped
18972    /// changing.
18973    ///
18974    /// The count lags the handler by a channel hop to the forwarding task, so a read straight after a
18975    /// call can miss the burst that call sent. Waiting for it to hold still is the cheap way to know
18976    /// the read is the whole of it.
18977    async fn settled_commit_count(wire: &WireRecord) -> usize {
18978        let mut last = wire.count(StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit);
18979        for _ in 0..80 {
18980            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)).await;
18981            let now = wire.count(StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit);
18982            if now == last {
18983                return now;
18984            }
18985            last = now;
18986        }
18987        last
18988    }
18989
18990    /// Gets a fixture's Exit-side bookkeeping out of the way: the whole of cycle one emitted, and the
18991    /// Exit credited with the service the successor gate asks of it.
18992    fn serve_the_opening_cycle<S>(
18993        mgr: &SessionManager<S>,
18994        generator: &SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>,
18995        pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym,
18996        params: &PixParams,
18997    ) -> anyhow::Result<()>
18998    where
18999        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
19000        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
19001    {
19002        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
19003            generator.next_share(pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
19004        }
19005        credit_returned_packets(mgr, pseudonym, required_returned_packets(params, 1));
19006        Ok(())
19007    }

19009    /// The Exit re-sends an unanswered successor request, so the Entry has to answer the re-sends of
19010    /// one it has already admitted with nothing at all.
19011    ///
19012    /// Once the first copy is admitted the Entry spends a fraction of a second per cycle at the
19013    /// deployed dimensions (longer for wide dimensions or a full batch) generating its commitment, and
19014    /// then publishing it, and every re-send already in flight lands on a watermark that is at or above
19015    /// the index it names. Answering one of them with a second commitment would announce a second
19016    /// deposit address for the same quota and burst the same polynomials again; answering it with a
19017    /// refusal would log a fault, per re-send, for a request that was served. A repeat names the batch
19018    /// committed last, which is what tells it apart from a stale one.
19019    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19020    async fn a_repeat_of_the_committed_successor_is_a_no_op() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19021        let params = wide_pix_params();
19022        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19023        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) = entry_with_recorded_pix_session(
19024            params,
19025            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
19026            wire.clone(),
19027        )
19028        .await?;
19029
19030        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19031            pseudonym,
19032            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19033        )
19034        .await
19035        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
19036        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19037        let after_opening = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
19038        assert!(
19039            after_opening > 0,
19040            "the opening batch must have sent its commitment burst"
19041        );
19042
19043        // The opening batch is a repeat of itself too: nothing special-cases it.
19044        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19045            pseudonym,
19046            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19047        )
19048        .await
19049        .context("a repeat of the opening batch must be accepted without effect")?;
19050        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19051        assert_eq!(after_opening, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19052
19053        serve_the_opening_cycle(&mgr, &generator, &pseudonym, &params)?;
19054        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19055            pseudonym,
19056            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
19057        )
19058        .await
19059        .context("the successor must be admitted once it has been earned")?;
19060        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19061        let after_successor = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
19062        assert!(
19063            after_successor > after_opening,
19064            "the successor must have sent a burst of its own"
19065        );
19066
19067        for resend in 1..=3 {
19068            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19069                pseudonym,
19070                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
19071            )
19072            .await
19073            .with_context(|| format!("re-send {resend} of the admitted successor must succeed"))?;
19074        }
19075        assert_eq!(
19076            0,
19077            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
19078            "a repeat must not announce a second deposit for the same cycle"
19079        );
19080        assert_eq!(
19081            after_successor,
19082            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
19083            "a repeat must not burst the same commitment again"
19084        );
19085        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and must not cost the Session");
19086
19087        bob_sender.close_channel();
19088        bob_handle.await??;
19089        Ok(())
19090    }
19091
19092    /// A request for indices the Session has already committed past, and that are not the batch it
19093    /// committed last, is dropped — quietly, and without costing the Session or committing anything.
19094    ///
19095    /// It is not `refuse_ssa_request`, which closes both halves: the worst such a request can be is an
19096    /// Exit that lost track of what it asked for, and the Exit's own deadlines already end that. The
19097    /// repeat of the batch actually committed to must still be recognised afterwards.
19098    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19099    async fn a_stale_request_is_dropped_without_effect() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19100        let params = wide_pix_params();
19101        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19102        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) = entry_with_recorded_pix_session(
19103            params,
19104            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
19105            wire.clone(),
19106        )
19107        .await?;
19108
19109        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19110            pseudonym,
19111            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19112        )
19113        .await
19114        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
19115        serve_the_opening_cycle(&mgr, &generator, &pseudonym, &params)?;
19116        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19117            pseudonym,
19118            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
19119        )
19120        .await
19121        .context("the successor must be admitted once it has been earned")?;
19122        assert_eq!(2, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19123        let committed = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
19124
19125        let err = mgr
19126            .handle_ssa_request(
19127                pseudonym,
19128                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19129            )
19130            .await
19131            .expect_err("a request for an index below the last committed batch must not be served");
19132        assert!(
19133            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
19134            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
19135        );
19136        assert_eq!(
19137            0,
19138            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
19139            "a stale request must not announce a deposit"
19140        );
19141        assert_eq!(committed, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "or send a commitment");
19142        assert_eq!(
19143            vec![pseudonym],
19144            mgr.active_sessions(),
19145            "a stale request is dropped, not fatal"
19146        );
19147
19148        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19149            pseudonym,
19150            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
19151        )
19152        .await
19153        .context("the batch actually committed to is still recognised as a repeat after a stale request")?;
19154        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19155
19156        bob_sender.close_channel();
19157        bob_handle.await??;
19158        Ok(())
19159    }

19167    /// How many `SsaCommit` messages one cycle's commitment burst is.
19168    fn burst_len(pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym, params: &PixParams) -> anyhow::Result<usize> {
19169        let chunking = HoprStartProtocol::ssa_commit_chunking(pseudonym)?;

19173    /// What `ReadyToDeposit` events a fixture's PIX stream has ready.
19174    ///
19175    /// [`drain_pix_events`], keeping the deposits rather than counting them, for the tests whose
19176    /// subject is *which* announcement was made and not only how many.
19177    async fn drain_deposits(
19178        events: &mut (dyn futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin),
19179    ) -> Vec<AgreedSsaQuota> {
19180        let mut seen = Vec::new();
19181        while let Ok(Some(event)) = timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), events.next()).await {
19182            if let HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit(quota) = event {
19183                seen.push(quota);
19184            }
19185        }
19186        seen
19187    }

19189    /// Why [`FlakySender`] refused a message.
19190    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
19191    struct InjectedSendFailure;
19192
19193    impl std::fmt::Display for InjectedSendFailure {
19194        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
19195            f.write_str("injected send failure")
19196        }
19197    }
19198
19199    impl std::error::Error for InjectedSendFailure {}
19200
19201    /// How many more `SsaCommit` messages a [`FlakySender`] lets through before it refuses the rest.
19202    ///
19203    /// Only commitment messages are counted: the Exit half of the same manager sends other traffic
19204    /// through the same sender, and a keep-alive spending the budget would move the point at which a
19205    /// burst is cut.
19206    #[derive(Clone)]
19207    struct SendBudget {
19208        allowed: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
19209        /// Commitment messages refused before `allowed` is consulted at all.
19210        refusals: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
19211    }
19212
19213    impl SendBudget {
19214        fn unlimited() -> Self {
19215            Self {
19216                allowed: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX)),
19217                refusals: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),
19218            }
19219        }
19220
19221        /// Lets `sends` more commitment messages through, then refuses every one.
19222        fn allow(&self, sends: u64) {
19223            self.allowed.store(sends, Ordering::SeqCst);
19224        }
19225
19226        /// Ends the failure: every send is let through again.
19227        fn restore(&self) {
19228            self.allow(u64::MAX);
19229        }
19230
19231        /// Refuses the next `sends` commitment messages, and goes back to [`allow`](Self::allow)'s
19232        /// budget after them: a transport that gives up once and then recovers.
19233        fn refuse_next(&self, sends: u64) {
19234            self.refusals.store(sends, Ordering::SeqCst);
19235        }
19236
19237        fn take(&self) -> bool {
19238            if self
19239                .refusals
19240                .fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |left| left.checked_sub(1))
19241                .is_ok()
19242            {
19243                return false;
19244            }
19245            self.allowed
19246                .fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |left| {
19247                    if left == u64::MAX {
19248                        Some(left)
19249                    } else {
19250                        left.checked_sub(1)
19251                    }
19252                })
19253                .is_ok()
19254        }
19255    }
19256
19257    /// A transport that fails on demand and recovers.
19258    ///
19259    /// A channel sender can only fail by being closed, for good. The failure the Entry's publication
19260    /// has to survive is a send that gives up under backpressure — and the next one succeeds.
19261    #[derive(Clone)]
19262    struct FlakySender {
19263        inner: UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
19264        budget: SendBudget,
19265    }
19266
19267    impl futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> for FlakySender {
19268        type Error = InjectedSendFailure;
19269
19270        fn poll_ready(
19271            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
19272            cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
19273        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
19274            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
19275                .poll_ready(cx)
19276                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
19277        }
19278
19279        fn start_send(
19280            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
19281            item: (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut),
19282        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
19283            if crate::testing::msg_type(&item.1, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit) && !self.budget.take() {
19284                return Err(InjectedSendFailure);
19285            }
19286            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
19287                .start_send(item)
19288                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
19289        }
19290
19291        fn poll_flush(
19292            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
19293            cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
19294        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
19295            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
19296                .poll_flush(cx)
19297                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
19298        }
19299
19300        fn poll_close(
19301            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
19302            cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
19303        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
19304            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
19305                .poll_close(cx)
19306                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
19307        }
19308    }
19309
19310    /// [`entry_with_recorded_pix_session`], over a [`FlakySender`] whose failures the test controls.
19311    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
19312    async fn flaky_entry(
19313        params: PixParams,
19314        wire: Arc<WireRecord>,
19315    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
19316        SessionManager<FlakySender>,
19317        Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
19318        HoprPseudonym,
19319        impl futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin,
19320        SendBudget,
19321        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
19322        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
19323    )> {
19324        let budget = SendBudget::unlimited();
19325        let wrapped = budget.clone();
19326        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, events, sender, handle) = entry_with_wrapped_sender(
19327            params,
19328            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
19329            wire,
19330            move |inner| FlakySender { inner, budget: wrapped },
19331        )
19332        .await?;
19333        Ok((mgr, generator, pseudonym, events, budget, sender, handle))
19334    }

19336    /// The members the Session still owes a publication, ascending.

19338    where
19339        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,

19347            .unpublished_indices())

19350    /// What `ReadyToDeposit` is still owed for `index`, as it was fixed when the cycle was staged.
19351    fn owed_announcement<S>(
19352        mgr: &SessionManager<S>,
19353        pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym,
19354        index: u32,
19355    ) -> anyhow::Result<AgreedSsaQuota>
19356    where
19357        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
19358        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
19359    {
19360        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
19361        slot.current_ssa_state
19362            .get()
19363            .context("a PIX session has SSA state")?
19364            .unpublished
19365            .lock()
19366            .members
19367            .get(&SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero")?)
19368            .cloned()

19372    /// A scoped re-request for the first `polys` polynomials of cycle `index`, as the Exit's own
19373    /// commitment timer would send it.
19374    fn rerequest(
19375        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
19376        params: PixParams,
19377        index: u32,
19378        polys: u16,
19379    ) -> SsaServerCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixDepositPayload> {
19380        SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(
19381            pseudonym,
19382            params,
19383            [(SsaIndex::new(index).expect("non-zero"), vec![(0u16, polys - 1)])],
19384        )

19387    /// The publication of a batch can be cut short by the transport, and a repeat of the request
19388    /// finishes it: one full burst and one announcement, then nothing more.
19389    ///
19390    /// The generator has moved by the time a commitment is published, and a transport that fails then
19391    /// leaves a watermark and a polynomial queue behind a request that reported an error. The Exit
19392    /// re-sends it all the same. Read as stale, every re-send would be logged as a fault; answered with
19393    /// a silent success, the cycle would never be announced — the Entry's upper layer would never be
19394    /// told to fund an address the Exit is waiting on — and the Exit would close on its deposit
19395    /// timeout. So the batch is recorded as the last one committed once it is staged, not once it is
19396    /// published, and what is still owed is kept until it has been.
19397    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19398    async fn a_repeat_resumes_a_publication_whose_first_send_failed() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19399        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19400        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19401        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19402            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19403        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
19404        assert!(burst >= 3, "the fixture needs a burst of several messages, got {burst}");
19405        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
19406
19407        // The transport refuses the very first message of the burst.
19408        sends.allow(0);
19409        let failure = mgr
19410            .handle_ssa_request(
19411                pseudonym,
19412                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19413            )
19414            .await
19415            .expect_err("a burst that cannot be sent must fail the request");
19416        assert!(
19417            is_a_cut_short_publication(&failure),
19418            "the gate admitted this request, so the failure is the transport's — reported as the non-fatal refusal, \
19419             not as a fault the dispatcher logs at `error!`, got {failure:?}"
19420        );
19421        assert_eq!(
19422            Some(SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?),
19423            mgr.sessions
19424                .get(&pseudonym)
19425                .context("session must exist")?
19426                .current_ssa_state
19427                .get()
19428                .and_then(SessionSsaState::committed_watermark),
19429            "the generator moved, so the watermark did too"
19430        );
19431        assert_eq!(vec![SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?);
19432        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "nothing was announced");
19433        assert_eq!(before, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "and nothing was sent");
19434        let staged = owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1)?;
19435
19436        // The transport recovers, and the Exit's re-send of the same request lands.
19437        sends.restore();
19438        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19439            pseudonym,
19440            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19441        )
19442        .await
19443        .context("a repeat of a request whose publication was cut short must finish it")?;
19444        assert_eq!(
19445            vec![staged],
19446            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events).await,
19447            "exactly one announcement, carrying what was fixed when the cycle was staged"
19448        );
19449        assert_eq!(
19450            before + burst,
19451            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
19452            "and exactly one full burst"
19453        );
19454        assert!(owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty());
19455
19456        // Now it is published, so a further repeat is the no-op it always was.
19457        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19458            pseudonym,
19459            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19460        )
19461        .await
19462        .context("a repeat of a published batch must succeed")?;
19463        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19464        assert_eq!(before + burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19465
19466        bob_sender.close_channel();
19467        bob_handle.await??;
19468        Ok(())
19469    }
19470
19471    /// A batch cut short part-way is finished from where it stopped: members already published are
19472    /// left alone, and the one that was cut is re-published whole.
19473    ///
19474    /// The request repeated here is the whole batch, as a conforming Exit sends it: it re-sends the
19475    /// batch, whole and unchanged, for as long as any member has reported nothing, including the ones
19476    /// whose commitment it already has.
19477    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19478    async fn a_resumed_batch_publishes_only_the_members_still_owed() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19479        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19480        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19481        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19482            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19483        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
19484        let batch = |first: u32| -> std::collections::BTreeMap<SsaIndex, HoprPixGroupElement> {
19485            let mut members = ssa_request_for(first);
19486            members.extend(ssa_request_for(first + 1));
19487            members
19488        };
19489
19490        // The first member goes out whole; the second is cut after one message.
19491        sends.allow(burst as u64 + 1);
19492        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19493            pseudonym,
19494            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch(1), []),
19495        )
19496        .await
19497        .expect_err("a batch whose second burst is cut must fail the request");
19498        assert_eq!(
19499            vec![SsaIndex::new(2).context("non-zero")?],
19500            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?,
19501            "the first member is published, the second is owed"
19502        );
19503        assert_eq!(
19504            vec![1],
19505            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events)
19506                .await
19507                .iter()
19508                .map(|quota| quota.ssa_id.ssa_index().get())
19509                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
19510            "only the member whose burst completed was announced"
19511        );
19512        assert_eq!(burst + 1, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19513
19514        sends.restore();
19515        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19516            pseudonym,
19517            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch(1), []),
19518        )
19519        .await
19520        .context("the repeat must finish the batch")?;
19521        assert_eq!(
19522            vec![2],
19523            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events)
19524                .await
19525                .iter()
19526                .map(|quota| quota.ssa_id.ssa_index().get())
19527                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
19528            "the resumption announces the member that was owed, and not the one already published"
19529        );
19530        assert_eq!(
19531            burst + 1 + burst,
19532            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
19533            "one full burst more, for that member alone"
19534        );
19535
19536        bob_sender.close_channel();
19537        bob_handle.await??;
19538        Ok(())
19539    }

19541    /// A batch cut at its first member stays owed in full, and a resumption publishes it in order.
19542    ///
19543    /// The member that failed is put back and the ones after it were never claimed, so all of them
19544    /// are still there. Handing the first back must not depend on the second being absent.
19545    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19546    async fn a_batch_cut_at_its_first_member_stays_owed_in_full() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19547        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19548        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19549        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19550            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19551        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
19552        let mut batch = ssa_request_for(1);
19553        batch.extend(ssa_request_for(2));
19554        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch.clone(), []);
19555
19556        sends.allow(0);
19557        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19558            .await
19559            .expect_err("a batch whose first burst is refused must fail the request");
19560        assert_eq!(
19561            vec![
19562                SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?,
19563                SsaIndex::new(2).context("non-zero")?
19564            ],
19565            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?,
19566            "the member that failed was put back and the one after it was never claimed"
19567        );
19568        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19569        let staged = [
19570            owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1)?,
19571            owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 2)?,
19572        ];
19573
19574        sends.restore();
19575        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19576            .await
19577            .context("the repeat must finish the whole batch")?;
19578        assert_eq!(
19579            staged.to_vec(),
19580            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events).await,
19581            "both members are announced, in ascending order, each once"
19582        );
19583        assert_eq!(2 * burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "one full burst each");
19584        assert!(owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty());
19585
19586        bob_sender.close_channel();
19587        bob_handle.await??;
19588        Ok(())
19589    }

19617        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
19618            .await
19619            .context("a re-request for a cycle cut short must be answered")?;

19621            vec![staged],

19623            "exactly one announcement for the cycle nobody had been told to fund"

19626            before + 1 + burst,

19629        );

19674    /// A resumption the transport cuts short does not hold up the rest of the re-request that
19675    /// prompted it.
19676    ///
19677    /// A re-request can name a cycle whose publication was cut short beside one that was published in
19678    /// full. The first is answered by resuming the batch and the second by its scoped parts, and the
19679    /// two are separate repairs. Returning on the resumption's failure left the second one waiting a
19680    /// whole re-request interval on the first.
19681    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19682    async fn a_cut_short_resumption_does_not_hold_up_the_rest_of_a_rerequest() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19683        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19684        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19685        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19686            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19687        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
19688        let mut batch = ssa_request_for(1);
19689        batch.extend(ssa_request_for(2));
19690        let (first, second) = (
19691            SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?,
19692            SsaIndex::new(2).context("non-zero")?,
19693        );
19694
19695        // The first member goes out whole; the second is cut after one message.
19696        sends.allow(burst as u64 + 1);
19697        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch, []))
19698            .await
19699            .expect_err("a batch whose second burst is cut must fail the request");
19700        assert_eq!(vec![second], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?);
19701        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19702        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
19703        sends.restore();
19704
19705        // The Exit asks for ten polynomials of each. The transport gives up on the first message of
19706        // the resumption and recovers straight after.
19707        sends.refuse_next(1);
19708        let failure = mgr
19709            .handle_ssa_request(
19710                pseudonym,
19711                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(
19712                    pseudonym,
19713                    params,
19714                    [(first, vec![(0u16, 9)]), (second, vec![(0u16, 9)])],
19715                ),
19716            )
19717            .await
19718            .expect_err("the resumption that was cut short is still reported");
19719        assert!(
19720            is_a_cut_short_publication(&failure),
19721            "reported as the non-fatal refusal, got {failure:?}"
19722        );
19723        assert_eq!(
19724            before + 1,
19725            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
19726            "the published cycle's ten polynomials went out all the same, in one message"
19727        );
19728        assert_eq!(vec![second], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?, "and the cut cycle stays owed");
19729        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "nothing was announced");
19730
19731        bob_sender.close_channel();
19732        bob_handle.await??;
19733        Ok(())
19734    }

19736    /// Moves the moment the Session's last batch went out back by a whole
19737    /// [`SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE`], as if the repeat about to be handled were arriving that much later.
19738    fn backdate_last_sent<S>(mgr: &SessionManager<S>, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym) -> anyhow::Result<()>
19739    where
19740        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
19741        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
19742    {
19743        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
19744        let state = slot.current_ssa_state.get().context("a PIX session has SSA state")?;
19745        let mut unpublished = state.unpublished.lock();
19746        let sent = unpublished.last_sent.context("the batch must have gone out")?;
19747        unpublished.last_sent = Some(
19748            sent.checked_sub(SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE)
19749                .context("the clock must reach back a grace")?,
19750        );
19751        Ok(())
19752    }
19753
19754    /// A repeat that arrives long after the batch went out in full has its bursts sent again, and
19755    /// nothing announced.
19756    ///
19757    /// Publishing a burst only means the local transport took it. If a relayer on the forward path
19758    /// dies, all of it can be lost, and then the Exit holds no part it could name in a scoped
19759    /// re-request. Its repeat is the only prompt left. A repeat that arrives within the grace may have
19760    /// crossed the burst and gets nothing, which is what keeps the ordinary in-flight repeats from
19761    /// costing a retransmission each.
19762    ///
19763    /// The opening batch stands in for a successor here. Nothing on the Entry tells them apart, and it
19764    /// spares the test serving a cycle first.
19765    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19766    async fn a_late_repeat_sends_the_published_bursts_again_without_announcing_them() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19767        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19768        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19769        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19770            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19771        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
19772        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []);
19773
19774        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19775            .await
19776            .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
19777        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19778        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19779
19780        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19781            .await
19782            .context("a repeat inside the grace must succeed")?;
19783        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "and send nothing");
19784
19785        backdate_last_sent(&mgr, &pseudonym)?;
19786        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19787            .await
19788            .context("a late repeat must be answered")?;
19789        assert_eq!(
19790            2 * burst,
19791            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
19792            "with the whole burst again"
19793        );
19794        assert_eq!(
19795            0,
19796            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
19797            "and no second announcement for the same cycle"
19798        );
19799
19800        // The re-send starts the grace over, so the repeats that crossed it get nothing.
19801        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19802            .await
19803            .context("a repeat right after a re-send must succeed")?;
19804        assert_eq!(2 * burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19805
19806        // A re-send the transport cuts short is not fatal, and also starts the grace over, so a
19807        // congested transport is not handed a burst on every repeat.
19808        backdate_last_sent(&mgr, &pseudonym)?;
19809        sends.allow(1);
19810        let failure = mgr
19811            .handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19812            .await
19813            .expect_err("a re-send that cannot get out must fail the request");
19814        assert!(
19815            matches!(
19816                failure,
19817                TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))
19818            ),
19819            "reported as the non-fatal refusal, got {failure:?}"
19820        );
19821        sends.restore();
19822        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19823            .await
19824            .context("a repeat right after a failed re-send must succeed")?;
19825        assert_eq!(2 * burst + 1, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19826        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19827        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session lives");
19828
19829        bob_sender.close_channel();
19830        bob_handle.await??;
19831        Ok(())
19832    }

19834    /// A lost burst whose cycle has no retransmissions left is given up on, once.
19835    ///
19836    /// The re-send of a published burst draws on the same per-cycle budget as a scoped re-request, so
19837    /// a peer cannot farm whole bursts out of this node by repeating its request. Once that budget is
19838    /// spent the generator refuses, and the cycle stops counting as announced, so the repeats after it
19839    /// do not even ask.
19840    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19841    async fn a_lost_burst_with_no_retransmissions_left_is_given_up_on() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19842        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19843        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19844        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, _sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19845            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19846        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
19847        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []);
19848
19849        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19850            .await
19851            .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
19852        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19853        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19854
19855        for _ in 0..hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS {
19856            generator.recommit(&pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?, [(0, 0)])?;
19857        }
19858
19859        backdate_last_sent(&mgr, &pseudonym)?;
19860        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
19861            .await
19862            .context("a spent cycle is given up on, which is not a failure of the request")?;
19863        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "nothing was sent");
19864        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "and nothing announced");
19865        assert!(
19866            mgr.sessions
19867                .get(&pseudonym)
19868                .context("session must exist")?
19869                .current_ssa_state
19870                .get()
19871                .context("a PIX session has SSA state")?
19872                .unpublished
19873                .lock()
19874                .announced
19875                .is_empty(),
19876            "the cycle is no longer one a late repeat sends again"
19877        );
19878        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session lives");
19879
19880        bob_sender.close_channel();
19881        bob_handle.await??;
19882        Ok(())
19883    }

19885    /// Once a cycle has used up its retransmissions it can never be published again, so it is dropped.
19886    ///
19887    /// Resuming spends one of a cycle's [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`] answers, and that cap is
19888    /// what keeps a peer from farming whole bursts out of this node by re-sending a request. Spent, the
19889    /// generator refuses and nothing is sent or announced. Keeping the member owed would only make
19890    /// every later re-send pay a blocking `recommit` and a log line for the same refusal, so it is
19891    /// dropped from the owed set instead, and the repeats after it are plain no-ops.
19892    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19893    async fn a_cycle_with_no_retransmissions_left_is_dropped_and_later_repeats_are_no_ops() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19894        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
19895        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
19896        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
19897            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
19898        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
19899
19900        sends.allow(0);
19901        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19902            pseudonym,
19903            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19904        )
19905        .await
19906        .expect_err("a burst that cannot be sent must fail the request");
19907        sends.restore();
19908
19909        let index = SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?;
19910        for _ in 0..hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS {
19911            generator.recommit(&pseudonym, index, [(0, 0)])?;
19912        }
19913        assert_eq!(vec![index], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?, "still owed until someone tries");
19914
19915        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19916            pseudonym,
19917            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19918        )
19919        .await
19920        .context("a spent cycle is given up on, which is not a failure of the request")?;
19921        assert!(
19922            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty(),
19923            "the cycle can never be published, so it is no longer owed"
19924        );
19925        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "it was never announced");
19926        assert_eq!(before, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "and nothing was sent for it");
19927
19928        for _ in 0..3 {
19929            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
19930                pseudonym,
19931                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
19932            )
19933            .await
19934            .context("later repeats are plain no-ops")?;
19935        }
19936        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19937        assert_eq!(before, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
19938
19939        // A re-request for it is scoped like any other, and the generator refuses it the same way.
19940        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
19941            .await
19942            .expect_err("the spent cycle has nothing left to re-send");
19943        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
19944        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session lives");
19945
19946        bob_sender.close_channel();
19947        bob_handle.await??;
19948        Ok(())
19949    }
