19994    /// A member the generator retains nothing for is dropped too, with nothing sent.
19995    ///
19996    /// The retained material is what a resumption rebuilds the burst from. When it is gone — pushed out
19997    /// by newer cycles — nothing will bring it back, and `recommit` says so with a different error from
19998    /// the spent-cap one.
19999    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20000    async fn a_member_with_nothing_retained_is_dropped_and_nothing_is_sent() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20001        let params = small_pix_params();
20002        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20003        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::<HoprPixSpec>::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
20004            polynomials_per_ssa: params.polys_per_ssa(),
20005            threshold: params.shares_per_poly(),
20006            surplus_shares: params.surplus_shares(),
20007        }));
20008        let (toolbox, _events) = PixToolbox::new(
20009            generator,
20010            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
20011        );
20012        let state = SessionSsaState::new(params);
20013        state.stage_unpublished([owed_quota(pseudonym, 1)?, owed_quota(pseudonym, 2)?]);
20014
20015        let (mut sender, mut sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>();
20016        resume_publication(
20017            pseudonym,
20018            pseudonym,
20019            &DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()),
20020            &state,
20021            &toolbox,
20022            &mut sender,
20023        )
20024        .await
20025        .context("members that can never be published are given up on, which is not a failure")?;
20026
20027        assert!(state.unpublished_indices().is_empty(), "neither stays owed");
20028        assert!(sent.try_recv().is_err(), "and nothing went on the wire");
20029        Ok(())
20030    }
20031
20032    /// A resumption that fails again is the same non-fatal refusal on every path, and leaves the cycle owed.
20033    ///
20034    /// Reached by a repeat of the request and by a scoped re-request alike. The dispatcher logs
20035    /// `NotAdmitted` at `debug!`, so a raw transport error from either path would have been an `error!`
20036    /// per attempt for something the Exit retries on its own.
20037    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20038    async fn a_resumption_cut_short_again_is_not_fatal_on_either_path() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20039        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
20040        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
20041        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
20042            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
20043        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
20044        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
20045        let index = SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?;
20046
20047        sends.allow(1);
20048        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20049            pseudonym,
20050            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20051        )
20052        .await
20053        .expect_err("a burst cut after one message must fail the request");
20054
20055        // The transport is still refusing, so each resumption is cut after nothing at all.
20056        sends.allow(0);
20057        let by_repeat = mgr
20058            .handle_ssa_request(
20059                pseudonym,
20060                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20061            )
20062            .await
20063            .expect_err("a repeat that cannot be published must not report success");
20064        assert!(is_a_cut_short_publication(&by_repeat), "got {by_repeat:?}");
20065        let by_rerequest = mgr
20066            .handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
20067            .await
20068            .expect_err("a re-request that cannot be published must not report success");
20069        assert!(is_a_cut_short_publication(&by_rerequest), "got {by_rerequest:?}");
20070        assert_eq!(
20071            vec![index],
20072            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?,
20073            "the cycle stays owed through both"
20074        );
20075        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
20076        assert_eq!(
20077            before + 1,
20078            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
20079            "only the first message ever got out"
20080        );
20081
20082        // And it is still finished once the transport is back.
20083        sends.restore();
20084        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
20085            .await
20086            .context("the next re-request finishes it")?;
20087        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
20088        assert_eq!(before + 1 + burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
20089
20090        bob_sender.close_channel();
20091        bob_handle.await??;
20092        Ok(())
20093    }
20094
20095    /// A member somebody else has claimed is not published by a second resumer.
20096    ///
20097    /// The scoped re-request path does not take the per-pseudonym request lock, so it can run beside
20098    /// the original publication or another resumption. The claim is what keeps them from announcing a
20099    /// deposit twice: whoever removes a member from the owed set is its publisher, and nobody else.
20100    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20101    async fn a_claimed_member_is_not_published_by_a_second_resumer() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20102        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
20103        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
20104        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
20105            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
20106        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
20107        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
20108
20109        sends.allow(0);
20110        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20111            pseudonym,
20112            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20113        )
20114        .await
20115        .expect_err("a burst that cannot be sent must fail the request");
20116        sends.restore();
20117
20118        // Another resumer is part-way through the cycle.
20119        let index = SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?;
20120        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
20121        let state = slot.current_ssa_state.get().context("a PIX session has SSA state")?;
20122        let claimed = state
20123            .claim_unpublished(index)
20124            .context("the cycle must be owed to be claimed")?;
20125
20126        // Neither a repeat nor a re-request may publish or announce it meanwhile.
20127        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20128            pseudonym,
20129            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20130        )
20131        .await
20132        .context("a repeat of a batch that is being published is not a fault")?;
20133        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
20134            .await
20135            .context("a re-request of a cycle that is being published is answered as a published one")?;
20136        assert_eq!(
20137            0,
20138            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
20139            "a second resumer must not announce the claimed member"
20140        );
20141        assert!(
20142            settled_commit_count(&wire).await <= before + 1,
20143            "nor send its burst: at most the scoped message of the re-request went out"
20144        );
20145        assert!(
20146            state.claim_unpublished(index).is_none(),
20147            "a claimed member cannot be claimed twice"
20148        );
20149
20150        // The claimant fails and hands it back; now one resumption publishes it, once.
20151        state.restore_unpublished(claimed);
20152        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20153            pseudonym,
20154            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20155        )
20156        .await
20157        .context("the repeat must finish the publication that was handed back")?;
20158        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20159            pseudonym,
20160            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20161        )
20162        .await?;
20163        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "announced exactly once");
20164        assert!(settled_commit_count(&wire).await >= before + burst);
20165
20166        bob_sender.close_channel();
20167        bob_handle.await??;
20168        Ok(())
20169    }
20170
20171    /// The announcement a member of `pseudonym`'s batch would be owed, for the tests that stage members
20172    /// directly rather than through a request.
20173    ///
20174    /// Any deposit address will do; its type depends on the curve this build is configured for, so one
20175    /// is derived rather than written down.
20176    fn owed_quota(pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, index: u32) -> anyhow::Result<AgreedSsaQuota> {
20177        let deposit_address = HoprPixSpec::group_to_deposit_address(
20178            SsaShareGenerator::<HoprPixSpec>::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
20179                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
20180                threshold: 2,
20181                surplus_shares: 1,
20182            })
20183            .new_ssa_commitment(&pseudonym, SsaIndex::MIN)?
20184            .ssa_commitment,
20185        )
20186        .context("a commitment has a deposit address")?;
20187        let ssa_index = SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero")?;
20188        Ok(AgreedSsaQuota {
20189            ssa_id: SsaId::new(pseudonym, ssa_index),
20190            deposit_address,
20191            quota_per_ssa: 1,
20192            deposit_data: PixDepositData {
20193                id: PixAddressId::new(&pseudonym, ssa_index),
20194                data: Box::default(),
20195            },
20196        })
20197    }

20199    /// Whether `error` is the non-fatal refusal a publication cut short by the transport is reported as.
20200    ///
20201    /// Told apart from the gate's own `NotAdmitted` refusals by what it says, because the point of the
20202    /// tests using it is that a cut is reported the same way on every path that can meet one.
20203    fn is_a_cut_short_publication(error: &TransportSessionError) -> bool {
20204        matches!(
20205            error,
20206            TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(reason))
20207                if reason.contains("was cut short") && reason.contains("still owed")
20208        )
20209    }
20210
20211    /// The owed set is claimed once, handed back whole, and replaced by a newer batch.
20212    #[test]
20213    fn owed_members_are_claimed_once_and_replaced_by_a_newer_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20214        let state = SessionSsaState::new(small_pix_params());
20215        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20216        let owed = |index: u32| owed_quota(pseudonym, index);
20217        let index = |index: u32| SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero");
20218
20219        state.stage_unpublished([owed(3)?, owed(4)?]);
20220        assert_eq!(vec![index(3)?, index(4)?], state.unpublished_indices());
20221
20222        let claimed = state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
20223        assert!(state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).is_none(), "a claim is exclusive");
20224        assert_eq!(
20225            vec![index(4)?],
20226            state.unpublished_indices(),
20227            "and takes the member out of the set"
20228        );
20229
20230        state.restore_unpublished(claimed);
20231        assert_eq!(
20232            vec![index(3)?, index(4)?],
20233            state.unpublished_indices(),
20234            "a member handed back is owed again, in its place"
20235        );
20236
20237        // A newer batch replaces the older one, and a straggling claimant of the old batch cannot
20238        // bring its member back into the new one.
20239        let straggler = state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).context("owed")?;
20240        state.stage_unpublished([owed(7)?]);
20241        assert_eq!(vec![index(7)?], state.unpublished_indices());
20242        state.restore_unpublished(straggler);
20243        assert_eq!(
20244            vec![index(7)?],
20245            state.unpublished_indices(),
20246            "an older batch's member has nothing left to be owed to"
20247        );
20248        Ok(())
20249    }
20250
20251    /// Only members whose publication completed are sent again, only once the batch has been out for
20252    /// a whole grace, and a re-send starts the grace over.
20253    #[test]
20254    fn a_late_repeat_resends_only_announced_members_once_per_grace() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20255        let state = SessionSsaState::new(small_pix_params());
20256        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20257        let owed = |index: u32| owed_quota(pseudonym, index);
20258        let index = |index: u32| SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero");
20259        let grace = SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE;
20260        let t0 = Instant::now();
20261
20262        state.stage_unpublished([owed(3)?, owed(4)?]);
20263        assert!(
20264            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 10, grace).is_empty(),
20265            "nothing has been announced yet"
20266        );
20267
20268        let first = state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
20269        state.complete_publication(first, t0);
20270        let second = state.claim_unpublished(index(4)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
20271        assert!(
20272            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace / 2, grace).is_empty(),
20273            "a repeat inside the grace may have crossed the burst"
20274        );
20275        assert_eq!(
20276            vec![index(3)?],
20277            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace, grace),
20278            "a member still being published is not sent again behind its claimant's back"
20279        );
20280        assert!(
20281            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace + grace / 2, grace).is_empty(),
20282            "a re-send starts the grace over"
20283        );
20284
20285        state.complete_publication(second, t0 + grace * 2);
20286        assert_eq!(
20287            vec![index(3)?, index(4)?],
20288            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 3, grace)
20289        );
20290
20291        state.forget_announced(index(3)?);
20292        assert_eq!(vec![index(4)?], state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 4, grace));
20293
20294        // A newer batch starts with nothing announced, and a straggling claimant of an older one
20295        // adds nothing to it.
20296        state.stage_unpublished([owed(5)?]);
20297        let straggler = state.claim_unpublished(index(5)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
20298        state.stage_unpublished([owed(7)?]);
20299        state.complete_publication(straggler, t0 + grace * 5);
20300        assert!(state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 10, grace).is_empty());
20301        Ok(())
20302    }
20303
20304    /// A request that finds another one in progress for the same Session is dropped on the spot.
20305    ///
20306    /// The holder can be anywhere in a long handler — waiting out the near-miss window, or part-way
20307    /// through generating a commitment, which at wide dimensions or a full batch takes seconds — and a
20308    /// queue of the Exit's re-sends behind it would park one `for_each_concurrent` slot each for all of
20309    /// that. Dropping costs nothing: either the holder admits the batch and the repeat is moot, or it
20310    /// does not and the repeat is the next attempt.
20311    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20312    async fn a_request_that_finds_the_lock_held_is_dropped_not_queued() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20313        let params = wide_pix_params();
20314        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
20315            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
20316
20317        let lock = mgr
20318            .ssa_request_locks
20319            .get_with(pseudonym, async { Arc::new(futures::lock::Mutex::new(())) })
20320            .await;
20321        let holder = lock.lock().await;
20322
20323        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
20324        let err = timeout(
20325            SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT,
20326            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20327                pseudonym,
20328                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20329            ),
20330        )
20331        .await
20332        .context("a request behind a held lock must come back at once instead of waiting for it")?
20333        .expect_err("a request that finds the lock held must not be served");
20334        assert!(
20335            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
20336            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
20337        );
20338        assert!(
20339            started.elapsed() * 4 < SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT,
20340            "dropping took {:?}, which is a wait",
20341            started.elapsed()
20342        );
20343        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
20344        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session is untouched");
20345
20346        // Released, the very same request goes through: nothing was remembered against it.
20347        drop(holder);
20348        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20349            pseudonym,
20350            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
20351        )
20352        .await
20353        .context("the request must be served once the lock is free")?;
20354        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
20355
20356        bob_sender.close_channel();
20357        bob_handle.await??;
20358        Ok(())
20359    }
20360
20361    /// A refusal is logged loudly once, and the repeats of it are not.
20362    ///
20363    /// The Exit re-sends a refused request every few seconds for as long as the gate stays shut, so
20364    /// the same refusal arrives over and over. Keyed on the lowest index asked for and the reason: a
20365    /// different reason for the same index, or the same reason for a different one, is news again.
20366    #[test]
20367    fn only_the_first_of_a_repeated_refusal_is_news() {
20368        let state = SessionSsaState::new(small_pix_params());
20369        let two = SsaIndex::new(2);
20370        let three = SsaIndex::new(3);
20371
20372        assert!(
20373            state.note_refusal(two, SsaRefusal::UnderServed),
20374            "the first refusal is news"
20375        );
20376        assert!(
20377            !state.note_refusal(two, SsaRefusal::UnderServed),
20378            "the same refusal for the same index is not"
20379        );
20380        assert!(
20381            state.note_refusal(two, SsaRefusal::Early),
20382            "a different reason for the same index is"
20383        );
20384        assert!(
20385            state.note_refusal(three, SsaRefusal::Early),
20386            "and so is the same reason for a different index"
20387        );
20388        assert!(!state.note_refusal(three, SsaRefusal::Early));
20389        assert!(
20390            state.note_refusal(None, SsaRefusal::Stale),
20391            "a request naming no index at all still has a key, and it is not the zero of 'no refusal yet'"
20392        );
20393    }
20394
20395    /// Concurrent `SsaRequest`s for one pseudonym must admit exactly one batch.
20396    ///
20397    /// Start messages are processed under `for_each_concurrent`, so several requests for the same
20398    /// Session run at once, and each reads the successor gate before any of them has advanced it.
20399    /// Requests are issued at distinct, ascending index ranges because that is the shape the
20400    /// generator's monotonic index cannot refuse — it rejects equal or lower indices, and an Exit
20401    /// numbering its batches upwards never offers one.
20402    ///
20403    /// **What this pins is the invariant, not the mechanism.** At this fixture's dimensions — two
20404    /// polynomials at threshold two — `new_ssa_commitment` returns in microseconds, so the window
20405    /// between reading the gate and advancing it is too narrow to hit: removing
20406    /// [`ssa_request_locks`](SessionManager::ssa_request_locks) leaves the outcome unchanged here.
20407    /// The window is a function of that call's cost, which scales with `polys x threshold` — around a
20408    /// second at the former 8192 x 64, so roughly a quarter of one at the deployed 4096 x 32 — and a
20409    /// fixture that large is not something to build into a unit test. So this test guards the property and the
20410    /// serialisation is justified by the shape of the code rather than by this failing without it.
20411    ///
20412    /// It does earn its place: it is what would catch the gate being made per-entry, the guard being
20413    /// taken after the gate instead of before it, or the handler gaining an await between the two.
20414    #[test_log::test(tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4))]
20415    async fn concurrent_ssa_requests_for_one_pseudonym_admit_one_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20416        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
20417
20418        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
20419        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
20420
20421        const BATCH: u32 = 2;
20422        const RACERS: u32 = 4;
20423
20424        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
20425            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
20426            threshold: 2,
20427            surplus_shares: 1,
20428        }));
20429        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
20430            generator.clone(),
20431            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
20432        );
20433        // This manager plays both halves, so its own Exit side opens a cycle and blocks on the
20434        // deposit pool. Answered on the way through; the deposits this test counts pass on unchanged.
20435        let mut pix_events = crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events, |_| Vec::new());
20436
20437        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
20438            max_ssas_per_ssa_request: BATCH as usize,
20439            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
20440                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
20441                ..Default::default()
20442            },
20443            ..Default::default()
20444        });
20445
20446        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
20447        bob_transport
20448            .expect_send_message()
20449            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
20450
20451        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
20452        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
20453        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
20454            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
20455            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
20456        });
20457        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
20458
20459        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20460        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
20461            pseudonym,
20462            StartInitiation {
20463                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
20464                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
20465                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
20466                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
20467            },
20468        )
20469        .await?;
20470
20471        let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
20472            .expect("identity element must be valid");
20473        let batch = |from: u32| {
20474            (from..from + BATCH)
20475                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
20476                .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>()
20477        };
20478
20479        // The opening batch, then emission far enough into its last cycle that exactly one successor
20480        // batch is legitimately admissible.
20481        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20482            pseudonym,
20483            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(1), []),
20484        )
20485        .await
20486        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
20487        assert_eq!(BATCH as usize, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
20488
20489        // Served for the batch, so that serialisation is the only thing deciding the outcome below.
20490        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required_returned_packets(&small_pix_params(), BATCH));
20491
20492        let min_emitted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
20493            &small_pix_params(),
20494            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
20495        );
20496        let mut sent = 0u32;
20497        for _ in 0..1024 {
20498            if generator
20499                .emission_progress(&pseudonym)
20500                .is_some_and(|p| p.is_serving_last_committed() && p.front_emitted >= min_emitted)
20501            {
20502                break;
20503            }
20504            sent += 1;
20505            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
20506        }
20507
20508        // Real tasks on a multi-threaded runtime, not `join_all`: `join_all` polls in order, so the
20509        // first future runs its gate check and its whole commitment phase before the second is polled
20510        // at all, and the requests never actually overlap. That shape passes with or without the
20511        // serialisation and so proves nothing about it.
20512        let barrier = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Barrier::new(RACERS as usize));
20513        let outcomes = futures::future::join_all((0..RACERS).map(|r| {
20514            let mgr = mgr.clone();
20515            let barrier = barrier.clone();
20516            let commitments = batch(BATCH + 1 + r * BATCH);
20517            tokio::spawn(async move {
20518                barrier.wait().await;
20519                mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20520                    pseudonym,
20521                    SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), commitments, []),
20522                )
20523                .await
20524            })
20525        }))
20526        .await
20527        .into_iter()
20528        .map(|joined| joined.expect("racer task must not panic"))
20529        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
20530
20531        let admitted = outcomes.iter().filter(|o| o.is_ok()).count();
20532        assert_eq!(
20533            1, admitted,
20534            "exactly one of {RACERS} concurrent requests may be admitted, got {admitted}: {outcomes:?}"
20535        );
20536        assert_eq!(
20537            BATCH as usize,
20538            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
20539            "only the admitted batch may produce deposit instructions"
20540        );
20541
20542        bob_sender.close_channel();
20543        bob_handle.await??;
20544        Ok(())
20545    }
20546
20547    /// An `SsaRequest` asking for more than [`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`] SSA
20548    /// commitments must be rejected outright, before any commitment is generated or any
20549    /// `ReadyToDeposit` is emitted — and a batch *at* the configured cap must be accepted, so that
20550    /// raising the knob is what actually admits a larger batch.
20551    ///
20552    /// Each accepted entry costs a full client commitment plus its own on-chain deposit, so without
20553    /// this cap one inbound packet could amplify into up to `MAX_SSAS_PER_REQUEST` (27) deposits.
20554    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20555    async fn entry_rejects_ssa_request_exceeding_configured_ssa_cap() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20556        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
20557
20558        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPixGroupElement;
20559        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
20560        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
20561
20562        /// Outcome of offering a batch: what `handle_ssa_request` returned, how many `SessionError`
20563        /// messages the Entry sent back, and whether it kept the Session.
20564        struct Outcome {
20565            result: errors::Result<()>,
20566            session_errors: usize,
20567            session_alive: bool,
20568        }
20569
20570        // `batch` entries offered against an Entry configured to accept at most `cap`.
20571        async fn offer_batch(cap: usize, batch: u32) -> anyhow::Result<Outcome> {
20572            // The PIX event stream must stay alive: an accepted batch emits one `ReadyToDeposit` per
20573            // entry, and a dropped receiver would fail the send and mask the acceptance as an error.
20574            let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
20575                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
20576                    polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
20577                    threshold: 2,
20578                    surplus_shares: 1,
20579                })
20580                .into(),
20581                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
20582            );
20583
20584            let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
20585                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
20586                    quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
20587                    ..Default::default()
20588                },
20589                max_ssas_per_ssa_request: cap,
20590                ..Default::default()
20591            });
20592
20593            // Count the SessionError replies: a refusal has to be *told* to the Exit, which cannot
20594            // otherwise observe it and has no path back to a new request.
20595            let session_errors = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
20596            let session_errors_tx = session_errors.clone();
20597            let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
20598            bob_transport
20599                .expect_send_message()
20600                .times(1..)
20601                .returning(move |_, data| {
20602                    if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionError) {
20603                        session_errors_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
20604                    }
20605                    Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
20606                });
20607
20608            let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
20609            let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
20610            let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
20611                pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
20612                while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
20613            });
20614            mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
20615
20616            let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20617
20618            mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
20619                alice_pseudonym,
20620                StartInitiation {
20621                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
20622                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
20623                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
20624                    additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
20625                },
20626            )
20627            .await?;
20628
20629            let session_id = alice_pseudonym;
20630            let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
20631                .expect("identity element must be valid");
20632
20633            // Indices start above whatever the Exit-side establishment already allocated, so the
20634            // accepted case is not rejected for non-monotonicity instead of for its size.
20635            let commitments: BTreeMap<_, _> = (100..100 + batch)
20636                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
20637                .collect();
20638
20639            let result = mgr
20640                .handle_ssa_request(
20641                    alice_pseudonym,
20642                    SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(
20643                        session_id,
20644                        PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?,
20645                        commitments,
20646                        [],
20647                    ),
20648                )
20649                .await;
20650
20651            let session_alive = mgr.active_sessions().contains(&session_id);
20652
20653            bob_sender.close_channel();
20654            bob_handle.await??;
20655
20656            Ok(Outcome {
20657                result,
20658                session_errors: session_errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
20659                session_alive,
20660            })
20661        }
20662
20663        // One over the default cap is rejected...
20664        let over_cap = offer_batch(
20665            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
20666            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST as u32 + 1,
20667        )
20668        .await?;
20669        assert!(
20670            matches!(
20671                over_cap.result,
20672                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
20673            ),
20674            "an over-cap SsaRequest must be rejected, got {:?}",
20675            over_cap.result
20676        );
20677        // ...and the refusal must be reported rather than left for the Exit to infer from its own
20678        // deposit timeout minutes later, and must not leave a Session behind that can never make PIX
20679        // progress.
20680        assert_eq!(
20681            1, over_cap.session_errors,
20682            "a refused SsaRequest must send exactly one SessionError back to the Exit"
20683        );
20684        assert!(
20685            !over_cap.session_alive,
20686            "a refused SsaRequest must tear down the Entry's half of the Session"
20687        );
20688
20689        // ...and the very same batch is accepted once the cap is raised to admit it, proving the
20690        // rejection is the configured cap talking and not some other validation.
20691        let raised = DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST + 1;
20692        let accepted = offer_batch(raised, raised as u32).await?;
20693        assert!(
20694            accepted.result.is_ok(),
20695            "a batch at the configured cap of {raised} must be accepted, got {:?}",
20696            accepted.result
20697        );
20698        assert_eq!(
20699            0, accepted.session_errors,
20700            "an accepted batch must not send a SessionError"
20701        );
20702        assert!(
20703            accepted.session_alive,
20704            "an accepted batch must leave the Session running"
20705        );
20706
20707        Ok(())
20708    }
20709
20710    /// A retransmission request must be capped on the *cycles* it names, not only on the runs the
20711    /// wire can carry.
20712    ///
20713    /// One 8-byte run names a whole cycle, so a request naming every retained cycle is answered with
20714    /// a full commitment burst for each — thousands of packets out of a single packet in. The
20715    /// generator's per-cycle attempt cap does not bound that: it bounds repeats of one cycle, and
20716    /// each cycle here is being asked for the first time.
20717    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20718    async fn entry_rejects_a_retransmission_request_naming_too_many_cycles() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20719        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
20720
20721        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPixGroupElement;
20722        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
20723        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
20724
20725        /// Commits `cap` cycles to an Entry capped at `cap`, then asks it to retransmit `cycles` of
20726        /// them, and reports what `handle_ssa_request` made of the second request together with every
20727        /// `SsaCommit` the Entry sent across both — one per cycle at these dimensions, so the
20728        /// commitment alone accounts for `cap` of them.
20729        ///
20730        /// Committing first is what gives the assertions their teeth: an uncapped handler answers
20731        /// every *retained* index it is named before it trips over the first one it does not hold, so
20732        /// the packet count — not the error — is what separates a gate from an accident. The count is
20733        /// read only after the send channel has drained, since the bursts are queued rather than sent
20734        /// inline and a running total would race them.
20735        async fn ask_for_cycles(cap: usize, cycles: u32) -> anyhow::Result<(errors::Result<()>, usize)> {
20736            let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
20737                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
20738                    polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
20739                    threshold: 2,
20740                    surplus_shares: 1,
20741                })
20742                .into(),
20743                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
20744            );
20745
20746            let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
20747                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
20748                    quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
20749                    ..Default::default()
20750                },
20751                max_ssas_per_ssa_request: cap,
20752                ..Default::default()
20753            });
20754
20755            // The amplification is the thing being bounded, so count what actually goes out.
20756            let commits = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
20757            let commits_tx = commits.clone();
20758            let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
20759            bob_transport
20760                .expect_send_message()
20761                .times(1..)
20762                .returning(move |_, data| {
20763                    if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit) {
20764                        commits_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
20765                    }
20766                    Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
20767                });
20768
20769            let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
20770            let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
20771            let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
20772                pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
20773                while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
20774            });
20775            mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
20776
20777            let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20778            mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
20779                alice_pseudonym,
20780                StartInitiation {
20781                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
20782                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
20783                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
20784                    additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
20785                },
20786            )
20787            .await?;
20788
20789            let params = PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
20790            let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
20791                .expect("identity element must be valid");
20792
20793            // Commit a full batch first, so there is real material for the retransmission to name.
20794            let commitments: BTreeMap<_, _> = (100..100 + cap as u32)
20795                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
20796                .collect();
20797            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
20798                alice_pseudonym,
20799                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(alice_pseudonym, params, commitments, []),
20800            )
20801            .await?;
20802
20803            // One run apiece, each covering its whole cycle: the cheapest request to send and the
20804            // most expensive to answer.
20805            let missing = (100..100 + cycles).map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), vec![(0u16, 1u16)]));
20806
20807            let result = mgr
20808                .handle_ssa_request(
20809                    alice_pseudonym,
20810                    SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(alice_pseudonym, params, missing),
20811                )
20812                .await;
20813
20814            bob_sender.close_channel();
20815            bob_handle.await??;
20816
20817            Ok((result, commits.load(Ordering::Relaxed)))
20818        }
20819
20820        // One cycle over the cap is refused whole, and — the part that matters — answered with
20821        // nothing at all, rather than with a burst for each retained cycle it managed to name first.
20822        let (over_cap, over_cap_commits) = ask_for_cycles(
20823            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
20824            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST as u32 + 1,
20825        )
20826        .await?;
20827        assert!(
20828            matches!(
20829                over_cap,
20830                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
20831            ),
20832            "a retransmission request over the cycle cap must be refused, got {over_cap:?}"
20833        );
20834        assert_eq!(
20835            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST, over_cap_commits,
20836            "a refused request must add nothing to the {DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST} messages the commitment \
20837             itself cost"
20838        );
20839
20840        // ...and the very same cycles are repaired once they fit the cap, so the refusal above is the
20841        // cap talking and not some other validation the request also trips.
20842        let (at_cap, at_cap_commits) = ask_for_cycles(
20843            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
20844            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST as u32,
20845        )
20846        .await?;
20847        assert!(
20848            at_cap.is_ok(),
20849            "a request at the cycle cap must be answered, got {at_cap:?}"
20850        );
20851        assert_eq!(
20852            2 * DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
20853            at_cap_commits,
20854            "every named cycle must be re-sent, one message each on top of the commitment's own"
20855        );
20856
20857        Ok(())
20858    }
20859
20860    /// A batch with one undecodable member must publish nothing at all.
20861    ///
20862    /// `handle_ssa_request` used to generate, send and emit per entry, deciding each member's fate
20863    /// before looking at the next. A batch whose *second* exit commitment failed to decode had
20864    /// therefore already sent the first member's `SsaCommit` burst and emitted its `ReadyToDeposit`
20865    /// — an instruction to put money on chain — for a request that is then rejected as a whole. The
20866    /// Exit has no cycle to spend that deposit against, and the deposit key needs its half.
20867    ///
20868    /// The first member is valid and the second is not, so a per-entry implementation passes the
20869    /// "batch is refused" half of this test while still leaking the first deposit.
20870    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
20871    async fn a_batch_with_one_undecodable_commitment_publishes_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
20872        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
20873
20874        use futures::FutureExt;
20875        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPixGroupElement;
20876        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
20877        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
20878
20879        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
20880            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
20881                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
20882                threshold: 2,
20883                surplus_shares: 1,
20884            })
20885            .into(),
20886            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
20887        );
20888
20889        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
20890            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
20891                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
20892                ..Default::default()
20893            },
20894            ..Default::default()
20895        });
20896
20897        // `SsaCommit` is the observable half of "a commitment was published"; `SessionError` is the
20898        // refusal. Both are counted, because the bug shows up as the two happening together.
20899        let commits = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
20900        let session_errors = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
20901        let (commits_tx, errors_tx) = (commits.clone(), session_errors.clone());
20902        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
20903        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
20904            if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit) {
20905                commits_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
20906            }
20907            if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionError) {
20908                errors_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
20909            }
20910            Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
20911        });
20912
20913        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
20914        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
20915        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
20916            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
20917            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
20918        });
20919        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
20920
20921        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
20922        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
20923            alice_pseudonym,
20924            StartInitiation {
20925                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
20926                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
20927                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
20928                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
20929            },
20930        )
20931        .await?;
20932
20933        let valid = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
20934            .expect("identity element must be valid");
20935        // All-ones is not a compressed point on the curve, so it fails before the subgroup check.
20936        // The length is taken from the type rather than written out: the group representation is
20937        // curve-dependent, and a literal silently becomes a *length* rejection under a different
20938        // `HoprPixSpec` — which is a different code path from the one under test.
20939        // Spelled out because the group repr is a `hybrid_array::Array` with several `AsRef` impls.
20940        let repr_len = AsRef::<[u8]>::as_ref(&PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes()).len();
20941        let garbage =
20942            HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(vec![0xffu8; repr_len].as_slice()).expect("length must be accepted");
20943        assert!(
20944            garbage.try_into_pix_group().is_err(),
20945            "the test fixture must actually be undecodable"
20946        );
20947
20948        let commitments: BTreeMap<_, _> = BTreeMap::from([
20949            (SsaIndex::new(100).expect("non-zero"), valid),
20950            (SsaIndex::new(101).expect("non-zero"), garbage),
20951        ]);
20952
20953        let result = mgr
20954            .handle_ssa_request(
20955                alice_pseudonym,
20956                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(
20957                    alice_pseudonym,
20958                    PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?,
20959                    commitments,
20960                    [],
20961                ),
20962            )
20963            .await;
20964
20965        let session_alive = mgr.active_sessions().contains(&alice_pseudonym);
20966
20967        // Drain the mock transport before counting: `mock_packet_planning` delivers on a spawned
20968        // task, so a count taken here would race the sends rather than observe them.
20969        bob_sender.close_channel();
20970        bob_handle.await??;
20971
20972        assert!(
20973            matches!(
20974                result,
20975                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
20976            ),
20977            "an undecodable member must be refused, got {result:?}"
20978        );
20979        assert_eq!(
20980            0,
20981            commits.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
20982            "no SsaCommit may be sent for a batch that is refused as a whole"
20983        );
20984        assert_eq!(
20985            1,
20986            session_errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
20987            "the refusal must be reported to the Exit"
20988        );
20989        assert!(
20990            !session_alive,
20991            "an undecodable commitment is terminal, like every other unacceptable-parameter case"
20992        );
20993
20994        // The point of the test: not one deposit instruction escaped for the valid first member.
20995        pin_mut!(pix_events);
20996        assert!(
20997            pix_events.next().now_or_never().flatten().is_none(),
20998            "no ReadyToDeposit may be emitted for a batch that is refused as a whole"
20999        );
21000
21001        Ok(())
21002    }
21003
21004    /// The Start protocol ingress channel must be sized for the worst-case commitment burst of a
21005    /// single SSA cycle, not for the number of sessions.
21006    ///
21007    /// A dropped `SsaCommit` is unrecoverable — there is no retransmission — so the queue has to
21008    /// absorb the whole commitment set a cycle can deliver, capped by the polynomial ceiling
21009    /// `check_pix_params` enforces.
21010    #[test]
21011    fn start_protocol_channel_is_sized_for_the_worst_case_commitment_burst() {
21012        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig::default();
21013        let capacity = start_protocol_channel_capacity(&cfg);
21014
21015        // Number of commitments implied by the largest quota this node accepts, clamped by the
21016        // number of polynomials it would actually admit.
21017        let commitments = (*cfg.pix_config.quota_range.end() / PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE).min(MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA as u64);
21018        let min_expected = commitments.div_ceil(MIN_COMMITMENTS_PER_SSA_COMMIT_MSG as u64) as usize;
21019
21020        assert!(
21021            capacity >= min_expected + cfg.maximum_sessions,
21022            "capacity {capacity} must cover the {min_expected}-message commitment burst plus room for {} concurrent \
21023             session setups",
21024            cfg.maximum_sessions
21025        );
21026
21027        // The commitment burst must be the term that was added, not incidental slack: the old
21028        // sizing was `maximum_sessions + 10` and carried no PIX component at all.
21029        assert_eq!(
21030            min_expected,
21031            capacity - cfg.maximum_sessions - START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
21032            "the PIX commitment burst must be an explicit component of the capacity"
21033        );
21034        assert!(
21035            min_expected > 0,
21036            "a non-zero accepted quota must imply commitment messages"
21037        );
21038
21039        // Guards against a units mistake (e.g. counting bytes rather than messages) turning this
21040        // into a multi-gigabyte ring allocation.
21041        assert!(capacity < 1_000_000, "capacity {capacity} is implausibly large");
21042    }
21043
21044    /// `quota_range` is operator-settable and the capacity it feeds is *reserved*, not merely
21045    /// enforced — `crossfire`'s array flavour pre-allocates every slot. So the derivation must be
21046    /// bounded independently of the configured quota.
21047    ///
21048    /// Regression test: an unclamped derivation asked for ~4.2e8 slots here (77 GB), which aborted
21049    /// the whole unit test binary with an allocation failure rather than failing one assertion. The
21050    /// sizing test above never caught it because it only exercises the default config.
21051    #[test]
21052    fn start_protocol_channel_capacity_is_bounded_for_any_quota_range() {
21053        // The commitment term saturates once the quota admits more commitments than there are
21054        // polynomials, so this is the largest value it can ever take.
21055        let saturated = (MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA as u64).div_ceil(MIN_COMMITMENTS_PER_SSA_COMMIT_MSG as u64) as usize;
21056
21057        for quota_end in [10_u64.pow(13), u64::MAX] {
21058            let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
21059                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21060                    quota_range: 0..=quota_end,
21061                    ..Default::default()
21062                },
21063                ..Default::default()
21064            };
21065            let capacity = start_protocol_channel_capacity(&cfg);
21066
21067            assert_eq!(
21068                capacity,
21069                saturated + cfg.maximum_sessions + START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
21070                "quota_range end {quota_end} must not grow the commitment term past the polynomial ceiling"
21071            );
21072        }
21073
21074        // The session term is reserved for exactly the same reason, and `maximum_managed_sessions`
21075        // validates up to 100 000 — so it needs its own ceiling, not just the commitment one.
21076        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
21077            maximum_sessions: 100_000,
21078            ..Default::default()
21079        };
21080        assert_eq!(
21081            start_protocol_channel_capacity(&cfg),
21082            saturated + MAX_CONCURRENT_START_EXCHANGES + START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
21083            "a large session limit must not grow the pre-allocated ring past the handshake ceiling"
21084        );
21085
21086        // The batch factor is reserved too: a batch of N draws N cycles' commitment sets into this
21087        // one channel, and a dropped `SsaCommit` is unrecoverable. It must scale the commitment term
21088        // and nothing else, and must itself be bounded by `MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE` even when the config
21089        // was never clamped by `SessionManager::new`.
21090        let batched = |ssas_per_request| {
21091            start_protocol_channel_capacity(&SessionManagerConfig {
21092                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21093                    quota_range: 0..=u64::MAX,
21094                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
21095                        ssas_per_request,
21096                        ..Default::default()
21097                    },
21098                    ..Default::default()
21099                },
21100                ..Default::default()
21101            })
21102        };
21103        let unbatched = SessionManagerConfig::default();
21104        for ssas_per_request in [1, 2, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE] {
21105            assert_eq!(
21106                batched(ssas_per_request),
21107                saturated * ssas_per_request + unbatched.maximum_sessions + START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
21108                "the commitment term must scale with ssas_per_request = {ssas_per_request}"
21109            );
21110        }
21111        assert_eq!(
21112            batched(MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE + 1),
21113            batched(MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE),
21114            "an unclamped ssas_per_request must not inflate the pre-allocated ring"
21115        );
21116        assert_eq!(
21117            batched(0),
21118            batched(1),
21119            "a zero ssas_per_request must not collapse the commitment term"
21120        );
21121    }
21122
21123    /// Verifies that once the exit/responder (Bob) has set up the SSA state, delivering coefficient
21124    /// commits for all polynomials causes the PIX event stream to emit `DepositNeeded`.
21125    ///
21126    /// ## Steps
21127    /// 1. Bob's manager is started with a `PixToolbox` configured for `polynomials_per_ssa=2, threshold=2,
21128    ///    surplus_shares=1`. Alice's session initiation is processed normally.
21129    /// 2. The exit has already registered an exit commitment from `handle_incoming_session_initiation`.
21130    /// 3. Coefficient 0 (constant terms across all polynomials) is delivered via `handle_ssa_commit` using identity
21131    ///    group elements as dummy commitments.
21132    /// 4. Coefficient 1 (linear terms) is delivered similarly.
21133    /// 5. After the second coefficient delivery, Bob's PIX event stream emits `DepositNeeded` with the correct `SsaId`
21134    ///    and `quota_per_ssa` matching `pix_params_to_quota(2, 2)`.
21135    /// 6. The event is received within a 2-second timeout.
21136    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21137    async fn exit_receives_ssa_commits_and_emits_deposit_needed_event() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21138        use std::collections::HashMap;
21139
21140        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::{HoprPixCommitmentProof, HoprPixGroupElement};
21141        use hopr_protocol_pix::{
21142            Field, PixGroup, PixScalar, PolynomialIndex, SsaCommitmentProof, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructor,
21143            SsaReconstructorConfig, SsaShareGenerator,
21144        };
21145        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
21146
21147        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
21148            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
21149            threshold: 2,
21150            surplus_shares: 1,
21151        };
21152
21153        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events_rx) = PixToolbox::new(
21154            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
21155            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
21156        );
21157        // This test reads the event stream itself, so the pool has to be played on the way through:
21158        // the Exit blocks its SSA request on the answer, and the request would otherwise be the
21159        // first event read here.
21160        let pix_events_rx =
21161            crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events_rx, |id| vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8; 3]);
21162
21163        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
21164            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21165                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
21166                ..Default::default()
21167            },
21168            ..Default::default()
21169        });
21170
21171        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
21172        bob_transport
21173            .expect_send_message()
21174            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
21175        // handle_incoming_session_initiation sends SessionEstablished + SsaRequest.
21176        bob_transport
21177            .expect_send_message()
21178            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
21179
21180        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
21181        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
21182        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
21183            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
21184            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
21185        });
21186        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox.clone()), None)?;
21187
21188        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
21189
21190        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
21191            alice_pseudonym,
21192            StartInitiation {
21193                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
21194                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
21195                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21196                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
21197            },
21198        )
21199        .await?;
21200
21201        // The exit commitment is registered by the supervisor's opening `RequestSsa`, which the
21202        // action driver carries out asynchronously — so wait for it rather than assume it.
21203        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(alice_pseudonym, SsaIndex::MIN);
21204        {
21205            let share_processor = pix_toolbox.share_processor.clone();
21206            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
21207                while !share_processor.contains_builder(&ssa_id) {
21208                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
21209                }
21210            })
21211            .await
21212            .context("the opening SSA request never registered an exit commitment")?;
21213        }
21214
21215        // Deliver coefficient 0 (constant terms across all polynomials).
21216        // Use the identity/infinity group element as a dummy commitment.
21217        // PixGroup<HoprPixSpec> = k256::ProjectivePoint, which has identity/infinity as all-zero bytes.
21218        let identity_element = {
21219            let g: PixGroup<HoprPixSpec> = Default::default();
21220            HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(g.to_bytes().as_ref()).expect("identity element must be valid")
21221        };
21222        let mut coeff_0_map = HashMap::new();
21223        for poly in 0..2 {
21224            coeff_0_map.insert(poly as PolynomialIndex, identity_element);
21225        }
21226        // The dummy constant terms sum to the identity, whose discrete logarithm is zero, so an
21227        // honest proof of knowledge over it is constructible — the Exit refuses the cycle without
21228        // one.
21229        let zero = <PixScalar<HoprPixSpec> as Field>::ZERO;
21230        let identity_proof = HoprPixCommitmentProof::from(
21231            SsaCommitmentProof::<HoprPixSpec>::prove(&ssa_id, &zero, &PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default())
21232                .expect("identity proof must be constructible"),
21233        );
21234        mgr.handle_ssa_commit(
21235            alice_pseudonym,
21236            SsaClientCommitmentMessage {
21237                session_id: alice_pseudonym,
21238                ssa_index: SsaIndex::MIN,
21239                coefficient_index: 0,
21240                commitment_proof: Some(identity_proof),
21241                coefficient_commitments: coeff_0_map,
21242            },
21243        )
21244        .await?;
21245
21246        // Deliver coefficient 1 (linear terms across all polynomials).
21247        let mut coeff_1_map = HashMap::new();
21248        for poly in 0..2 {
21249            coeff_1_map.insert(poly as PolynomialIndex, identity_element);
21250        }
21251        mgr.handle_ssa_commit(
21252            alice_pseudonym,
21253            SsaClientCommitmentMessage {
21254                session_id: alice_pseudonym,
21255                ssa_index: SsaIndex::MIN,
21256                coefficient_index: 1,
21257                commitment_proof: None,
21258                coefficient_commitments: coeff_1_map,
21259            },
21260        )
21261        .await?;
21262
21263        // The first coefficient commitment should trigger DepositNeeded.
21264        pin_mut!(pix_events_rx);
21265        let event = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2), pix_events_rx.next())
21266            .await
21267            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("timeout waiting for pix event: {e}"))?
21268            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("pix_events_rx closed without emitting an event"))?;
21269
21270        assert!(matches!(
21271            event,
21272            HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(AgreedSsaQuota { ssa_id: ref received_ssa_id, .. }, _)
21273            if received_ssa_id == &ssa_id
21274        ));
21275
21276        let HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(quota, _) = event else {
21277            unreachable!();
21278        };
21279        assert_eq!(quota.quota_per_ssa, pix_params_to_quota(&small_pix_params()));
21280
21281        bob_sender.close_channel();
21282        bob_handle.await??;
21283
21284        Ok(())
21285    }
21286
21287    /// Verifies that a PIX Session whose Entry never answers the `SsaRequest` is closed when the
21288    /// commitment deadline expires.
21289    ///
21290    /// This used to be spelled as a deposit-timeout test, with `max_ssa_delivery_time: 0` and a
21291    /// 50 ms `max_deposit_wait`. A zero delivery time makes the *commitment* deadline fire
21292    /// immediately, so the assertion held whatever the deposit deadline did — it would have passed
21293    /// with that deadline removed entirely. The deposit deadline cannot be reached from this
21294    /// fixture at all: arming it needs a `CommitmentVerified`, and a mock transport has no Entry to
21295    /// send one. That path is covered end-to-end by `hopr-lib`'s `deposit_timeout_closes_session`.
21296    ///
21297    /// So `max_deposit_wait` is set far out of reach here, leaving the commitment deadline as the
21298    /// only thing that can close the Session.
21299    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21300    async fn session_is_closed_when_the_entry_never_commits() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21301        use std::time::Duration;
21302
21303        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
21304        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
21305
21306        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
21307            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
21308            threshold: 2,
21309            surplus_shares: 1,
21310        };
21311
21312        let (pix_toolbox, _) = PixToolbox::new(
21313            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
21314            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
21315        );
21316
21317        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
21318            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21319                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
21320                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
21321                    // Short, so the deadline under test fires quickly.
21322                    max_ssa_delivery_time: Duration::from_millis(50),
21323                    // Scaled with it, since it has to stay under the delivery deadline. Nothing arms
21324                    // it here — the Entry sends no commitment at all, so there is no scope to
21325                    // re-request and the deadline under test is the only one that can fire.
21326                    commitment_recommit_interval: Duration::from_millis(10),
21327                    // Under the delivery deadline for the same reason. It would not fire here in any
21328                    // case — this is the opening batch, which is never re-sent.
21329                    ssa_request_resend_interval: Duration::from_millis(20),
21330                    // Far out of reach, so it cannot be what closes the Session.
21331                    max_deposit_wait: Duration::from_secs(3600),
21332                    ..Default::default()
21333                },
21334                ..Default::default()
21335            },
21336            ..Default::default()
21337        });
21338
21339        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
21340        // handle_incoming_session_initiation sends SessionEstablished + SsaRequest (2 messages).
21341        bob_transport
21342            .expect_send_message()
21343            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
21344        bob_transport
21345            .expect_send_message()
21346            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
21347
21348        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
21349        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
21350        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
21351            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
21352            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
21353        });
21354        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox.clone()), None)?;
21355
21356        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
21357
21358        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
21359            alice_pseudonym,
21360            StartInitiation {
21361                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
21362                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
21363                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21364                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
21365            },
21366        )
21367        .await?;
21368
21369        // Session is active after establishment.
21370        assert_eq!(vec![alice_pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions());
21371
21372        // The supervisor arms the commitment deadline once the `SsaRequest` goes out and closes the
21373        // Session 50 ms later; the teardown that follows is asynchronous.
21374        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), async {
21375            while mgr.num_active_sessions() > 0 {
21376                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
21377            }
21378        })
21379        .await
21380        .context("session should be closed once the commitment deadline expires")?;
21381
21382        assert!(mgr.active_sessions().is_empty());
21383
21384        bob_sender.close_channel();
21385        bob_handle.await??;
21386
21387        Ok(())
21388    }

21390    /// The surplus an Entry offers must survive the round trip: stored by the Exit, then echoed
21391    /// back in the `SsaRequest` it sends.
21392    ///
21393    /// It is the one negotiated value with no other consumer — it is not part of the priced quota,
21394    /// so no quota check would notice it going missing, and the Exit does not act on it yet. Every
21395    /// other dimension is pinned several times over by the checks around it.
21396    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21397    async fn exit_stores_and_echoes_the_offered_surplus() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21398        use hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig;
21399        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
21400
21401        // Distinct from every default, so a value read from local config instead of the wire is
21402        // visibly wrong rather than accidentally right.
21403        const OFFERED_SURPLUS: u8 = 37;
21404
21405        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
21406            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
21407                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
21408                threshold: 2,
21409                surplus_shares: TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES,
21410            })
21411            .into(),
21412            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
21413        );
21414
21415        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
21416            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21417                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
21418                ..Default::default()
21419            },
21420            ..Default::default()
21421        });
21422
21423        let echoed: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<PixParams>>> = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
21424        let echoed_clone = echoed.clone();
21425        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
21426        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
21427            if let Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(req)) = HoprStartProtocol::try_from(data.data)
21428                && let Ok(params) = req.dimensions()
21429            {
21430                echoed_clone.lock().unwrap().push(params);
21431            }
21432            Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
21433        });
21434
21435        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
21436        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
21437        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
21438            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
21439            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
21440        });
21441        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
21442
21443        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
21444        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
21445            alice_pseudonym,
21446            StartInitiation {
21447                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
21448                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
21449                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21450                additional_data: pix_additional_data(2, 2, OFFERED_SURPLUS),
21451            },
21452        )
21453        .await?;
21454
21455        let expected = PixParams::try_new(2, 2, OFFERED_SURPLUS, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
21456
21457        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&alice_pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
21458        let ssa_state = slot.current_ssa_state.get().context("pix state must be set")?;
21459        assert_eq!(
21460            expected, ssa_state.params,
21461            "the Exit must keep the surplus the Entry offered, not its own"
21462        );
21463
21464        // The echo does not go out inline: the supervisor's opening `RequestSsa` is carried out by
21465        // the action driver spawned once the Session is published, which is what keeps
21466        // `SessionEstablished` ahead of `SsaRequest` on the wire.
21467        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
21468            while echoed.lock().unwrap().is_empty() {
21469                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
21470            }
21471        })
21472        .await
21473        .context("the supervisor's opening SsaRequest never reached the wire")?;
21474
21475        bob_sender.close_channel();
21476        bob_handle.await??;
21477
21478        let echoed = echoed.lock().unwrap().clone();
21479        assert_eq!(
21480            vec![expected],
21481            echoed,
21482            "the SsaRequest must echo back exactly what was offered"
21483        );
21484
21485        Ok(())
21486    }
