21488    /// Verifies that `check_pix_params` rejects out-of-bounds parameters that pass the
21489    /// quota-range check but exceed the protocol limits.
21490    ///
21491    /// This is a regression test for the incentive-bypass fix (round-1 finding #1).
21492    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21493    async fn check_pix_params_must_reject_invalid_bounds() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21494        let mgr =
21495            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
21496                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21497                    quota_range: 0..=10_000_000_000_000,
21498                    ..Default::default()
21499                },
21500                ..Default::default()
21501            });
21502
21503        let offer = |additional_data: u64| StartInitiation {
21504            challenge: 0,
21505            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
21506            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21507            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(additional_data),
21508        };
21509        // Packed by hand rather than through `pix_additional_data`, because that helper refuses to
21510        // build the very values under test. The layout it mirrors is pinned in `PixParams`' own
21511        // tests. The suite is this build's, so that the dimension cases below fail on their
21512        // dimensions rather than on a curve mismatch — that rejection has its own test.
21513        let packed = |polys: u16, shares: u8, surplus: u8| {
21514            ((LOCAL_PIX_SUITE as u64) << 62)
21515                | ((polys as u64) << 48)
21516                | ((shares as u64) << 40)
21517                | ((surplus as u64) << 32)
21518        };
21519
21520        // polys_per_ssa > MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA (16192), and zero, with a valid quota -> should reject
21521        for polys in [0, MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA + 1, u16::MAX] {
21522            assert!(
21523                decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(polys, 128, 0))).is_none(),
21524                "should reject polys_per_ssa {polys}"
21525            );
21526        }
21527
21528        // shares_per_poly < MIN_POLY_THRESHOLD with a valid quota -> should reject. There is no
21529        // matching upper-bound case: the threshold is a byte on the wire, so `MAX_POLY_THRESHOLD`
21530        // cannot be exceeded by anything a peer is able to send.
21531        for shares in [0, 1] {
21532            assert!(
21533                decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(8192, shares, 0))).is_none(),
21534                "should reject shares_per_poly {shares}"
21535            );
21536        }
21537
21538        // Valid params should still be accepted, and arrive intact — including the surplus, which
21539        // no other check looks at and which would therefore be free to go missing.
21540        let (accepted, batch_size) =
21541            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(8192, 128, 37))).context("should accept valid params")?;
21542        assert_eq!(PixParams::try_new(8192, 128, 37, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?, accepted);
21543        assert_eq!(1, batch_size);
21544
21545        // Every surplus a byte can hold is legal.
21546        for surplus in [0, 1, u8::MAX] {
21547            assert_eq!(
21548                Some((PixParams::try_new(8192, 128, surplus, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?, 1)),
21549                decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(8192, 128, surplus)))
21550            );
21551        }
21552
21553        Ok(())
21554    }
21555
21556    /// The Exit refuses a client whose PIX curve suite is not the one this node was built for.
21557    ///
21558    /// The curve is a build-time property on both sides and is not negotiated, so the only two
21559    /// outcomes are "same suite" and "refused". This matters because it happens *before* the Exit
21560    /// commits: every later PIX field — each coefficient commitment, the proof of knowledge — is
21561    /// sized by the curve, so a mismatch that got past here would surface as undecodable Start
21562    /// traffic on a Session both sides believed they had established.
21563    ///
21564    /// The quota range is wide open, so nothing but the suite can be doing the rejecting.
21565    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21566    async fn check_pix_params_must_refuse_a_foreign_curve_suite() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21567        let mgr =
21568            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
21569                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21570                    quota_range: 0..=10_000_000_000_000,
21571                    ..Default::default()
21572                },
21573                ..Default::default()
21574            });
21575
21576        let offer = |suite: hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite| StartInitiation {
21577            challenge: 0,
21578            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
21579            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21580            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(
21581                PixParams::try_new(8192, 128, 37, suite)
21582                    .expect("test dimensions must be valid")
21583                    .into_additional_data(0),
21584            ),
21585        };
21586
21587        let foreign = match LOCAL_PIX_SUITE {
21588            hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::BabyJubJub => hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::Secp256k1,
21589            hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::Secp256k1 => hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::BabyJubJub,
21590        };
21591
21592        assert!(
21593            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(foreign)).is_none(),
21594            "a client offering {foreign} must be refused by a {LOCAL_PIX_SUITE} Exit"
21595        );
21596        assert!(
21597            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)).is_some(),
21598            "and the same dimensions on this build's own curve must still be accepted"
21599        );
21600
21601        // A suite identifier no curve claims is refused as well, rather than read as a third curve.
21602        let unknown = StartInitiation {
21603            challenge: 0,
21604            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
21605            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21606            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(
21607                (0b11u64 << 62) | (8192u64 << 48) | (128u64 << 40) | (37u64 << 32),
21608            ),
21609        };
21610        assert!(
21611            decode_and_check(&mgr, &unknown).is_none(),
21612            "an unknown suite identifier must be refused"
21613        );
21614
21615        Ok(())
21616    }
21617
21618    /// The Exit judges an offer by its quota alone; the split is the Entry's choice.
21619    ///
21620    /// The surplus is insurance against the return relayers the *Entry* picks for its SURBs, and only
21621    /// the Entry knows how far it trusts them: one expecting most of them to fail may buy
21622    /// `4096 × (2 + 102)`, which carries ~86 % share loss where the deployed split carries ~50 %. What
21623    /// the Exit has a stake in is how much it serves for one deposit, which is the quota —
21624    /// `polys × (threshold + surplus)` shares — so every split whose quota fits `quota_range` is
21625    /// accepted, whatever its ratio of surplus to threshold, and the Entry's successor gate then
21626    /// follows the tolerance it bought.
21627    ///
21628    /// Reconstructor memory is also reserved from the offered dimensions, at admission against
21629    /// `max_live_cycle_bytes`. That is a capacity check, and one the configuration validator holds to
21630    /// admitting a Session at any split of the advertised quota — not a policy on the split.
21631    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21632    async fn the_exit_judges_an_offer_by_its_quota_alone() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21633        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
21634        let offer = |params: PixParams| StartInitiation {
21635            challenge: 0,
21636            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
21637            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21638            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0)),
21639        };
21640
21641        // The default range, in shares, is a quarter of the deployed cycle up to the whole of it:
21642        // 113 664 ..= 454 656.
21643        for (polys, threshold, surplus, quota_shares) in [
21644            (4096u16, 2u8, 102u8, 425_984u64),
21645            (1024, 2, 255, 263_168),
21646            (16192, 2, 26, 453_376),
21647            (4096, 32, 79, 454_656),
21648        ] {
21649            let params = PixParams::try_new(polys, threshold, surplus, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
21650            assert_eq!(quota_shares * PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE, pix_params_to_quota(&params));
21651
21652            let (accepted, _) = decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(params)).with_context(|| {
21653                format!("{polys} x ({threshold} + {surplus}) fits the default quota range and must be accepted")
21654            })?;
21655            assert_eq!(params, accepted, "the split must arrive as offered");
21656        }
21657
21658        // The same threshold and the most surplus the byte carries, at a polynomial count whose quota
21659        // — 1 052 672 shares — is past the top of the range. Refused, and by the quota alone.
21660        let over = PixParams::try_new(4096, 2, u8::MAX, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
21661        assert!(pix_params_to_quota(&over) > *IncomingSessionPixConfig::default().quota_range.end());
21662        assert!(
21663            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(over)).is_none(),
21664            "an offer whose quota exceeds the range must be refused"
21665        );
21666
21667        Ok(())
21668    }
21669
21670    /// Verifies that dispatching too many `UnverifiableShare` events closes the session.
21671    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21672    async fn too_many_unverifiable_shares_closes_session() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21673        let params = small_pix_params();
21674        let quota = pix_params_to_quota(&params);
21675        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
21676            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
21677            threshold: 2,
21678            surplus_shares: 1,
21679        };
21680
21681        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
21682            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
21683            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
21684        );
21685
21686        let mgr =
21687            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
21688                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
21689                    quota_range: quota..=quota,
21690                    max_live_cycle_bytes: max_cycle_budget_for_quota(quota, 1),
21691                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
21692                        max_deposit_wait: Duration::from_secs(1),
21693                        ..Default::default()
21694                    },
21695                    ..Default::default()
21696                },
21697                ..Default::default()
21698            });
21699
21700        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
21701        bob_transport
21702            .expect_send_message()
21703            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
21704        bob_transport
21705            .expect_send_message()
21706            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
21707
21708        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
21709        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
21710        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
21711            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
21712            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
21713        });
21714        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox.clone()), None)?;
21715
21716        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
21717
21718        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
21719            alice_pseudonym,
21720            StartInitiation {
21721                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
21722                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
21723                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
21724                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0)),
21725            },
21726        )
21727        .await?;
21728
21729        // Session is active
21730        assert_eq!(vec![alice_pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions());
21731
21732        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(alice_pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("non-zero"));
21733
21734        // Exactly one event, reporting the absolute total the reconstructor would carry for a single
21735        // failed polynomial. There is no tolerance to exhaust first.
21736        let result = mgr
21737            .dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
21738                ssa_id,
21739                observed_total: 1,
21740                peer: crate::supervision::test_peer(),
21741            })
21742            .await;
21743        // Forwarding succeeds even for the event that closes: the supervisor decides, and it does so
21744        // after the send has been accepted.
21745        assert!(result.is_ok(), "dispatch_pix_event should not return an error");
21746
21747        // The supervisor's `Close` reaches the driver asynchronously, so the teardown it triggers
21748        // is observed rather than assumed.
21749        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
21750            while mgr.num_active_sessions() > 0 {
21751                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
21752            }
21753        })
21754        .await
21755        .context("session was not closed after too many unverifiable shares")?;
21756
21757        assert!(mgr.active_sessions().is_empty());
21758
21759        bob_sender.close_channel();
21760        bob_handle.await??;
21761
21762        Ok(())
21763    }

21765    /// Verifies that `allocate_session_slot` signals waiters via `.send(())` rather than
21766    /// dropping the senders. The `Ok(Ok(()))` path in `handle_ssa_request` must be live.
21767    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21768    async fn allocate_session_slot_must_signal_waiters_not_cancel_them() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21769        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
21770        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
21771
21772        // Register a waiter before the slot is allocated
21773        let (tx, mut rx) = oneshot::channel::<()>();
21774        mgr.slot_allocated
21775            .lock()
21776            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
21777            .entry(session_id)
21778            .or_default()
21779            .push(tx);
21780
21781        let (session_tx, _) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY);
21782
21783        // Allocate the slot — this should signal the waiter. The slot is inserted here so that the
21784        // `commit` below can find it: that is where the token `admit` returns lands.
21785        let slot = SessionSlot {
21786            session_tx,
21787            routing_opts: DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(session_id)),
21788            abort_handles: Default::default(),
21789            surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::from(SurbBalancerConfig::default())),
21790            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
21791            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
21792            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
21793            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
21794            pix_fill: Default::default(),
21795            returned_packets: Default::default(),
21796            cycle_budget: None,
21797            admission_token: Default::default(),
21798            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
21799        };
21800        let guard = mgr.allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone());
21801        assert!(guard.is_some(), "slot allocation must succeed");
21802
21803        // The waiter should receive Some(()) — the direct signal, not Canceled
21804        assert!(
21805            matches!(rx.try_recv(), Ok(Some(()))),
21806            "waiter must be signaled with Ok(()), not canceled"
21807        );
21808
21809        guard.unwrap().commit(Some(&slot), None, 0);
21810
21811        Ok(())
21812    }
21813
21814    /// Builds a slot for `session_id` that is not yet in any cache, for the guard tests below.
21815    fn unregistered_slot(session_id: SessionId) -> SessionSlot {
21816        let (session_tx, _) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY);
21817        SessionSlot {
21818            session_tx,
21819            routing_opts: DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(session_id)),
21820            abort_handles: Default::default(),
21821            surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::from(SurbBalancerConfig::default())),
21822            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
21823            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
21824            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
21825            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
21826            pix_fill: Default::default(),
21827            returned_packets: Default::default(),
21828            cycle_budget: None,
21829            admission_token: Default::default(),
21830            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
21831        }
21832    }
21833
21834    /// A commit that finds its slot already gone must still commit the Session.
21835    ///
21836    /// The Session *was* established on this path — the Exit sends `SessionEstablished` before it
21837    /// commits, so an Entry can close or answer with a `SessionId`-scoped `SessionError` in that
21838    /// window — so the guard must be marked committed rather than rolled back, and the Session still
21839    /// counted. Only the admission is skipped: there is no slot left to carry its token. Skipping the
21840    /// commit instead would drift `METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS` down (the teardown already decremented it)
21841    /// and leave the teardown's "session closed" unpaired.
21842    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21843    async fn a_commit_without_a_slot_still_commits_the_session() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21844        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
21845        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
21846        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
21847
21848        let slot = unregistered_slot(session_id);
21849        let mut guard = mgr
21850            .allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone())
21851            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
21852
21853        // The teardown wins the race and removes the slot before the commit runs.
21854        assert!(
21855            mgr.sessions.remove(&session_id).is_some(),
21856            "the slot must have been registered"
21857        );
21858
21859        guard.commit(None, Some(&admission), 0);
21860
21861        assert!(
21862            guard.committed,
21863            "a Session that was established must be committed, not rolled back, even with no slot left"
21864        );
21865        assert_eq!(
21866            admission.admitted(&session_id),
21867            0,
21868            "with no slot to carry the token, nothing may be admitted"
21869        );
21870        assert_eq!(
21871            admission.retired(&session_id),
21872            0,
21873            "a commit that admitted nothing must retire nothing"
21874        );
21875        Ok(())
21876    }
21877
21878    /// A teardown that claims the token cell before `commit` runs forces the commit to retire its own
21879    /// admission.
21880    ///
21881    /// The order is the Exit-side one: `SessionEstablished` goes out before the commit, so a peer can
21882    /// close in that window. The teardown claims the cell and reads `NONE` (a no-op retire), and the
21883    /// commit then finds its `set` rejected — so it retires the admission it just made, or the ring
21884    /// would leak with no teardown ever removing it.
21885    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21886    async fn a_teardown_claiming_the_cell_first_forces_the_commit_to_retire_its_admission() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21887        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
21888        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
21889        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
21890
21891        let slot = unregistered_slot(session_id);
21892        let mut guard = mgr
21893            .allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone())
21894            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
21895
21896        // The teardown gets there first: it claims the cell and reads `NONE`, so its scheduled retire
21897        // is a no-op.
21898        assert_eq!(
21899            slot.claim_admission_token(),
21900            AdmissionToken::NONE,
21901            "an uncommitted slot's claimed token must be NONE"
21902        );
21903
21904        // The commit still runs and admits, but cannot record the token — so it must retire it.
21905        guard.commit(Some(&slot), Some(&admission), 100);
21906
21907        let minted = admission.minted_tokens();
21908        assert_eq!(
21909            minted.len(),
21910            1,
21911            "the commit must still admit the Session it was told to commit"
21912        );
21913        assert_eq!(
21914            admission.retire_tokens(),
21915            vec![minted[0]],
21916            "the admission the commit could not record must be retired by the commit itself"
21917        );
21918        Ok(())
21919    }
21920
21921    /// A commit must size the ring from a target the Entry announced before it.
21922    ///
21923    /// The Exit answers `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive can
21924    /// be processed while the ring does not exist yet. Its raise has no admission to widen; it records
21925    /// the figure on the slot, and the commit has to start from the larger of it and the target
21926    /// announced at establishment — otherwise an Entry that announces its main tier early gets a
21927    /// ping-tier ring and evicts everything minted past it (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739, one interleaving
21928    /// earlier).
21929    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21930    async fn a_commit_must_size_the_ring_from_a_target_announced_before_it() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21931        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
21932        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
21933        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
21934
21935        let slot = unregistered_slot(session_id);
21936        let mut guard = mgr
21937            .allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone())
21938            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
21939
21940        // The Entry's main tier, announced while the Session is established but not yet committed.
21941        slot.note_raised_surb_target(6_887);
21942        guard.commit(Some(&slot), Some(&admission), 688);
21943
21944        assert_eq!(
21945            vec![6_887],
21946            admission.admitted_targets(),
21947            "the commit must admit at the largest target already announced, not the ping tier"
21948        );
21949        Ok(())
21950    }
21951
21952    /// A commit whose re-read finds a *successor's* slot on the same pseudonym must not admit into it.
21953    ///
21954    /// The pseudonym is client-chosen and reusable, so a slot can be torn down and reallocated under
21955    /// the same key between a Session's `SessionEstablished` send and its parked commit. That commit
21956    /// re-reads the cache by key to land its token in the cached copy, and the copy it finds is then
21957    /// the successor's — admitting into it would stamp the successor's ring with this Session's token,
21958    /// and the successor's own commit would find the cell occupied and retire the successor's live
21959    /// admission, dropping a running Session to the quarantine. This is the commit-vs-commit arm the
21960    /// teardown-vs-commit test above does not reach: the slot is *present*, just not this one's, so the
21961    /// ownership marker — not absence — has to reject it.
21962    ///
21963    /// A true concurrent commit is not drivable from a test without instrumenting the manager, so the
21964    /// interleaving is built explicitly: A allocates and is torn down (freeing the key), B is allocated
21965    /// under the same key, and only then does A's parked commit run through `commit_slot_guard`.
21966    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
21967    async fn a_commit_must_not_admit_into_a_successors_slot_on_the_same_pseudonym() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
21968        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
21969        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
21970        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
21971        mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone()));
21972
21973        // A allocates and then loses its slot to a teardown, which also claims the cell.
21974        let mut guard_a = mgr
21975            .allocate_session_slot(pseudonym, unregistered_slot(pseudonym))
21976            .context("A's slot allocation must succeed")?;
21977        let slot_a = mgr
21978            .sessions
21979            .remove(&pseudonym)
21980            .context("the teardown must have found A's slot")?;
21981        assert_eq!(
21982            slot_a.claim_admission_token(),
21983            AdmissionToken::NONE,
21984            "A's teardown must claim the cell and read nothing, so its scheduled retire is a no-op"
21985        );
21986
21987        // B is allocated under the same key before A's commit resumes. B's slot is the one the cache
21988        // now hands back for that pseudonym.
21989        let guard_b = mgr
21990            .allocate_session_slot(pseudonym, unregistered_slot(pseudonym))
21991            .context("B's slot allocation must succeed under the freed pseudonym")?;
21992
21993        // A's commit re-reads the key and finds B's slot, which it must refuse as not its own.
21994        commit_slot_guard(&mut guard_a, &mgr.sessions, pseudonym, mgr.surb_admission.clone(), 100);
21995
21996        assert!(
21997            guard_a.committed,
21998            "A was established, so its commit must still mark it committed"
21999        );
22000        assert_eq!(
22001            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
22002            0,
22003            "A must not admit into B's slot — a foreign slot is no more A's to admit into than an absent one"
22004        );
22005        assert_eq!(
22006            admission.retired(&pseudonym),
22007            0,
22008            "A must not retire anything either: it admitted nothing"
22009        );
22010
22011        // B's own commit is the one that admits, and it must land on B's untouched cell.
22012        let mut guard_b = guard_b;
22013        commit_slot_guard(&mut guard_b, &mgr.sessions, pseudonym, mgr.surb_admission.clone(), 100);
22014        assert_eq!(
22015            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
22016            1,
22017            "B's commit is the only admission on this pseudonym and must still happen"
22018        );
22019        assert!(
22020            admission.retire_tokens().is_empty(),
22021            "B's live admission must not be retired by A's commit — the successor ring is not A's to release"
22022        );
22023        Ok(())
22024    }
22025
22026    /// What the Exit reports back to its pool must be what the Exit sent.
22027    ///
22028    /// The pool answers over a channel and nothing stops it answering for an SSA that is not in the
22029    /// batch, or for another Session entirely. Those replies are dropped from the wire; they must be
22030    /// dropped from the Exit's own memory of the batch too. Keying whole replies by `id.ssa_index()`
22031    /// did not do that: a foreign reply naming an in-batch index displaced the good entry, and
22032    /// `DepositNeeded` then handed the pool back deposit data belonging to another Session.
22033    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
22034    async fn a_foreign_deposit_reply_must_not_displace_what_the_exit_sent() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22035        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
22036
22037        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22038        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22039        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN];
22040
22041        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
22042            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
22043                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
22044                threshold: 2,
22045                surplus_shares: 1,
22046            })
22047            .into(),
22048            Arc::new(SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default())),
22049        );
22050        drop(pix_events);
22051        let _ = pix_toolbox;
22052
22053        let ssa_state = SessionSsaState::new(PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?);
22054
22055        // What the pool sent: the right entry, then a same-index entry belonging to another Session.
22056        let replies = vec![
22057            PixDepositData {
22058                id: PixAddressId::new(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN),
22059                data: b"mine".as_slice().into(),
22060            },
22061            PixDepositData {
22062                id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, SsaIndex::MIN),
22063                data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
22064            },
22065        ];
22066
22067        // Only the validated map is remembered, which is the whole point.
22068        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, replies)?;
22069        ssa_state.remember_sent_deposit_data(&validated);
22070
22071        let recalled = ssa_state.take_sent_deposit_data(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN);
22072        assert_eq!(
22073            b"mine".as_slice(),
22074            recalled.data.as_ref(),
22075            "the Exit must recall the payload it actually sent"
22076        );
22077        assert_eq!(
22078            PixAddressId::new(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN),
22079            recalled.id,
22080            "the id must name this Session and this index"
22081        );
22082
22083        // Consumed exactly once; a second cycle would see empty rather than a stale entry.
22084        assert!(
22085            ssa_state.take_sent_deposit_data(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN).is_empty(),
22086            "taking must remove the entry"
22087        );
22088
22089        Ok(())
22090    }
22091
22092    /// Runs [`request_deposit_data`](SessionManager::request_deposit_data) against a pool that answers
22093    /// with exactly what `script` returns, in that order.
22094    ///
22095    /// `script` is handed the ids the Exit asked for and returns the replies the pool will send, one
22096    /// at a time — which is what makes reply *ordering* expressible, and ordering is the only thing
22097    /// the tests below differ on from a run that never had a problem.
22098    ///
22099    /// The pool holds its sender open after the script runs out, rather than dropping it and ending
22100    /// the stream. A pool that closes the channel ends the read all by itself, which would let a test
22101    /// pass on that alone — the reason the collection stopped is exactly what these tests are about,
22102    /// so the only things left to stop it are the ones under test.
22103    async fn request_deposit_data_answered_with(
22104        session_id: SessionId,
22105        batch: &[SsaIndex],
22106        script: impl FnOnce(Vec<PixAddressId>) -> Vec<PixDepositData> + Send + 'static,
22107    ) -> errors::Result<HoprPixDepositData> {
22108        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
22109            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
22110                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
22111                threshold: 2,
22112                surplus_shares: 1,
22113            })
22114            .into(),
22115            Arc::new(SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default())),
22116        );
22117
22118        tokio::task::spawn(async move {
22119            let mut events = Box::pin(pix_events);
22120            if let Some(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositDataRequest(request)) = events.next().await {
22121                let mut created = request.deposit_data_created;
22122                for reply in script(request.deposit_ids) {
22123                    if created.send(reply).await.is_err() {
22124                        return;
22125                    }
22126                }
22127                // Held open, not dropped — see above. The task is torn down with the test's runtime.
22128                std::future::pending::<()>().await;
22129            }
22130        });
22131
22132        SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::request_deposit_data(
22133            &pix_toolbox,
22134            session_id,
22135            batch,
22136        )
22137        .await
22138    }
22139
22140    /// A reply the batch has no place for must not cost a reply that was asked for.
22141    ///
22142    /// The pool answers over one channel, and nothing about that channel separates a reply for this
22143    /// batch from another Session's. Reading a fixed number of *items* — one per requested SSA — let
22144    /// the first kind spend a slot belonging to the second, so a pool that answered every SSA and
22145    /// merely spoke out of turn lost the Session on the answer that got truncated.
22146    ///
22147    /// Ordering is the whole test: the same foreign reply arriving *after* the batch was complete
22148    /// never cost anything, because the collection had already stopped.
22149    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
22150    async fn a_foreign_reply_before_a_valid_one_must_not_truncate_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22151        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22152        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22153        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
22154
22155        let collected = request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, move |ids| {
22156            std::iter::once(PixDepositData {
22157                id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, SsaIndex::MIN),
22158                data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
22159            })
22160            .chain(ids.into_iter().map(|id| PixDepositData {
22161                id,
22162                data: b"mine".as_slice().into(),
22163            }))
22164            .collect()
22165        })
22166        .await
22167        .context("a pool that answered every requested SSA must not fail the request")?;
22168
22169        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, collected)
22170            .context("every SSA in the batch must come out with an entry")?;
22171
22172        assert_eq!(batch.len(), validated.len(), "the whole batch must be covered");
22173        for index in batch {
22174            assert_eq!(
22175                b"mine".as_slice(),
22176                validated[&index].0.as_ref(),
22177                "index {index} must carry this Session's payload"
22178            );
22179        }
22180
22181        Ok(())
22182    }
22183
22184    /// A second answer for an SSA already answered must not cost an SSA still outstanding.
22185    ///
22186    /// Same failure as the foreign reply above, from the other direction: the repeat is a reply the
22187    /// batch has no place for, and counting items charged it against the one SSA that had not been
22188    /// answered yet. Which copy of the repeat wins is not what is under test here — that
22189    /// [`deposit_data_for_batch`] takes the later one is incidental — only that the reply after it
22190    /// still arrives.
22191    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
22192    async fn a_duplicate_reply_before_a_valid_one_must_not_truncate_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22193        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22194        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
22195
22196        let collected = request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, |ids| {
22197            let mut replies = ids
22198                .iter()
22199                .map(|id| PixDepositData {
22200                    id: *id,
22201                    data: vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8].into_boxed_slice(),
22202                })
22203                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
22204            // The repeat of the first answer is inserted before the last one, so counting items
22205            // would have stopped on it and never read the SSA it was hiding.
22206            replies.insert(1, replies[0].clone());
22207            replies
22208        })
22209        .await
22210        .context("a pool that repeated itself but answered every SSA must not fail the request")?;
22211
22212        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, collected)
22213            .context("every SSA in the batch must come out with an entry")?;
22214
22215        assert_eq!(batch.len(), validated.len(), "the whole batch must be covered");
22216        for index in batch {
22217            assert_eq!(
22218                &[index.get() as u8],
22219                validated[&index].0.as_ref(),
22220                "index {index} must carry its own payload"
22221            );
22222        }
22223
22224        Ok(())
22225    }
22226
22227    /// Tolerating replies the batch has no place for must not become waiting for the deadline.
22228    ///
22229    /// Reading until every requested id is answered has no natural end when the pool never answers
22230    /// one, so the read is capped at twice the requested count. A pool that talks without ever
22231    /// closing the gap is cut off there and the request fails on the gap — which is the same
22232    /// verdict the deadline would reach, minus the [`DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`] spent reaching
22233    /// it, with the Session held open throughout.
22234    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
22235    async fn a_pool_answering_only_noise_must_fail_on_the_cap_not_the_deadline() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22236        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22237        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22238        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
22239
22240        // Exactly the cap, and not one of them is for this Session.
22241        let noise = move |ids: Vec<PixAddressId>| {
22242            ids.iter()
22243                .flat_map(|id| {
22244                    std::iter::repeat_n(
22245                        PixDepositData {
22246                            id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, id.ssa_index()),
22247                            data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
22248                        },
22249                        2,
22250                    )
22251                })
22252                .collect()
22253        };
22254
22255        // Well under the deadline: the point is that the cap ends the read, not the clock.
22256        let result = timeout(
22257            Duration::from_secs(1),
22258            request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, noise),
22259        )
22260        .await
22261        .context("the cap must end the read long before DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT")?;
22262
22263        assert!(
22264            matches!(
22265                result,
22266                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(
22267                    _
22268                )))
22269            ),
22270            "a pool that answered none of the requested SSAs must fail the request, got {result:?}"
22271        );
22272
22273        Ok(())
22274    }
22275
22276    /// The reply that lands exactly on the cap still counts.
22277    ///
22278    /// One reply earlier and the batch would be complete without the cap ever mattering, so this is
22279    /// the only arrangement that tells `take(2 * requested)` apart from `take(2 * requested - 1)`:
22280    /// every requested SSA is answered, but the last answer is the last reply the read will accept.
22281    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
22282    async fn the_last_reply_the_cap_allows_must_still_complete_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22283        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22284        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
22285        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
22286
22287        let collected = request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, move |ids| {
22288            // One unusable reply per requested id, then the answers themselves — `2 * requested`
22289            // replies in total, with the one that closes the gap sitting on the boundary.
22290            ids.iter()
22291                .map(|id| PixDepositData {
22292                    id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, id.ssa_index()),
22293                    data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
22294                })
22295                .chain(ids.iter().map(|id| PixDepositData {
22296                    id: *id,
22297                    data: vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8].into_boxed_slice(),
22298                }))
22299                .collect()
22300        })
22301        .await
22302        .context("the answer landing on the cap must be read, not cut off by it")?;
22303
22304        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, collected)
22305            .context("every SSA in the batch must come out with an entry")?;
22306
22307        assert_eq!(batch.len(), validated.len(), "the whole batch must be covered");
22308        for index in batch {
22309            assert_eq!(
22310                &[index.get() as u8],
22311                validated[&index].0.as_ref(),
22312                "index {index} must carry its own payload"
22313            );
22314        }
22315
22316        Ok(())
22317    }

22319    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
22320    // PIX egress gate pressure
22321    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
22322
22323    /// The egress path opens exactly one block episode per park, and closes it when the park ends.
22324    ///
22325    /// Asserted here rather than in the gate's own tests because the wiring is what can be wrong:
22326    /// the gate reports a verdict, and this is the only place that turns the verdict into an
22327    /// episode. A permit path that forgot to would leave `hopr_pix_gate_blocks_total` silent while
22328    /// egress was stalled -- exactly the fault the metric exists to surface.
22329    #[tokio::test]
22330    async fn a_parked_egress_packet_opens_and_closes_one_block_episode() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22331        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
22332
22333        probe::reset();
22334        // Strict prepay: the first packet is refused before anything is served.
22335        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
22336
22337        let permit = acquire_egress_permit(
22338            Some(gate.clone()),
22339            DestinationRouting::Return(HoprPseudonym::random().into()),
22340            ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(
22341                SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG,
22342                b"payload".as_slice(),
22343            )?),
22344        );
22345
22346        assert_eq!(
22347            1,
22348            probe::get("gate_blocks/predeposit_exhausted"),
22349            "the refusal must be counted as one episode beginning"
22350        );
22351        assert_eq!(
22352            0,
22353            probe::get("gate_block_observations/predeposit_exhausted"),
22354            "and must stay open while the packet is still parked"
22355        );
22356
22357        // Funding wakes the parked writer, which ends the episode.
22358        gate.release_service();
22359        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), permit)
22360            .await
22361            .context("funding must wake the parked packet")?
22362            .context("a funded gate must admit it")?;
22363
22364        assert_eq!(1, probe::get("gate_blocks/predeposit_exhausted"), "still one episode");
22365        assert_eq!(
22366            1,
22367            probe::get("gate_block_observations/predeposit_exhausted"),
22368            "resuming must close the episode exactly once"
22369        );
22370        Ok(())
22371    }
22372
22373    /// Cancelling a parked packet closes its episode too.
22374    ///
22375    /// The case `Drop` exists for: a Session torn down while a writer is parked drops the permit
22376    /// future without ever resolving it, and a timer that only closed on the resume path would be
22377    /// left open for every Session that died blocked.
22378    #[tokio::test]
22379    async fn dropping_a_parked_egress_packet_closes_its_episode() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22380        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
22381
22382        probe::reset();
22383        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
22384
22385        let permit = acquire_egress_permit(
22386            Some(gate.clone()),
22387            DestinationRouting::Return(HoprPseudonym::random().into()),
22388            ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(
22389                SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG,
22390                b"payload".as_slice(),
22391            )?),
22392        );
22393        // Poll it once so the episode is actually begun inside the future.
22394        assert!(
22395            timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), permit).await.is_err(),
22396            "the packet must park rather than resolve"
22397        );
22398
22399        assert_eq!(1, probe::get("gate_blocks/predeposit_exhausted"));
22400        assert_eq!(
22401            1,
22402            probe::get("gate_block_observations/predeposit_exhausted"),
22403            "a cancelled park must still close its episode"
22404        );
22405        Ok(())
22406    }
22407
22408    /// A poisoned gate is counted as a refusal but opens no episode.
22409    #[tokio::test]
22410    async fn a_closed_gate_refuses_without_opening_an_episode() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22411        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;

22462    /// Offers `gate` one return packet, counted against `estimator` the way a data sink counts it.
22463    fn offer_counted_packet(
22464        gate: &Arc<ServiceGate>,
22465        estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
22466    ) -> anyhow::Result<EgressPermit> {
22467        Ok(acquire_egress_permit(
22468            Some(gate.clone()),
22469            DestinationRouting::Return(HoprPseudonym::random().into()),
22470            count_return_packet_surb(estimator, small_outgoing_packet()?),
22471        ))
22472    }

22474    /// A counted packet the gate fails never reaches routing resolution, so it gives its SURB back,
22475    /// whether the gate was closed before it came or was poisoned while it was parked.
22476    #[tokio::test]
22477    async fn a_counted_packet_the_gate_fails_should_give_its_surb_back() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22478        use crate::balancer::SurbFlowEstimator;
22479
22480        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
22481        estimator.produced.fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
22482
22483        let closed = ServiceGate::new(10, 10);
22484        closed.poison();
22485        assert!(
22486            offer_counted_packet(&closed, &estimator)?.await.is_err(),
22487            "a poisoned gate must refuse"
22488        );
22489        assert_eq!(
22490            10,
22491            estimator.saturating_diff(),
22492            "the refused packet's SURB is back in the held count"
22493        );
22494
22495        // Strict prepay: the packet parks, and poisoning fails the park.
22496        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
22497        let mut parked = offer_counted_packet(&gate, &estimator)?;
22498        assert!(
22499            futures::poll!(&mut parked).is_pending(),
22500            "the packet must park rather than resolve"
22501        );
22502        assert_eq!(9, estimator.saturating_diff(), "a parked packet stays counted");
22503
22504        gate.poison();
22505        assert!(parked.await.is_err(), "poisoning must fail the park");
22506        assert_eq!(10, estimator.saturating_diff(), "the failed packet's SURB is back too");
22507        Ok(())
22508    }

22510    /// A parked packet dropped with its Session's sink gives its SURB back too, whether or not the sink
22511    /// had polled it yet.
22512    #[tokio::test]
22513    async fn a_counted_packet_dropped_while_parked_should_give_its_surb_back() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22514        use crate::balancer::SurbFlowEstimator;
22515
22516        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
22517        estimator.produced.fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
22518        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
22519
22520        drop(offer_counted_packet(&gate, &estimator)?);
22521        assert_eq!(
22522            10,
22523            estimator.saturating_diff(),
22524            "a park dropped before its first poll gives its SURB back"
22525        );
22526
22527        let mut parked = offer_counted_packet(&gate, &estimator)?;
22528        assert!(
22529            futures::poll!(&mut parked).is_pending(),
22530            "the packet must park rather than resolve"
22531        );
22532        drop(parked);
22533        assert_eq!(10, estimator.saturating_diff(), "and so does one dropped mid-park");
22534        Ok(())
22535    }

22537    /// An admitted packet stays counted. It goes on with its refund, for routing resolution to give back
22538    /// if it starves there, whether the gate admits it at once or once the supervisor funds the park.
22539    #[tokio::test]
22540    async fn a_counted_packet_the_gate_admits_should_keep_its_surb_counted() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22541        use crate::balancer::SurbFlowEstimator;
22542
22543        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
22544        estimator.produced.fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
22545        let refund = SurbRefund::to(estimator.refunded.clone());
22546
22547        let (_, data) = offer_counted_packet(&ServiceGate::new(10, 10), &estimator)?
22548            .await
22549            .context("a gate with budget must admit at once")?;
22550        assert_eq!(
22551            refund, data.surb_refund,
22552            "admitted at once, the packet keeps its refund"
22553        );

22555        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
22556        let mut parked = offer_counted_packet(&gate, &estimator)?;
22557        assert!(
22558            futures::poll!(&mut parked).is_pending(),
22559            "the packet must park rather than resolve"
22560        );
22561        gate.release_service();
22562        let (_, data) = timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), parked)
22563            .await
22564            .context("funding must wake the parked packet")?
22565            .context("a funded gate must admit it")?;
22566        assert_eq!(
22567            refund, data.surb_refund,
22568            "admitted after a park, the packet gets its refund back"

22572        Ok(())

22574
22575    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
22576    // The action driver's decision to re-send an SSA request
22577    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
22578
22579    /// A request as the driver would have stored it after sending.
22580    ///
22581    /// Any Start message will do: the decision only ever hands back a reference to what was stored,
22582    /// and the tests tell it apart from a copy by address.
22583    fn stored_request(session_id: HoprPseudonym) -> HoprStartProtocol {
22584        HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
22585            session_id,
22586            flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState.into(),
22587            additional_data: 0,
22588        })
22589    }
22590
22591    /// A reconstructor with a pending Exit registration for each of `indices`, as a sent request leaves it.
22592    fn reconstructor_awaiting(
22593        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
22594        indices: &[u32],
22595    ) -> anyhow::Result<(SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>, Vec<SsaId<HoprPseudonym>>)> {
22596        let reconstructor = SsaReconstructor::<HoprPixSpec>::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default());
22597        let ssa_ids = indices
22598            .iter()
22599            .map(|&index| {
22600                let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(index).context("SSA indices are non-zero")?);
22601                reconstructor.new_exit_commitment(ssa_id, small_pix_params())?;
22602                Ok(ssa_id)
22603            })
22604            .collect::<anyhow::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
22605        Ok((reconstructor, ssa_ids))
22606    }
22607
22608    /// Delivers the whole constant-term set of `ssa_id`, which is what an Entry's answer is.
22609    ///
22610    /// The dummy constant terms sum to the identity, whose discrete logarithm is zero, so an honest
22611    /// proof of knowledge over it is constructible — the same filler the commitment tests use.
22612    fn complete_commitment(
22613        reconstructor: &SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>,
22614        ssa_id: SsaId<HoprPseudonym>,
22615    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22616        use hopr_protocol_pix::{Field, PixGroup, PixScalar, PolynomialIndex, SsaCommitmentProof};
22617
22618        let zero = <PixScalar<HoprPixSpec> as Field>::ZERO;
22619        let proof = SsaCommitmentProof::<HoprPixSpec>::prove(&ssa_id, &zero, &PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default())
22620            .context("the identity proof must be constructible")?;
22621        let polys = small_pix_params().polys_per_ssa() as PolynomialIndex;
22622        let state = reconstructor.insert_coefficient_commitments(
22623            ssa_id,
22624            0,
22625            Some(proof),
22626            (0..polys).map(|poly| (poly, PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes())),
22627        )?;
22628        anyhow::ensure!(state.is_verifiable, "the fixture must have completed the commitment");
22629        Ok(())
22630    }
22631
22632    /// A pending batch is re-sent as the stored message itself, not as a rebuilt one.
22633    ///
22634    /// Identity matters here: a rebuilt request would carry new Exit secrets, which the reconstructor
22635    /// refuses as a duplicate of the pending commitment, and the deposit pool answers a batch once.
22636    #[test]
22637    fn a_pending_batch_is_resent_as_the_stored_message() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22638        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22639        let (reconstructor, ssa_ids) = reconstructor_awaiting(pseudonym, &[1, 2])?;
22640        let last_request = (ssa_ids.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym));
22641
22642        match resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &ssa_ids, &reconstructor) {
22643            ResendDecision::Send(message) => assert!(
22644                std::ptr::eq(message, &last_request.1),
22645                "the stored message must go out, not a copy of it"
22646            ),
22647            refusal => anyhow::bail!("a pending batch must be re-sent, got {refusal:?}"),
22648        }
22649        Ok(())
22650    }
22651
22652    /// Ids that are not exactly the stored batch are refused, and before any registration is consulted.
22653    ///
22654    /// The reconstructor here holds no registrations at all, so a mismatch that was decided *after*
22655    /// reading them would come out as `RegistrationGone`.
22656    #[test]
22657    fn a_resend_of_anything_but_the_last_batch_sent_is_refused() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22658        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22659        let ids = |indices: &[u32]| -> anyhow::Result<Vec<SsaId<HoprPseudonym>>> {
22660            indices
22661                .iter()
22662                .map(|&index| Ok(SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero")?)))
22663                .collect()
22664        };
22665        let reconstructor = SsaReconstructor::<HoprPixSpec>::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default());
22666        let last_request = (ids(&[3, 4])?, stored_request(pseudonym));
22667
22668        for (label, asked) in [
22669            ("an earlier batch", ids(&[1, 2])?),
22670            ("a prefix of the batch", ids(&[3])?),
22671            ("a superset of the batch", ids(&[3, 4, 5])?),
22672            ("the batch in another order", ids(&[4, 3])?),
22673            ("another Session's batch", {
22674                let other = HoprPseudonym::random();
22675                vec![
22676                    SsaId::new(other, SsaIndex::new(3).context("non-zero")?),
22677                    SsaId::new(other, SsaIndex::new(4).context("non-zero")?),
22678                ]
22679            }),
22680        ] {
22681            assert!(
22682                matches!(
22683                    resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &asked, &reconstructor),
22684                    ResendDecision::NotLastRequest
22685                ),
22686                "{label} is not the last request sent"
22687            );
22688        }
22689
22690        assert!(
22691            matches!(
22692                resend_payload(None, &last_request.0, &reconstructor),
22693                ResendDecision::NotLastRequest
22694            ),
22695            "with nothing stored there is nothing to send"
22696        );
22697        Ok(())
22698    }
22699
22700    /// A member whose registration is gone refuses the whole batch, wherever it stands in it.
22701    ///
22702    /// Gone is retired or idled out. Either way the Entry's answer would reach an Exit with nothing to
22703    /// match it against, so asking for it again can only waste a SURB.
22704    #[test]
22705    fn a_resend_with_a_missing_registration_is_refused() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22706        for retired_position in [0, 1] {
22707            let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22708            let (reconstructor, ssa_ids) = reconstructor_awaiting(pseudonym, &[1, 2])?;
22709            let last_request = (ssa_ids.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym));
22710            assert!(
22711                matches!(
22712                    resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &ssa_ids, &reconstructor),
22713                    ResendDecision::Send(_)
22714                ),
22715                "the control: before the retirement the batch is sent"
22716            );
22717
22718            reconstructor.retire_ssa(ssa_ids[retired_position]);
22719            assert!(
22720                matches!(
22721                    resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &ssa_ids, &reconstructor),
22722                    ResendDecision::RegistrationGone
22723                ),
22724                "a batch whose member {retired_position} was retired must not be re-sent"
22725            );
22726        }
22727        Ok(())
22728    }
22729
22730    /// A member whose commitment is complete is no reason to refuse the batch.
22731    ///
22732    /// The supervisor re-sends the whole batch for as long as *any* member has heard nothing, and the
22733    /// Entry publishes a batch one member after another, so a complete first member beside a second
22734    /// that never arrived is exactly the state a publication cut at a member boundary leaves. The
22735    /// Entry's repeat branch publishes only the members it still owes, so sending the whole batch costs
22736    /// nothing for the one that is done, short of a repeat late enough to mean a burst was lost.
22737    #[test]
22738    fn a_resend_goes_out_while_any_member_is_still_waiting() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22739        for completed_position in [0, 1] {
22740            let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22741            let (reconstructor, ssa_ids) = reconstructor_awaiting(pseudonym, &[1, 2])?;
22742            let last_request = (ssa_ids.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym));
22743
22744            complete_commitment(&reconstructor, ssa_ids[completed_position])?;
22745            assert!(
22746                matches!(
22747                    resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &ssa_ids, &reconstructor),
22748                    ResendDecision::Send(_)
22749                ),
22750                "member {completed_position} is complete and the other is not, so the batch is sent whole"
22751            );
22752        }
22753        Ok(())
22754    }
22755
22756    /// A batch whose every member is complete is refused: the Entry has answered in full.
22757    ///
22758    /// What the supervisor may still have queued is a tick that raced the last answer, and it must find
22759    /// nothing to send.
22760    #[test]
22761    fn a_resend_for_a_batch_complete_in_full_is_refused() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22762        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22763        let (reconstructor, ssa_ids) = reconstructor_awaiting(pseudonym, &[1, 2])?;
22764        let last_request = (ssa_ids.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym));
22765
22766        for ssa_id in &ssa_ids {
22767            complete_commitment(&reconstructor, *ssa_id)?;
22768        }
22769        assert!(
22770            matches!(
22771                resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &ssa_ids, &reconstructor),
22772                ResendDecision::CommitmentComplete
22773            ),
22774            "a batch whose every member completed must not be re-sent"
22775        );
22776        Ok(())
22777    }
22778
22779    /// A missing registration decides before completeness does, whichever member is which.
22780    #[test]
22781    fn a_missing_registration_outweighs_a_complete_one() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22782        for (retired_position, completed_position) in [(0, 1), (1, 0)] {
22783            let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22784            let (reconstructor, ssa_ids) = reconstructor_awaiting(pseudonym, &[1, 2])?;
22785            let last_request = (ssa_ids.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym));
22786
22787            complete_commitment(&reconstructor, ssa_ids[completed_position])?;
22788            reconstructor.retire_ssa(ssa_ids[retired_position]);
22789            assert!(
22790                matches!(
22791                    resend_payload(Some(&last_request), &ssa_ids, &reconstructor),
22792                    ResendDecision::RegistrationGone
22793                ),
22794                "member {retired_position} is gone and member {completed_position} is complete"
22795            );
22796        }
22797        Ok(())
22798    }

22800    /// Retiring any member of the stored batch forgets the request, and retiring anything else does not.
22801    #[test]
22802    fn retiring_a_member_forgets_the_stored_request() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22803        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
22804        let id = |index: u32| -> anyhow::Result<SsaId<HoprPseudonym>> {
22805            Ok(SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero")?))
22806        };
22807        let batch = vec![id(3)?, id(4)?];
22808
22809        for member in &batch {
22810            let mut last_request = Some((batch.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym)));
22811            forget_request_of(&mut last_request, member);
22812            assert!(
22813                last_request.is_none(),
22814                "{member} is a member, so the request goes with it"
22815            );
22816        }
22817
22818        let mut last_request = Some((batch.clone(), stored_request(pseudonym)));
22819        forget_request_of(&mut last_request, &id(2)?);
22820        forget_request_of(&mut last_request, &id(5)?);
22821        forget_request_of(
22822            &mut last_request,
22823            &SsaId::new(HoprPseudonym::random(), SsaIndex::new(3).context("non-zero")?),
22824        );
22825        assert_eq!(
22826            Some(&batch),
22827            last_request.as_ref().map(|(ids, _)| ids),
22828            "the retirement of an earlier batch, a later one or another Session's must not drop it"
22829        );
22830
22831        let mut nothing = None;
22832        forget_request_of(&mut nothing, &batch[0]);
22833        assert!(nothing.is_none(), "forgetting nothing leaves nothing");
22834        Ok(())
22835    }

22841    /// One percent of the target, at least 32, and never more than a quarter of it.
22842    #[test]
22843    fn the_keep_alive_reserve_should_be_one_percent_of_the_target_and_never_more_than_a_quarter() {
22844        for (target, reserve, why) in [
22845            (19_264, 192, "production target: one percent"),
22846            (2_400, 32, "test-scale target: the floor"),
22847            (3_200, 32, "one percent is the floor exactly"),
22848            (10_000, 100, "one percent above the floor"),
22849            (128, 32, "smallest target the floor fits in a quarter of"),
22850            (40, 10, "a shallow buffer keeps three quarters for data"),
22851            (0, 0, "no buffer, no reserve"),
22852        ] {
22853            assert_eq!(reserve, keep_alive_surb_reserve(target), "{why}");
22854        }
22855    }
22856
22857    fn data_packet() -> anyhow::Result<EgressItem> {
22858        Ok((
22859            DestinationRouting::Return(HoprPseudonym::random().into()),
22860            ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(
22861                SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG,
22862                b"payload".as_slice(),
22863            )?),
22864        ))
22865    }
22866
22867    /// The Exit must not spend its last SURBs on data: they are what its keep-alives, level reports
22868    /// and distress signals go out on. At the reserve the sink holds the packet, and it counts it
22869    /// against the stock only when it goes on; once the stock is above the reserve again it goes.
22870    #[tokio::test]
22871    async fn data_should_be_held_back_while_the_surb_stock_sits_at_the_keep_alive_reserve() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22872        let (tx, mut forwarded) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<EgressItem>();
22873        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
22874        let balancer = balancer_with_target(3_200);
22875        let reserve = current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer);
22876        assert_eq!(32, reserve);
22877        estimator.produced.store(reserve, Ordering::Relaxed);
22878
22879        let mut sink = Box::pin(exit_data_egress(
22880            tx.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
22881            HoprPseudonym::random(),
22882            estimator.clone(),
22883            balancer,
22884            None,
22885            true,
22886        ));
22887        let item = data_packet()?;
22888        let sending = tokio::spawn(async move { sink.send(item).await });
22889
22890        assert!(
22891            timeout(
22892                Duration::from_millis(3 * SURB_RESERVE_POLL.as_millis() as u64),
22893                forwarded.next()
22894            )
22895            .await
22896            .is_err(),
22897            "a stock at the reserve must not send data"
22898        );
22899        assert_eq!(0, estimator.estimate_surbs_consumed(), "a held packet consumes nothing");
22900        assert!(!sending.is_finished());
22901
22902        // A level report or a refill brings one more SURB than the reserve.
22903        estimator.produced.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
22904        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), forwarded.next())
22905            .await
22906            .context("the packet must go once the stock is above the reserve")?
22907            .context("the sink must have forwarded it")?;
22908        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sending).await???;
22909        assert_eq!(1, estimator.estimate_surbs_consumed());
22910        Ok(())
22911    }
22912
22913    /// The common case: above the reserve nothing waits, and the packet is booked as it was.
22914    #[tokio::test]
22915    async fn data_should_pass_straight_through_above_the_keep_alive_reserve() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22916        let (tx, mut forwarded) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<EgressItem>();
22917        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
22918        estimator.produced.store(33, Ordering::Relaxed);
22919
22920        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
22921        let balancer = balancer_with_target(3_200);
22922        assert!(
22923            hold_for_surb_reserve(session_id, &estimator, &balancer).is_none(),
22924            "no hold, no allocation"
22925        );
22926
22927        let mut sink = Box::pin(exit_data_egress(
22928            tx.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
22929            session_id,
22930            estimator.clone(),
22931            balancer,
22932            None,
22933            true,
22934        ));
22935        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sink.send(data_packet()?))
22936            .await
22937            .context("above the reserve the packet must not wait")??;
22938        assert!(forwarded.try_recv().is_ok(), "forwarded");
22939        assert_eq!(1, estimator.estimate_surbs_consumed());
22940        Ok(())

22943    /// Data the Exit sends is counted with the refund of its SURB, as every return packet is: a packet
22944    /// the gate refuses gives its SURB back at once, and one the sink forwards carries the refund on, for
22945    /// routing resolution to give back if it finds no SURB.
22946    #[tokio::test]
22947    async fn data_the_exit_sends_should_carry_the_refund_of_its_surb() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
22948        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
22949        estimator.produced.store(40, Ordering::Relaxed);
22950
22951        let closed = ServiceGate::new(10, 10);
22952        closed.poison();
22953        let (tx, _never_forwarded) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<EgressItem>();
22954        let mut refused = Box::pin(exit_data_egress(
22955            tx.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
22956            HoprPseudonym::random(),
22957            estimator.clone(),
22958            balancer_with_target(3_200),
22959            Some(closed),
22960            true,
22961        ));
22962        assert!(
22963            timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), refused.send(data_packet()?))
22964                .await
22965                .context("a closed gate answers at once")?
22966                .is_err(),
22967            "a closed gate must refuse"
22968        );
22969        assert_eq!(
22970            40,
22971            estimator.saturating_diff(),
22972            "the refused packet's SURB is back in the held count"
22973        );
22974
22975        let (tx, mut forwarded) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<EgressItem>();
22976        let mut sink = Box::pin(exit_data_egress(
22977            tx.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
22978            HoprPseudonym::random(),
22979            estimator.clone(),
22980            balancer_with_target(3_200),
22981            None,
22982            true,
22983        ));
22984        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sink.send(data_packet()?))
22985            .await
22986            .context("above the reserve the packet must not wait")??;
22987        let (_, data) = forwarded.try_recv().ok().context("the sink must have forwarded it")?;
22988        assert!(data.surb_refund.is_counted(), "a forwarded packet carries its refund");
22989        assert_eq!(
22990            39,
22991            estimator.saturating_diff(),
22992            "and is counted until it takes its SURB"
22993        );
22994        data.surb_refund.give_back();
22995        assert_eq!(
22996            40,
22997            estimator.saturating_diff(),
22998            "a packet that finds no SURB gives it back"
22999        );
23000        Ok(())
23001    }

23032    /// The Exit's state for a Session whose Entry asks for `target` and has shown, by a keep-alive, that
23033    /// it refills the Exit's stock.
23034    fn balancer_with_target(target: u64) -> Arc<BalancerStateValues> {
23035        let balancer = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
23036            target_surb_buffer_size: target,
23037            ..Default::default()
23038        }));
23039        balancer.note_counterparty_refills();
23040        balancer
23041    }
23042
23043    /// An Entry without a SURB balancer announces no target, so the Exit's balancer runs at its own fallback
23044    /// (50 at the defaults, a reserve of 12; an Entry that predates this announces the same figure itself).
23045    /// Such an Entry attaches one SURB to each data packet and sends no keep-alives: nothing would raise the
23046    /// stock above the reserve. Until a keep-alive shows the Entry refills, the Exit sends at any stock.
23047    #[tokio::test]
23048    async fn data_should_not_be_held_for_an_entry_that_has_not_shown_it_refills() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
23049        let (tx, mut forwarded) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<EgressItem>();
23050        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
23051        estimator.produced.store(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
23052        let balancer = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
23053            target_surb_buffer_size: 50,
23054            ..Default::default()
23055        }));
23056        assert_eq!(12, current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer));
23057
23058        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
23059        let mut sink = Box::pin(exit_data_egress(
23060            tx.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
23061            session_id,
23062            estimator.clone(),
23063            balancer.clone(),
23064            None,
23065            true,
23066        ));
23067        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sink.send(data_packet()?))
23068            .await
23069            .context("the reply must not wait for a stock the Entry will never send")??;
23070        assert!(
23071            forwarded.try_recv().is_ok(),
23072            "forwarded on the one SURB the request brought"
23073        );
23074
23075        balancer.note_counterparty_refills();
23076        assert!(
23077            hold_for_surb_reserve(session_id, &estimator, &balancer).is_some(),
23078            "once the Entry refills, a stock at the reserve holds data again"
23079        );
23080        Ok(())
23081    }

23083    /// The reserve follows the target the Entry asks for now, not the one the Session opened with: an
23084    /// Entry that lowers its target keeps the stock below the old reserve, and with the old reserve the
23085    /// data would be held for good.

23087    async fn a_lowered_target_should_lower_the_reserve_and_release_held_data() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
23088        let (tx, mut forwarded) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<EgressItem>();
23089        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
23090        let balancer = balancer_with_target(7_000);

23092        estimator.produced.store(40, Ordering::Relaxed);
23093
23094        let mut sink = Box::pin(exit_data_egress(
23095            tx.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
23096            HoprPseudonym::random(),
23097            estimator.clone(),
23098            balancer.clone(),
23099            None,
23100            true,
23101        ));
23102        let item = data_packet()?;
23103        let sending = tokio::spawn(async move { sink.send(item).await });
23104        assert!(
23105            timeout(
23106                Duration::from_millis(3 * SURB_RESERVE_POLL.as_millis() as u64),
23107                forwarded.next()

23109            .await
23110            .is_err(),
23111            "40 SURBs are below the reserve of a 7000 target"

23114        // The Entry lowers its target: the reserve of 160 is 32, and 40 SURBs are above it.
23115        balancer.target_surb_buffer_size.store(160, Ordering::Relaxed);
23116        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), forwarded.next())
23117            .await
23118            .context("the packet must go once the lowered reserve is below the stock")?
23119            .context("the sink must have forwarded it")?;
23120        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sending).await???;
